#### THE WIRE TYPES GET A GENERATOR AND IT SHIPS PROVING ITSELF ON ONE TYPE ON PURPOSE, THE DESIGN WAS WRONG ABOUT WHERE THE BOUNDARY ENDS, EVERY CORRECTION ROUND THE FOUR TASK REVIEWS FOUND WAS PROSE — FIVE OF THE SIX WRITTEN BY THE PLAN OR THE SPEC RATHER THAN BY AN IMPLEMENTER — AND THE WHOLE-BRANCH REVIEW THEN FOUND A CRITICAL IN A FILE NO TASK EDITED (2026-08-29, branch `wire-type-generation`, `b77fd04..a61db33`, 22 commits, plus the entry commits)

Design: [`../specs/2026-08-29-wire-type-generation-design.md`](../specs/2026-08-29-wire-type-generation-design.md). Plan: [`2026-08-29-wire-type-generation-plumbing.md`](2026-08-29-wire-type-generation-plumbing.md).

Opens the slice filed at the close of `sharing-aware-decode` under "WHAT STAYS OPEN" — *"`web/src/types.ts` learned the new variant; nothing gates that it will learn the next one. The Rust `Decoded` enum and the TypeScript union are kept in agreement by hand."* What ships here is the plumbing that ends the hand-keeping: a default-off `ts` feature on `redextape-core` and `redextape-wasm`, `ts-rs` derives generating TypeScript into a gitignored `web/bindings/`, `web/src/types.ts` re-exporting a generated type instead of declaring it, and generation wired into `pnpm run typecheck`, `test` and `build` — deliberately NOT into `build:app`, which is the one script the Dockerfile's Rust-free stage runs — into the CI `web` job as a step of its own, and into `scripts/setup-dev.sh` so a fresh clone typechecks.

**IT GENERATES EXACTLY ONE TYPE, AND THAT IS THE DESIGN'S §11 RATHER THAN AN UNFINISHED JOB.** `Span` is the whole of `web/bindings/` at this commit. `grep -c '^export type [A-Za-z]' web/src/types.ts` reads 17, and **all but one of those are derivable**: sixteen name a Rust `struct` or `enum` that can carry a `TS` derive — eleven in `redextape-core`, five in `redextape-wasm` — and PRs 2 and 3 move those sixteen, together with roughly 87 lines of prose that relocate from TypeScript comments into Rust doc comments. The exception is `Classified`, and it is named here rather than only under WHAT STAYS OPEN because a bare "seventeen" beside the spec's "sixteen" was two counts of overlapping sets with neither set defined where it was used. Prose relocation is where a slice of this shape stops landing, so the pipeline is proved end to end before any of it moves: the generated `Span` was compared field by field against the hand-written one it replaced, `usize` generated `number` rather than `bigint`, and the plan's stop condition for the `bigint` class did not fire.

##### THE ONE OPEN QUESTION THE DESIGN CARRIED IS SETTLED, AND THE ROW WAS SHOWN CAPABLE OF FAILING BEFORE IT WAS RELIED ON

Design §14 question 1 — does `ts-rs` 10.1.0's runtime build for `wasm32-unknown-unknown`? — was not measured when the design was written. It does: `cargo check --target wasm32-unknown-unknown -p redextape-core --lib --features ts` is clean, and `scripts/check-all.sh` now carries a clippy row, a test row and a wasm32 row for the `ts` configuration of each of the two crates that have the feature — that row among them.

A gate row that passes is worth nothing until it has been shown able to fail, which is this repository's standing rule — *a gate that would pass anything is worse than no gate*, the bar the wasm gate was written to. So `mimalloc` was forced into the `ts` feature and the row was run: it failed on `libmimalloc-sys v0.1.49`, C code compiled under `--target=wasm32-unknown-unknown` that cannot find `wchar.h`, exit 101. The edit was then reverted and the row went green again. The demonstration is the record that the leg is live, and it stands whichever way the answer had gone.

##### THE DESIGN WAS WRONG ABOUT WHERE THE BOUNDARY ENDS, AND A REVIEW OF A COMMENT IS WHAT FOUND IT

Task 1's review was scoped to a Cargo.toml comment. It counted the `serde` derives in `redextape-core` and got fifteen, against the twelve the design's inventory implied. Chasing that gap produced a distinction the design had never drawn: **the boundary has classes, and §1 had inventoried one of them.**

`Session::link_index` does not go through serde at all. It hand-assembles a columnar JS value with `js_sys::Uint32Array` and `Reflect::set`, and its TypeScript mirror is `LinkIndexWire` in `web/src/link.ts` — twelve fields, camelCase names, typed-array columns. `LinkIndex`'s `Serialize` derive is dead weight for the wire, and **`ts-rs` cannot generate `LinkIndexWire`**, because the shape is produced by marshalling code rather than by a type; generating from the Rust declaration would emit a confidently wrong file describing snake_case fields and `Array<[Span, TokenClass]>` where the wire carries `lambdaSpanStart: Uint32Array`. `compile`'s return value is assembled the same way.

That type lives in `web/src/link.ts`, **not in `web/src/types.ts`** — outside the single file the design's inventory was built from, which is exactly why the first draft could imply that file was the whole boundary. The correction is recorded as spec §1.1, which now carries the full four-class table and accounts for all fifteen core derives so that nobody recounts: eleven generated, one hand-assembled (`LinkIndex`), two serialized with no TypeScript consumer yet (`TermTree`, `TermNode`), and one whose only use site is `serde(skip)`ped (`Dir`). So this slice, complete, makes seventeen types undriftable and leaves a twelve-field wire type hand-written and unwatched. Naming that is the point of the correction.

##### EVERY CORRECTION ROUND ON THIS BRANCH WAS PROSE, AND FIVE OF THE SIX WERE THE PLAN'S OR THE SPEC'S OWN TEXT

**The implementation was approved on its first PER-TASK review, every task.** Four tasks, four Approved verdicts, and no mechanism — no `.rs`, no manifest key, no shell, no `package.json` wiring — was changed because a review of ONE TASK'S DIFF asked for it. The only non-prose fix inside the task sequence, `b7202a4`, came from running the gate rather than from reading a diff, and has its own section below. Every task-review finding was about a sentence, and the sentences were mostly not written by the people implementing:

**THE QUALIFIER "PER-TASK" IS DOING REAL WORK IN THAT PARAGRAPH, AND IT WAS ADDED AFTER THE FACT.** The sentence originally read "approved on its first review, every task", and offered "no mechanism was changed because a review asked for it" as the branch's summary. **The whole-branch review then changed three mechanisms** — `web/package.json`, `scripts/setup-dev.sh` and `scripts/check-all.sh`, one of them a Critical — and each is recorded in its own section below. Four green task reviews were the CONDITION for that review being worth running, not a reason to skip it, which is the standing conclusion this file already holds. A branch summary written before the last review is a summary of part of the branch.

1. `102391c` — a count of core's wire types asserted in a Cargo.toml comment without being run. Replaced with the property rather than a bigger number.
2. `130fc6d` — a causal mechanism. The comment justified forwarding the `ts` feature to core by a dangling-import hazard; the review looked for an instance and found none. Every field across the wasm crate's five wire types is `bool`, `String`, `usize`, `u64`, the wasm-local `RunStatus`, or `NodeId`, and `NodeId` is a transparent alias for `u32` that inlines as a TypeScript `number` and generates no import at all. **The forwarding is right and the stated reason was not**, so the comment now says the switch is coherent rather than load-bearing, and names what would make it load-bearing later.
3. `9820b6a` — that same field-type list, imprecise: several of those fields are `Option`-wrapped.
4. `4750abf` — a wrong class framing in the spec, which had called Class A "serialized by serde" when `Move` carries no serde derive at all. `Move` never crosses the wire; `RuleView.moves` is `Vec<String>`, stringified by `viewmodel::move_text`, and `Move` gains a `TS` derive only as that field's override target.
5. `3014def` — a `.gitignore` comment asserting that `typecheck`, `test` and `build:app` regenerate the bindings, which was Task 4's wiring and not yet true of the tree. Fixed by **deleting** the clause rather than rewording it, on the ground that a removal cannot introduce a fifth false claim.
6. `6b98a25` — the same class again, in a different file: `web/src/types.ts`'s new header asserting the same run-order that Task 4 had not yet wired.

**Five of those six sentences were written in a task brief, the plan or the spec and applied verbatim by an implementer** — rounds 1 and 2 are the two lines Task 1's brief printed for `redextape-wasm`'s `[features]` block, round 4 is the spec's own §1.1, round 5 is the five-line `.gitignore` comment Task 2's brief printed, and round 6 is the header paragraph Task 3's brief printed. **The sixth is the interesting one: round 3's defect was introduced by round 2's fix.** Correcting the mechanism required naming the field types, the naming was wrong in detail, and the only text on this branch that no brief authored is text written to correct a brief.

Rounds 1 through 3 are all the same comment block above `redextape-wasm`'s `ts` feature, which now runs to nine comment lines and was corrected three times. **The rule this branch earned and wrote into its own plan: write the tree you have, not the tree the next task will build.** Both of the last two rounds are a comment describing a state a later task creates, and both were caught by a reviewer reading the comment against the tree in front of it rather than against the plan. A seventh prose fix landed for the same reason one step out: `86ada48` corrects `check-all.sh`'s own header, which said "Six hooks" and named two tree-wide gates, when the file it describes has nine hooks and four `always_run` ones — a stale count nobody had re-derived, and `scripts/setup-dev.sh` printed the same six to anyone running it.

##### A DEFECT NO TASK'S DIFF CONTAINED, FOUND BY RUNNING THE GATE RATHER THAN BY REVIEWING IT

`scripts/check-all.sh` gained a `base|test|-p redextape-core --features ts` row in Task 1. Task 4 ran the gate, and the run left an untracked file behind.

`ts-rs` writes its generated TypeScript during `cargo test`, and it resolves `TS_RS_EXPORT_DIR` **against each crate's manifest directory**, not against the workspace root — so "unset" does not mean "nowhere", it means "beside the crate". Every gate run was therefore writing `crates/redextape-core/bindings/Span.ts`, untracked, and outside `.gitignore`'s `/web/bindings/` entry. A `git add -A` would have committed it.

**This is the exact hazard the design had already documented, reached by a second route nobody guarded.** §9 records it as a probe finding for `build:bindings`, which is why the `package.json` script sets the variable explicitly; nothing carried that reasoning across to the gate's own Rust leg, and no task's diff contains the defect, because the row and the derive that makes it write anything landed in two different tasks. The fix is both halves: `check-all.sh` exports `TS_RS_EXPORT_DIR="$PWD/web/bindings"` once for every leg, **and** `.gitignore` ignores `crates/*/bindings/` — because the by-hand `cargo test -p redextape-core --features ts` that this branch's own steps tell a developer to run still scatters, and ignoring it is the only thing that protects a tree where the gate was not the thing that ran.

##### AND THE DESIGN'S CLAIM THAT THE TREE'S ONE RUNTIME AGREEMENT CHECK "RUNS IN NOTHING" IS FALSE

Design §1.1 records, as a finding about the tree independent of this slice, that `assertTokenClasses` is called from exactly one place — `web/src/main.ts:201`, immediately after `init()` — and that *"the browser tests under `web/tests/browser/` build their own DOM shell and import modules directly; none imports `main.ts`. So the one runtime agreement check in the tree fires only when a human opens the app."* This entry was scheduled to file that as an open item. **It does not survive being run.**

`web/src/main.ts:1532` is `export const ready = main()`, evaluated at module scope, and twenty-six of the forty-four browser test files in the default set import `../../src/main`, most of them as `await (await import('../../src/main')).ready`. Importing that module runs `main()`, which awaits `init()` and then calls `assertTokenClasses(tokenClasses())` against the real wasm export. Measured by sabotage rather than by reading: appending a `'Drifted'` member to `TOKEN_CLASSES` and running the browser project fails **26 of 44 files**, each at `assertTokenClasses` reached through `main src/main.ts:201`, with

```
Error: TOKEN_CLASSES has drifted from the Rust enum:
  ts:   Ident,Nat,...,TapeSymbol,Move,Drifted
  rust: Ident,Nat,...,TapeSymbol,Move
```

The sabotage was reverted and `git status --porcelain` was empty afterward. The check runs in the `web` CI job on every pull request, and a drifted `TOKEN_CLASSES` reddens it. **What is true of the tree is the narrower half of the claim** — `assertTokenClasses` covers `TokenClass` and nothing else, and `encodings()` covers `EncodingKind`; every other type on the boundary has no runtime check at all. That is still the argument for generation. It is not the argument the spec printed, and the spec no longer prints it: `3bb2de8` struck the claim through in §1.1 and marked it *FALSE, AND RETRACTED*, recording the sabotage, the 26-of-44 result, and the reason the original grep — `from '.*main'` — could not have matched a dynamic import. The same commit corrected §5, whose "strictly stronger" comparison of the compile-time pin against `assertTokenClasses` had rested on the retracted claim and now reads "earlier, not stronger". **The claim survived a design, a plan and four task reviews because nobody ran it**, and the thing that falsified it took one sabotage and thirty seconds.

##### AND THE FRESH-CLONE STEP COULD NOT RUN ON A FRESH CLONE

`scripts/setup-dev.sh` gained a generation block guarded on `if [ -d web/node_modules ]`. **That script never runs `pnpm install`**, so on a genuinely fresh clone the directory does not exist and the block is skipped — in exactly the case its own comment and this entry's opening paragraph claim it closes. It fired only on a re-run, after someone had already done the thing that made it unnecessary. Measured by moving `web/node_modules` aside and running the block both ways: the old guard skips, the new one writes `web/bindings/Span.ts`.

The precondition was also the wrong one. `pnpm run build:bindings` reads no `node_modules` at all — it shells out to `cargo`, which the nextest block above it already establishes — so pnpm's presence is the real requirement, and `command -v pnpm` is what every other optional block in the file tests.

**AND IT WAS THE ONE BLOCK THAT COULD KILL THE SCRIPT FOR A REASON THAT IS NOT A MISSING TOOL.** The blocks above abort on a missing hard precondition of `scripts/check-all.sh`, which is the honest answer to an environment that cannot run the gate. This one is a BUILD: it fails on no network during a first clone, or on `ts-rs` not yet being in the cargo registry cache. Under `set -euo pipefail` that killed the script before `pre-commit install`, **leaving a clone with no hooks because a download timed out**. It is non-fatal now and names the cause rather than swallowing it; verified by shimming `pnpm` to exit 1 and confirming the script reaches its next step at exit 0.

##### AND A SECOND CONFIG THE GATE BUILT BUT NEVER LINTED OR TESTED, WHICH IS THE ONE THING ITS OWN LEG TABLE FORBIDS

`scripts/check-all.sh`'s leg table states the rule it is built around: *"Every config gets clippy AND tests; a config that is built but never tested is a blind spot."* This branch created TWO feature configurations and gave one of them its three rows. `redextape-core --features ts` got clippy, tests and a wasm32 build; `redextape-wasm --features ts` — created by the same task, and compiled by `pnpm run build:bindings` on every typecheck — got none. The crate's only row was `base|wasm|-p redextape-wasm --lib`, which is default-features, and pre-commit's `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets` is default-features too, so `-D warnings` never ran against that configuration anywhere.

**A rule stated in the file that breaks it is not self-enforcing, and nothing else was going to notice.** `check_legs()` validates that every row's tier and kind are dispatchable; it cannot know which configurations exist. The three matching rows are added, mirroring the core triple's shape and placed with the crate's existing row, and each was run before being committed: clippy clean, `70 tests run: 70 passed, 0 skipped` under nextest with the paired `--doc` run, and the wasm32 check clean.

**One stale figure fell out of the same edit.** `ensure_wasm_target`'s comment opened "CALLED FROM THREE ROWS ON PURPOSE" while the table already held four `wasm` rows — it had been written when there were two. It now names the property (`base|wasmprobe|`, then every `wasm` row) and gives no count, for the reason `check-doc-figures.sh`'s own header gives for not counting the documents it covers.

##### AND A CRITICAL IN A FILE NO TASK EDITED: `build:app` STARTED NEEDING CARGO, AND THE DOCKER STAGE THAT RUNS IT HAS NONE

Task 4 chained generation onto three scripts, `build:app` among them. `Dockerfile` stage 2 is `FROM node:26-slim`, copies only `web/` and the `/app/pkg` stage 1 produced, and runs exactly `pnpm run build:app` — under a comment that states the invariant being broken: *"`build:app`, not `build`: this stage has no Rust toolchain — stage 1 already produced /app/pkg."* Installing Rust would not have rescued it either; that stage has no `Cargo.toml`, no `Cargo.lock` and no `crates/`.

**IT WAS REPRODUCED RATHER THAN REASONED ABOUT.** `docker build .` was run to completion against the tree as Task 4 left it, and failed at stage 2's last step:

```
 > [web 8/8] RUN pnpm run build:app:
0.374 $ pnpm run build:bindings && vite build
0.591 $ TS_RS_EXPORT_DIR=$PWD/bindings cargo test -p redextape-core --features ts export_bindings && ...
0.594 sh: 1: cargo: not found
0.604 [ELIFECYCLE] Command failed.
------
Dockerfile:38
ERROR: failed to build: failed to solve: process "/bin/sh -c pnpm run build:app" did not complete successfully: exit code: 1
```

The fix restores the split: `build:app` is `vite build` again, and `build` chains `build:wasm && build:bindings && build:app` so a local full build still generates. `typecheck` and `test` keep their chain — neither is in the image. `web/bindings/` also joins `.dockerignore`, beside `web/dist/` and `web/coverage/` and for the same reason: generated output, never an input. Leaving it in the context would let a developer's already-generated copy hide exactly this dependency from a local build, on a directory a fresh CI checkout does not have. With that exclusion in place `docker build .` completes, exit 0, and stage 2 logs `$ vite build` / `✓ built in 129ms` — the type-only `import type { Span } from '../bindings/Span'` is erased by the bundler, so `vite build` never looks for the file.

**NO CI JOB WOULD HAVE SAID SO, WHICH IS WHY IT HAD TO BE BUILT BY HAND.** The `docker` job is `if: github.event_name != 'pull_request'` and is not in `gate`'s `needs`. The pull request goes green; the post-merge push to `main` fails; the image tag `docker-compose.yml` deploys from stops being published. This is the second invariant in that one file whose only possible check is a human running the build — the `HEALTHCHECK` comment records the first, reached by a different route and for the same structural reason.

**NO PER-TASK REVIEW COULD HAVE FOUND IT, AND THIS IS THE THIRD TIME THIS FILE HAS RECORDED THAT.** `Dockerfile` appears in no task's diff on this branch, and a task review is scoped to one task's diff. The hazard was in UNCHANGED code whose correctness depended on a property the changed code removed — the same shape as the uncapped printer found in `redextape-wasm` two entries above, and the same shape as the `TS_RS_EXPORT_DIR` scatter recorded in this one. **What hid it from the design as well was a false premise.** §9 claimed `typecheck`, `test` and `build:app` would depend on `build:bindings` *"as they already depend on `build:wasm`"*, and nothing did except `build`. That sentence made the edit a no-op by construction, so the enumeration of who else calls `build:app` never happened: **a premise asserting that a change is not a change deletes the audit that would have found the change.** §9 now says so in place of the claim.

##### WHAT STAYS OPEN

- **PR 2 — the eleven derivable core types**, their prose relocated, the four fidelity overrides of design §6, and the no-`bigint` test shown failing with an override removed. **PR 3 — the five wasm types**, the `TOKEN_CLASSES` compile-time pin shown failing with a name removed, and `types.ts` reduced to the barrel it becomes. `grep -c '^export type [A-Za-z]' web/src/types.ts` reads 17 at this commit and **sixteen of those are derivable**; the seventeenth is `Classified`, `pub type Classified = Vec<(Span, TokenClass)>`, a type alias with no derive site, which stays hand-written over two generated types permanently. Design §11 calls PR 2 "the twelve core types": twelve core DECLARATIONS, eleven of which move.

  **CORRECTION (2026-08-31, found by PR 2's whole-branch review) — TWO OF THIS BULLET'S THREE CLAIMS DID NOT HOLD.** The `TOKEN_CLASSES` compile-time pin is filed on PR 3 above; it shipped in PR 2 instead. PR 2 is the commit that deletes `export type TokenClass = (typeof TOKEN_CLASSES)[number]` — the derivation the pin replaces — and the review's own Finding 1 caught the doc block still claiming that derivation existed one commit after it was gone; the replacement had to land with the deletion, not a PR later. Design §11 was corrected the same way, for the same reason. And "the four fidelity overrides of design §6" overstates PR 2 by one: only three sit on a `redextape-core` type and shipped here (`LambdaState.step`, `TmState.step`, `RuleView.moves`); the fourth, `TmStatus.total_steps`, is `redextape-wasm`'s and ships with PR 3 instead — design §11 is corrected there too. See the entry below for both, measured rather than argued.
- **`LinkIndexWire` stays hand-written and unwatched.** Twelve fields in `web/src/link.ts` mirroring a columnar value `Session::link_index` assembles by hand. Generation cannot reach it. Closing it needs a different mechanism than a derive — either the marshalling moves behind a serde-serializable type, or the columnar shape gets a gate of its own — and neither is attempted in this slice.
- **`TermTree` and `TermNode` will generate files nothing imports** once PR 2 lands, being serialized with no TypeScript consumer yet. Harmless, and named so their appearance in `bindings/` is not read as a bug.

  **CORRECTION (2026-08-31, PR 2's own roadmap entry) — THEY DID NOT.** `TermTree` and `TermNode` are design §1.1's Class C — serialized, with no `TS` derive — and PR 2 derives Class A's twelve core types only. Class C was never in PR 2's scope, so nothing generated a file for either this PR; `web/bindings/` carries twelve files at PR 2's close and neither name is one of them. Whether they ever get a derive is unscheduled, not merely delayed one PR.
- **Nothing compares the generated types against the measured wire.** `crates/redextape-wasm/tests/browser.rs` pins runtime shapes measured out of a real browser and the generator asserts static types; no test compares the two. That is the division of labour the tree already had, made no worse.
- **`build:bindings` WRITES BUT NEVER PRUNES, AND NOTHING WILL NOTICE A STALE GENERATED FILE.** `ts-rs` only writes; no step removes a `web/bindings/*.ts` whose Rust type was renamed or deleted. The orphan survives and the tree still typechecks, because `web/src/types.ts` names each import explicitly rather than re-exporting the directory — so a renamed type generates a second file and the first one simply stays, describing a shape that no longer exists. **Immaterial at one type and a real hazard from PR 2 onward**, where eleven files land at once and a rename during prose relocation is the likely trigger. The likely fix is a `rm -rf bindings &&` prefix inside `build:bindings`, which makes the directory a pure function of the current Rust declarations. **Deferred to PR 2 deliberately**: it costs a full regeneration on every typecheck, and that trade is worth measuring against the twelve-type run rather than the one-type run.

  **MEASURED (2026-08-31, PR 2's own roadmap entry).** A warm `pnpm run build:bindings` over the actual twelve-type run costs about three quarters of a second wall clock — three consecutive runs read `0.751s`, `0.753s`, `0.773s` total — against the one-type figure of `0.706s` measured above, for a different script on a different commit (no prune, no swap, no lock, no guard); the two are not a controlled comparison and no delta is attributed between them (ten consecutive warm runs of the current script alone spread `0.761s`–`0.825s`, the same order of magnitude as the difference an earlier draft of this bullet attributed to eleven more types compiling). What the figure answers on its own is whether regenerating on every typecheck is worth its cost, and roughly three quarters of a second answers it: the trade holds. The fix that ships alongside this measurement is not the naive `rm -rf bindings &&` this bullet sketched — see the entry below for why.
- **`web/bindings/` is generated and gitignored, so a stale one typechecks.** A tree where generation has not run since a Rust edit is internally consistent and wrong. The build wiring makes that hard rather than impossible, and `assertTokenClasses` — which does run, see above — is the only check that compares against the loaded module.

The per-job durations came from the pull request's `get_status` endpoint — `list_jobs` 404s on this Forgejo build, and `list_run_jobs` returns statuses without timings, so `get_status` is the one surface that carries both.

**`docker` SKIPPED, AS IT ALWAYS DOES ON A PULL REQUEST — AND ON THIS BRANCH THAT EXEMPTION WAS NOT FREE.** Every previous entry could record the skip as costing nothing because the branch touched no `Dockerfile`, `.forgejo/` or compose file. This one broke the image build and no CI job on the pull request could have said so: `docker` is gated off for pull requests AND is absent from `gate`'s `needs` list, so it is doubly invisible. `docker build .` was therefore run by hand at `6f6bbb4`, to completion, exit 0, with stage 2 executing `pnpm run build:app` — and that hand-run is the only evidence that exists for the fix. **A job that never runs on a pull request is not a gate, and a branch that changes what its stages can execute has to supply the evidence itself.**

**NO CAUSAL CLAIM IS ATTACHED TO ANY DURATION ABOVE**, per this file's standing note on CI timing variance. What can be stated without inference is what the branch added for `rust` to do: six new `LEGS` rows — clippy, test and a wasm32 `cargo check` for `redextape-core --features ts`, and the same three for `redextape-wasm --features ts` — a feature configuration nothing compiled before. `web` gained one cargo-invoking step. Run 327, the previous entry's, read `rust` 11m43s and `web` 2m17s on a different branch, a different tree and a different runner state; the two runs are not a controlled comparison and the difference is not attributed here.

Design: [`../specs/2026-08-29-wire-type-generation-design.md`](../specs/2026-08-29-wire-type-generation-design.md). Plan: [`2026-08-30-wire-type-generation-core-types.md`](2026-08-30-wire-type-generation-core-types.md).

PR 2 of 3, opened by PR 1's own WHAT STAYS OPEN list above. Generates design §1.1's Class A core types — eleven carrying a serde derive plus `Move`, which does not — relocates their prose from `web/src/types.ts` into the Rust doc comments `ts-rs` copies verbatim, and gates every generated file against carrying `bigint`. What stays hand-written on the core side is **one structural alias with no derive site**, not a backlog: `Classified = Vec<(Span, TokenClass)>` is a type alias, has nowhere to put a `#[derive(TS)]`, and stays a one-line re-export permanently, over two types that are themselves generated. PR 3 is the five `redextape-wasm` types, named in full under WHAT STAYS OPEN below.

##### THE DESIGN'S PRESCRIBED OVERRIDE WAS WRONG, AND NO GATE ON EITHER SIDE OF THE BOUNDARY COULD HAVE SAID SO

§6 prescribes `#[ts(type = "Array<Move>")]` for `RuleView.moves`, the one override this design gets by inspection rather than by the wire measurement the other three carry. It is wrong, and it fails silently in a way that is the whole finding: `#[ts(type = "Array<Move>")]` generates the literal text `moves: Array<Move>` with **no import statement for `Move`** anywhere in the file. `tsc` never sees the gap, because `web/bindings/RuleView.ts` only enters the TypeScript program when something imports it — and at PR 2's own commit, before Task 4 rewired `types.ts`, nothing yet did. No Rust-side gate can see it either: `no_generated_type_carries_bigint` and `the_gate_covers_every_exported_type` both read the string `ts-rs` writes, and an absent import is not a string that is present. `#[ts(as = "Vec<Move>")]` emits both the reference and the import, and is what shipped. The design is corrected in place at §6 to say so, with the counterexample.

##### `SERDE(SKIP)` IS HONOURED, AND `REDEXTAPE-CORE` HAS NO FIFTH FIDELITY CLASS

Design §14 question 2 asked whether a `#[serde(skip)]`ped field could cross anyway through some path `ts-rs` doesn't share with `serde`. `LambdaState.redex` is `#[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", serde(skip))]` and carries no `#[ts(skip)]` of its own; `ts-rs`'s default `serde-compat` feature reads the same attribute and omits the field from the generated type regardless. `redex` does not appear in `web/bindings/LambdaState.ts`. Answered for this crate: no fifth fidelity class exists here, beyond the three overrides §6 assigns to core (`LambdaState.step`, `TmState.step`, `RuleView.moves`) and the `Array<Move>` correction above.

##### THE WHOLE-BRANCH REVIEW FOUND A CRITICAL FOUR CLEAN PER-TASK REVIEWS STRUCTURALLY COULD NOT

Every task's per-task review came back clean — Task 2's own coverage test took four revisions to get there, each one caught by sabotage rather than by reading, before its review found nothing left to fix. Four clean per-task reviews are the condition for running the whole-branch review, not a reason to skip it, and it earned the distinction again: its first round found `web/src/types.ts`'s `TOKEN_CLASSES` doc comment still describing a derivation the **same commit** had deleted. `TokenClass` used to be `(typeof TOKEN_CLASSES)[number]` — the array was the source. Generating `TokenClass` from Rust removed that line and left the array's doc block asserting the mechanism was still there, with nothing left connecting the two. **The safety loss was measured, not argued**: deleting `'Binder'` from `TOKEN_CLASSES` produced four `tsc` errors before this branch existed — all `TS2345`, all in `tests/node/spans.test.ts` (lines 53, 54, 56 and 57, a literal `'Binder'` argument no longer assignable to the narrowed parameter type `Classified[number][1]` takes), none of them a `switch`/`case`, and none outside that one test file — and zero after this branch's Task 4 landed — a silent hole a per-task review of Task 4's diff alone could not see, because Task 4's diff is a re-export, not a comment. The fix pulls design §5's compile-time pin — planned for PR 3 — into this PR instead: `Missing`/`Extra` types in `web/src/types.ts`, `Exclude<...>` in both directions between `TOKEN_CLASSES` and the generated `TokenClass` union, demonstrated failing both ways (a name removed from the array, a name added that the Rust enum lacks), each producing its own `TS2344` naming the offending member, clean typecheck restored between and after.

##### CLOSING THE PRUNING HAZARD TOOK TWO FIXES, AND THE SECOND ONE SHIPPED A CRITICAL OF ITS OWN

PR 1's own entry deferred `build:bindings`'s pruning gap here by name, "measured against the twelve-type run" — that measurement is in the VERIFICATION block below. The whole-branch review's first fix for it was a plain `rm -rf bindings &&` prefix in `package.json`; its second review round found that shape leaves `web/bindings/` deleted and never rebuilt if `cargo test` fails mid-generation — the exact case a fresh clone with no network hits — and replaced it with `scripts/build-web-bindings.sh`: generate into a scratch directory, then swap it into place with two renames, so a failed run never touches the last-good copy.

**That fix was the one that shipped a Critical.** The scratch directory and its `.old` backup used two fixed, shared names. Two concurrent invocations — exactly what `pnpm run typecheck` and `pnpm run test` running back to back, or two developers' pre-commit hooks firing at once, produce — raced: the second run's unconditional `rm -rf` deleted the first run's already-populated scratch mid-flight, the first run's swap then moved the **second** run's directory into place, and the loser's final `mv` found nothing there to move. `web/bindings` ended up **not existing at all**, both runs exited 0, and the twelve files were stranded under `bindings.old`. The shape this fix replaced — the naive inline `rm -rf bindings &&` — raced clean five times out of five when tested; the fix built to close a race nobody could make fire opened one that fired on every attempt.

**The guardrail that caught it was the discipline this file already has a name for: reproduce, don't reason.** The review round that found it did not read the swap logic and conclude it was safe — each of the two renames is individually correct on its own — it raced the mechanism directly and the destruction reproduced. The fix — `mktemp -d` per-process scratch names plus an `mkdir`-based lock around the swap, with a `trap` cleanup and a bounded reclaim of a lock left by a dead holder — was accepted only after the same discipline ran the other way, against the fixed script: 8 concurrent pairs of the script directly, 3 concurrent pairs of `pnpm run typecheck`, and one deliberate kill between the two renames — 12 races total. The 11 plain concurrent pairs (8 + 3) all exited 0, with `web/bindings` intact at twelve files and no scratch or lock directory left behind. The kill race is different in kind, not degree: it was `kill -9`'d mid-swap on purpose, so it did not exit 0, and `web/bindings` was briefly absent at the instant of the kill. Nothing was lost — the pre-kill copy and the freshly-generated one both survived intact under distinct scratch names — and a plain re-run of the real script reclaimed the dead lock and restored `web/bindings` to twelve files without manual cleanup, but the killed run's own scratch pair stayed on disk afterward, an orphan a human has to remove by hand: the one case among the twelve where a scratch directory WAS left behind.

##### THE COVERAGE GATE TOOK FOUR REVISIONS PLUS THREE MORE IN REVIEW, EACH DEFEATED BY AN ORDINARY SPELLING OF THE SAME ATTRIBUTE, AND THE BRANCH STOPPED WIDENING RATHER THAN CLAIM A FIFTH FIX WAS THE LAST ONE

`the_gate_covers_every_exported_type` exists to catch a type that derives `TS` without being added to the hand-maintained `generated()` list. Reaching a version that actually holds took four successive narrowings of a blacklist, each defeated by sabotage rather than by reading: counting `ts(export)` occurrences, defeated by moving the attribute between two types at a fixed count; the substring `"ts(export)"`, defeated by `ts(rename = "Foo", export)`; the substring `"derive(ts_rs::TS)"`, defeated by `derive(Default, ts_rs::TS)` and by `use ts_rs::TS;` plus a bare `derive(TS)`; and a ban on `use ts_rs::` under `src/`, defeated by `use ts_rs as tsrs;` plus `derive(tsrs::TS)` — a crate alias that puts `tsrs::TS`, not `ts_rs::TS`, on the derive line. The whole-branch review then found three more gaps past that fourth narrowing, each answered structurally rather than with a fifth banned spelling: a crate alias with a leading `::` that the fourth narrowing's own substring match still missed, closed by rewriting the check as a whitelist over every mention of `ts_rs` rather than adding a fifth blacklist entry; a derive routed through a loose file at the crate root, outside `src/` entirely, closed by widening the whitelist's scan to the whole crate; and a `#[path]` attribute resolving **outside** `CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR` altogether, one directory further out than the widened scan reaches — named rather than closed, below.

**The branch stopped widening and named the boundary instead.** Four widenings each bought exactly one more round before the next spelling or the next file location moved the target; a fifth widening — following `#[path]` one directory further, or two — is defeated the same way, forever, because the scan reads `.rs` files by physical location under a root and has no notion of Rust's module system to resolve where an attribute sends the compiler. The scan is now a whitelist (every mention of `ts_rs` in the crate's own `.rs` files must equal one canonical derive line, byte for byte, or the scan panics naming the file and line) over the whole crate root rather than `src/` alone, and its own doc names three routes that remain open rather than claiming none do: a `Cargo.toml` dependency rename (`bindgen = { package = "ts-rs" }`, which never writes the bytes `ts_rs` anywhere this scan reads), a macro that expands to the marker only at its call site, and a `#[path]` resolving outside the crate root.

**The structural alternative not taken, and why**: `ts-rs`'s own derive macro emits one `export_bindings_*` test per exported type, so `cargo test -p redextape-core --features ts --lib -- --list` reads 12 on a clean tree and 13 under every one of the three constructions above — a count that comes from macro expansion, which sees every derive site `rustc` actually compiles, rather than from source text a `#[path]` or a rename can route around. This gate does not take that route, but not for the build-lock hazard an earlier draft of this entry gave — **that reason does not reproduce, and was checked rather than repeated**: run from inside a test, `cargo test -p redextape-core --features ts --lib -- --list` completes under both `cargo nextest run` and plain `cargo test`, exiting 0 and counting 12 `export_bindings` tests each, in well under a tenth of a second warm — no serialization behind a second build, no deadlock, under either harness. **The decision to keep the text scan stands anyway, on reasons that do hold.** The structural route couples a gate to the STABILITY OF CARGO'S OWN COMMAND-LINE OUTPUT — a surface this project does not control and has no test pinning — where the text scan depends on nothing but the crate's own source. It pays a real cost on a cold build, compiling the workspace a second time from inside the gate itself, where the text scan pays none whether the build is warm or cold. And this branch had already shipped one late change to this exact generation mechanism — the scratch-directory swap two sections above — that introduced a Critical of its own, which argues against trading a gate that works for a differently-shaped one absent a reason stronger than a hazard that, measured, is not there. The text scan pays for avoiding those costs with the four-widenings history above it; the `--list` count would not need widening again, but nothing measured here forces the trade.

Three fix rounds running, a round fixed exactly the counterexample it was handed, and the next review round found the next instance of the *same class* — a new attribute spelling past the blacklist, a new file location past `src/`-only, a seventh stale citation the six-citation "fix" never searched for, a claim about which sabotage collides with `tm/machine.rs`'s existing `pub struct Rule` that was true of one construction and stated as though it were true of all four. Round 4 opened by measuring that claim directly — a byte-for-byte diff of the fenced block against `ts_bindings.rs` — and found 162 stale lines, plus all five transcripts quoting line numbers and message text the gate no longer carried; that is what round 4 actually swept, closing it by replacing the block with the shipped file verbatim and re-running every transcript fresh, confirmed by an empty diff afterward. **No round's sweep came back complete.** Each covered the one class it was pointed at, and a different class of the same failure — not searching for a claim's siblings before calling it fixed — survived into the next round every time, round 3 included.

##### THE DESIGN'S PRESCRIBED OVERRIDE WAS WRONG FOR THE SECOND TIME, AND THE MECHANISM IS THE ONE PR 2 ALREADY FOUND

§6 prescribes `#[ts(type = "number")]` for `TmStatus.total_steps`, which is `Option<u64>`. Measured before this plan was written: `ts(type = ...)` substitutes the **whole** field type, `Option` and all, so the prescribed form generates `total_steps: number` and silently drops the `| null` that `None` puts on the wire. This is the same mechanism PR 2 hit on `RuleView.moves`, where §6's `ts(type = "Array<Move>")` emitted the reference with no import for `Move` anywhere in the file: in both cases the prescription was written as though the attribute edits the part of the type that is wrong, and in both cases it replaces the whole type, taking the correct parts with it. Both prescriptions were the ones §6 got by inspection rather than from the wire measurement its other overrides carry. `LambdaState::step` and `TmState::step`, the two `redextape-core` fields that took `ts(type = "number")` in PR 2, are bare `u64` and remain correct — which is what makes this a trap rather than an error: the prescribed form is right for a bare field and wrong for the same integer behind an `Option`, and nothing about the attribute says so. Three forms were measured producing `number | null` — `ts(type = "number | null")`, `ts(as = "Option<u32>")` and `ts(as = "Option<f64>")` — and the literal one shipped, because it states what the wire carries without asserting a Rust type this field does not have. Design §6 carries a second CORRECTION block recording it, beside the `Array<Move>` one from PR 2.

##### A GATE THAT PASSES ON THE DEFECT, AND TWO MEASUREMENTS WHOSE CONTRAST IS THE ARGUMENT

With the design's own `ts(type = "number")` in place, both Rust-side gates report `2 tests run: 2 passed, 0 skipped`. Neither is broken: `no_generated_type_carries_bigint` looks for `bigint` in the generated text and there is none in `number` to find, and `the_gate_covers_every_exported_type` compares which types derive `TS` against the hand-maintained list, not what any field says. **The two `tsc` measurements are the finding, and it is their contrast that carries it.** At the commit that added the derives, before `web/src/types.ts` imported anything from `../bindings/`, `pnpm run typecheck` under exactly that sabotage **exited 0** — `tsconfig.json`'s `include` is `["src", "tests", "vite.config.ts"]`, which reaches the generated directory by no route other than an import from inside `src` or `tests`, and `types.ts` still hand-declared `TmStatus`, so `tsc` never opened the file. At the commit that made `types.ts` the barrel, the same sabotage produced **three `TS2322` errors**, one per test fixture assigning a literal `null` to the field: `replies.test.ts`'s and `session-client.test.ts`'s `compiled` fixtures, and `results.test.ts`'s `TmLeg` fixture in its `'shows the TM reason and no width when that backend declines'` test. **`web/src/results.ts` produced no error at all.** `resultRows` reads `total_steps` and narrows it on `!== null`, and that narrowing compiles clean against the wrong type — a `number` compared against `null` is not something `tsc` reports. So no production source file catches this: three test fixtures are the whole check, and a refactor that stopped constructing a `TmStatus` with `total_steps: null` in it would remove the last thing watching this class with no signal that anything had changed. Both passages that carry this — the Rust doc on the field and design §6 — state the `tsc` dependency as a structural condition on that import existing plus each measurement as a dated fact, rather than as an ongoing claim; a reviewer's proposed "at this commit / until Task 3" hedge was rejected for being the same defect displaced in time.

##### THE SCANNER MOVED RATHER THAN BEING COPIED, AND THE MOVE WAS ACCEPTED ONLY AFTER PR 2'S FOUR SABOTAGES FIRED AGAINST THE MOVED COPY

`ts_derive_scan` now lives in `redextape-test-support`, parameterised by the crate root to scan and the path of the scanner's own file to exclude, and both crates' gates call it. One implementation is the point: the scan took four narrowings plus three more in review before it held, and a second copy drifts from the first the moment one of them is widened again. The move was verified the way this file's standing rule requires — by re-running the sabotages the original was measured against, not by reading the diff. All four fired against the moved copy: a type carrying the derive but absent from `generated()` (the panic names `Sneaky`); a crate alias, `use ::ts_rs as tsrs;`, which the fourth narrowing's own substring match missed (the panic names the file, the line number and the offending text); a `u64` field with its override deleted (the panic names `LambdaState`); and a `pub struct` appended to the caller's gate file, which makes the scanner's self-exclusion unsafe (the panic names that file and refuses). A reviewer independently reproduced two of them rather than accepting the report, and checked the dependency claim the same way — `cargo tree -i proptest` — rather than trusting `default-features = false` to mean what it says. **The dev-dependency is target-gated, and `--lib` cannot demonstrate that.** `redextape-test-support` enters `redextape-wasm`'s graph only under `cfg(not(target_arch = "wasm32"))`, so nothing in it can break the `wasm-pack test` browser leg; the invocation that shows this is `cargo check --target wasm32-unknown-unknown -p redextape-wasm --all-targets`, because `--lib` never builds a dev-dependency at all and so could not have distinguished a working gate from a missing one. Both the plan and `scripts/check-all.sh` run the `--lib` form; the `--all-targets` form is in the VERIFICATION block below, with the `cargo tree` figures that show the crate present in the host dev graph and absent from the wasm32 one.

##### THE WHOLE-BRANCH REVIEW FOUND A DESTRUCTIVE PATH THREE CLEAN TASK REVIEWS COULD NOT, AND THE PLAN IS WHAT HID IT

`scripts/build-web-bindings.sh` runs two cargo legs into one scratch directory and then swaps that directory into place. It guarded the swap by asking whether *at least one* `.ts` file had appeared anywhere in that shared directory — a check that was complete for exactly as long as only one leg produced anything, because then "one file exists" and "the leg that matters produced" were the same statement. This branch made the second leg produce five files and left the guard alone, so either leg's output alone satisfied it. **The failure that opens is silent and destroys the tree it exists to protect.** A wasm leg that stopped producing — a derive removed, the `ts` feature regressing, or a `ts-rs` upgrade renaming the `export_bindings_*` prefix so the test filter matches nothing, all of which exit 0 — would ride in on core's twelve files, pass the guard, rename the last-good seventeen-file directory away, let the `EXIT` trap delete it, and install a twelve-file tree **at exit 0**: the one outcome the script's entire header exists to prevent. **The plan is what hid it.** It asserted, in prose, *"That script needs no change"* — as a fact rather than as a measurement — and having decided the guard was fine, nobody asked what had changed underneath it. No per-task review could have found this: each reads one task's diff, and the guard appears in no task's diff; what changed was the truth of an assumption in a file nobody touched. The fix gives each leg its own scratch subdirectory and checks each non-empty independently, by name, before either is trusted, with no file count hard-coded anywhere — the property checked is that every leg produced something, which is invariant to how many types any crate has or to a third crate being added later. **Demonstrated at this commit rather than asserted**: with the wasm leg's cargo invocation commented out, `pnpm run build:bindings` exits 1 with `build-web-bindings.sh: the redextape-wasm leg exited 0 but .../wasm contains no .ts files — refusing to touch the last-good web/bindings. A cargo test filter that matches nothing exits 0 having written nothing, so 'cargo exited 0' was never evidence that redextape-wasm's generation happened.`, and `web/bindings/` is untouched at seventeen files with no scratch or lock directory left behind.

##### THEN READING THAT FIX FOUND A THIRD INSTANCE OF THE SAME CLASS, WHICH NEITHER COVERAGE GATE CAN SEE

The same change that made both legs produce also made their merge unsafe, one line below the guard the review had just fixed. `mv "$CORE_DIR"/*.ts "$WASM_DIR"/*.ts "$TMP_DIR/"` flattens two directories into one, so a type of the same name exported from both crates lands on one basename and `mv` silently keeps whichever it writes last. **Neither coverage gate can see that**: each compares only its own crate's derive sites against its own `generated()` list, so both stay green while the shipped file is one crate's type wearing the other's name. It was impossible before this branch for the same reason the guard was adequate before this branch — one leg was always empty — which makes it the third instance of a single class: *a check that was complete only because one side of it was empty*. `check_no_leg_collisions` now refuses before the merge, naming the colliding basenames and both crates. **Demonstrated at this commit**: a temporary `Cut` added to `redextape-wasm`, colliding with `redextape-core`'s `Cut.ts`, makes `pnpm run build:bindings` exit 1 with `build-web-bindings.sh: redextape-core and redextape-wasm both generated: Cut.ts — refusing to touch web/bindings. A type of that name is exported from both crates, so 'mv' would silently keep whichever leg it wrote last, and neither crate's coverage gate can see it`, with `web/bindings/` left at seventeen files; removing the temporary type returns it to exit 0 and seventeen files. The concurrency story PR 2 established is unchanged and was re-raced at this commit, with both new checks in place rather than only the ones PR 2 raced: five concurrent `pnpm run build:bindings` runs all exit 0, `web/bindings/` intact at seventeen files, no scratch directory and no lock left behind, and `git status --porcelain` empty afterward.

##### `REDEXTAPE-CORE`'S OWN GATE WAS HANDING OUT THE OVERRIDE THIS BRANCH HAD JUST DISPROVED

`no_generated_type_carries_bigint` in `redextape-core` told anyone who tripped it, in its assertion message, that the field "needs `#[cfg_attr(feature = "ts", ts(type = "number"))]`" — with no caveat about `Option`. That message is correct for every field core has today, all of which are bare `u64`, and it is the exact instruction that produces this branch's defect the moment someone adds an `Option<u64>` to a core type: trip the gate, follow what it says, and the `| null` disappears from the wire type with both gates green. The failing gate would be the cause. Task 2's review could not have found it — Task 2 wrote `redextape-wasm`'s gate and never opened core's — and neither could Task 1's, which moved the shared scanner and not the per-crate assertion text. The whole-branch review's fix round matched core's wording to the sibling gate this branch had just written (an override is needed, `ts(type = "number")` for a bare field, `ts(type = "number | null")` for one behind an `Option`) and scoped design §6's "the two `redextape-core` fields in the table above are unaffected" to those fields rather than leaving it to be read as clearing the guidance for the next one. **The instance was in `redextape-wasm`; the class was a sentence in `redextape-core` telling the next person to reproduce it.**

##### A FIGURE THAT WAS RIGHT, AND A "CORRECTION" THAT MEASURED A DIFFERENT QUANTITY

The design says, in three places, that sabotaging `TOKEN_CLASSES` reddens "26 of 44 browser test files". A fix round flagged the figure as stale on the ground that the browser test directory holds 47 files, of which 27 reference `../../src/main`, and — correctly — declined to write a new number it had not measured. **The document was right and the correction was measuring something else.** `web/vite.config.ts` excludes three `PROBE_FILES` from the browser project unless `REDEXTAPE_PROBE` is set, so the project runs 44 of the 47, and one of the 27 main-referencing files is a probe, leaving 26 — both halves re-derived at this commit in the VERIFICATION block below. The whole-branch review then ran the actual sabotage rather than the proxy: baseline `44 passed (44)` / `269 passed (269)`; with `'Binder'` changed to `'Drifted'` in `TOKEN_CLASSES`, `26 failed | 18 passed (44)`. All three figures were left untouched and a dated line was added where the figure was originally established, recording the re-measurement and the reason the proxy reads 47. **The near-miss is the lesson, not the figure**: a proxy count was offered as a correction to a real measurement by a round whose whole purpose was refusing to guess, and it would have replaced a right number with a wrong one under the banner of rigour. "Reference the module under test" and "redden when it drifts" are different quantities, and a count of the first is not evidence about the second.

##### THREE OF THIS BRANCH'S DEFECTS WERE PROSE THE PLAN WROTE ASSERTING A MECHANISM NOBODY HAD MEASURED, AND THE ONE MECHANICAL PLAN DEFECT WAS REJECTED BY A GATE THE MOMENT IT LANDED

Four defects on this branch were written by the plan rather than by an implementer, and the asymmetry between them is worth stating plainly. Three were prose asserting a causal mechanism nobody had measured: the two passages dictated verbatim saying "what catches it is `tsc`", false at the commit that added the derives, where both Rust gates passed and typecheck exited 0; the follow-up fix naming `resultRows`'s `!== null` narrowing as a catcher, contradicted by the measurement in the very next paragraph of the same doc comment, which had already recorded that `results.ts` produced zero errors; and "That script needs no change", which hid the destructive path two sections above. The fourth was mechanical — a doc comment the plan dictated that named `ts_rs` in prose, inside a crate whose own scan treats every mention of that string outside the canonical derive line as a failure — **and it could not ship**: the gate refused it the moment it landed, and it was reworded to the hyphenated package name before anything was committed. **A gate rejected the mechanical error instantly and nothing rejects a false sentence.** The three prose defects each shipped and survived until a review measured the claim; each was found by measurement, never by re-reading. The corrections followed the same rule the branch learned from them: the `resultRows` fix INVERTED the claim rather than deleting it, because "no production source file catches this, and three test fixtures are the whole check" is a stronger statement than silence, and the same round's sweep found three more copies of that misattribution in the plan plus one unmeasured causal claim in design §1.1. A fifth plan-authored defect belongs to a different class and is recorded above: the scanner move's substitution table listed only the phrases containing `CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR`, and eleven sentences kept pointing at the wrong crate or the wrong file afterward — found by a sweep rather than by a gate or a measurement, which is the third mechanism this branch used and the only one that finds stranded deictics. **Once, the discipline ran the other way**: a fix round's own research subagent reported that two "compile-time pin" claims were false, and the round overrode it — it read `browser.rs`'s `scratch_methods_that_must_not_exist` and confirmed the claims were true. A subagent's result is a claim to check, not a result.

##### THE `docker` JOB'S PR EXEMPTION, RESTATED PER PR 1'S OWN INSTRUCTION TO SAY SO EVERY TIME

`docker` does not run on pull requests and is absent from `gate`'s `needs`, so a pull request goes green on a `Dockerfile` this branch broke and the failure appears only on the post-merge push to `main`. PR 1 of this slice broke the image build in exactly that blind spot — its own entry above records `docker build .` failing at stage 2's last step against the tree its Task 4 left, with no pull-request job that could have said so, found only because a human ran the build. **How this branch was checked, from the diff rather than from memory**: `git diff --name-only 7c29b23..2df9a58` lists fourteen files, and none of them is a `Dockerfile`, a `.dockerignore`, a `.forgejo/` workflow, a compose file, or `web/package.json` — so no stage's command changed and no build step was added; `build:bindings` still invokes the same script PR 2 gave it, and `build:app` is still `vite build`. What did change that a stage compiles is `crates/redextape-wasm/Cargo.toml` and `Cargo.lock`, and stage 1 runs `wasm-pack build crates/redextape-wasm --release --target web`. That is precisely the kind of claim PR 1 made by reading a manifest and had falsified by a build, so **the command stage 1 runs was run at this commit rather than reasoned about**: `wasm-pack build crates/redextape-wasm --release --target web` exited 0 and wrote a complete `pkg` (the `.wasm`, its `.d.ts`, the JS shim and `package.json`), with the working tree clean afterward. No duration is quoted and no causal claim is attached, per this file's standing note. The manifest change is a dev-dependency under `[target.'cfg(not(target_arch = "wasm32"))'.dev-dependencies]`, which `wasm-pack build` does not compile at all and which does not appear in the wasm32 dependency graph even with dev edges included (VERIFICATION below). A job that never runs on a pull request is not a gate, and the evidence for this one is a human having run its first stage.

##### WHAT STAYS OPEN

- **No gate covers an override that changes a field's NULLABILITY, and this is the class this PR opened rather than closed.** `no_generated_type_carries_bigint` sees only the `bigint` an unoverridden `u64` produces, and `the_gate_covers_every_exported_type` sees only which types derive `TS`; an override that swaps a correct `number | null` for `number` passes both. `tsc` refuses it only while `web/src/types.ts` imports the type from `../bindings/` **and** something assigns a literal `null` to the field — today that is three test fixtures and no production file, so the check disappears the day those fixtures change shape, with nothing firing to say so.
- **`LinkIndexWire` stays hand-written and unwatched**, unchanged by this PR and now named in `types.ts`'s own header so the barrel cannot be read as claiming the whole boundary is generated. Generation cannot reach a columnar value assembled by hand at the boundary; closing it needs a different mechanism than a derive.
- **`TermTree` and `TermNode` stay serialized with no `TS` derive and no schedule** — design §1.1's Class C, corrected in PR 1's entry above and unchanged here.
- **The coverage scan's three named remaining routes** — a `Cargo.toml` dependency rename, a macro expanding to the marker only at its call site, and a `#[path]` resolving outside the crate root — are named in the scanner's own doc and not closed; both crates now inherit exactly those three from one implementation instead of two copies with their own. **Each gate is also per-crate by construction**, so a type exported under the same name from both crates is invisible to both; `check_no_leg_collisions` in the generation script is what refuses that, and it is a script check rather than a gate.
- **Nothing compares the generated types against the measured wire.** Unchanged from PR 1 and PR 2: `browser.rs` measures, the generator asserts, and no test compares the two.
- **`web/bindings/` is generated and gitignored, so a stale one still typechecks.** A tree where `build:bindings` has not been re-run since a Rust edit satisfies both the `TOKEN_CLASSES` pin and `tsc`; `assertTokenClasses` remains the one check that compares against the loaded wasm module rather than against a file on disk.
