#### THE FOUR STANDING λ MINORS CLOSE, THE `unreachable!` LIST THAT HAD SAID FIVE SINCE JULY STOPS CARRYING A COUNT AT ALL BECAUSE FOUR DIFFERENT ANSWERS WERE PUT IN WRITING FOR IT AND TWO OF THEM WERE CORRECTIONS, THE WHOLE-BRANCH REVIEW DEFEATED THIS BRANCH'S OWN NEW GATE IN ONE COMPILE WITH THE EXACT CONSTRUCTION THE GATE'S MODEL FILE RECORDS AS HAVING BROKEN ITS OWN BLACKLIST, AND FOUR OF THIS BRANCH'S DEFECTS WERE WRITTEN BY THE PLAN RATHER THAN BY AN IMPLEMENTER (2026-09-01, branch `minor-findings-cleanup`, `65e8fac..c012754`, 10 commits, plus the entry commits)

Plan: [`2026-09-01-minor-findings-cleanup.md`](2026-09-01-minor-findings-cleanup.md). **No design document, by explicit decision** — the scope and the one real design fork (how to trap the `Drop` else-branch: a runtime `debug_assert`, a compile-time gate, or both) were both settled in-session before the plan was written, so a spec would have recorded a decision already made. Both were taken.

A cleanup slice with no new capability: it closes the four findings left STILL OPEN under *"Minor findings from the λ structural-sharing review (2026-07-31)"* above and re-files the `unreachable!` paragraph under *"Minor findings from the same review"* further up. Nothing in `src/` changed behaviour — the whole-branch diff is +62/−26 in `lambda/term.rs` (a `debug_assert`, a strengthened test), +9/−0 of `lib.rs` doc comment, one name added to `lambda.rs`'s re-export list, four import sites that got one line shorter, and one new 142-line test file. **The two lessons below are the entry's real content**, and both are about lists rather than about λ terms.

##### WHAT SHIPPED, TASK BY TASK

**Task 1 — the silently empty else-branch gets both a runtime trap and a compile-time gate**, because they answer different questions. `impl Drop for LambdaTerm` now reads `Rc::get_mut` into a binding, `debug_assert!`s that it is `Some`, and only then takes the iterative teardown path; if a live weak handle ever makes it `None`, the destructor has already degenerated to the compiler's recursive drop glue, and the assert says so in the message rather than leaving a deep term to overflow the stack. `crates/redextape-core/tests/no_weak_handles.rs` refuses the spelling before it can run: it walks `redextape-core/src`, flags any line carrying one of its `NEEDLES` spellings, and carries its own self-test — an offending half whose probes must all be caught and a benign half of comment lines that must not be. Both halves were demonstrated by sabotage, not argued.

**Task 2 — `lambda.rs` re-exports `Node`**, so a consumer that matches on a term needs one import instead of two. `grep -rn 'lambda::term::Node' crates/redextape-core | wc -l` went 6 → 2. **Four sites got shorter, not the three the plan asserted**; the two survivors are named in the closed bullet above and neither is residue. The plan's rationale for "three" failed by looking only for braced `lambda::{…}` siblings and missing a bare single-item `use redextape_core::lambda::Dir;` sitting directly above the `Node` line in `tests/viewmodel_contract.rs`'s `walk`.

**Task 3 — the across-step sharing assertion now checks the sibling its message names.** `before_ids.intersection(&after_ids).next().is_some()` asked only for *some* surviving allocation anywhere in the term; the new form collects `(branch index, allocation id)` for the untouched sibling at every `App` branch along the redex path and compares the two vectors, so a failure names the level that stopped being shared. The old form was not merely differently worded, and the proof is a contrast rather than a claim: see below.

**Task 4 — the doc-comment finding was closed in the opposite direction to the one it was filed in.** Filed as *"the λ `App` drop-test trio is over-documented relative to the `LetRecGroup` pair it invokes as its model"*, it was measured and found inverted: the `LetRecGroup` twin had no doc comment at all, and the λ trio's right-nested member carries a sabotage record its own sibling lacks. The fix levels the `LetRecGroup` pair up. The diff is pure addition — no `-` lines — which is what proves there was nothing to trim, and had the finding been implemented as filed it would have deleted a sabotage record to buy stylistic symmetry.

##### LESSON ONE — A LIST OF INSTANCES WITH NO GATE GOES STALE SILENTLY, AND THIS ONE PRODUCED FOUR DIFFERENT NUMBERS

The `unreachable!` paragraph said **five** from July. The tree held **nine**. The correction this branch was told to make said **eight**. The verification command that correction shipped with printed **seventeen**, because its filter strips `//` only at column one and so counts the macro's own name inside indented comments and doc lines. The eight-versus-nine gap was `redextape-native`'s `measure.rs` — a library path in a crate nobody thought to look in, since every prior instance had been in `redextape-core`. **The decision — the repository owner's, overriding the correction the plan had prescribed — was to stop stating a count and state the property instead**, following `Cargo.toml`'s `[workspace.lints.clippy]` comment, which has been handling this identical class for months by naming `lambda/term.rs`'s `shift` and adding that it *"is not the only one"*. The re-filed paragraph names every site by symbol and says what they have in common; a tenth site added tomorrow makes the paragraph incomplete but does not make it wrong, which is the difference a count destroys.

**Nothing mechanical was ever going to catch this, and nothing will.** `scripts/check-doc-figures.sh` — the gate this repo built precisely because a README figure went stale unnoticed — reads a hard-coded table whose file column holds four grammar READMEs and the root `README.md`. It has no `docs/superpowers/**` row, so every figure in this roadmap, including the ones in this entry, is held only by whoever re-measures it.

**This is the second standing list in this file measured against the tree and found wrong, and the first one has the same shape down to the arithmetic.** The encoding-site survey filed under the extension tracks above — *"No structural link between `EncodingKind` and the files keeping local encoding lists"* — records of itself that *"the site survey undercounted three times, which is itself the finding worth recording"*: filed at 6 sites across 5 files, re-grepped to **13 sites across 10 files in 3 shapes**, then a **14th site in a 4th shape** during execution, then a **15th** found by a whole-branch review after the task was believed done. Six, thirteen, fourteen, fifteen for one list, two of them written down as corrections — against five, eight, nine, seventeen for this one, also two of them written down as corrections. **And this file already carried the measurement that predicts both**, in the *"grep the tree for a falsified claim"* lesson: *"The enumeration written before the grep was short again, for the fifth consecutive time on this class, which is now less a warning than a measurement: on this codebase, a list of consequence sites written from memory runs ~2x short."* Five to nine is 1.8x. The prediction was in the file, one screen from the list it predicted, and the list still shipped short.

**What closed the encoding survey was not a better count.** It was `macro_rules! encoding_kinds!`, a registry that makes the enumeration complete by construction. No equivalent exists for `unreachable!` short of enabling `clippy::unreachable`, which is refused on its merits above, so this list gets the other available answer: state the property, name the sites, and carry no number. The deferred-accessibility list earlier in this file names the same failure mode about itself in its own opening sentence — *"The risk of deferring is that it silently never happens, which is why this is a list with instances rather than a note saying a11y is on the todo."* Instances make the drift findable. They do not make it fire.

##### LESSON TWO — THE WHOLE-BRANCH REVIEW DEFEATED THIS BRANCH'S OWN GATE IN ONE COMPILE, WITH THE CONSTRUCTION THE GATE'S MODEL FILE RECORDS AS HAVING BROKEN ITS OWN BLACKLIST

`use std::rc::Rc as Handle;` then `Handle::downgrade(&t.0)` mints a weak handle to a term's allocation under `src` and contains none of the three needles the gate shipped with — not `Rc::downgrade`, not `Weak<`, not `rc::Weak`. The gate reported `2 tests run: 2 passed, 0 skipped`. **The gate's own doc had asserted that `Rc::downgrade` "catches the only way to mint one", and that sentence is where the defect lives:** `Rc::downgrade` is the only *function*, but a needle matches a *spelling*, and the doc collapsed the two. The fourth needle is bare `downgrade`, which strictly subsumes the first and cost nothing to add — `grep -rn 'Weak\|downgrade' crates/*/src/` had no match workspace-wide.

**The construction that beat it is a crate alias, and this repo has a file whose entire doc comment is about crate aliases beating a blacklist.** `redextape-test-support`'s `ts_derive_scan.rs` — the file this gate's doc cites as its model for the *name your routes* convention — records four review rounds in which a crate alias — `use ts_rs as tsrs;` then `derive(tsrs::TS)` — was one of four spellings that each walked past the previous wording, and states the conclusion in its own words: *"Four rounds, four spellings, because a blacklist can only ever enumerate the spellings someone has already thought of, and there is always one more — this function's own history is the proof."* **The new gate borrowed that file's convention and not the lesson that forced it.** Borrowing a document's form is not borrowing its content, and the tell is that the borrowed gate is still a blacklist while the file it was modelled on had already inverted to a whitelist for exactly this reason.

##### FOUR OF THIS BRANCH'S DEFECTS WERE WRITTEN BY THE PLAN, NOT BY AN IMPLEMENTER, AND BOTH PER-TASK FIX ROUNDS WERE FOR PLAN-AUTHORED PROSE

Task 1's Important was the plan's three benign gate fixtures, none of which contained any needle — so the comment filter they exist to exercise was unexercised by its own self-test *and* by the tree, and deleting the filter reddened nothing. Task 2's Important was the plan's "three sites get shorter" rationale, wrong by the braced-sibling blind spot above. The whole-branch review's I3 was the plan having stopped describing the code it ships. Its I4 was the correction the plan prescribed for Task 5 being itself wrong. **Both per-task fix rounds were dispatched against plan-authored prose:** each implementer built what the plan specified, and what needed repairing was what the plan specified — though repairing it took code changes in both cases, which is why "the plan was wrong" is not a cheaper finding than "the code was wrong". That is a recurring shape here — the wire-type entry above records three of its defects as prose the plan wrote asserting a mechanism nobody had measured, while its one *mechanical* plan defect was rejected by a gate the moment it landed — and the working conclusion is that a plan's prose is a claim exactly as much as its numbers are, and gets checked the same way or not at all.

##### `42c985c`'S SUBJECT LINE WAS THE CORRECTION "THREE" → "FOUR", AND IT LEFT THREE SIBLINGS OF THAT ERROR IN THE FILE IT WAS CORRECTING

The commit that fixed Task 2's miscount appended the corrected rationale and left the paragraph **62 lines above it still asserting three**. Step 5 still expected a grep of 3, where the true before/after is 6 → 2. The plan's File Structure table, its Files list and its `git add` line all still omitted `tests/viewmodel_contract.rs`, the fourth file the correction itself was about. **Fixing the instance and leaving its sibling one screen away, inside the very commit whose subject line was the correction.** The fix round that closed it found three further stale plan quotations beyond the one the review had named — its own edits had invalidated Task 1 Step 4, Task 3 Step 1 and Task 4 Step 2 — and resynced all four by programmatic extraction, machine-verified byte-identical against the shipped files, which is the only form of this that keeps holding.

##### THE FOURTH NEEDLE'S ONLY EVIDENCE WAS A GITIGNORED TRANSCRIPT, AND `c012754` IS WHAT PINNED IT IN THE TREE

The fix round added bare `downgrade` to `NEEDLES` and proved it by sabotage — but every one of the self-test's four offending probes also matched one of the other three needles, so **deleting `downgrade` from `NEEDLES` left the whole suite green**. The needle's only demonstration lived in `.superpowers/sdd/`, which is git-ignored and will not survive the merge. A fifth offending probe, `"    let w = Handle::downgrade(&t.0);"` — verified character by character to contain none of `Rc::downgrade`, `Weak<`, `rc::Weak` — now pins it, and removing the needle reddens `the_scan_catches_every_spelling_it_claims_to_and_no_prose` naming that exact string. **This is the same class as Task 1's own Important, one level up:** a check that cannot fail, inside a gate whose whole premise is that a check nobody has seen fail is worth nothing.

##### TASK 4'S DOC CLAIM WAS MEASURED RATHER THAN REASONED

The `LetRecGroup` pair's new doc says what makes the pair a pair, and it is falsifiable: deleting the bindings drain from `take_core_children`'s `LetRecGroup` arm aborts `dropping_deep_letrecgroup_chain_through_a_binding_value_does_not_overflow` **alone**, while the twin still passes; deleting the `body` unlink instead aborts `dropping_deep_letrecgroup_chain_through_body_does_not_overflow` **alone**, while the first still passes. Both were run, both mirror images reproduced, and `core.rs` was reverted after each. The alternative — writing "each test covers one child" and moving on — would have been one more prose mechanism nobody had measured, on a branch whose defects were largely exactly that.

##### WHAT STAYS OPEN

- **The third direct-then-`defunc` copy is untouched and still needs real design.** `tm.rs`'s `lower_program`, `sourcemap.rs`'s `tm_half` and `tm/attribute.rs`'s `lower_mapped` all answer *"lower this Core, retry through `defunc` only on `Unsupported`, never on `TooDeep`"*, and `sourcemap.rs` admits the duplication in a comment. It was excluded from this slice by decision, for the reason it has always carried: the three callers want different outputs from the same decision, so folding it is a design change and not a cleanup, and a slice scoped to four cosmetic minors is the wrong place for one.
- **The `unreachable!` sites, with the verdict unchanged.** Removing them means changing the types so the impossible arm cannot be written. The paragraph above now states the property and names the sites by symbol; what it no longer states, permanently, is how many there are.
- **`lambda::reduce::Owner` had the identical papercut `Node` had and was deliberately not taken; it is re-exported now.** Seven files imported it on a line of its own (`src/viewmodel.rs`, `tests/ts_bindings.rs`, `tests/lambda_provenance.rs`, `tests/zipper_equivalence.rs`, and the three `examples/*_probe.rs`), an eighth matches on it by fully-qualified path in `tests/viewmodel_contract.rs`, and `lambda.rs`'s `pub use reduce::{…}` line carried `Status`, `Step` and `Trace` but not `Owner` — the same shape as the `Node` bullet, where the module's other matched-on types were re-exported and one was not. It was not taken because **the bullet that slice closed named `Node`**: another re-export is another public-API addition, and a cleanup slice that starts generalising its own findings is how it stops being one. **The boundary moved because the repository's owner asked for it once the branch's other work was done and the cost had been measured at one line** — `Owner` joins the existing `pub use reduce::{…}`, colliding with nothing in `lambda`'s namespace. `grep -rn 'lambda::reduce::Owner' crates/ | wc -l` went **12 → 2 import lines and 5 fully-qualified uses, 6 hits in total**: six of the seven import sites collapsed into a sibling `use …lambda::…` line already in scope, and what is left is the one import that could not shorten plus the five fully-qualified matches in `tests/viewmodel_contract.rs`, which are not imports and were not touched.
- **The seventh `Owner` site is `tests/lambda_provenance.rs`, and the reason it did not shorten is the whole reason this was measured site by site.** Its only `lambda` siblings are `use redextape_core::lambda::reduce::reduce_step;` and `use redextape_core::lambda::term::{LambdaTerm, Node, abs, app, app_owned, beta, var};`. `reduce_step` is not re-exported from `lambda.rs`, and the `term` line carries `abs`, `app`, `app_owned`, `beta` and `var`, which are not either — so merging `Owner` into either one adds a line instead of removing one. **The `Node` round got this class wrong in the opposite direction**, by looking only for already-braced `lambda::{…}` siblings and missing a bare single-item one, which is how it claimed three sites where four got shorter. The criterion used here is *any* other `use …lambda::…;` line in the same scope, braced or bare, naming something `lambda.rs` re-exports — and `tests/ts_bindings.rs`, whose only sibling was the bare `use redextape_core::lambda::Cut;`, is precisely the site that criterion catches and the earlier one would have missed. Each of the seven was checked against its own sibling lines rather than against a pattern.
- **`Rc::new_cyclic` was a real route past the no-`Weak` gate, named and deliberately not gated — and it is gated now, as the fifth needle.** Its closure receives a weak handle to the allocation being built, and the call need name neither the type nor the method, so no spelling-based needle reached it. It was left open because adding bans is how a cleanup slice becomes unbounded, and the review had asked only that it be named. **The boundary moved because the repository's owner asked for it once this branch's other work was done and the cost had been measured at zero:** `grep -rn 'new_cyclic' crates/` matched exactly one line, the gate's own doc, so the needle bans nothing that exists. It is spelled bare rather than `Rc::new_cyclic` for the reason the fourth needle is bare — `use std::rc::Rc as Handle;` then `Handle::new_cyclic(..)` carries no path-qualified form, and that alias construction is precisely what walked past this gate mid-branch — and it is pinned by an offending probe matching `new_cyclic` and none of the other four, checked character by character and then by sabotage: removing the needle reddens `the_scan_catches_every_spelling_it_claims_to_and_no_prose` naming that exact string. **What stays open is the part gating one more spelling cannot touch.** `NEEDLES` is still a blacklist and still holds only the spellings somebody has already thought of; the routes the gate's doc names — a macro expanding to the construction at its call site, a `#[path]` resolving outside `src`, and a handle minted in `tests/` or `examples/` the day a public accessor hands out a term's `Rc` — got shorter by one without getting complete, and the file now says so in those words.
- **The gate's ban is wider than the invariant, on purpose.** The invariant is about `Weak<Node>` specifically; the gate refuses any weak handle anywhere under `redextape-core/src`, because narrowing it to the one type means parsing Rust rather than scanning lines, and the false positives it would buy are cheap while the false negative is a stack overflow at teardown. Of the routes its doc still names, **the one that puts a handle in `tests/` or `examples/`, outside the walk root, is unreachable today only because `LambdaTerm`'s `Rc` field is private and no `pub fn` in the crate returns one** (`grep -rn -- '-> *Rc<\|-> *std::rc::Rc<\|-> *&Rc<' crates/redextape-core/src/` finds one hit, a private `fn` returning `Rc<Frame>`). Privacy, not the gate, is what confines minting to one file. It becomes a real route the day a public accessor hands out the `Rc`, and the doc now states it as that conditional rather than as a hole.
- **`src/lambda/lower.rs`'s `mod tests` import block is mergeable and out of scope.** Its `crate::lambda::decode::decode`, `crate::lambda::reduce::{MAX_REDUCTION_STEPS, reduce_to_normal_form}` and `crate::lambda::term::Node` lines are all re-exported from `lambda.rs` and could be one line. It is excluded because the `decode` and `reduce` lines were spelled by submodule path *by choice* and were never forced by `Node`'s absence — the class this slice fixed is "the sites where `Node`'s absence forced an extra line", not "every mergeable `lambda` import in the crate". **That boundary currently lives only in a per-slice plan document**, which is why it is restated here.
- **Two Minors stay deferred, and each now carries why it was declined in the round that took the other two.** `no_weak_handles.rs`'s `offending_lines` skips `//` comments but not `/* */` blocks — **declined because Rust block comments nest**, so handling them correctly is not a predicate over one line but a line-spanning nesting-depth state machine: parsing logic added to a scanner, bought for a construct that appears zero times under `redextape-core/src`, and bought against a failure mode that is already the safe one, since a needle inside a block comment is a loud false positive rather than a silent miss. And its `walk` duplicates in miniature the private recursive walker inside `redextape-test-support`'s `ts_derive_scan.rs` — **declined because sharing it means widening that crate's public API**, exporting a walker for roughly ten lines of `read_dir` boilerplate in order to couple two gates whose scan roots and needle sets both differ; the coupling is the cost, not the saving. **Both differ from `new_cyclic` and `Owner` in the same way, which is the answer to why two of the four moved:** those two cost zero lines and one line respectively and each closed something named, while these two each buy a new kind of surface — parsing logic in one, public API in the other — for nothing measurable in the tree today.

**`scripts/check-all.sh` RAN IN ITS FULL FORM, AND THAT IS A DIFFERENCE FROM EVERY EARLIER ENTRY IN THIS FILE RATHER THAN A DETAIL.** Its own closing line is quoted rather than the run called green:

```
$ ./scripts/check-all.sh
all configs green -- base, LLVM and browser
(exit 0)
```

Every previous entry that runs this script quotes the other closing line -- `green, but PARTIAL -- these tiers were SKIPPED: LLVM browser. This is NOT a full gate on its own.` -- because every previous entry ran it with `--no-llvm --no-browser`. This one skipped no tier, so no such caveat applies and none is written here. **It ran at this branch's head, one commit past the commit the figures above were measured at**, and the two commits between them touch only this roadmap file, so nothing it exercised changed underneath them. `git status --porcelain` was empty when it finished.

**CI, ADDED AFTER THE MERGE RATHER THAN BEFORE IT, AND THAT ORDER IS ITSELF WORTH RECORDING.** This entry shipped saying *"no pull request exists at the time of writing and no run has happened"* — true when written, false within the hour, and nothing in the tree would ever have said so. **THIS IS A RECURRENCE OF A FAILURE THIS FILE HAD ALREADY WRITTEN DOWN, NOT A NEW ONE**, and the first draft of this paragraph claimed otherwise — it asserted that *"every previous slice added its CI paragraph on the branch once the first run went green"*, which measurement refutes twice over. `grep -c '^#### '` reads 74 entries and `grep -c 'Run [0-9]\+ '` reads 6, so a CI paragraph is the exception here rather than the rule. And the asm-reader slice's PR 2 entry already did exactly this: its *"no CI run has produced a result to name"* went false the instant the result arrived and, in the words of the entry that caught it, **sat directly above the result it denied.** A sentence whose truth depends on when it is read is the defect this entry's first lesson is about — committed by the entry itself, then committed again by the paragraph written to correct it, which reached for a universal it had not counted.

**Pull request #72, merged as `4d18e2e` (squash).** Run 340 (API id 1330) green on `bf739c6` — **inferred from the push sequence rather than read, because `get_run` exposes no head SHA**, and named anyway because "the branch head at the time it ran" is a relationship, which this file has its own entry about. Run 342 (API id 1334) green on `0ab00d3`, the head read back from the pull request rather than assumed. **Run 341 (API id 1333) reads `cancelled`, and it is not a failure — it is self-inflicted and the mechanism is worth naming**: the workflow's `pull_request` trigger includes `edited`, so editing the body to keep it accurate while a run was in flight re-triggered everything and Forgejo cancelled the run underneath it. The same body edit is this forge's documented way to re-run a pipeline, having no rerun endpoint; it cannot tell *"re-run this"* from *"I fixed a sentence"*. Batch body edits before a run starts or after it ends, never during.

**Run 343 (API id 1335) is the post-merge push run on `4d18e2e`, and it is the first execution of `docker` on this work.** All ten jobs reported: `detect`, `linear-history`, `rust`, `rust-slow`, `rust-llvm`, `rust-browser`, `web`, `gate` and `docker` all `success`, with `rust-scoped` `skipped`. **That `docker` row is the one this entry could not have before**, because the job is skipped on pull requests and absent from `gate`'s `needs` — so #72 going green said nothing about the image, exactly as this section warned before the merge. This branch changes no `Dockerfile` and adds no build step, and the image now has a green build to show for it rather than an argument.

**No per-job durations are quoted.** The job listing carries no timestamps of any kind, and this file has an entry's worth of history about single-pair wall-clock comparisons on a runner that shares this machine.

#### THE TWO WIDTH SEARCHES FOLD AND 45 DANGLING `brief` REFERENCES GO, THE FILINGS SAID 15 SITES AND TWO COPIES WHERE THE TREE HELD 45 AND FIVE — THE THIRD STANDING LIST IN THIS FILE MEASURED AGAINST THE TREE AND FOUND SHORT — THE COUNT TAKEN WHILE WRITING THE SPEC WAS ITSELF SHORT BECAUSE A CASE-SENSITIVE FILE SELECTOR FED A CASE-INSENSITIVE COUNT, THE PLAN'S PREDICTION ABOUT ITS OWN NEW TEST WAS WRONG FOR THE THIRD SLICE RUNNING AND MEASURING IT HERE MAKES IT WRONG IN BOTH DIRECTIONS, AND THE ARGUMENT THAT LICENSED RUNNING TWO AGENTS AT ONCE — DISJOINT TOOLCHAINS — WAS FALSE (2026-09-02, branch `search-fold-and-brief-refs`, `45aa45a..abbd532`, 12 commits, plus the entry commits that necessarily follow it)

Design: [`2026-09-02-search-fold-and-brief-references-design.md`](../specs/2026-09-02-search-fold-and-brief-references-design.md). Plan: [`2026-09-02-search-fold-and-brief-refs.md`](2026-09-02-search-fold-and-brief-refs.md). Two unrelated cleanups taken in one branch because they are file-disjoint and each is too small to justify a branch of its own: item A folds two copies of the TM field-width search into one helper, item B stops 45 sites pointing at a per-task brief that has never been a file in this repository. **Neither adds a capability and neither changes what any program computes** — `git diff --shortstat 45aa45a 217cb7a` reads 33 files, +881/−110, of which the design and the plan are two files and 703 of the 881 added lines. Item B changed **two** lines that are not comments, which is a deviation from the plan's own rule and is recorded as one below. **Everything below WHAT SHIPPED is a finding rather than a feature**, and most of them are about measurements rather than about code.

##### WHAT SHIPPED

**Item A — one `search_width` on the library path, and both entry points now call it.** `crates/redextape-core/src/tm.rs` grew `fn search_width<T>(mut at: impl FnMut(usize) -> Option<T>, overflowed: impl Fn(&T) -> bool) -> Option<(T, usize)>`, which owns the `MIN_FIELD_WIDTH`/doubling/`MAX_FIELD_WIDTH` ladder and the rule that only the overflow guard retries. `run_tm_fitted` maps its `None` onto `(TmRun::TooLarge, None)` and `run_tm_described` onto `Err(TmRun::TooLarge)`; `run_tm_fitted`'s unbounded-encoding branch stays ahead of the call, because it runs one attempt and is not part of the search. `run_tm_described`'s doc claim *"Mirrors `run_tm_fitted`'s search"* was **deleted rather than reworded** — after the fold there is no second search to mirror, and a claim about another function is the drift the item existed to remove. The retry rationale moved onto the helper it describes. One test was added, `the_two_entry_points_fit_the_same_width`, and no existing assertion was edited.

**Item B — 45 sites across 27 files, each read and dispositioned with the file open.** Three dispositions: name the document the fact actually came from, drop the possessive where the brief was only provenance, or reword where the reference is load-bearing. **The replacement wording was deliberately NOT written by the spec**, on the ground stated in §3.1: the `wire-type-generation` slice recorded five of its six correction rounds as prose the plan or the spec had written, and a spec composing 45 comments from outside the files would have reproduced exactly that. `git diff -U0 6f0d99c 217cb7a | grep -E '^\+' | grep -oE '20[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}[a-z0-9-]*\.md'` finds **13 added lines naming 9 distinct documents**, every one of which exists on disk, and every one named by filename only — the citation gate rejects `file:line` and accepts a path, which is why disposition 1 is spelled the way it is.

##### THE FILING SAID 15 SITES ACROSS 10 FILES; THE TREE HELD 45 ACROSS 27, AND THIS IS THE THIRD STANDING LIST IN THIS FILE TO BE MEASURED AND FOUND SHORT

The July filing is reproducible to the site: `git grep -n 'the brief' 45aa45a -- 'crates/**/*.rs' | wc -l` still reads **15**, across **10** files. The class measured with the scoping its own filing did not state — case-insensitive, the whole tracked tree, less `briefly`, less `LICENSE.md`'s GPL boilerplate, less `docs/` — reads **45 sites across 27 files** at the same commit. **3.0x on sites, 2.7x on files.** The filing's grep was scoped twice without saying so: to `*.rs`, and to the literal lowercase string `"the brief"`. Seven of the 45 are in `web/src/` — production source, not tests — and no measurement scoped to `crates/**/*.rs` could ever have reached one of them.

**This file has now done this three times, and it carries the sentence that predicts it.** The encoding-site survey ran **6 → 13 → 14 → 15** sites (5 → 10 files), two of those numbers written down as corrections. The `unreachable!` list ran **5 → 8 → 9**, with a fourth answer of **17** produced by a filter that counted the macro's own name inside indented comments. This one runs **15 → 45**, the largest ratio of the three. And the *"grep the tree for a falsified claim"* lesson above states the prediction outright: *"on this codebase, a list of consequence sites written from memory runs ~2x short."* Six to fifteen is 2.5x, five to nine is 1.8x, fifteen to forty-five is 3.0x. **The prediction has sat in this file since 2026-07-31**, in the entry headed *"the lesson this branch cost the most to learn: grep the tree for a falsified claim, not the document that stated it first"*, and both standing lists measured against the tree since — the `unreachable!` one on 2026-09-01 and this one on 2026-09-02 — shipped short anyway. That is enough repetitions that the working rule is not "re-grep before filing" but "a filed site list is an estimate until a command is quoted beside it."

##### THE COUNT TAKEN WHILE WRITING THE SPEC WAS ITSELF SHORT, BY A DUMBER MECHANISM THAN ANY OF THE THREE — AND THE SENTENCE THAT NAMED THAT BUG MISCOUNTED IT TOO

The first per-file tally taken while writing the design selected files case-**sensitively** (`grep -l brief`) and then counted within each file case-**insensitively** (`grep -ic brief`). Every file carrying only uppercase `BRIEF` was therefore dropped from the listing before anything counted it. Re-run at `45aa45a`, the case-sensitive selector picks **23 files holding 35 sites**; the case-insensitive one picks **32 files holding 45**. The selector cost **10 sites across 8 files** — `crates/redextape-core/tests/viewmodel_contract.rs`, `web/src/compile.ts`, `web/src/main.ts`, `web/src/replies.ts`, `web/src/session-worker.ts`, `web/src/style.css`, `web/tests/browser/scratch-edit.test.ts` and `web/tests/browser/tm-blank-buffer.test.ts` — plus a ninth dropped file, `web/tests/browser/two-lambda-panes.test.ts`, whose only match is an uppercase `BRIEFLY` and which holds no site at all. **35 → 45 is 1.3x on top of the filing's 3.0x, and it is the same defect one level in:** a measurement is not evidence until its own selection step is checked, and the selection step is the part nobody reads.

**The design's own sentence about this bug is wrong in the same direction, and it is corrected here rather than quietly.** It reads *"which is five of the seven `web/src/` sites"*. Five is the number of `web/src/` **files** the selector dropped; the number of **sites** in them is **seven — all of them.** `web/src/compile.ts` and `web/src/replies.ts` carry two apiece and `main.ts`, `session-worker.ts` and `style.css` one apiece, and none of the five contains a lowercase `brief` anywhere, so the selector took every `web/src/` site the item had. A sentence written to record a files-versus-sites confusion made a files-versus-sites confusion.

##### THE ROADMAP ITEM NAMED TWO COPIES OF THE SEARCH; THE TREE HELD FIVE, AND THREE OF THEM ARE DELIBERATELY NOT FOLDED

Item 3 of the TM-header slice's *"Still open after slice 2"*, struck above, named `run_tm_fitted` and `run_tm_described`. `git grep -n 'fn widths()' 45aa45a -- crates/` finds three more: `tests/tm_bank_invariant.rs`, `tests/tm_width_equivalence.rs` and `examples/width_report.rs`, each a `fn widths() -> Vec<usize>` re-encoding the same ladder. Their bodies are byte-identical to each other today and still are after this branch — extracted at `217cb7a` they hash to one `md5sum`, `d2354c2b646b7044a694357d6770acc5`.

**They stay duplicated, and that is the decision rather than the oversight.** They are independent models of the search, and two of them carry assertions that are *about* the ladder rather than about a program: `tm_width_equivalence.rs`'s `assert!(widths_seen.iter().any(|&w| w > MIN_FIELD_WIDTH), ...)`, whose message is `"no program ever needed a retry"`, and `tm_bank_invariant.rs`'s `the_split_covers_the_whole_cross_product`, whose `assert_eq!(emitted, expected, ...)` checks `EMITTED` against the cross product of `widths()` and `encodings_at` — two files, not one. Routing them through `tm.rs` would make them walk whatever the search says and stop being able to disagree with it. This repository has already paid for the opposite choice, twice, and both precedents are bold verdict sentences inside entries rather than headings themselves — the entries carrying them are the `####` headings, at lines 14193 and 13122. The `nvim-plugin-dir` entry (14193) records three green end-to-end verifications of a plugin that produced no colour at all, because every harness *"registered its own `FileType` autocmd calling `vim.treesitter.start`"* — the thing under test — and gives the verdict as **"The instrument was the defect, and that outranks the missing call."** The asm-reader PR 3 entry (13122) states the general form; its own sentence is hard-wrapped mid-word across two lines ("...what it" / "watches..."), so the clause that greps to it whole is the half that survives the wrap on one line, **"watches cannot notice that thing changed"**, credited there to the λ-hang thread in a different subsystem. What the slice added instead is one doc line per copy saying so, plus a paragraph on `search_width` itself pointing back at them, because **without that the next sibling search finds three identical functions and folds them**, which is precisely how the assertion above stops being able to fail.

**Those two citations replaced one this entry nearly shipped, and the near miss belongs here.** The design states this same argument by naming *"the `harness-supplied-the-thing-under-test` finding"*, and the first draft of this paragraph copied it. `git grep -n harness-supplied 217cb7a` matches that spec and nothing else — one hit, in the document that wrote the phrase: it names a lesson recorded outside the tree, so a reader following it finds nothing. **A dangling pointer, in the entry closing a sweep of 45 dangling pointers, written by copying a citation instead of resolving it** — which is disposition 1 of item B's own rule applied to this entry, and the reason both replacements point at prose inside this file that a reader can actually find: one by the `####` heading it sits under, the other by the unwrapped phrase quoted above, chosen because the sentence it belongs to is itself split across a line wrap.

##### THE PLAN PREDICTED ITS OWN NEW TEST WOULD REDDEN UNDER SABOTAGE AND IT DOES NOT — AND RE-RUNNING BOTH SABOTAGES HERE MAKES THAT TRUE IN BOTH DIRECTIONS RATHER THAN ONE

Task 1 Step 8 named `the_two_entry_points_fit_the_same_width` as a test Sabotage A (*never retry*) would redden. Re-run at `217cb7a` on the shipped tree, `if overflowed(&got) && width < MAX_FIELD_WIDTH {` replaced by `if false {`, `cargo nextest run -p redextape-core --no-fail-fast` reports **50 of 959 failed** — and the new test is not among them; it is at `PASS [0.081s] (715/959)`. **It cannot be.** After the fold both entry points call the one broken helper, so they agree with each other while both being wrong, and a test that asserts only agreement is blind to a fault they share. The test's own doc comment said this before the prediction was written: *"a divergence in how each one CALLS the helper is invisible to a test of the helper itself."* Both the implementer and the reviewer reached the explanation independently.

**Measuring rather than relaying widens it.** Sabotage B (*start at the ceiling*, `MIN_FIELD_WIDTH` → `MAX_FIELD_WIDTH`) reddens **10 of 959**, and the new test passes under that one too, at `PASS [0.152s] (758/959)` — a fact the branch's own ledger does not contain, because only Sabotage A had been checked against the prediction. **So the new test reddens under neither sabotage of the shared helper, not merely under one.** That is not a defect in it: a third sabotage run here, replacing `run_tm_described`'s overflow predicate with `|_d| false` so that one caller drives the shared helper differently, reddens **7 of 959** *including* the new test, on `` assertion `left == right` failed: `40 + 2` under unary / left: 64 / right: 4 `` — the same shape as the pre-fold Step 3 sabotage that qualified the test before it was trusted. **The fold is guarded by the other 50, and the new test guards the one axis the fold created.** Its role is narrower than the plan claimed and exactly as wide as its own doc comment claimed.

**This is the third slice running whose defect was a plan-authored prediction about a mechanism nobody had measured.** The `wire-type-generation` entry records three such; the `minor-findings-cleanup` entry records four plan-authored defects and both of its per-task fix rounds dispatched against plan prose. The pattern is stable enough to state as a rule: **a plan's prose is a claim exactly as much as its numbers are, and a sentence predicting which test will fail is the cheapest kind of claim to check and the easiest to skip.**

##### THE ARGUMENT THAT LICENSED RUNNING TWO AGENTS CONCURRENTLY WAS FALSE, AND IT IS RECORDED AS A NEAR MISS RATHER THAN A LUCKY ONE

Item A and item B were run as two concurrent agents, split along what the controller called the toolchain boundary: `web/` on pnpm and biome, `crates/` on cargo, on the repository's own recorded lesson that parallel agents need disjoint **toolchains** and not merely disjoint files. **`web/` and `crates/` do not have disjoint toolchains.** `web/package.json` line 14 reads `"typecheck": "pnpm run build:bindings && tsc --noEmit"`, line 9 reads `"build:bindings": "bash ../scripts/build-web-bindings.sh"`, and that script's lines 189–190 are two `cargo test -p … --features ts export_bindings` invocations. The web agent ran `pnpm run typecheck` once before noticing, and so compiled the Rust workspace while the other agent's edits to `tm.rs` were mid-flight.

**Nothing broke.** The run only wrote gitignored output under `pkg/` and `web/bindings/`, `git status` stayed clean outside `web/`, and the agent switched to `npx tsc --noEmit` for every later check. **The finding is not the outcome, it is that the safety argument was false as stated** — the two agents were not separated by the thing the split was justified on, and the run that proved it was invoked by the agent the split was meant to fence off. A concurrency argument that names a boundary has to be checked against the scripts on both sides of it, and `package.json`'s `typecheck` script is one `grep` away.

**And switching away from `pnpm run typecheck` could not have avoided it, which is the part that makes this structural rather than a slip.** `.pre-commit-config.yaml` line 125 is `entry: bash -c 'cd web && pnpm run typecheck'`, fired by `files: ^web/.*\.(ts|tsx)$` — so the repository's own commit gate takes the same route into cargo on **every** web-only commit, and `03b9d28`, the web half's commit, therefore compiled the Rust tree a second time while item A was mid-flight, through a hook the agent did not choose and could not decline without `--no-verify`. **There is no configuration of this repository in which a `web/` agent and a `crates/` agent are toolchain-disjoint.** What made the concurrency safe was the thing the plan asserted separately and which held — the two agents' *file* sets are disjoint, and cargo's own lock serialises the builds rather than corrupting them — so the correct version of the argument was available and simply was not the one written down.

##### TWO OF THE 45 SITES WERE INSIDE STRING LITERALS, NOT COMMENTS, AND THE SWEEP IS NOT COMMENTS-ONLY

The plan's Global Constraints and the design's scope boundary both say item B touches comments only and that no executable line may change. Two sites in the plan's own inventory are inside string literals: `crates/redextape-core/examples/lambda_sharing_probe.rs`, a continued `\n\` line inside a `println!`, and `crates/redextape-core/examples/step_survey.rs`, a `&str` in the `SUPPLEMENTARY_PROBES` data array. Editing them changes what those two probes print. **The repository owner's decision was to keep both edits**, and the reviewer independently agreed it is a real byte-level breach and rated it Minor: neither string is asserted by any test, both are pure diagnostic prose, the replacements are accurate, and `step_survey`'s now names `PROBES` — a real constant in the same file — where it used to name a document that never existed.

The measurement is exact and it is the reason the deviation can be stated as small rather than argued as small: filtering item B's whole diff (`git diff -U0 6f0d99c 217cb7a`) down to changed lines that are not `///`, `//!`, `//`, `/* */` or their continuations leaves **eight lines in three files**. Four of them are in `web/src/style.css` and are the interior of a CSS `/* */` block, so they are comments after all. The other four are the two string-literal sites, one `-`/`+` pair each. **Two edited sites in the whole sweep are not comments, and both are named here.** What the entry must not say, and does not, is that the sweep was comments-only.

##### THE ONE IMPORTANT FINDING, AND WHY IT IS THE CHARACTERISTIC FAILURE OF A UNIFORMLY-APPLIED REPLACEMENT PHRASE

`tests/lambda_foreign_reader.rs`'s *"THE RESIDUAL"* paragraph is the file's own honesty check: it draws the line between what in the file was derived from doc comments (the grammar, the encodings, TAPL's β rule) and what came from outside them (the corpus, the `FTy` set, the caps, the pipeline). At `45aa45a` it read *"whose heap layout came from **its** brief, nothing about the GRAMMAR or the ENCODINGS here came from **the** brief"* — two different documents, distinguished by nothing but a possessive. The disposition-3 rewording replaced both with the same phrase and then bound them with *"those same out-of-band instructions"*, which asserts that `tm_foreign_reader.rs` and `lambda_foreign_reader.rs` were built under one document. They were not: the first's heap layout is specified in `2026-07-28-tm-header-hardening-and-tooling.md` and the second's corpus, `FTy` enum and pipeline in `2026-07-28-lambda-foreign-reader-and-typed-decode.md`, both verified by reading the tasks rather than taken on the reviewer's word.

**A false identity claim, created by a uniform replacement, inside the exact paragraph whose job is to qualify the file's independence.** That is the failure mode a sweep like this one has: the rule that makes 45 edits consistent is the same rule that flattens a distinction one of the 45 was carrying, and it flattens it hardest where the original was terse. The fix names both plan documents explicitly on both halves of the sentence, which the reviewer judged **stronger** than the disposition-3 wording it replaced — a precise citation in place of a reworded hedge — and dropped *"same"* entirely so nothing binds the two clauses back together. Naming only one side would have left the other implicit and rebuilt the same ambiguity in miniature.

##### NO GATE HOLDS EITHER RESULT, AND THE CLASS IS CLOSED ONLY FOR THE SPELLING THAT WAS SEARCHED

**A `check-brief-references.sh` was considered and deliberately not built** (design §3.4). `brief` is an ordinary English word: it appears legitimately as `briefly`, in `LICENSE.md`'s GPL boilerplate, and in any future prose that wants it, so the gate would be a blacklist needing an allowlist beside it — and `docs/` would need excluding by path, because the roadmap, the plans and the specs must keep their occurrences. That is the shape of gate this repository has watched get defeated repeatedly, most recently one entry above, where a crate alias walked past a three-needle blacklist in one compile. **So the number below is held by nothing except the fact that it was re-measured while writing this paragraph, and the property is what to carry forward rather than the count: at the commit this entry is written from, no tracked source file outside `docs/` cites a per-task brief.** A file that reintroduces one tomorrow makes that sentence false and nothing in the tree will say so.

**`docs/` is a boundary, not an exemption, and the argument for it is already written down in the gate that enforces the neighbouring rule.** `scripts/check-citations.sh`'s own header makes it for the same directory and the same reason: *"A citation in source is a POINTER — go look here — and it stops being true the moment the target moves. A citation in a dated spec, plan or roadmap entry is an OBSERVATION — on that date, this was at that line — and rewriting it would falsify the record."* Rewriting `docs/`'s occurrences would falsify the record rather than fix a pointer. **This entry is itself the demonstration**: the `docs/` figures below moved because writing this paragraph moved them, which is what an append-only log does and why no gate can hold that number either.

**And the 45 was a measurement of a spelling, not of a class.** The inventory was `grep -ic brief` less `grep -ic briefly` over every tracked file outside `docs/` and `LICENSE.md` — that command and no other. A comment citing the same absent document without using that word — *"the task instructions"*, *"the prompt"*, *"what T8 asked for"* — is the identical defect and this sweep could not see it. **The class is closed for the word `brief`.** Two of the replacements written here spell the same referent as *"the out-of-band task instructions"*, so the branch has demonstrably created text the search that found the class would not find.

##### VERIFICATION

Every figure here was produced by the command beside it and re-run for this entry rather than copied from a task report or from the branch's ledger, including the ones a report had already stated. The class figures are measured at `45aa45a`, this branch's merge base with `main`, because that is the commit they are claims about; the sabotage, `check-all.sh` and suite figures are measured at `217cb7a`, the branch's last commit before this entry was first written, or on the working tree that commit plus this entry produced. **The commit-count and `docs/` figures were re-measured a second time, at `4e398f0`** — the commit that closed findings 1, 5 and 10 above — because the entry-fixing commits between `217cb7a` and `4e398f0` moved both. This fixing commit moves them once more by existing, which is why it is named as the measurement point rather than assumed to be one: **the commit that corrects a figure necessarily sits one commit outside the range that figure reports**, so the number below is true through `4e398f0` and this commit is the one after it, not folded in. **The three sabotage runs were performed here, not quoted** — each is a one-line edit to `tm.rs`, and `git status --porcelain` was empty again after each revert. Sabotage A's run appends a proptest regression seed to `crates/redextape-core/tests/three_way_oracle.proptest-regressions`; that file was reverted along with the sabotage, which is worth naming because it is the one artifact of these runs that is tracked and would otherwise have been committed.
