#### PLAN 7 PART 6a-ii, SHARE LINKS: `share` HOLDS A LINK TO THE PROGRAM, ITS ENCODING, THE WORKSPACE AND EACH LEG'S STEP, IN A POPOVER WITH THE LINK SELECTED IN ITS FIELD AND `copy link` UNDER IT; A LINK OPENS AT START-UP AHEAD OF BOTH STORES AND WHEN PASTED INTO AN OPEN PAGE, CLEARS ITS FRAGMENT AND OFFERS AN `undo` UNTIL IT IS WITHDRAWN; AND EACH LEG IS CARRIED TO ITS LINK'S STEP AS THE FRAMES REACH IT, CONTINUED UP TO TEN TIMES AND CLAMPED WITH ONE NOTICE WHERE THE RUN ENDS FIRST — AND THE FIX TASK MADE `share` A DISCLOSURE AND KEPT A LATEST-LINK GUARD AS A DEFENCE, SINCE IN CHROME TWO READS OF A LINK NEVER OVERLAP; THE WHOLE-BRANCH REVIEW FOUND A HOSTILE LINK'S WORKSPACE UNBOUNDED, NOW 64 SPLITS DEEP AND 64 LEAVES FOR A LINK AND A STORED LAYOUT ALIKE, A REAL PRESS ON `undo` LOST WHEN A CLAMP REDREW ITS NOTICE, AND FOUR TEST FILES WITH THIN MARGIN ON A SLOW RUNNER (2026-10-01, branch `plan7-part6a-ii-share-links`, `e143c38..52164d6`, 32 commits, plus this entry)

**Part 6a-ii of Plan 7** ([design](../specs/2026-09-29-plan7-part6a-examples-and-links-design.md), [plan](2026-09-30-plan7-part6a-ii-share-links.md)), the second of part 6a's two PRs, the spec's §1 6a-ii row; 6a-i, the examples and the stored program, merged as #120. It touches `web/` and `docs/` only: no Rust, no wasm, no new dependency, and no build output the app imports. Outside `docs/` it changes 41 files, +4,131/−96. Seven of the 32 commits touch only `docs/`: the spec's two amendments before the plan (`bb42183`, `adaecb8`), the plan (`9c241de`, 3,614 lines), the spec's notes from the plan and its fix task (`afa14d1`), its two amendments after the whole-branch review (`596b69e`, `8a68304`), and the correction of the second (`1d09b60`). `c1e8b48` changes the spec and one test.

**The user's decisions**, on 2026-09-30 and 2026-10-01:

- **Before the plan**: `share` sits after the bar's spacer, before `appearance`, where the spec first put it after `examples ▾` (the prototype's finding 1, `adaecb8`); and the open's `undo` is withdrawn at the next edit that changes the program and the next encoding chosen, as a pick's is (`bb42183`), and is offered by every later notice about the same open until then, however long after the open's own notice has gone (`adaecb8`).
- **After Task 4, one end-of-plan fix task, 4b**: `share` a disclosure, with no `aria-haspopup`, while `settings` keeps `aria-haspopup="menu"`, recorded as open; and a latest-wins guard in `openLink`. When 4b measured that the overlap it guards cannot happen in Chrome, the user kept the guard as a defence for an engine that reads a link across tasks, tested with a gated `DecompressionStream` stand-in.
- **After the whole-branch review** (spec `596b69e`): a workspace's tree is bounded, for a link's layout and a stored one alike; a share made while a link's position is pending carries that position for the program on screen; and an open's clamps share one notice. The bound was first 8 splits deep and 32 leaves. The fix wave's first part measured `+ view` building trees past it by itself, and the user raised it to 64 and 64 (`8a68304`).
- **During the fix wave**: every notice's action sits at the line's end, a copy's delete's, a palette removal's and a pick's as well as a link's, which keeps a press on it across a redraw.
- **And binary as the default encoding**, for a first visit and a pick, asked for on 2026-10-01, is its own PR after this one, not folded in (WHAT THIS DID NOT CLOSE).

##### WHAT 6a-ii BUILT

- **The link's codec** (`share-link.ts`, Task 1). A link is `#s=` and the unpadded base64url of the deflate-raw of the UTF-8 of `{ version: 1, program, encoding, workspace, positions }`, through the browser's own `CompressionStream`, with `workspace` as `serializeWorkspace` writes it. `decodeLink` refuses padding, a stray character, a cut or trailing deflate stream and text that is not UTF-8, and inflates a kilobyte at a time up to `MAX_LINK_BYTES`, 8 MiB, refusing a payload one byte over; `share-link-inflate.test.ts` holds the kilobyte feed in Chrome, since node's `DecompressionStream` takes its whole input at once. A link opens whole only when every field holds; with anything else and a string `program`, the program opens alone, under the link's encoding where this build has it; with neither, it is unreadable. No test pins an encoder's bytes: a frozen version 1 link, written by `encodeLink` in Chrome, pins the reading. **Since the fix wave, reading a link cannot throw**: a throw while its workspace is read opens the program alone, and any other makes the link unreadable.
- **`share`** (`share-popover.ts`, Task 2), after the spacer and before `appearance`, a disclosure since 4b: `aria-controls` and `aria-expanded`, and no `aria-haspopup`. Its popover is built again on each open, as the workspace menu is: a read-only field named `link`, holding the link to what is on the page, focused, with its text selected as the link fills it; `copy link`, disabled with its reason until the link is made, and absent where the page has no clipboard; and up to two lines describing the field — `this link is N characters long — some chat and mail apps cut links past 2,000` past 2,000 characters, and which views will open on the program because a copy is not included. A refused copy says the link is selected in the field. The popover keeps the `1rem` gutter the other header menus keep.
- **Opening a link** (`main.ts`, Task 3). At start-up, after `init()` and ahead of both stores, and on `hashchange` for one pasted into an open page. Opened whole, a link replaces the program, its encoding and the workspace, and every view is built again on the program through `PaneHost.rebuildViews`; the copies stay listed and their bindings are dropped. The fragment is cleared with `history.replaceState` whatever the link held, and the notice says `opened a shared link`, or what a program-alone open left out, or `this link could not be read — nothing was changed`. **The open's `undo`** puts back the program, its encoding, the workspace and each copy's view, moving a λ copy's editor back into its view since Task 3's review (`PaneHost.moveBack`), and says `put back the program and the workspace`, with the focus in the source editor or on `share`. It is held apart from the notice that carries it: withdrawn at the next edit that changes the program, the next encoding chosen, its own use or another open, and offered again by any later notice about the same open. An open that applies, and its `undo`, close `share`'s popover, whose link is to the program they replace.
- **A link's positions** (`share-positions.ts`, Task 4). Each program leg's step is held on `LegState.pending` until the frames reach it, where the step line says `going to step 3,000 from the link`; it applies once a frame past it has arrived, or once the recording has stopped on it. After the run's `result`, a leg short of its step is continued one at a time, λ then asm then TM, at most ten times, and where the run ends first, or the ten continues do not reach it, the leg is clamped and said about. **Since the fix wave, an open's clamps share one notice**, which each clamp redraws to name every leg stopped short so far, why, and the step each shows, carrying the open's `undo`. A step gesture takes a leg from its link, and every other way positions end is a recompile, whose first reply drops them.
- **The fix task's two changes** (4b). `share` became a disclosure (above), and `openLink` takes a ticket, so an open whose read ends after a later link's has begun is dropped unsaid.
- **And the fix wave's**: a workspace's tree is bounded in `layout.ts`'s `parseTree` at 64 splits deep and 64 leaves, and a leaf id's number at 10^9, for a link's layout and a stored one alike; a notice that offers the action already shown keeps its button, at the line's end; and a share carries a leg's pending step for the program on screen.

The branch adds 19 test files holding 151 tests: 75 in four node files and 76 in fifteen browser files.

##### THE PLAN WAS BUILT AND REPLAYED BEFORE IT WAS HANDED OUT

Every task was built, gated and sabotaged in a scratch worktree on branch `plan7-part6a-ii-proto`, off `90d181c`, whose commits `a15ad2f`, `98a6c7c`, `7ddc48c` and `20cc260` are the plan's four tasks, and the plan's code blocks are that prototype's patches. The plan was then rebuilt task by task from its own blocks on a fresh worktree at `90d181c`: 4 trees of 4 identical to the prototype's outside `docs/`, every red and green step as written, and **71 of 71 sabotages fired**, 16, 20, 19 and 16. Replaying found nothing to correct; one red count differing from the prototype's first, since a case was added after it; and the browser project peaked at 6.9G to 9.8G across the tasks' green steps and the coverage run, under the 16G cap.

**What the prototype found**, each answered in the plan's code:

1. **`share` after `examples ▾` cost a header row** at 390 and 360 px in some presets and styles; before `appearance` it costs none, with one copy or eleven. Decided by the user, as above.
2. **The page puts no bound on a fragment**, so the inflate cap is the one bound a link's bytes have.
3. **Node's `DecompressionStream` takes its whole input at once**, so the kilobyte feed is a browser test.
4. **Three of the codec's refusal cases were blind as first written**: a payload that is not UTF-8, `[7]` as positions, and "unpadded" checked on one payload that needed no padding.
5. **§5.2's "selects its text on `toggle`" selected an empty field**, since the link arrives after the popover has shown; the field is selected as it is filled.
6. **A clipboard permission reaches Chrome only when it names Playwright's browser context**, so a "refused" case had passed whatever the code did.
7. **`share`'s popover needs the menus' gutter**, measured at six widths in each preset.
8. **§5.3's `resetViews` kept a λ view drawing the opener's display** under the link's workspace: `PaneHost.rebuildViews` builds every view again.
9. **§5.4's "`seek` stops following" does not hold on the newest frame**, so a position applies once a frame past it has arrived.
10. **What in the first draft changed nothing is not in the code**, each found by a sabotage that failed nothing.
11. **An open's `undo` meets the copies cap only at start-up**, with more copies bound than the cap; `share-open-cap.test.ts` takes that path.
12. **Two of the popover's cases were blind as first written.**

Findings 5, 8 and 9 are dated notes in the spec (`afa14d1`). **What the spec left to the plan**, and how the plan fixed it: the inflate cap (`MAX_LINK_BYTES`, 8 MiB); the pending step line's words; the clamp's and the tenth continue's notices; the program-alone notice; the popover's two lines; a used `undo`'s words and focus; and `share`'s popup kind, which the plan fixed as `aria-haspopup="menu"`, as `settings` has, and 4b replaced with a disclosure.

##### WHAT EXECUTING THE PLAN FOUND

**Tasks 1 to 4 ran in turn**, in one worktree, by subagent-driven development. Each task's patches applied with no drift, each task's tree was the prototype's — Task 4's by patch id, since Task 3's fix came before it — and every red step, green step and sabotage matched the plan: 71 of 71 fired again. Tasks 1, 2 and 4's reviews were clean but for Minors, which went to the ledger.

**Task 3's review said "needs fixes"**, with two Importants, fixed in `f5b52bc`:

- **A pasted link's `undo` left a λ copy's editor in custody** instead of on its view, found by reading the code: the view came back offering *move the editor here*. `PaneHost.moveBack` now claims the first view moved back for a held editor. The test's setup had moved the editor off the view before the open, so it could not see this.
- **Two waits in `share-open-hashchange.test.ts` were already true when they began**, so a case could not fail for what it names. Each paste now waits on what only its own open produces. Of the fix's eight sabotages, one was inert: an open's `replaceProgram` withdraws the earlier offer before `announceOpen` reads it, so a later open keeping the earlier `undo` never took effect. A sabotage that did took its place.

**4b, the fix task** (`f353355`, `1e8d1e8`, `afa14d1`, and `c1e8b48` after its review): `share` as a disclosure, the latest-wins guard, and the spec's notes on the plan's findings 5, 8 and 9. **The guard's overlap is unreachable in Chrome, as measured**: links whose payloads inflate to 1,000 to 8,388,608 bytes were read in 0.5 to 14.6 ms while 0 `MessageChannel` tasks and 0 `setTimeout(0)` callbacks ran, in HeadlessChrome 151.0.7922.34 (spec §A.5), so a read ends before a later `hashchange` can be dispatched. The guard is a defence, not the fix of a race a Chrome user could meet, and a test holds it with a gated `DecompressionStream` stand-in. It orders reads that have begun, so a link whose `hashchange` is still queued when an earlier read ends is lost when that open clears the fragment (WHAT THIS DID NOT CLOSE). 6 of 6 and 9 of 9 sabotages fired. **4b's review found one Important**: the §5.3 note and §11's row claimed "no task" ran and named a browser version, beyond what §A.5's probe counted and printed. The probe now logs its user agent, and the note quotes exactly what it counts (`c1e8b48`).

##### THE WHOLE-BRANCH REVIEW

Of `e143c38..c1e8b48`, with the ledger's Minors to triage. **Ready to merge with fixes**: one Critical, four Importants and seven Minors.

- **C1. A link's workspace had no structural bound**, and the spec's only bound, the inflate cap, bounds bytes. A tree 6,000 splits deep made `decodeLink` throw out of the open: at start-up `main()` rejected with no views and the fragment kept, so every reload did it again. One 1,200 deep opened whole and stored its layout before the page died, and that stored layout alone then killed every later load, until site data was cleared, and with it the user's program and copies. A link holding 400 views opened and stored them, and took seconds a gesture. A leaf id such as `pane-1e300` set a leaf counter that `+ 1` cannot move.
- **I1. Four browser files had thin margin on a slow runner**: three clicked the open's `undo` after a wait that scales with the CPU, racing `NOTICE_MS`, and `share-positions.test.ts` failed 2 of 16 at a 25% CPU quota. The product offered the `undo` as the spec says; the tests spent the window on recordings their properties did not need.
- **I2. A real press on `undo` was lost when a clamp's notice offered it again**: `paint` built a new button after words of another length, and Chrome dispatched no `click` at all for a press whose button was replaced. Synthetic `.click()` tests could not see it.
- **I3. Nothing held that an edit withdraws a clamp's `undo`**: deleting `offer.notice = notice` passed the suite, and a live `undo` past an edit throws the edit away.
- **I4. No browser test opened a start-up link with positions**, the path every clicked link takes, and the comment at the hold was false at start-up.
- **The Minors**: when two legs clamped, the first clamp's notice was never seen (m1); the popover kept the replaced program's link through an open (m2); a share made while a position was pending carried the catch-up's head (m3); m4 and m5, below; the ledger's Minors (m6), triaged into those to fix and those to leave; and comment widths (m7), left.

**The fix wave**, four parts in turn, each test first and each new or changed test sabotaged, then a re-review of the whole wave:

- **A1** (`92625d9`, `97036ee`, `989fc92`; 10 of 10 sabotages): the tree bound, the leaf-id bound, and `decodeLink` total. **A1 stopped first and asked**: under the first bound of 8 and 32, `+ view` builds deeper and wider trees by itself — 9 splits deep with 11 leaves after 7 presses in a row — so the bound would have reset layouts the app makes. The user raised it to 64 and 64. A tree `+ view` builds has two splits fewer than it has leaves, so the leaf bound is the one it meets: the 61st press in a row builds a tree the bound refuses, not the 63rd the amendment said (`1d09b60`). A depth bound of 63 or more refuses the same trees; the depth bound decides where the reading of a deeper one stops. A `.catch` at the open's call sites was left out, since no input can reach it once `decodeLink` cannot reject.
- **A2** (`5a56d64`, `53cf88a`, `8d5875a`, `912601b`; 14 of 14): I2, m1, m2 and m3. **Keeping the button was not enough**: by real input over eight kinds of redraw, Chrome clicks only where the press and the release land on the same element, dispatching nothing when the pressed element is removed and clicking the common ancestor when it moves. So `paint` keeps the button for the same action, and the action sits at the line's end, on the first line where the words wrap. The several-leg clamp wordings are A2's own, sorted λ, asm, TM and grouped by reason: `the link's λ step 100 and asm step 100 are past the end of this run — showing λ step 7 and asm step 5`, and with mixed reasons, `… — showing step 15,695; its asm step 500 is past the end of this run — showing step 84`. The one-leg wordings are unchanged.
- **B** (`ebf10aa`, `62a2099`, `079d600`, `09b7227`; 34 of 34): I1, I3 and I4. The three files' links carry two-line programs, their `undo` is clicked before any wait that scales with the CPU, and the λ layout is read once its tree has arrived; `share-positions` opens `fact(4)` and `sum_to(5)` under `binary`. **B also fixed a race the brief did not name**: at 25% the step-gesture case failed on its own assertion, since the run's `result` posted a continue before the real click landed. The case now holds the `result` until the click has landed, rather than lengthening a wait.
- **C** (`c385fc9`, `821976e`, `82b6e3a`, `b901689`; 19 of 19): the triage's rows to fix, among them the codec's doc figures no gate held, now properties; a bare `#s=` held unreadable; the copies line counting two views of one copy as two; the popover's gutter cases in each preset; the stale "once" claims in `main.ts`; and one node case per step gesture, each taking its leg from the link.

**The re-review** of `c1e8b48..b901689`: **ready to merge with fixes**, no Critical and no Important. Every earlier Critical and Important was resolved, each by a test a sabotage showed can fail, and every slow-runner claim it re-ran reproduced. Its three Minors were fixed (`389ce3a`, `52164d6`; 3 of 3 sabotages): the copies line for two views of one copy now reads `both λ · copy 1 views`, where C's read `the λ · copy 1 and λ · copy 1 views`; a test's name claimed a page that does not scroll sideways; and one long doc line. Two it asked to record, below.

##### THE CHECK BY HAND

Run at `52164d6` against `pnpm exec vite --port 5199 --strictPort` from this worktree's `web/`, in Playwright's Chromium 151.0.7922.34, headless, by two scratch scripts driving real pointer and keyboard input, and a third that probed one finding. Each width and scheme had a fresh browser context, so each page opened with nothing stored: `Object.keys(localStorage)` read `[]` before the page's own scripts ran, in all four. Light and dark are `prefers-color-scheme`, with the app's appearance at its default, `system`, and each context was granted the clipboard. The scripts took 26 screenshots, not tracked.

- **The first visit**, in all four: Explorer, `sum_to(5)`, and the strip `λ 15 · 951 reductions`, `asm 15 · 84 instructions` and `TM 15 · 40,261 transitions · width 16`.
- **`share` opened by a click twelve times**, once per width, scheme and preset: the field focused with the whole of its link selected, `copy link` enabled under it, `aria-expanded` true, nothing scrolling inside the popover, and the page's `scrollWidth` equal to its width. Escape closed it, with the focus back on `share`. The popover's `[left, right]` was the same in light and dark and in every preset: `[537.4, 1049.4]` at 1280×800, from y = 37, its right edge on `share`'s; and `[16, 374]` at 390×844, a `1rem` gutter each side. Both are the prototype's figures.
- **Copying.** `copy link` by pointer said `link copied`, and the clipboard held the link. By keys, Enter on `share` opened it with the field focused and selected, Tab reached `copy link`, and Enter copied. Ctrl+C in the selected field copied it too.
- **The copies line**, with a copy made on the λ view from its `⋯` menu: `copies are not included — the λ · copy 1 view will open on the program`, named by the field's `aria-describedby`, at 1280 light, the popover still `[537.4, 1049.4]`, and at 390 dark, still `[16, 374]`. With a second view of that copy added by `+ view`: `copies are not included — both λ · copy 1 views will open on the program`. With the copy, the 390 page's header took a fourth row, 181 px against 136, in Instrument's Explorer, the style a fresh context opens on (WHAT THIS DID NOT CLOSE).
- **The line past 2,000 characters**, on a program of 400 comment lines: a 2,967-character link, and `this link is 2,967 characters long — some chat and mail apps cut links past 2,000`, named by `aria-describedby`, at 1280 light and at 390 dark, `[16, 374]` there with the page not widened.
- **A link pasted into the address bar of an open page**, at 1280 and at 390: a link to `let y = 10; y + 5` in Debugger, made by `share` in another context. The page took its program and its workspace; neither the address bar nor `location.hash` kept the fragment; and the notice said `opened a shared link`, with `undo` at the line's end. At 1280 the words end at x = 147 and `undo` runs from 1,217 to 1,264, 1,070 px apart; at 390 it runs from 327 to 374. A real click on `undo` put back `sum_to(5)` and Explorer, said `put back the program and the workspace`, and left the focus in the source editor. At 1280 the page held two views of λ copy 1 when the link was pasted.
- **The same link opened in a new tab**, at 1280 and at 390: the link's program in Debugger over the stored one, the fragment gone, and `opened a shared link` with `undo`, in the same places.
- **`fact(4)` at λ step 3,000.** Picked from `examples ▾` and shared, its link carried λ 1,386, asm 69 and TM 79,047. With λ moved to 3,000 through the app's own `encodeLink`, it was opened in a new tab at 1280, in Explorer. λ's step line went from `step 256 of 256… — going to step 3,000 from the link`, through `step 1,386 of 1,386 — going to step 3,000 from the link (oldest kept: step 1)` and `step 2,768 of 2,768 — going to step 3,000 from the link (oldest kept: step 1,388)`, to `step 3,000 of 3,024…`, 1,457 ms after the tab opened. `share` there carried λ 3,000, asm 69 and TM 79,047, and that link, opened in another tab, reached step 3,000 the same way, in 1,466 ms.
- **The console** logged no error on the eight pages whose console the scripts read. The first script's four first pages are not among them: it stopped on its own mistake before it read theirs, reading the λ step line inside a view when its workspace drew the line in the step bar.

**One finding, outside this lane: at 390 px in Debugger the step bar widens the page whenever its line is long.** The page a link was pasted into read `scrollWidth` 405 while its bar said `step 951 of 951 — recompiling`. The probe found the same 405 for that line with no link, and 486 with `fact(4)` picked from `examples ▾` and no link, its bar saying `step 1,386 of 1,386 — history is full (oldest kept: step 1)` with `keep recording` running to x = 486. The branch changes neither `step-bar.ts`, `step-controls.ts` nor the bar's styles, and a link's pending line is one more long line of the same kind. It is the sideways scroll the plan recorded at 320 px, at a phone's width, and it goes to the controller, not into this branch.

##### WHAT THIS DID NOT CLOSE

- **Not open, though the plan listed them: `aria-haspopup="menu"` on `share`**, which 4b made a disclosure, **and two `hashchange`s whose reads overlap**, which in Chrome cannot happen (4b's measurement, above); the guard is a defence for another engine.
- **`aria-haspopup="menu"` on `settings`**, whose popover is not a menu either (the user's 4b decision).
- **A queued `hashchange` is lost when an earlier read clears the fragment** (4b's concern): the guard orders reads that have begun. Unreachable in Chrome, where a read never spans a task; dropping an open whose fragment is no longer `location.hash` when its read ends would close it.
- **The first review's Minors left as they are**: `Uint8Array.from` walking a long fragment through the iterator protocol, speed only; `reader.cancel()` not awaited; the base64url helpers repeated in a test, which must not import what it tests; the long-link line joining `aria-describedby` after the field has the focus, so a screen reader may not speak it; the refused copy's words when the popover closed while the write was pending; an encode that rejects leaving `copy link` disabled until the popover's next open; the popover's 600 and 700 px gutter figures, which no test holds; a used `undo` whose program equals the link's leaves the offer set, which nothing can then offer again; `showWorkspace`'s two layout passes; the open's `undo` mounting a λ editor that was in custody on the first view moved back, as `moveBack`'s contract allows; a user's continue on another leg during the link's continues, which can count a continue that never ran; the `lambda-tree` exception in `share-positions.ts`, which guards nothing reachable; the pending step line's `(oldest kept: step 1)` after `from the link`; 4b's `share-open-latest` case, which cannot tell the second open's offer from the first's; `1e8d1e8`'s subject, which reads as a fix a Chrome user could see; run noise; the spec's §5.2 note naming `CompressionStream` as the asynchronous step, unprobed; and comment lines past 120 characters, which `biome ci` passes.
- **The 61st `+ view` press in a row builds a layout the next load resets**, and a link to such a layout opens its program alone, with no warning to the sharer. **From the 5th press the newest view is 0 px wide.** Both are `+ view`'s, outside this lane.
- **The page scrolls sideways at 320 px in Debugger and Stage**, 36 px with every menu shut: the step bar is 356 px wide. **And at 390 px in Debugger whenever the bar's line is long** (THE CHECK BY HAND): 15 px for `— recompiling`, and 96 px for `fact(4)`'s `history is full` with `keep recording`, both with no link; a link's pending line is one more such line. Outside this lane, since the branch changes nothing in the bar; `header-menus-narrow`'s share cases hold that the popover does not widen the page further.
- **The header's fourth row at 390 px with a copy**, in Instrument's Explorer and Debugger and in Paper's Debugger, which predates `share`; THE CHECK BY HAND saw it in Instrument's Explorer.
- **A share made during the link's own compile carries every step the link carried**, including one for a leg that compile will decline, until its `compiled` reply drops it. That is A2's reading of the user's "for the program on screen", the program whose compile the session's generation names now, which the controller accepted.
- **The several-leg clamp wordings are A2's**, and the spec does not word them. **The combined notice is said once per redraw**: on a three-leg clamp the live region was set three times in 31 ms, each sentence naming λ, so a screen reader that queues polite updates hears λ's clause three times; the last sentence is complete.
- **`share-positions`' `fact(12)` cases have the thinnest margin**: in B's runs at 25%, *continue 3* took up to 9.3 s as a whole case, its wait and two real clicks to add a view, against a 10 s `until` on the wait alone; in this entry's run it took 7,307 ms, and the slowest `fact(12)` case 8,105 ms. `fact(12)`'s continues are λ only, about 1,400 frames each, so heavy by design.
- **Every notice's action sits at the line's end**, a copy's delete, a palette's removal and a pick's as well as a link's: at 1280 px the `undo` after `opened a shared link` stands 1,070 px from the words (THE CHECK BY HAND).
- **m4: on a slow device the start-up open's `undo` can go before the page settles**, since `NOTICE_MS` runs from the end of `main()`; a later clamp offers it again, as the spec says.
- **m5: for about 300 ms after a link opens, a reload loses its program but keeps its workspace**: the layout and the emptied bindings are written during the open, the program only when its compile posts, with the fragment already cleared.
- **The Rust gates and `check-slow.sh` were not run.** The branch touches no Rust and no wasm, so `check-all`'s Rust legs, `check-slow.sh` and the llvm-cov floor would test the tree `main` already passed. The image, which no PR job builds, was built and run (VERIFICATION).
- **Next: binary as the default encoding**, for a first visit and a pick (`EXAMPLE_ENCODING` in `examples.ts`), the user's request of 2026-10-01, as its own PR.

##### VERIFICATION

Run on 2026-10-01 at `52164d6`, the last commit to touch code, from `web/`, after `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`, which found it up to date. `pkg/` and `pkg-lsp/` were built when the worktree was set up and not rebuilt: the branch changes no crate, no grammar, no `Cargo.toml` or `Cargo.lock`, and neither `web/package.json` nor `web/pnpm-lock.yaml`. The coverage gate ran under `flock <the lane's browser lock> systemd-run --user --wait --collect --pipe -p MemoryMax=16G -p MemorySwapMax=0`, with `PATH`, `HOME`, `CARGO_HOME` and `RUSTUP_HOME` passed through, at the default workers; it was not OOM-killed, so no second run with `VITEST_MAX_WORKERS=4` was needed. The seven scans ran again with this entry staged, before it was committed.

```
pnpm exec biome ci --error-on-warnings  → exit 0, 335 files (1 info)
pnpm run typecheck                      → exit 0
pnpm run test:coverage                  → exit 0, 216 files / 2,053 tests (node 64 / 1,019, browser 152 / 1,034); 97.41 / 91.35 / 98.29 / 98.77 against 95 / 89 / 97 / 97; 45.00 s; peak 9.7G, no swap
pnpm run build:app                      → exit 0
scripts/check-{text-bytes,citations,attributions,doc-figures,shared-docs,lua,colours}.sh, --self-test then alone, from the root → 14 of 14 exit 0, at 52164d6 and with this entry staged
docker build --network=host, docker run --network host → exit 0; health healthy; GET / 200, its four assets 200; removed
```

**The image was built and run on the host's network, not as the plan says.** This machine's running kernel, 7.2.6-arch2-1, has no module tree, since its package has moved to 7.2.7-arch1-1, so `veth` cannot load: `docker build` failed at its first uncached `RUN`, `pnpm run build:app`, and `docker run -d -p 8099:80` failed before starting, each with Docker's bridge unable to add its `veth` pair ("operation not supported"). `--network=host` changes only the network the build's `RUN` steps and the container use; nginx then answered on the host's port 80. A reboot into the installed kernel would let the plan's two commands run as written.

**The slow runner.** Each browser test file the branch adds or changes, the 18 that `git diff --name-only e143c38..52164d6 -- web/tests/browser` lists less `harness.ts`, ran alone under the lane's browser lock at a 25% CPU quota, and the ten `share-open*` files again at 10%, as `flock <the lane's browser lock> systemd-run --user --wait --collect --pipe -p CPUQuota=<Q>% --setenv=PATH="$PATH" --working-directory="$PWD" pnpm exec vitest run --project browser --reporter=verbose tests/browser/<file>`. **25% and 10% of one core are both harsher than either CI runner**: the whole-branch review measured 10% slowing this branch's waits 17.7 to 22.3 times, where runner `450440e2`, the slower, is two to six times slower than this machine. The slowest case is each file's slowest under the verbose reporter; `beforeAll` is not a case.

#### THE STEP BAR WRAPS INSTEAD OF WIDENING THE PAGE: ITS TITLE AND EVERY CONTROL ARE ONE LINE THAT WRAPS, SO AT 320 AND 390 PX IN DEBUGGER AND STAGE THE PAGE KEEPS ITS WIDTH, THE STEP TEXT IS NO LONGER A COLUMN A FEW CHARACTERS WIDE AND `keep recording` CAN BE CLICKED, WHILE AT 1280 PX EVERY BOX STAYS WHERE IT WAS (2026-10-01, branch `step-bar-wraps`, `d79a8d4..8a2e51b`, 7 commits, two of them this entry's earlier versions, `84e213c` and `bdbbd3e`, plus this revision)

**A fix, in `web/` only, to a layout bug on `main`.** #121's entry left it open under WHAT THIS DID NOT CLOSE: the page scrolled sideways at 320 px in Debugger and Stage, and at 390 px in Debugger whenever the step bar's line was long. The layout is the one the user chose on 2026-10-01, "title joins the transport". There is no spec or plan file; this entry is the design. Five commits of code and tests: `9555807` the stylesheet and its test, `8ac7a69` a sibling test that allowed the old overflow, `f62e5dd` the new test's waits, and `115648b` and `8a2e51b` the new test's comments, after the whole-branch review and its re-review (REVISED, below). `84e213c` and `bdbbd3e` are this entry's earlier versions.

##### THE BUG

The one step bar (`step-bar.ts`, the `steps` switch at `bar`, which Debugger and Stage set) was `.step-bar-inner`, a flex row that never wrapped, holding the title `λ · program` and `.controls` (`step-controls.ts`: `↺ ◀ ▶ ⏵`, the speed select, the step text and the continue button), itself a flex row that never wrapped. A row like that is no narrower than its items' narrowest widths added together, so on a phone it widened the page, or kept the width by shrinking the one item that could shrink, the step text, to its longest word.

Measured on `d79a8d4`'s stylesheet in the browser tier (Vitest's Chromium, the default style, Instrument), each example picked from `examples ▾`, the same in Debugger and Stage:

| Page | Line on the bar | `scrollWidth` | Bar | Step text |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 320 px | `sum_to(5)`'s `step 951 of 951` | 356 | 81 px | 28 px wide, 4 lines |
| 390 px | the same | 390 | 81 px | 32.34 px wide, 4 lines |
| 320 and 390 px | `fact(4)`'s `step 1,386 of 1,386 — history is full (oldest kept: step 1)`, with `keep recording` | 486 | 171 px | 49 px wide, 9 lines; `keep recording` ends at x = 486.19 |

In every one of them the title is on 2 lines too. The lane's brief quoted 358, 489, and step columns 29 and 51 px wide, from a live page. #121's entry and the browser tier give 356 and 486, and this entry quotes the browser tier's.

##### THE FIX

Three rules in `style.css`'s `THE ONE STEP BAR` block, nothing else:

- **`.step-bar-inner` wraps:** `flex-wrap: wrap`, `row-gap: var(--space-1)` and `column-gap: var(--space-2)`, in place of `gap: var(--space-3)`.
- **`.step-bar .controls` is `display: contents`,** in place of `margin-top: 0`. Its buttons, its select, its step text and its continue button become items of `.step-bar-inner`'s row beside the title, so the title and every control flow as one line that wraps, and the title costs the bar no row of its own. An element with no box has no margin, so `.controls`' top margin needs no override there.
- **`.step-bar-title` gains `margin-inline-end: calc(var(--space-3) - var(--space-2))`.** The row's gap is now the controls' own, `var(--space-2)`, and the title's gap before `↺` was `var(--space-3)`; the margin keeps it.

**`display: contents` is safe on `.controls` because the element carries no role and no ARIA attribute.** `stepControls` in `step-controls.ts` creates it as a `div` and sets its class and nothing else. Some browsers drop a `display: contents` element's role from the accessibility tree, and the rule's comment says so, for whoever adds one. **The prototype's `min-width: 0` on `.step-bar-inner` is not in the fix:** every case passes without it.

Measured the same way on `f62e5dd`, the same in Debugger and Stage:

| Page | Line | `scrollWidth` | Bar | Rows |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 320 px | `sum_to(5)` | 320 | 62.38 px | 2: the title and `↺ ◀ ▶ ⏵`; the speed and the step text |
| 390 px | `sum_to(5)` | 390 | 60 px | 2: the title, the transport and the speed; the step text |
| 320 px | `fact(4)` | 320 | 135.38 px | 4: the title and the transport; the speed; the step text, 288 px wide on 2 lines; `keep recording` |
| 390 px | `fact(4)` | 390 | 111 px | 3: the title, the transport and the speed; the step text, 358 px wide on 2 lines; `keep recording` |

**At 1280 px nothing moved.** In both presets and under both lines, each of the 30 boxes the bar draws (7 for `sum_to(5)`'s line and 8 for `fact(4)`'s, in each preset) has the same left, right, top and height as on `d79a8d4`, with a largest difference of 0 px, and the bar is 38 px tall on both.

**Two lines no example reaches, set by hand on the bar's step text in Debugger.** `step 951 of 951 — recompiling`, which #121's entry measured widening a 390 px page to 405, with no continue button: 405 on `d79a8d4` at 320 and at 390 px; 320 and 390 on `f62e5dd`. A link's pending line, `step 1,386 of 1,386 — going to step 3,000 from the link (oldest kept: step 1)`, with `keep recording`: 486 on `d79a8d4` at both widths, the bar 243 px tall and the step text on 13 lines; 320 and 390 on `f62e5dd`.

##### WHAT ELSE READS THE BAR

- **Every `.ts` line in `web/src` and `web/tests` naming `step-bar`, `stepBar` or `StepBar`**, comments aside: `main.ts`, `step-bar.ts` and `draw.ts` build, show and redraw it. In the tests, `workspace-boot`, `share-open` and `share-open-hashchange` read `#step-bar`'s `hidden`, `workspace-restore` its speed select's value, `harness.ts` and the node tier's `harness.test.ts` its id, the node tier's `step-bar.test.ts` its pure `barTarget`, and the browser `step-bar.test.ts` reaches the title, the step text and the buttons by descendant selectors and presses them with `.click()`. None reads a box, and a descendant selector matches through `display: contents`.
- **Every query of a `.controls` without a `[data-leaf]` or `.view-steps` in its selector**: 13 lines, each run inside a view's pane, through a `pane()`, `host()` or `asmHost()` helper or a `pane` argument that is a `[data-leaf]` element, or with `.pane` in the selector. None reaches the bar's.
- **Every browser test file that reads geometry** (`getBoundingClientRect`, `getClientRects`, `offset*`, `elementFromPoint`, `scrollWidth`, `clientWidth` or `checkVisibility`, anywhere in the file): 32. Two of them name the bar, and the same two read the page's width: the new file, and `header-menus-narrow.test.ts` (the last bullet). Three more put Debugger or Stage, or the stage switch, on the page: `copy-header` measures view headers and views, `link-hold` grid rows inside a pane, and `share-popover` header buttons. None of the three measures the bar or the page's width. The first version of this bullet came from a grep that needed the geometry call and a word naming the bar on one line, so a read on another line than its target's name was invisible to it; the whole-branch review checked `tm-pane-editor`, `share-popover`, `link-hold`, `copy-header` and `header-menus-narrow` by hand and found the same.
- **`focus-handoff.ts`'s `usable`**, through which the bar's continue button hands the focus on, reads `isConnected`, `:disabled`, a `[hidden]` ancestor and the tab order, and no box.
- **One test read the width the bar gave the page.** `header-menus-narrow.test.ts`'s share cases let the page scroll sideways by as much as it did with every menu shut, and called the 36 px at 320 px in Debugger and Stage open. `8ac7a69` removes that allowance and its parameter, so those cases hold the page's own width as the examples and workspace cases do; on `d79a8d4`'s stylesheet its two 320 px cases in Debugger and Stage fail on it, `expected 356 to be less than or equal to 320`.

##### THE TESTS

- **`step-bar-narrow.test.ts` (new, 12 cases), one mount.** For each of `sum_to(5)`'s line and `fact(4)`'s, picked from `examples ▾`, it waits for the line on the bar and then for the run's result, in two waits. Each case first asserts what it means to measure: the page's width, the preset on the workspace button, the bar on the page and naming `λ · program`, the line (the short one's pattern and no continue button, or `history is full` and `keep recording` drawn), the page not scrolled sideways, and the bar in view after a vertical scroll only. Then:
  - **at 320 and 390 px, in Debugger and Stage (8 cases):** the page's `scrollWidth` is no more than its width; every box the bar draws (the title, each button, the select, the step text) lies between 0 and the page's width; in `fact(4)`'s cases `elementFromPoint` at `keep recording`'s centre is the button; a step text on more than one line is as wide as the bar's content box, to 0.5 px; and `↺`'s vertical centre is the title's, to 1 px.
  - **at 1280 px, in Debugger and Stage (4 cases):** every box on the title's vertical centre, to 1 px; the title at the bar's content edge; `↺` `var(--space-3)` after the title and each later box `var(--space-2)` after the one before, to 0.5 px, the two gaps of `d79a8d4`'s rules. **That is all they hold, not where each box is**: the 0 px comparison above is the probe's, measured once.
- **Red on `d79a8d4`'s stylesheet: 8 failed, 4 passed** (the 1280 px cases): `the page’s scroll width: expected 356 to be less than or equal to 320` (`sum_to(5)`, 320 px), `expected 486 to be less than or equal to 320` and `... 390` (`fact(4)`), and `a wrapped step text’s width: expected 32.34375 to be greater than or equal to 357.5` (`sum_to(5)`, 390 px). None failed on a precondition.
- **Eight sabotages, replayed at `f62e5dd`, each run over the whole file, restored from a saved copy and checked with `cmp`. All fired:**

| the wrap kept, `display: contents` replaced by `flex-wrap: wrap; margin-top: 0` (both containers wrap) | the 8 phone cases, each on `↺ on the title’s row: expected 28.25 to be less than 1`; every assertion before it passed |
| everything kept but the title's margin | the 4 desktop cases, `the gap before back to the oldest kept step: 8px, not 16px` |

Each keeps the row, the title at the bar's content edge and the two gaps, which is all those cases hold. The 1280 px case's comment claimed each box where the old bar put it until `115648b`, which says this.

  **Which property holds the user's layout.** The plain wrap on both containers keeps the page's width, every box inside it, `keep recording` clickable and the step text unsqueezed: only `↺ on the title’s row` tells it from the chosen layout, where the title costs no row of its own.
- **Margin on a slow runner.** Each changed browser file passed alone under a 25% CPU quota at `f62e5dd`: `step-bar-narrow` 12 of 12, `header-menus-narrow` 29 of 29. The new file's longest wait is `fact(4)`'s result after its line: over three runs at that quota its line took 2,495 to 2,687 ms from before the pick's two clicks and its result 6,204 to 7,900 ms more, each against `until`'s 10,000 ms; unconstrained, 772 and 1,494 ms. **One wait for both, as `9555807` had it, fit inside its 10 s at that quota in one run and not in two.** In `timing-25%.log` it took 9.5 s. In `timing2-25%.log` `fact(4)`'s hook failed with `timed out after 10000ms waiting for idle`. In `timing3-25%.log`, a run that timed the two separately, the clicks took 301 ms, the line came 3.1 s after them and the result 10.2 s after them, past one wait's 10 s. `f62e5dd` split the wait in two. Its commit message gives 3.4 s and 10.5 s, timed from before the clicks; the test's comment said the same until `115648b`.

##### CHECKED BY HAND

The bar was screenshotted in Debugger at 320, 390 and 1280 px, under both lines, light and dark, on `d79a8d4`'s stylesheet and on `f62e5dd`'s: 24 images (scratch, not tracked). On `f62e5dd` the rows are the ones the table above lists, in both appearances. No step text breaks inside a number: at 320 px `fact(4)`'s line breaks as `step 1,386 of 1,386 — history is full` / `(oldest kept: step 1)`, and at 390 px as `... (oldest kept:` / `step 1)`. On `d79a8d4` the bar is cut off at the page's edge at 390 px under `fact(4)`, the title stands on 2 lines and the step text in a column one or two words wide. `sum_to(5)`'s 1280 px images show glyph fragments along the bar's top edge, on both stylesheets alike; they were not traced.

##### WHAT THIS DID NOT CLOSE

- **Explorer's per-view strip.** Explorer draws no bar; each view carries its own strip (`.view-steps .controls`) in a pane that scrolls sideways. At 390 px under `fact(4)` the λ view's pane is 189 px wide from x = 201, and its strip runs to x = 599.19, where `keep recording` ends, so the button sits outside the pane until the pane is scrolled; the pane's scroll width is 398. The same on `d79a8d4` and `f62e5dd`; the brief's 603 was the live page's. Out of this lane's scope, which left `.view-steps` alone.
- **Held and measured in Instrument only**, the default style. Paper and Terminal were not measured.
- **The `— recompiling` and link lines are held by no test.** They were measured once, by hand, above; the test holds `sum_to(5)`'s and `fact(4)`'s.
- **The new file picks its examples under `unary`**, which a pick sets on `main`. Binary as the default encoding, the other lane of 2026-10-01, makes a pick set `binary`; its brief predicts `fact(4)`'s λ leg still fills its history there. If it does not, this file fails on its precondition, `the long line`, not on a measurement.
- **The new file's wait for `fact(4)`'s result** took up to 7,900 ms against `until`'s 10,000 ms at a 25% CPU quota. At 50%, in one run at `115648b`, its line took 1,398 ms from before the pick's clicks and its result 2,825 ms more; `sum_to(5)`'s 1,393 and 1,422 ms (`timing-probe.py 50% 1`, scratch, under the lock and cap).
- **The 1280 px cases hold one row and the old bar's two gaps, not each box's position** (THE TESTS): the review's three sabotages there, a padding or a larger font on the title and a wider padding on the bar, pass them. The positions against `d79a8d4` were measured once, by the probe.

#### BINARY IS THE DEFAULT ENCODING: A FIRST VISIT, EVERY EXAMPLE PICK AND A REFUSED STORED PROGRAM OPEN UNDER `binary`, AND THE MANIFEST IS DECLARED UNDER IT — THE CLOSURE'S TM LEG NOW ENDS, AND `fact(12)`'S FILLS ITS HISTORY WHERE `unary` DECLINED IT; EIGHT TEST FILES BEYOND THE FOUR THAT HELD THE OLD DEFAULT LEANED ON IT BY USING `binary` AS THE ENCODING THAT IS NOT THE DEFAULT, ONE FAILING AND SEVEN STILL GREEN WITH AN ASSERTION THAT COULD NO LONGER FAIL A PATH THAT TOOK THE DEFAULT; THE WHOLE-BRANCH REVIEW FOUND THE FIRST SUCH FIX BLIND TO THE OTHER WRONG FALLBACK, THE PICKER'S FIRST OPTION, AND ITS RE-REVIEW FOUND ANOTHER SUCH FILE, SO EVERY `binary` IN `web/tests` WAS SWEPT: TWO PATHS HELD UNDER `binary` ALONE GOT A `unary` HALF, AND IN THE PAIRS FOR A START-UP'S THREE PATHS EACH FILE NAMES THE OTHER (2026-10-01, branch `binary-default-encoding`, `97e65ae..5e2d4d6`, 11 commits, three of them this entry's earlier versions, `17a264b`, `6864966` and `85ea174`, plus this revision)

**A change of default in `web/` only, the user's decision of 2026-10-01**, which #121's entry named as next. `EXAMPLE_ENCODING` in `web/src/examples.ts` becomes `'binary'`. It is the one constant behind three defaults: the program a first visit opens on, the program a refused stored one is replaced by, and every pick from `examples ▾`. A stored program keeps its own encoding, and a share link carries its own. The picker still lists `unary, binary` in that order, because it lists what `encodings()` returns in the order Rust declares the encodings; only its selection defaults to `binary`.

##### WHAT EACH EXAMPLE DOES UNDER `binary`

The manifest's outcomes are the default encoding's (6a spec, row 12), so they are declared again. The 6a spec's §2.7 measured both encodings on 2026-09-29, and its `binary` column said two rows would change. Its new §A.6 probe, run on this branch, gives §2.7's steps, stops and values again under both encodings, every one equal, and `examples.test.ts` holds the outcomes:

| Example | λ | asm | TM under `binary` | Value |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `let x = 40; x + 2` | 7, ended | 5, ended | 405, ended | 42 |
| a closure | 9, ended | 30, ended | **13,294, ended** (under `unary`, 73,958 of 79,307, history full) | 42 |
| `is_even(6)` | 654, ended | 79, ended | 14,964, ended | true |
| `fact(4)` | 1,386, history full | 69, ended | 30,846, ended | 24 |
| `map` and `fold` | 555, ended | 260, ended | 69,008 of 91,785, history full | 9 |
| `sum_to(5)` | 951, ended | 84, ended | 12,976, ended | 15 |
| `fact(12)` | 1,406, history full | 181, ended | **75,850 of 481,964, history full** (under `unary`, declined) | 479001600 |

A figure is the last step a leg's first recording posted, and "of N" the run's length where the history filled first. λ and asm are the same under both encodings. Two descriptions change, to the words the user chose: the closure's is `a function that captures n; every leg ends at 42`, and `fact(12)`'s is `a value too wide for unary: λ and the TM fill their histories, asm ends`. `fact(12)`'s slot and title stay.

**The margins, by the bytes each first recording spent.** §A.6 also sums each frame with the sizer the worker charges it with — `protocol.ts`'s `lambdaFrameBytes`, `tmFrameBytes` and `asmFrameBytes` — against `HISTORY_BYTES`, 33,554,432. Under `binary`, of the legs that end, `sum_to(5)`'s λ spends the most, 22,004,386 bytes (65.6%), and `is_even(6)`'s λ the next most (49.5%). Of the legs whose history fills, `map` and `fold`'s TM records 69,008 of its 91,785 steps (75.2%). `examples.test.ts`'s doc quoted the closure's `unary` TM alone, 73,958 of 79,307; it gives `sum_to(5)`'s λ and `map` and `fold`'s TM now, each with its measure, and no `unary` figure, since the test makes no `unary` run. **Under `unary`, `fact(4)`'s TM ends at step 79,047 having spent 31,720,374 bytes, 94.5% of its history**: a margin as narrow as the closure's, which neither that doc nor the spec had named.

##### THE TESTS

- **The four files that held `unary` as the default now hold `binary`**: `examples.test.ts`, through the manifest; `first-load.test.ts`, the picker and the stored program on a first visit; `program-restore-invalid.test.ts`, a refused stored program; and `examples-menu.test.ts`, a pick. The menu file chose `binary` before its pick so the pick had an encoding to replace. The page opens under `unary`, the encoding `setup.ts` stores its program under, which now is one, so that step became a precondition, and the undo is held at `unary`. Its case that chooses an encoding to withdraw the undo chose `binary`, which after a pick is no change; it chooses `unary`.
- **Eight more files leaned on the old default**, each by using `binary` as the encoding that is not the default. One failed: `program-quota-return.test.ts` opens on the first-load example, then changes the encoding to `binary` and back. Under the new default that is no change, and `d79a8d4`'s copy of the file fails against this branch's app on "counts a change of encoding alone" (`expected '' to be 'the program is not being saved — this…'`). It changes to `unary` and back now, after a precondition. Seven stayed green, each with an assertion expecting `binary` that could no longer fail a path that took the default in place of the right encoding: `share-open-alone.test.ts`, `examples-undo-format.test.ts`, `program-restore.test.ts`, `share-open.test.ts`, `share-open-deep.test.ts`, `share-open-hashchange.test.ts` and `share-open-latest.test.ts`. This branch's first version found the first of the seven, the re-review the second and third, and the sweep the last four.
- **`share-open-alone.test.ts`, and the whole-branch review.** The file stored its program under `binary`, "not the default, so it is told apart from one"; `d79a8d4`'s copy of it passes sabotage 3 below, which 6a-ii's plan wrote for this file. It stores `unary` now. The review found that fix blind the other way. With two encodings, one stored value differs from one wrong fallback and equals the other: `binary` differs from the picker's first option and is the default, and `unary` differs from the default and is the picker's first option, which is what `picker.value` reads at that point of start-up, before the page's program has set it. `share-open-alone-binary.test.ts` is new: the same open with `binary` stored, in one case. A second file, because a file mounts the app once. Sabotages 3 and 4 show each file failing the fallback the other cannot.
- **`examples-undo-format.test.ts`, and the re-review.** It chose `binary` before its pick, as the menu file had, so under the new default the pick changed nothing and both its `expect(picker().value).toBe('binary')` after an undo could not fail. It is in a file this branch had not touched. It starts from the page's `unary` now, as a precondition, and expects `unary` after both undos, its second case choosing `unary` itself first so that it stands on its own; `6864966`'s copy of it passes sabotage 5, and it fails it.
- **So the class was swept: every `binary` in `web/tests`**, 99 lines in 28 files at `7909994`, where the sweep was made, each read and given one of three verdicts: an explicit encoding where the default does not matter; an encoding used as "not the default", whose assertion can no longer fail a fallback to the default; or one half of a pair whose other half is held elsewhere. With two encodings, an assertion's expected value always equals one wrong source, since the default is `binary` and the picker's first option is `unary`. So a path that yields an encoding needs two assertions to be held against both, one expecting each. Seven of the ten paths below have both, and three have one:

##### THE DOCS

- **`examples.ts`.** The module doc turns around: the outcomes are `binary`'s, and under `unary` two descriptions would say something else, `fact(12)`'s TM being declined there and the closure's filling its history. `EXAMPLE_ENCODING`'s doc says it is not the picker's first.
- **`examples.test.ts`.** The margins paragraph, as above, each figure with its measure and none ranked.
- **`main.ts`, above `openExample`.** The editor's own undo leaves the encoding at `EXAMPLE_ENCODING`, named there by the constant and not by its value; `d79a8d4`'s doc named `unary`.
- **`setup.ts`.** Its doc said the browser tier's program is stored "under the default encoding". It says now that `unary` is deliberate, the encoding the tier's files were written and measured against, and not the default since 2026-10-01. The stored value is unchanged.
- **The 6a spec.** Notes dated 2026-10-01 in §3 (rows 11 and 12), §4.1, §4.4, §4.5 and §4.6, saying what is now true with the figures, and one under §9's out-of-scope line "Declared outcomes under `binary`"; nothing above them is rewritten. §A.6 holds the probe's source. §11's row says it ran at `0fed5f9` and was re-run at later commits of the branch, each run printing the same 14 rows: at `ac35350`, `4b8ddf8`, `7909994` and `5e2d4d6`, each compared with `diff`.

##### WHAT THIS DID NOT CLOSE

- **The picker still lists `unary` first.** Its order is Rust's, through `encodings()`; only the selection defaults to `binary`.
- **A returning visitor's stored program keeps `unary`.** A stored program keeps its own encoding, and nothing migrates it.
- **The files that keep `setup.ts`'s program still start under `unary`**, where they did. Ten files start with no stored program the app takes, and open on the first-load example under `binary` now: `first-load`, `program-blocked`, `program-quota` and `program-quota-return` remove it; `program-restore-invalid` stores one under `ternary`; `storage-blocked`'s reads of storage throw; and `asm-copy-restore`, `divider-drag`, `pane-floor` and `tm-buffer-restore` clear storage before they mount. Four more overwrite it with a program of their own: `program-restore`, `share-open-alone`, `share-open-alone-binary` and `share-open-deep`. This branch changes three of the ten. The other seven, those last four with `program-blocked`, `program-quota` and `storage-blocked`, changed where they start with the default, with no line of theirs changed: `tm-buffer-restore` types `let x = 40; x + 2` and detaches its 405-step `binary` TM now, not the 2,870-step `unary` one. Nine of the ten run in the suite and pass; `pane-floor` is a probe outside the default set, and was not run.
- **A pair is held by its two docs and its preconditions, not by a gate.** A change of the default, or of the picker's order, fails the preconditions. Deleting one half of a pair fails nothing.
- **Three paths are held under one encoding.** A pick sets the default, so only `binary` can be expected of it. The undo of a pick, and a pasted link's program alone, are held under `unary` only, which cannot fail a path that took the picker's first option.
- **No browser test pastes a link whose encoding the build lacks.** That open takes the page's encoding (`opened.encoding ?? picker.value`); `ternary` is in a link only in the two start-up `share-open-alone` files and in `tests/node/share-link.test.ts`. The sweep found it, and it is as it was on `main`.
- **The readout does not say that a TM leg's history filled.** `fact(12)`'s line in the menu now says the TM fills its history. Picked under the default, the readout's TM segment reads `TM 479001600 · 481,964 transitions · width 32`, the whole run's total and its value, and `map` and `fold`'s reads `TM 9 · 91,785 transitions · width 4`; neither names a full history. The λ segment does say when its recording stopped: `λ not finished · 1,406 reductions · recording stopped before the run did — the term is not finished reducing`. The whole-branch review's probe found it, and this branch changes nothing in `readout.ts`. It is a follow-up of its own.
- **The examples test runs `binary` alone.** A `unary` leg that flips fails nothing here: `fact(4)`'s TM at 94.5% of its history, or the closure's at 73,958 of 79,307.
- **`fact(12)`'s TM leg now records under the default**, where `unary` declined it. At `CPUQuota=25%`, one sample each, the seven examples' runs took 613 to 6,303 ms, `fact(12)`'s 6,303 ms, against `examples.test.ts`'s `RUN_MS` of 20,000 ms. Nothing here measured CI's slower runner.
- **The 6a-i and 6a-ii plans and their roadmap entries describe `unary` as the default**, as it was when they ran. They are records, and are left.

#### TWO EDITS LOST AROUND A `format` IN FLIGHT IN A COPY: A BUILD REPLY RE-SEEDED THE EDITOR OVER THE EDIT THE FORMAT HAD TAKEN OFF THE DEBOUNCE, AND A DEBOUNCE THAT SENT DURING A FORMAT LEFT THE OLDER TEXT FOR A DELETE'S OR A PAUSE'S `flush()` TO SEND AFTER IT — THE FIRST FOUND AS A TEST RED ON `main`'S PUSH RUN 512 ON THE SLOWER RUNNER AND AS OLD AS #110'S GUARD, THE SECOND FOUND BY THE WHOLE-BRANCH REVIEW; THE RUN'S OTHER RED TEST REACHED FOR *EDIT A COPY* WHILE ITS λ VIEW HELD NO FRAME, AS ONE SIBLING DID (2026-10-02, branch `copy-reseed-during-format`, `4a9f7f8..deaea03`, 7 commits, one of them this entry's first version, `42d8bbf`, plus this revision)

**Two product fixes and two test fixes, in `web/` only.** `main`'s push run 512 for #123 (`97e65ae`) failed its `web` job on runner `450440e2` with two tests, in files neither #123 nor #124 changes. `lsp-copy-diagnostics.test.ts`'s `reformats a copy without losing an edit made inside the debounce window` read `'tapes 1\nstart s\n\nstate s: accept\n'` where a `state t` block had been typed, and `storage-blocked.test.ts`'s `still says that copies are not being saved, beside the program` threw `no edit-a-copy control in the λ view’s menu`. The same tree, `4d531c6`, had passed that job on that runner in #123's own run 510, 2,065 of 2,065. `docker` was skipped on run 512, so no image was built from `97e65ae`; run 515, for `4a9f7f8`, was green, with `docker` among the jobs that passed and `rust-scoped` skipped.

##### WHAT WAS WRONG

- **A copy's build reply re-seeded its editor while a format held the pending edit.** `ScratchEditor.setText` is how a build's reply re-seeds a copy's editor, and since #110 it does nothing while the debounce timer is set, because the editor is then newer than any reply. `format()` clears that timer at its start and owes the edit it took to `onEdit` until the server answers. For that round trip no timer is running and no build has carried the edit, so the reply to the build posted before it was applied: the older text replaced the edit, and the format's own answer was refused as overtaken (`applyEdits`). `format()` then sends whatever the editor holds as the edit it owed, which by then is the older text; that last step is read from the code, since under `main`'s file each placed case below stops at the assertion before the one that reads the build. `SessionClient` drops a reply only once a newer build has been posted, and the format posts none until it is answered.
- **The hole is as old as the guard.** #110 (`422f73e`) added `if (this.#timer !== null) return` to `setText` in the commit whose `format()` already cleared `#timer`. #112 (`18f8225`) added the field `#formatPending` so that `flush()` could reach the edit a format holds, and its doc names the blind spot for `flush()`; `setText` went on reading the timer alone.
- **That order explains run 512's first failure, by inference.** The test types its settled text, waits 400 ms, types the edit and clicks *format*. The 300 ms debounce posts the settled text's build, so a reply more than 100 ms away lands after the edit and the click. Nothing in CI showed this happening; the placed race below ends a TM copy on the text that run reported.
- **A debounce that sent during a format left the format's older text to be sent after it.** Found by the whole-branch review, and older than this branch: `#send` did not clear `#formatPending`. Typing that overtakes a format sets a debounce of its own; once that had sent the editor's text, the field still held the text the format had taken, and a delete's or a pause's `flush()` sent it after the newer one. The copy's record went back to the older text, which is what a delete's undo restores and what a pause keeps.
- **The second failure was the test's, by inference of the same kind.** A λ view offers *edit a copy* only while it holds a frame (`LambdaPane`'s `#refreshDetach`), so the control is absent from a compile's `compiled` reply until the first frame drawn for it. The case before the failing one ends when its format lands, with the compile that format starts still to run, and the failing case opens the view's menu with nothing between. Run 512's log has the thrown message and nothing that times the reach against that compile; with that time held open, `main`'s body throws the same message. The product does what the umbrella's §4 rule asks of a control that cannot apply.
- **A CPU quota reproduces neither**, as #110's entry found of its own failure. On `97e65ae`, the two files passed 13 of 13 twice at `CPUQuota=25%`, and at 10% twice failed elsewhere, on `timed out after 10000ms waiting for the first compile`.

##### WHAT CHANGED

- **`ScratchEditor.setText` does nothing while `#formatPending` is set either.** The format's own continuation sends the edit.
- **`#send` drops `#formatPending`**, since it sends everything the editor holds, and `flush()` leaves that to it. `format()`'s comment said a later debounce cleared the field; it now does.
- **`keystrokes-in-flight.test.ts`, three new tests**, for a TM, a λ and an asm copy. Each types its edit and clicks *format* from inside the app's own post of the earlier build, and keeps the `textDocument/formatting` request back until that build's reply has landed, since the two answers come from two workers and nothing else orders them. Each asserts that no newer build was posted before the reply, what the editor held when the reply had landed, what it holds after the format's answer, and the text of the last build posted, which is the edit reaching the copy. Taps and holds a failed case leaves are cleared after each case.
- **`scratch-editor.test.ts`, two new tests**: a seed is refused while a format holds an edit with no timer running, and applied once the format is answered; and a `flush()` after a debounce that sent during a format sends nothing.
- **`storage-blocked.test.ts`'s case waits for the formatted program's result before it opens the menu**, and `program-blocked.test.ts`'s case 3 waits for its edited program's. Each waits for the strip to be idle on its own program's value: `compile.ts`'s `schedule` turns the strip to running at the edit, and the `result` arm turns it to idle and draws in one task.

##### THE SIBLING SEARCH

- **Every reader of "an edit is pending" in `ScratchEditor`.** Three members decide on it, `flush`, `setText` and `format`; `flush` and `format` read both `#timer` and `#formatPending`, and `setText` read the timer alone. `#send`, which sends the editor's whole text, left the field set. `setText` has two callers, `CopyEditor.setEditor` for TM and asm copies and `LambdaPane.setEditor`, reached from `replies.ts`'s three reply arms; `pane-host.ts`'s `mountScratchEditor` calls `setEditor` only where no editor exists. A TM or an asm copy is re-seeded from its record and a λ copy from the term its build printed, and all three lost the edit.
- **Every browser test that reaches for a fork control while a compile runs**, since reading the 63 test files that contain `detach` would not show which reach lands inside a compile. A hook in `setup.ts` reported each `querySelector` or `querySelectorAll` from a test whose selector contains `detach` while `#results` read `running`, after the page's first idle; and `session-worker.ts` paused 2,000 ms after posting `compiled`, so the strip reads running for at least 2.3 s after an edit. Both were removed after.
- **It reported three reaches before the fixes and two after.** `program-blocked.test.ts`'s case 3 clicked the λ view's control behind a `?.` with its edit's compile running, found none under the pause and timed out on `the copy`; fixed above. `tm-scratch-fork.test.ts`'s `leaves the source session running` reaches a TM view's control mid-run on purpose, and asserts that the strip reads `running`. `lsp-outline.test.ts`'s `is withdrawn from a TM view until it holds a copy` clicks a TM view's control with `42`'s compile running. A TM view's control is set from the program's text at `compiled` (`CopyEditor`'s `#refreshDetach`), the hook found it present, and the case's assertions hold for whichever machine it copies. Neither is changed.
- **What the hook does not see**: a reach during a page's first compile, where the control goes from absent to present once; a reach by a selector that does not contain `detach`; a reach more than 2.3 s after an edit with no wait on idle; and the seven files `vite.config.ts`'s `PROBE_FILES` keeps out of the tier, which is 154 of the 161 test files. One of the 63 is among those seven, with `detach` in a comment.
- **Two instruments were blind before one was not.** A first sweep with only a 700 ms pause failed `program-blocked.test.ts` alone, and `main`'s `storage-blocked.test.ts` passes under it. The hook later reported that case's reach with the control found and the strip running, so here the reach does not fall where the control is absent, with the pause or without it. Whether it falls before `compiled` or after the first frame was not timed. That is why the hook reads the strip rather than waiting for a control to be absent. And the second sweep's hits were first counted with a search anchored to the start of a line, which finds a hit only under a failed test: a passing test's hit prints after a timestamp. It reported one reach where there were three.

##### WHAT PROVING IT FOUND

- **`main`'s `scratch-editor.ts` fails the five new tests, each on its property, in three runs of three.** The TM copy read `'tapes 1\nstart s\n\nstate s: accept\n'` when the reply had landed, which is the text run 512 reported; the λ copy read `λz. z`, the older build's term as the worker prints it, where `\y.   y   y` had been typed; the asm copy read the listing that loads `#4` where one loading `#5` had been typed. No placed reply was overtaken. The seed test read `\x. x`, and the flush test counted two sends.
- **Six sabotages of `scratch-editor.ts`, each failing the assertions aimed at it, among the 18 tests of the two files.** With `setText`'s new condition removed, the three placed cases fail on what the editor held at the reply and the seed test on its text. With `#send`'s clear removed, the flush test fails on its count. With `format()` sending the text from before the format, the three placed cases fail on the text of the last build and the flush test on its last assertion. With the format's answer never applied, the three placed cases fail on the editor's text after the answer. With the continuation leaving the field set, the seed test fails on its last assertion, a seed refused with nothing pending. With `format()` leaving the edit on the timer, the seed test fails on its precondition.
- **The fork control across one recompile, one run.** Its edit at 0 ms: the run posted at 310 ms; `compiled` at 343 ms with the control absent; the first `lambda-frames` reply at 403 ms with it still absent, since that arm draws on the next frame; present at 408 ms.
- **`main`'s `storage-blocked.test.ts` body fails with run 512's message when that time is held open**, and the new wait rides it out: with every reply of every worker after `compiled` kept from the app, the old body throws `no edit-a-copy control in the λ view’s menu`, 1 failed and 5 passed as on the run; with the wait, and the replies released after 1,500 ms, 6 of 6.
- **The whole browser tier passes with the 2,000 ms pause in**, 154 files and 1,053 tests, with the two reaches above reported.
- **`test:coverage`'s totals moved between three runs with no change under what moved.** On `b42217b`'s tree it read 97.49 / 91.43 / 98.36 / 98.85, at `cafb6b9` 97.42 / 91.38 / 98.36 / 98.79 and at `deaea03` 97.5 / 91.43 / 98.43 / 98.86. By file, the rows that differ are `term-map.ts`'s, 96.64, 93.28 and 96.64 of statements, and `main.ts`'s, 94.62, 94.62 and 94.75; no commit in the range touches either file.

##### THE TWO REVIEWS

**The whole-branch review**, of the first three commits as they then stood, `4a9f7f8..cd1c0b4`, whose tree is `b42217b`'s, read from git objects while the first replay ran in the checkout. No Critical finding, one Important and seven Minor.

- **Important: `#send` never cleared `#formatPending`**, the second defect above. Its sequence was written as a unit test first, which sent twice; `885cbab` is the fix.
- **Minor, all taken.** The new block's doc said every reply re-seeds from the copy's record, which is false of a λ copy. The placed cases asserted the editor and not what reached the copy, and `setText`'s condition had no unit test: `cafb6b9` and `885cbab` add both. Taps and holds had no cleanup. `#formatPending`'s doc did not name its new reader. Two commit messages said more than their diffs: the commits were replayed with the two messages reworded, which is why that review's SHAs are not this range's, and the tree after is the tree before, `96d0086`. The seventh asked for this entry.

**The re-review**, of `885cbab`, `cafb6b9` and this entry's first version, `42d8bbf`, which no review had read. No Critical finding, four Important and eleven Minor, and none in what the product does: it traced `#send`'s clear through each order of typing, flushing, destroying and answering and found no edit lost.

- **Important, in a test's doc**: the flush test's heading said the format is left nothing to send, where its continuation still sends the newer text. `deaea03` rewords it.
- **Important, in this entry, three**: the second failure's mechanism was written as fact, and here it could only be inferred; "sent twice" below was given for one order where it holds in both; and one run of the control's timeline was quoted from a log that holds only the totals. This revision marks the first, widens the second and drops the third.
- **Minor.** `deaea03` takes those in the code: the seed test had no precondition that no timer holds the edit, three comments in `scratch-editor.ts` said more than the code does, and the new assertions' messages were of two kinds or missing. It changes no line of `scratch-editor.ts` that is not a comment. The seed test's second half had no sabotage, and the record's `sab.py` gained the two that fail it. The rest were in this entry and are taken in this revision, among them a sentence that contradicted WHAT THIS DID NOT CLOSE, sentences that claimed more than their runs covered, figures the table left out, and the tier's seven excluded files and overlapping formats, which were not named.

##### WHAT THIS DID NOT CLOSE

- **A format that applies sets a debounce.** `applyEdits` dispatches through the update listener, so 300 ms after a format the formatted text is sent again and the copy is built from it twice, the server is told the formatted text only then, and a build's reply landing inside those 300 ms is refused by the timer. Read by both reviews and here; not changed, and not measured.
- **Typing that overtakes a format is sent twice, in either order.** Where its debounce fires first, `format()`'s continuation sends again because the text is not what it asked about; the third sabotage shows it, where the flush test lists two sends. Where the answer comes first, the continuation sends and the debounce that typing set sends again; read, and no test counts builds in that order.
- **Two formats in flight share the one field.** With *format on blur* on, a click on `⋯` and then *format* starts two. Read by the re-review as losing nothing; no test covers it, and the placed cases click without a blur.
- **`format()`'s `if (owed)` under `#destroyed` cannot be reached**, since `destroy()` flushes first. Left as it is.
- **`lsp-outline.test.ts`'s case still clicks a TM view's control with a compile running.** Which machine it copies depends on the order; its assertions do not.
- **`program-blocked.test.ts`'s `?.click()` still turns an absent control into a ten second wait** named `the copy`. The wait before it is what keeps the control there.
- **The coverage of `term-map.ts` and of `main.ts` is not the same from run to run**, above. Not looked into.
- **Neither order was observed on CI.** The evidence is the placed race for the first failure and the held replies for the second.
