##### THE REVIEW

**A whole-branch review by a reviewer who had not seen the work, at the first commit: two Critical, two Important, six Minor; then its re-review of the fixes, READY with three Minor: two comment paragraphs past 120 columns (seven, on a search), `frame-cost`'s floor giving its margin at 12 where it is 6, and `MAX_WARM_BUFFERS`' doc still giving a λ buffer's figures from before this branch with no date; all taken in `5683077`.** Its probes and logs are in the record's `review/`.

- **C1, the wasm crate's browser test** read the spans as an array of pairs; `check-all.sh`'s browser leg failed on it, and so did this branch's own first gate run. Fixed in `fa50113`.
- **C2, the premise of the memory changes was false** (WHAT A λ RING HOLDS). The reviewer measured retained typed arrays counted by `usedJSHeapSize`, posted ones too, and dropped ones counted for one collection; the controller re-measured it before changing anything. The additions are gone, every λ reading follows two collections, and every figure in this entry and in the docs was re-taken.
- **I1, the three instruments could not fail on a broken reading**: the reviewer's sabotages all passed. The floors above and M1 to M5 are the answer.
- **I2, `scratch.ts`' `MAX_WARM_BUFFERS` doc said the budget now allowed raising the cap**, true for λ copies only. The paragraph is gone; DECISIONS says what happens to the cap.
- **Minors**: `TOKEN_CLASSES`' and `assertTokenClasses`' docs said nothing read a class by index; the commit message named the inflated figures and called `v8.serialize` "a structured clone" without its caveat; `LAMBDA_LEG_RETENTION_RATIO`'s doc quoted a probe run taken on the old constant; `span_words` panicked in a debug build on a start past its end, and its refusals had no test; two preconditions sat inside a reading; `frame_cost_probe.rs`' `json_b` now spells a span as twelve JSON numbers, which its doc now says. All taken.
- **What the review found sound**: the wire format, its endianness and stride; `serde-wasm-bindgen` 0.6.5 writing bytes into a fresh, exactly sized `Uint8Array` with `serialize_bytes_as_arrays` off; `decorationRanges` honouring `byteOffset`; the ts-rs override; `lambdaFrameBytes`' charge, recomputed for `map`'s 253 frames as 6,343,013; and no other reader of a frame's spans in `web/src`, the worker, persistence, share links, the LSP or the CLI.

##### WHAT THIS DID NOT CLOSE

- **`MAX_WARM_BUFFERS`**, 11, does not fit a page of TM copies: DECISIONS. Its own pull request, next.
- **`SPAN_BYTES`, 80, charges a span 6.37 times what it holds**, so a λ history holds fewer frames than `HISTORY_BYTES` of heap would allow. Kept, by decision.
- **A λ copy's first recording was not timed in the browser**: `share-positions`' continues are this branch's browser measurement.
- **`frame_cost_probe.rs`' `json_b` for a λ row is not comparable with one taken before this branch**: it spells a span as twelve JSON numbers.

#### `MAX_WARM_BUFFERS` IS 8, WHERE IT WAS 11: A λ COPY SET IT, AND SINCE #136 AND #137 A TM COPY COSTS MORE; EIGHT TM COPIES OF `map-fold` UNDER `binary`, THE COSTLIEST COPY OF A SHIPPED EXAMPLE, WITH THE MACHINE THE PAGE KEEPS FOR EACH, COME TO 485.70 MiB WITH THE PAGE AND NINE TO 541.53, AGAINST THE 512 MiB BUDGET (2026-10-07, branch `warm-copy-cap`, `ab0950d..db09ca5`, 5 commits, plus this entry)

**A follow-up to #137, and two decisions of the user's.** #137's entry (DECISIONS) recorded the first: the warm-buffer probe priced λ copies only, a TM copy measured more, and the user chose "Lower to 9": one cap for every copy kind, set by the costliest, in a pull request of its own. The whole-branch review then found that nine copies are over the budget once the page's own copy of each machine is priced (THE REVIEW, C1), and the user chose "Cap 8 (Recommended)", the same rule priced with it. There is no spec or plan file; this entry is the design. Code commits: `c18b38e`, a cap of 9 and the probe's TM case; `3ccf65e`, comment lines only, what the cap covers and what it cannot; `ee5a762`, the review's findings, among them the cap of 8; `9799c5e`, a test file that needed room for nine copies; `db09ca5`, the re-review's Minors.

##### WHAT SET THE CAP, AND WHAT CHANGED

`MAX_WARM_BUFFERS` is how many copies may hold a worker at once. Its doc's threshold, pre-registered in 5d-ii-d: a page at the cap, every warm copy holding a real term with its ring driven to exhaustion, must sit at or below 512 MiB of main-thread heap and summed per-thread wasm memory, and the cap is the largest count that satisfies it. 5d-ii-d set 11 from λ copies, then the costliest: about 44.5 MB each. Since a TM frame's tapes and a λ frame's spans cross from the worker as one string and one byte string (#136, #137), a full TM ring holds 29.3 MB and a full λ ring 7.9, and a λ copy costs 16.42 MB in the probe. A TM copy's worker also holds more wasm: 25,362,432 bytes for `map-fold` under `binary`, where a λ copy's held 8,519,680.

##### WHAT A COPY COSTS, EVERY KIND

Throwaway browser files, each a copy of `buffer-affordability.test.ts` with its cases skipped and one added, priced one copy at a time, as a worker builds it, records it once to `HISTORY_BYTES` charged and holds it, the ring rebuilt on the page and read after two forced collections. One run each, and none of them held the page's copy of a TM machine, which only the TM case below does.

| A TM copy, n = 1 (bytes) | `unary` | `binary` |
|---|---|---|
| `map-fold` | 52,794,396 | **54,334,652** (wasm 25,362,432, ring 28,972,220) |
| `fact-12` | no machine | 51,585,008 |
| `closure` | 42,067,500 | 19,966,696 |
| `fact` | 39,449,656 | 24,120,648 |
| `sum-to` | 24,648,116 | 16,035,040 |
| `is-even` | 19,167,908 | 16,538,020 |
| `arithmetic` | 9,588,652 | 8,830,616 |

- **With the machine the page keeps counted**, through the TM case's `tmRound`, the review's run kept the order: `map-fold` under `binary` 58,545,848 bytes, under `unary` 56,119,708, `fact-12` under `binary` 55,037,816.
- **A λ copy at rest**, its worker and ring only: 16,444,164 bytes at most of the fork steps this lane tried, `fact-12`'s at step 0, and 17,241,868 at step 200 in the review's run; from step 250 the fork is refused, the term too large to print at `LAMBDA_BYTE_BUDGET`.
- **An asm copy**, its worker and ring only: 9,454,688 bytes at most, `map-fold`'s; its run ends in 260 steps.

So the copy that sets the cap is a TM copy of `map-fold` under `binary`, the app's default encoding.

##### THE CHANGE

- **`MAX_WARM_BUFFERS` is 8.** Every test that exercises the cap imports the constant; none spells a number.
- **The probe gains a TM case.** `affordability-tm-worker.ts` builds a `TmScratch` from the copy's machine text, makes the three calls a copy's first reply is made from, records its TM leg to `HISTORY_BYTES` charged, runs its value run to the end in `VALUE_CHUNK` chunks and holds the scratch, as `session-worker.ts`'s `onTmScratch` does, and answers what a copy's `tm-scratch-compiled` and last `tm-value` replies hand the page. The case compiles `map-fold` under `binary` on the page for its machine text and prices n of those copies at n = 1, 2, 4, the cap and one past it: each ring, and beside it the machine, tape names, status and value `replies.ts` keeps on the copy's session entry whether or not a view shows it, read after two collections with the replies' frame arrays dropped, and refuses a copy whose machine has no states. It derives the cap from reading (a)'s intercept as the λ case does, and prints the page at the cap and one past it against the budget.
- **`MAX_WARM_BUFFERS`' doc** says what set 8, what "at rest" means, that a copy a view shows holds more that was not measured, and the two copies no count prices.
- **`vite.config.ts`** no longer says the probe runs eleven workers.
- **`MAX_WARM_BUFFERS`' doc names a floor of 7 for the tests**: `copy-edit-leaving.test.ts` keeps seven copies on its page by its end and `stage-tab-titles.test.ts` six, their copies outliving their tests, counted before every test of every browser file in the re-review's sweep.
- **`copy-editor-mount.test.ts` deletes each test's copies after it.** It made nine copies on its one page and never deleted one, so its ninth fork waited on the cap: at 8, `offers move the editor here on TM, and the view that gives it up keeps its copy's value` timed out "waiting for the copy's editor", the one failure in the gate's 2,247 tests at `ee5a762`. An `afterEach` deletes every copy through the copies menu, the loop `two-lambda-panes.test.ts` uses for the same reason; the file passes 9 of 9 at full speed and at a quarter of a core.

| The TM case, four runs | n = 8 | n = 9 |
|---|---|---|
| copies' wasm | 202,899,456 | 228,261,888 |
| copies' rings, with what the page keeps for each | 265,402,000 | 298,575,856 |
| with reading (a)'s intercept, 40,993,517 to 40,997,888 | 485.70 to 485.71 MiB, fits | 541.53 MiB, does not |

Its marginal, from n = 1 and n = 4, read 58,535,454.67 and 58,537,982.67 bytes in the first two runs, and reading (a) derived 8 in all four. In the same runs the λ case derives 30 and 28 for readings (a) and (b).

##### WHAT NO COUNT PRICES

Both of these were past any count's reach at 11 as well.

- **A λ copy grows each time its recording is continued.** Through the probe's λ worker, stepped 200,000 times, `fact-12`'s λ copy held 69,206,016 bytes of wasm and 75,754,024 in all, in one run; at rest it holds 16,444,164. Each `[continue]` records another `HISTORY_BYTES` and the ring keeps one, while the worker's wasm memory, which never shrinks, grows with the run; the review's session stepped 600,000 times held 208,863,232 bytes of wasm.
- **A copy a user writes can be larger than any shipped one**: an asm copy's worker reached 168.4 MiB under `COPY_CAPS` (Plan 7 part 5's entry, `asm-copy-memory.test.ts`).

A TM copy continued to its end gains no wasm, in the review's runs on three machines, and neither does one rebuilt five times by edits.

##### THE TESTS

- **The probe's TM case is the measurement of the number.** The probe is on `vite.config.ts`'s probe list, run on demand as a copy. Its file's header says it pins no measured figure and asserts nothing about the budget, so the case prints its two fit lines and the derived cap, which `MAX_WARM_BUFFERS`' doc reads. What it asserts: each copy's ring evicted, so its history filled; each holds at least a tenth of `HISTORY_BYTES`; each value run ended; each copy's machine has states; and the machine text is over a million units.
- **The sabotages** (`sab/run-cap-sabs.py`), copies of the probe, run while the case still asserted its fit lines. With the cap read as 11, eleven copies needed 608.51 MiB without the machine held; read as 9, nine needed 540.99 MiB; read as 8 before the machine was held, nine fit at 504.87; read as 7, eight fit at 485.16; and with the page's copy of each machine and value dropped from the case, it derived 9 and nine fit at 503.04 MiB. Each failed the assertion it aimed at; each printed fit line is the same with the assertions gone. A worker answering no machine, the last, fails the case: "BLOCKED: a TM probe worker answered no machine".
- **Every test that exercises the cap** follows the constant: `scratch-cap`, `tm-blank-buffer-cap`, `share-open-cap` and `two-lambda-panes` in the browser tier, `scratch` and `sessions` in node. One that did not exercise it needed its room, `copy-editor-mount` (THE CHANGE), and its failure at `ee5a762` is its RED.

##### THE REVIEW

**A whole-branch review by a reviewer who had not seen the work, at `3ccf65e`: one Critical, one Important, eight Minor; then its re-review of the fixes at `9799c5e`: no Critical or Important, six Minor, all taken in `db09ca5`.** Its probes are in the record's `review/probes/`.

- **C1, the page's copy of each machine.** `replies.ts`'s `tm-scratch-compiled` arm keeps a copy's machine, tape names and status on its session entry whether or not a view shows it, 4,485,864 and 4,483,346.67 bytes a copy for `map-fold` under `binary`, and the probe's worker dropped them. With them held, nine copies came to 543.77 MiB and the cap derived 8. The controller confirmed the store in the code and the reviewer's probe against the worker, and put the decision to the user.
- **I1, the case contradicted its file's header**: two budget assertions and a pinned length. Resolved toward the header.
- **Minors**: the λ copy at rest quoted at 16.44 MB where step 200 costs 17.24; the replies' frame arrays held through the reading, 0.28 MB a copy; an assertion that could not fail; a frame count given as the step count; "lists" for a doc naming three; the cap given as eleven in `vite.config.ts` and a 5d-ii-d paragraph; the page baseline unprinted; a worker field nothing read. All taken.
- **The re-review's Minors**: two checks in `tmRound` that could not fail, now one that can; the floor of 7 the tests need; the λ and asm copies' figures counted without what the page keeps, against a TM figure counted with it; the order of the shipped TM copies argued from machine-text length, which does not order them; "over half a gigabyte" unmeasured; a ring figure rounded. Its first review had judged the tests' need for room from the highest copy number any test spells, which could not see `copy-editor-mount.test.ts`, whose labels are interpolated; its count before every test replaced it.
- **What the review found sound**: the TM worker does what `onTmScratch` and `recordLeg` do, in the same order; every consumer of the cap uses the constant, and the suite passed at 9; reading the TM case's page baseline after its compile can only lower the cap; the sabotages do not depend on timing.

##### WHAT THIS DID NOT CLOSE

- **A byte budget.** A continued λ copy and a hand-written copy cost more than any count can allow for (WHAT NO COUNT PRICES). Pricing them needs the page to know what each copy holds, not how many there are.
- **A copy a view shows** also holds its view's tables and an editor with its text; a page of those was not measured.
- **Two test files keep copies across tests** and need a cap of 7 or more; only `copy-editor-mount.test.ts` was changed to delete them.
- **Dated specs** still give the cap as 11: Plan 7 part 2's and 5d-iv's design documents, as written at the time.

#### ABOUT, HELP, LICENCES AND PRIVACY PAGES BESIDE THE APP, REACHED FROM AN `about ▾` MENU BEFORE `settings`, NAMING THE BUILD'S COMMIT AND A COPYRIGHT YEAR FROM THE VIEWER'S CLOCK; THE SITE SHIPPED NO THIRD-PARTY LICENCE NOTICE AT ALL, AND NOW LISTS 18 npm PACKAGES OF CODE, 24 CRATES, 5 TOOLCHAIN RUNTIMES AND 2 FONTS WITH THEIR OWN TEXTS, HELD TO THE LOCKFILES BY A THIRTEENTH PRE-COMMIT HOOK (2026-10-08, branch `about-pages`, `8dc603d..fa93c45`, 15 commits, plus this entry)

**The user asked for an about page and a licence page "and anything else like that you recommend".** Help and privacy were the two recommendations taken. The design is `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-07-about-pages-design.md`, whose dated notes record what the prototype and the reviews changed; the plan is `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-10-08-about-pages.md`, whose code is the pre-review replay.

##### WHAT EXISTED

The workspace is GPL-3.0-only and nothing in `web/` said so. The built site's four JavaScript chunks held no licence notice (spec §2.2), though it bundles CodeMirror, the vim keymap and `web-tree-sitter` under MIT, whose notice must travel with every copy, and two dozen crates under MIT or Apache-2.0. The two font licences were served under `/licenses/` and linked from nowhere. CI passed `COMMIT_HASH` into the image and nothing read it. The forge sends every anonymous visitor to its login page, so the source link is the public GitHub mirror, which the forge pushes on every commit.

##### THE PAGES

`about.html`, `help.html`, `licences.html` and `privacy.html` sit beside `index.html` as Vite inputs and share `style.css`, a small `pages.css`, a nav, and a footer that `pages.ts`'s `initPage` fills with the copyright line, the build and its source link. The about menu's links open each in a new tab, so the app keeps its stepping position, which a reload loses. The pre-paint script moved out of `index.html` into `prepaint.ts`, and a Vite plugin inlines it wherever a page writes `<!-- prepaint -->`, so every page paints in the stored theme from one copy. `build-info.ts` names the build `build <short hash>` with a link to the mirror's tree at that commit, or `dev build` and `main`; the copyright line is `© 2026 Davey Hughes`, widening to `© 2026–YYYY` on the viewer's clock and never written into a file.

The help page's prose was checked against each `keydown` handler and the step controls' labels; the privacy page's against the measured hosting (Cloudflare in front, no cookie, one same-origin script) and the ten `redextape.*` storage keys. Tests hold the help page's editor-key table to `navKeymap` and `LINK_KEY`, row by row and key by key, and the privacy page's key table to every key literal in `src/`, in any quotes, refusing one built in a template.

##### THE NOTICES

`web/scripts/licences.ts`, run by Node directly, writes the committed `web/src/third-party-licences.json`: redextape's own `LICENSE.md`, then every npm package `src/`, its CSS and the pages import or load, walked along dependencies, with `vite` and `rolldown` by name for the helpers they put in the chunk; every crate `cargo tree` names for each wasm build; and the toolchains' runtimes no package manager reports — the Rust standard library, `compiler-builtins`, `dlmalloc`, `hashbrown`, and Emscripten's runtime inside `web-tree-sitter` — from texts committed under `web/scripts/toolchain-licences/` at the versions that built the shipped files. Each text is stored once; the output sorts by code unit. `scripts/check-licences.sh` regenerates it and fails on any difference, with a self-test, in pre-commit and in CI's `web` job; it says to run `pnpm install` when `node_modules` is not the lockfile's. `licences-page.ts` draws it, every text through `textContent`.

##### DECISIONS

The user's, in order: all four pages; static pages opened in a new tab; the GitHub mirror as the source; Davey Hughes as the holder, the year a range from 2026; notices generated into a committed file and checked, over generating them at build time or adopting `cargo-about`; the menu **before** `settings`, after the prototype found that after it a Tab from `settings` reached `about ▾` and not the notice line's *undo* — 12 of `base16-remove.test.ts`'s 15 cases failed; and, after Task 4's review, listing the toolchains' runtimes rather than narrowing the page's claim.

##### THE REVIEW

A prototype passed the whole suite and an image, was replayed task by task, and the five replayed commits were cherry-picked. Each task then had a fresh review, a whole-branch review followed, and a review of that fix round; every finding was fixed with a sabotage showing its test can fail. What they found that nothing had:

- **The plugin was untested.** Deleting it from `vite.config.ts` left every test green while every page shipped without the script; each page now runs through a server built from the config, and the page list is held to the build's inputs.
- **The notices under-listed.** A licence file was matched only at the start of its name, which missed rolldown's `THIRD-PARTY-LICENSE`, the esbuild and Rollup notices behind the very helpers rolldown is listed for. The standard library's `hashbrown` and `compiler-builtins` and its allocator ship in both builds and no tool names them. Conversely `cargo metadata`'s workspace feature union listed the workspace's own `indexmap`, `hashbrown`, `equivalent` and `foldhash`, copies no build compiles: 24 crates, not 28.
- **The check depended on the machine.** `localeCompare` made the file's bytes differ under Danish and Estonian collation, so pre-commit would fail on an untouched tree there.
- **Several tests could not fail.** `BUILD`'s passed with its key misspelt; the storage-key scan missed any key with a digit or a dash; the controls gate never walked a link.
- **The pages said things the code does not do.** F12 and F2 in a λ copy's editor; a "standard" keymap; a menu that stayed open after a pick, against every header menu's convention.
- **The fix rounds' own text.** The final review found three false statements in the previous fix commit — a test header misstating its blind spot, a comment, a spec note — as this repository's correction rounds keep doing.

##### WHAT THIS DID NOT CLOSE

- **No favicon.** Every page load still 404s `/favicon.ico`, as before this branch.
- **A crate the standard library links that never panics** leaves no path in a stripped `.wasm`, so the toolchain test cannot see it; `compiler-builtins` was found by name in an unstripped build. A new Rust release should be checked the same way.
- **The help page's views table** is checked by reading the handlers, not by a test; only the editor table is held.
- **Without JavaScript** a deployed page's footer says `dev build`, the HTML's default.
- **`/about` without `.html`** falls back to the app, as every unknown path does.
- **`aria-haspopup` on `settings`** is still the open question it was; `about ▾` carries none, as `share` does not.

#### A RUN OPENS ON STEP 0, READY TO STEP FROM ITS START, WHERE IT OPENED ON THE LAST STEP ITS RECORDING REACHED; `⏭` AFTER `▶` GOES TO THE NEWEST RECORDED STEP, AND A RING KEEPS THE WHOLE OF THE RECORDING THAT FILLS IT, WHERE IT DROPPED THAT RECORDING'S FIRST FRAMES (2026-10-08, branch `start-at-step-zero`, `8f954d9..0fe3ad5`, 2 commits, plus this entry)

**The user asked for it, "a quick thing before other things":** "the asm, tm, and lambda programs all start with the
execution of them at the end — can we make them so they're ready to be executed from the program start?" Every view of
a run, the program's or a copy's, opened on its newest frame, because `History`'s play head followed the frontier from
the first frame on, and a recompile cleared it back to following.

##### WHAT CHANGED

- **`History` starts not following, and `clear` resets it so.** A run, a recompile and a copy open on step 0 however far
  the worker records behind them. The head follows again once the user takes it to the frontier — `▶` onto the newest
  frame, `seek` to it, or `⏭` — as before. `forward` on the newest frame also turns following on, so the frames a
  frontier `▶` asks for carry the head, which a run that opened on its only frame would otherwise never do.
- **A ring keeps the frames before its newest within its budget**, where it kept every frame within it.
  `record-loop.ts` checks a leg's allowance before each step, so a recording that spends it posts up to one frame past
  it, and the allowance is the ring's budget. The old rule dropped the first frames of the very recording that filled
  the ring — two of the 75,025 `session-memory.test.ts`'s TM leg pushed (`HISTORY_BYTES`' doc) — so that run would
  have opened on step 2. A ring now holds up to one frame past `HISTORY_BYTES`.
- **`⏭`, "to the newest recorded step", after `▶` in every strip and in the step bar**, live while the head is behind
  the newest frame (`ControlState.canToNewest`), never asking the worker for more. Hack has no `⏭`, so it is an
  `icons.ts` icon, as `⏵` is. When `keep recording` goes away under the focus, `⏭` is next after `▶` to take it.
  **`⏭` is disabled by its own press**, and a focused button that is disabled drops the focus to `<body>`
  (`extend-focus-probe.test.ts`), so the strip hands the focus on before it disables `⏭`: to `◀`, then `↺`, `▶`, play
  and the speed select (`0fe3ad5`, from the review).
- **The two icon buttons are as wide as the glyph buttons**, 29 px at 15 px where they were 35: `⏭` and its gap took
  43 px from the title's row, and at 1280 px in Explorer the TM view's strip at `step 12,976 of 12,976` needed 430.2 px
  of the 424.1 its row had, so the header wrapped and the view's panels dropped 31 px. A playing run's would have
  dropped once its count gained a digit. At 29 px it needs 418.2.
- **`LinkPositions.#stop` puts the head on the leg's last step itself**, which following used to have done.

##### DECISIONS

The user's: the request, and `⏭` after `▶` over no new control, offered once it was clear that nothing else reaches a
run's end: playing `session-memory.test.ts`'s 75,025 TM frames takes 15.0 s at the fastest speed and 2.6 hours at
the default.

Mine, each stated in the code or a test: the icon buttons' width above; a link's pending position waits on step 0
until the frames reach it, rather than riding the frontier; *edit a copy* forks the step on screen, so step 0 unless
the user moves; and the controls gate holds the TM diagram's *show states* to its name alone (below).

##### THE TESTS

Before any test moved, the change failed 83 browser tests in 26 files, and 96 in 27 with `⏭` in the strips. Nearly
every one waited for `step N of N` at open, stepped back from the end, or pinned a figure the ring's new rule moves.
They press `⏭`, step forward where they stepped back, or read step 0. **Some still passed and checked nothing**, and
were changed with the rest: `app.test.ts`' *stops following once the user scrolls* set `scrollTop = 0` on a rule table
already at 0 and clicked a disabled `◀`, and the on-demand `lambda-tree-cost.test.ts` would have clicked it 300 times a
program and timed nothing.

Where a fixture's premise was the run's end, the fixture moved there by `⏭`: `tm-view-narrow.test.ts` measures the TM
view at `sum_to(5)`'s end, and `buffer-cool-warm.test.ts` forks a normal form. Some figures moved because the ring keeps
more: `fact(4)`'s λ line was long in part because its first recording lost frames and the line named the oldest it
kept, which it no longer does, so `view-strip-narrow` and `step-bar-narrow` press `keep recording` once to make it long
again; `share-positions.test.ts`' oldest kept steps
are 2,769 and 14,272 where they were 2,770 and 14,273, and its `1,387` case lands on 1,387, which the ring now keeps.
`session-memory.test.ts` asks that the TM leg pushed `HISTORY_BYTES`, where it asked for an eviction.

At 481 px in Debugger and Stage the step bar's row no longer holds its step text, which takes a second row: 22 px off
`main`'s height, re-pinned in `inspector-phone.test.ts`. **The controls gate holds *show states* to its name alone**:
it is out of the tab order, its row's Enter does what it does, and focusing it redraws its row, so the focus lands on
`<body>`, with or without `preventScroll`. The gate first met it on step 0, whose group has its row.

Every new behaviour was sabotaged and its tests went red: following on from the start (8 node cases red), `clear`
leaving it on (2), the old eviction rule (10, across `history` and `share-positions`), no following from a frontier
`forward` (1), following from an empty one (1), `#stop` not seeking (5), `canToNewest` live at the frontier (1), `⏭`
landing one short (4 browser), the icon buttons at 35 px (1 browser), and `⏭` disabling with no hand-off (2 browser:
the strip's own case and a real `Enter` in the app).

##### THE REVIEW

One whole-branch review of `0b3fdb3`, by a fresh agent reading the code, told the goal and not my conclusions; it ran
nothing, since the gates held the browser. It found no Critical or Important finding. Its first Minor was real and is
fixed in `0fe3ad5`: every keyboard press of `⏭` dropped the focus to `<body>`, as above. It also named `[continue]`
from a head parked on step 0, below; that a shared link now carries step 0 for every leg the user has not moved, which
is the step on screen, as a link always carried; and that `↺` on a one-frame ring turns following on, as it did before.

##### WHAT THIS DID NOT CLOSE

- **`keep recording` from a head parked on step 0** leaves it parked, and as the ring drops old frames the head lands
  on the oldest kept step, not on the new frames. That is the parked head's existing rule; before this branch a head
  at rest was at the frontier and followed.
- **The TM header at 1280 px in Explorer has 5.9 px to spare** at `step 12,976 of 12,976`, under one character of the
  step text's 7.0 px (147 px for its 21).
- **The step bar at 481 px** takes two rows in Debugger and Stage.
- **The TM diagram's *show states* cannot hold the focus**, as above; nothing a user does focuses it, so it is not fixed
  here.
- **`◀` pressed onto step 0, and `▶` pressed onto an ended run's last step, still drop the focus to `<body>`**, as they
  did before this branch; only `⏭`, which does it on every press, hands it on.

#### EACH COMBINATION OF VIEWS KEEPS ITS OWN ARRANGEMENT, THE HEADER'S TOGGLES AND THE VIEW KEYS CHOOSE IT, AND A FRESH PAGE OPENS ON THE SOURCE BESIDE THE TM VIEW, WHERE IT OPENED ON ALL FOUR (2026-10-12, branch `view-layouts`, `7cbac7d..ad45a3f`, 88 commits, plus this entry and `05828bc`, the user's answer on the toggle keys; then `8fcc4e3`, `babb610` and `b64120d`, made with the pull request open, and this entry brought up to them twice)

**The user asked for it:** the default layout "is interesting but it's cluttered. I want to make it easy to cycle
through some layouts and/or customize exactly what windows you're seeing", most often the source beside one of the TM,
λ and asm views. This is the first of four pull requests of
`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-11-view-layouts-design.md`, its §4 to §8; panel resizing (§11), moving a view (§9) and
drag and drop (§10) follow, and views in windows of their own after those. The design was approved, amended after a
prototype the user tried, and amended again as the reviews of this branch changed it: its §16 and §17 list each
change with what caused it.

##### WHAT CHANGED

- **A combination of views has an arrangement, and the workspace remembers one for each.** A combination is the kinds
  the tree on screen holds. `Workspace.arrangements` keeps the tree last shown for every other combination, under a
  key that spells its kinds in `KIND_ORDER`, and `arrangements.ts`'s `enter` is what a gesture's write of the tree
  goes through. So a switch away and back shows the tree that was left, and a `✕` on a kind's last view followed by
  that kind's toggle shows the tree before the `✕`. A combination's first visit shows `layout.ts`'s
  `defaultArrangement`: in a wide area, columns side by side, so the one divider that spans the area is the vertical
  one; in a tall area the same trees on their side.
- **Four toggles in the header, `source`, `asm`, `λ`, `TM`** (`#views-shown`), each pressed where the tree on screen
  holds a view of its kind. They are `index.html`'s own markup, so they hold their place from the first paint. The
  last pressed one is `aria-disabled`, keeps the focus, and says why on its tooltip and on the notice line; a tooltip
  says what a press does and counts the views where a kind has several. In a window 40rem wide or narrower they are
  hidden, and a view's `✕`, `+ view` and the view keys still choose the views. Terminal's header has half the column
  gap in a window 85rem wide or narrower, so that the toggles do not cost it a second row at 1280 px.
- **A switch parks a view, and a `✕` closes one.** A parked view keeps its pane off the page, as a Stage tab that is
  not selected keeps its own: the copy it shows, that copy's editor, what it had open, and where it was scrolled to.
  The surfaces the views share — the step bar's target, the link status line, the running focuses — read the views of
  the tree on screen and never a parked one. `MAX_TREE_LEAVES` bounds every live view, on screen or remembered, and an
  add or a switch past it is refused with a notice that counts them.
- **One id is one view, of one kind.** A pick in a view's title changes its kind and keeps its id, so two trees can
  name an id as two kinds. A switch enters such a leaf under a new id (`arrangements.ts`'s `reidentified`) and both
  views are kept. The design as approved rebuilt the view in place, which destroyed a parked view of a copy.
- **View keys: `Ctrl+.`, then one key.** `]` and `[` go round four stops (the source beside asm, beside λ, beside TM,
  then all four); `1` to `4` are the toggles; `Escape` or the prefix again leaves. `Ctrl` may be held through the
  second key or not. `view-keys.ts` is a two-state machine with no DOM in it and one capture-phase listener on
  `window`; a hint lists the keys over the foot of the page and the live region says them; `help.html`'s table is
  held to the machine's own. A key held down is one press, and a view key closes every open popover before it acts.
- **A fresh page opens on the source beside the TM view**, a row in a wide area and a column in a tall one, and *reset
  preset* goes back to it. A workspace stored with four views is kept as it is.
- **A focus the app moves scrolls nothing after a pointer's gesture, and shows the focused control after a key's**
  (`pane-host.ts`'s `moveFocus`): an editor is shown by its caret. A bare `focus()` on a view's first control put the
  source view back at its top when the `✕` of the view beside it was pressed.

**Six defects older than this branch are fixed in it**, the first two because the toggles lean on what they broke,
the rest because the reviews reached them:

1. **Every rebuild of the layout reset every scroll position**, in the views that stayed as well: the TM rule table
   at 120 px was at 0 after another view's toggle. `pane-host.ts` holds each view's scrollers, its own scroll box
   among them, across every rebuild, through `state-table.ts`'s `restoreScroll`, so a box that follows the run comes
   back following.
2. **A view off the page went on holding the editor of a copy it no longer showed.** With the older view of a copy a
   Stage tab that was not selected, a delete and its *undo* threw `a λ pane was handed a second editor while still
   holding one`.
3. **Which view shows which copy was stored only at a fork, a pause and a delete**, so a copy's view closed with `✕`
   left its binding behind and a reload gave the copy to the view built in its place. It is stored each time the
   layout is applied.
4. **A divider dragged with the pointer left the focus on `<body>`**, and a key typed after it went nowhere. The focus
   is given back to what had it.
5. **`layout.ts`'s `resize` answered a share of nothing or less** where the two views beside a divider could not both
   hold the least share: from a row of 20 equal views, one arrow key on such a divider stored a workspace the next
   load threw away. A divider between two such views does not move, which is so from a row of 11.
6. **An opened link's notice named legs no view showed**: the λ and asm legs' steps, on a page of the source and the
   TM view. A leg stopping short is said only where the tree has a view of it.

##### DECISIONS

The user's, each in the design's §3 and §16.1: toggles and a cycle key; a pair side by side, and rearrangeable; one
arrangement for each combination; the first load on the source beside the TM view; a prefix chord and then one key;
the toggles in the order source, asm, λ, TM; in a wide window columns side by side, so that no divider and no view
runs the whole width; and the cycle keys `]` and `[` with `Ctrl` held or not, after "ctrl+n opens a new window for
me". With the pull request open (the design's §16.4): a workspace stored with four views is kept as it is; the keys
on a layout that types `.` with Shift or `[` and `]` with Option or AltGr stay as built, the change wanted "later
on, but not anytime soon"; and Terminal's header is fixed here.

Mine, each stated in the code or the design, and the design's §16.3 lists the ones that are the user's to overrule:
the toggles hidden in a narrow window, where the other choice moves them into the workspace menu; a switch that
parks and a `✕` that closes, after the prototype that parked both failed `scratch-buffers.test.ts` and
`workspace-restore.test.ts`; a leaf entered under a new id where its id is live as another kind; a pointer's gesture
scrolling nothing and a key's showing the focused control; a view key closing open popovers, where the other choice
leaves the mode unarmed under one; the last toggle `aria-disabled`; an opened link keeping no scroll position; the
words of the two notices at the bound; and a divider that does not move where its two views cannot both hold the
least share.

##### THE TESTS

**The tests keep starting where they were written.** `web/tests/browser/setup.ts` stores a workspace of four views
for every file, spelled out in the harness as `fourViews()`, and a file that tests the first load removes it before
it mounts. `showFourViews` and `resetToFourViews` put a page back on that tree with real presses and throw unless it
ends there. `defaultLayout` and `defaultWorkspace` take the area's shape as a required argument, so a test that means
the default says for which area.

**A seed is how a test goes on passing while it checks nothing**, and the reviews found that it had: a case that
asked for no step controls in a view the page did not have, a case whose *reset preset* did the work its `✕` was
there to show, titles that said "the default" of the seeded tree, and a defect (the scroll lost to a focus move)
that only the first-load tree shows. So `default-views-gestures.test.ts` and `focus-scroll.test.ts` run the
gestures whose outcome depends on the tree's shape on the two trees a visitor is given.

`tests/node/arrangements.test.ts` holds `enter`'s two properties over 24 generated sequences of 60 gestures —
toggles, cycle keys, closes, adds, kind-changing picks and drags — twelve from the first load's two views and twelve
from a workspace of 60 live views, where switches and adds are refused at the bound; after every gesture the
workspace reads back through `parseWorkspace`. `harness.ts`'s `focusInPage` holds the focus to an element inside the
page after each gesture; one fails it, a pointer press on a part of the page that takes no focus, which the browser
leaves on `<body>`.

Every new mechanism was sabotaged by one edit and its test seen to fail, and each edit a review predicted would pass
every test was run: where it passed, an assertion was added and the edit run again. The edits, the failing lines and
the logs are in the fix groups' notes in `~/temp/redextape-view-layouts-record/reviews/`.

##### WHAT THIS DID NOT CLOSE

- **Five points of the design's §16.3**, which are the user's: the toggles in a narrow window; `+ view` halving the
  focused view in a layout of columns; the new id for a leaf live as another kind; the pointer's and the key's halves
  of the focus rule; and the view that takes the focus after a `✕`, which for the first view of a second column is
  the one diagonally across.
- **The keys on a layout that types `.` with Shift, or `[` and `]` with Option or AltGr**, are refused: read from the
  layouts and run on none. The user wants the change later, and not soon.
- **The timeout of `lambda-deep-outline.test.ts` on CI at `46c25f1`**, above: seen once, not reproduced, its cause
  not known. The next one will say what the page read.
- **The TM tapes' scroll bar flashes on every step**, the user noted on 2026-10-12, to be avoided. Not looked into:
  neither its cause nor whether `main` does it.
- **Everything here was measured in the browser tests' Chromium.** Firefox and WebKit are unmeasured, the prefix
  chord and `:focus-visible` after a pointer press among what they may do differently.
- **A parked view that showed a copy comes back on the program after a reload**, and after an opened link's undo; the
  copy is in the copies menu.
- **A workspace stored with four views is not migrated**, so a returning visitor sees the new first load only after
  *reset preset*.
- **A build before this one refuses a workspace that stores panel state or a display for a parked view**, resets to
  its default and overwrites what was stored. A rollback loses the remembered arrangements.
- **`main.ts` fills the `encoding` select and `#appearance` late**, as on `main`, so `share`, `about` and `settings`
  move left as the page loads, and in a window narrow enough the header gains a row then. Terminal's header takes a
  second row under about 1,254 px, on this machine's monospace.
- **On the Stage, a delete's undo can still mount a copy's editor on a tab that is not selected**, as on `main`.
- **A phone in Debugger with the inspector open has a views area wider than it is tall**, so a first load or a reset
  there puts two narrow views side by side; and a page first laid out with no size stores a row.
- **The view keys' hint sits below the top layer**, so a popover reaching the foot of the page would cover it;
  `Ctrl+[`, vim's Escape, is the previous layout while the mode is armed.
- **`reseedingSlots` takes a copy's editor down only for a view off the page**, and no test can hold that condition:
  with it dropped every test passes, and `copy-edit-leaving.test.ts`'s pause case then passes with its flush removed.
- **A view's `⋯` menu moves 34 px when a compile lands under it.**
- **A divider in a row of 11 equal views or more does not move**: the least share is a tenth of the split, which two
  of them cannot both hold. Before this branch such a divider moved once, the same way whichever way it was dragged,
  and then never again.
- **Two probes outside the default run fail as they do on `main`**: `pnpm run test:probe` and `test:probe:tm`.
- **Panel resizing, moving a view, drag and drop**: the design's §11, §9 and §10, the next three pull requests.

#### THE REGIONS INSIDE A VIEW CAN BE RESIZED: A BOUNDARY BETWEEN TWO IS DRAGGED BY THE HEADER OF THE PANEL UNDER IT OR MOVED WITH THE ARROW KEYS, EACH PANEL HAS A MAXIMISE BUTTON, AND THE WORKSPACE KEEPS THE SIZES, WHERE EACH PANEL HAD THE SHARE THE STYLESHEET FIXED (2026-10-13, branch `panel-resizing`, `91bc3ba..60a33b4`, 8 commits, plus this entry; then `5bae683`, `47a4f59`, `b38a863` and `e2617e4`, which answer a review, and the commit that brings this entry up to date)

**The user asked for it** with the first pull request's prototype open: "we need to be able to resize things like
rules, state diagram, etc. they can't just be fixed in place". This is the second of four pull requests of
`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-11-view-layouts-design.md`, its §11; moving a view (§9) and drag and drop (§10)
follow. A prototype of all four views was built first and he tried it running: what he said changed it twice, and
the design's §11 is rewritten as built, with §18 listing each change and what caused it and §19 what a review of the
branch then found.

##### WHAT CHANGED

- **A boundary between two regions of a view, in all four views.** `panel-stack.ts` gives each open region a share of
  its view's height, written as one custom property, `--share`, which the stylesheet's `flex` reads; it draws a
  `role="separator"` under each open region that has an open region below it, named for the two ("resize rules and
  state diagram"). Dragging it gives one region more of the view and the other less: no other region changes and the
  view does not grow. A drag stops where either neighbour would go under its floor. `↑` and `↓` move a focused
  boundary a fiftieth of what the open regions share, and `Enter` or a double click puts both regions back as they
  are built.
- **A panel's header is the handle for the boundary above it.** A press on the bar's own part, outside its controls,
  drags that boundary. Nothing is drawn for a boundary at rest or under the pointer: the pointer is an open hand over
  a handle and a closed one from the press to the release. A line is drawn for a key's focus alone.
- **A maximise button on each panel**, after its other actions, named for its panel and carrying `aria-pressed`.
  Pressed, its panel takes the view's spare height and every other panel is drawn closed (`panel.ts`'s `drawOver`),
  with what each stores left alone. Pressing it again, opening another panel by its disclosure, or closing the
  maximised one ends it. It is not stored.
- **The λ view and the source view share their height.** The λ term was capped at six tenths of the window whatever
  its view's height, and takes its view's spare height. The source editor takes its view's and scrolls a long program
  inside its own box, so the source view's header stays where it is; the outline's cap is four tenths of its view,
  where it was `40vh`.
- **Three regions start at the height they have today**, and take a share only at the first drag beside them: a
  copy's text, the term map (120 px) and the source outline. A copy's text joins its view's regions, so its editor can
  be given room the rules have.
- **`Workspace.panelSizes`** holds a view's shares, in a field that may be absent: written once a gesture, for the two
  regions its boundary parts and no other, kept for a view a switch takes off the page, dropped with a view a `✕` or
  *reset preset* closes, and carried by a link for the views on screen. A gesture that ends with its boundary where
  it began writes nothing. A share is a ratio: what the page is given is the open regions' shares with the least of
  them as 1, so that the regions left open fill their view.
- **`separator.ts` is the layout divider's gesture**, taken out of `layout-view.ts`, which now calls it: one
  implementation for a divider between views and a boundary between panels.
- **`help.html`** lists the boundary's keys and the header's drag.

**One defect the move exposed is fixed.** CodeMirror puts its own scroll position back when it is focused at 0
(`@codemirror/view` 6.43.8's `observers.focus`), and a link's *undo* builds every view again and focuses the source
editor in the same task. With the editor scrolling inside its own box, the editor at 120 px under a link's program
stayed at 120 under the program the undo put back. `pane-host.ts`'s `startEditorsAtTop` tells the editors of a view
built again that they are at their start. An opened link was not seen to do the same.

##### DECISIONS

The user's, each in the design's §18.1, with the prototype open: a panel's header as the handle, after "I think I
would prefer the actual grip mouse icon on the status bar for that section"; nothing drawn for a boundary and the
pointer's two hands, after "I think we should remove the little indicator bar since it's visual noise and just use
the mouse style for a hand and a gripped hand for this"; and, of five choices put to him, "the choices are fine": the
three regions that start at their own height, the λ term and the source editor keeping their floor under a maximise,
the source editor scrolling inside its share, and the registers and the call stack as one region whose two panels
close each other under a maximise.

Mine, each stated in the code and listed in the design's §18.2: a boundary directly under the upper of its two
regions; no boundary while a panel is maximised, and a panel stored closed drawn open while it is; the floors of the
regions that had none; the arrow key's step; a finger's press on a header left alone; the line for a key's focus; the
term map drawn at each frame of a drag; *reset preset* keeping the shares of a view it keeps; a gesture that moves
nothing writing nothing; and, answering the review, a gesture storing the two regions it parts in the measure of the
regions that were over their floors, the source view's `✕` putting its own elements back as they are built, and a
gesture ending at its pointer's release wherever that lands.

##### THE TESTS

Six new browser files and two new node cases. `panel-boundaries.test.ts` holds the gesture on an asm view built
directly, which has three regions, so a drag has one that must not move: the boundaries drawn and named, a drag, the
floor, a pointer that overshoots a floor and comes back, the header as a handle, a press on a control, a finger, the
two hands, the keys and the reset. `panel-maximise.test.ts` holds the button and its three ways out, by the view's own
`panel` event, the one thing that writes a panel's state. `panel-regions.test.ts` holds the regions that start at
their own height, and the λ term's rows over its box at each of 75 frames of a drag on a term of 19,997 nodes.
`panel-sizes-stored.test.ts`, `panel-sizes-restore.test.ts` and `panel-sizes-restore-lambda.test.ts` hold the
workspace through the real app: one write a gesture, a view parked, a view closed, *reset preset*, and a load.

**Every drag is the driver's own where one move is enough.** Three kinds of case need more and make their own pointer
events, and each says so: a pointer that overshoots and returns, a finger, and a press that is held.

**Twenty-two cases held the source view's own box to its scroll and hold the editor's now**, in
`focus-scroll.test.ts`, `scroll-kept.test.ts` and `divider-drag-focus.test.ts`. Two changed what they hold and not
only where: a key's focus on the source view's first control is in sight wherever the editor is scrolled to, and
moves nothing. The half of that rule that moves a view is held by a new case on a TM view in a window 420 px tall.
`tm-view-narrow.test.ts`'s case at 1280 px is re-pinned for the maximise buttons, 32.78 px.

**54 sabotages on the branch, each one edit, each seen to fail the test meant for it**: 42 on the replay the plan was
cut from, one for the fix made after it, and 11 for the review's. Getting to the first 43 took three rounds. The prototype's first round had 36, of
which two failed nothing and a third failed one of the two tests meant for it; the replay's first pass had three more
that failed nothing. Four were gaps, each closed by a test: nothing held `normaliseWorkspace`'s drop of a closed
view's shares, which is *reset preset*'s road; nor a panel that a maximise hides withdrawing its offer to follow;
nor a λ view built with the shares its leaf holds; nor the term map drawn again when a maximise ends in a view too
short for its floors, which the canvas's own resize observer now does. One was a sabotage in the wrong task: with
every region of an asm view a panel, a maximise leaves no two regions open to draw a boundary between. And one was a
case that could not fail, a press in the editor after an opened link, which was removed: only a link's *undo* reaches
that defect.

**One test read a canvas between a change and its redraw.** `panel-sizes-restore-lambda.test.ts` found the term map
360 px tall holding a drawing 363 tall, once in a whole-suite run. A probe found the view's own height settling as
the page's fonts arrive, with the map drawn again at each change; the case waits for the fonts and two frames, and
the commit that first explained it otherwise says so in the one after it.

##### THE REVIEW

The user asked for "a medium review", and one reviewer read the branch at `2abe33b` without running it. It reported
ten findings, shown to him as reported; he said "fix all". Each was given a test before anything was changed, and the
first run of those tests failed nine of eleven. The design's §19 has a row for each.

- **A region with a share under 1 did not fill its view.** A share goes to `flex-grow`, and factors that add up to
  less than 1 leave the rest of the view empty: a listing dragged to a share of a half, alone once its neighbours
  were closed, ended 391.5 px short of its view's bottom, and a maximised term map with a quarter 403.5 px short.
- **A gesture stored every open region's height as its share**, a region on its floor among them, which is as tall
  as its floor whatever its share. The fix for a gesture that moves nothing had held for that one case. A gesture
  now stores the two regions its boundary parts, in the measure of the regions that were over their floors, to six
  figures where a ten-thousandth lost a small share's ratio.
- **Three things were left held.** A maximise, when its panel left the view: a copy's text maximised and its editor
  taken down left every other panel drawn closed. A gesture, when another began on another handle or when its view
  left the page under the press, since no release reached the handle and a stack that holds a gesture draws no
  boundary. And the source view's own elements, at its `✕`, which the entry before this change listed as left open.
- **A closed outline, maximised, listed the program it last showed**, and a boundary said 50 where its upper region
  was drawn at 9 of the two's hundred.

**Two findings did not reproduce as written.** The road given for a gesture held for good was a key held as its view
leaves the page, where `separator.ts` commits nothing for a separator off the page. The tests' Chromium blurs a
separator while it is still on the page, for a removal, a `replaceChildren` and a move to another parent, so that
branch is not reached in it; the same hazard was reproduced by a pointer's road and fixed there, and the stack now
ends a gesture whose handle is neither held nor focused. And the tenth, the cost of writing every share at each
change of a two-panel region's size, had nothing to measure: two changes of a view's width wrote no region's style.
The work was taken out all the same.

**One of the eleven sabotages of these fixes failed nothing at first**: what a pixel is worth taken from every region
with a share, one on its floor among them. A case with a region on its floor beside one over its own holds it.

##### WHAT THIS DID NOT CLOSE

- **One review has read this branch, and it did not run it.** The first pull request had eight reviews and three
  rounds of fixes (the design's §17). The fixes for this one's findings have been read by their author alone.
- A gesture whose handle is neither held nor focused is ended by the stack (`panel-stack.ts`'s `#alive`), for a
  browser that blurs a separator after it has left the page. No test runs that branch: the tests' browser blurs
  first.
- WebKit is unmeasured, as before. A finger's drag of a boundary was made with the tests' own pointer events and on
  no phone.
- Above the λ term and the source editor there is no header, so the 8 px strip is the one handle there and the

  on this branch, which does not change that code: after one step the row's scroll box was another element and its
  `scrollLeft` had gone from 40 to 0.
- The design's five open points (§16.3) are as they were.

#### UNDER `--coverage` A BROWSER TEST FILE'S PAGE IS COLLECTED WHEN THE NEXT FILE STARTS, WHERE V8'S PRECISE COVERAGE KEPT EVERY PAGE A TAB HAD RUN, WITH ITS WEBASSEMBLY MEMORIES, UNTIL THE SLOWER CI RUNNER'S TABS HAD NO ROOM LEFT FOR ONE (2026-10-13, branch `coverage-collects-pages`, `ef4c9df..276b7ad`, 2 commits, plus this entry)

**`main` was red after #142's merge.** Run 569, `ef4c9df`, failed its `web` job twice on CI's slower runner
(`450440e2`), and `docker` needs `web`, so no image was published for it. The first attempt failed
`lambda-deep-outline.test.ts` and two cases of `share-open-start-clamp.test.ts`, the second
`lambda-deep-code.test.ts`; each deep-term case printed what its page read, by the diagnostic #141 added: `redextape
hit a problem and recovered: WebAssembly.instantiate(): Out of memory: Cannot allocate Wasm memory for new instance`.
The pull request's own run of the same tree, 568, had passed on the faster runner (`4360ddec`). Run 563, on #141, had
failed `lambda-deep-outline.test.ts` on the slower runner too, before the diagnostic existed; that it was the same
cause is an inference.

##### THE CAUSE

- **One renderer process has room for 123 or 124 WebAssembly memories, and a worker's count against its page's.** A
  probe page made one-page memories until one was refused: 123. A worker then made none while the page held them,
  and the page none while a worker held 123. The app, mounted and compiled, holds four.
- **CI runs `pnpm run test:coverage`, and under coverage no finished page was ever collected.** Vitest starts V8's
  precise coverage once in each tab and never stops it (`@vitest/coverage-v8`'s browser module: "Browser mode should
  not stop coverage as same V8 instance is shared between tests"), and while it is on V8 holds every feedback vector
  as a root (`Coverage::SelectMode` in V8's `debug-coverage.cc`: "Root all feedback vectors to avoid early
  collection"). #116's `gc()` at each file's start freed nothing. Eight files in one tab: the earlier pages alive at
  each start 0, 1 … 7, the JS heap 15.5 MiB to 83.6, the room for memories 124 to 112, every page after the first
  keeping two.
- **The slower runner runs three files at once, about seventy to a tab; the faster runs eleven, about nineteen.**
  Counted from the job logs' finishing times and durations. The browser suite grew from 174 files at `7cbac7d` to 211
  and 217 over the two view-layouts pull requests, and the last slower-runner run to pass whole was 566, at 274 files.
- **Reproduced here in two tabs.** Stock `main`, the whole coverage gate in two tabs: 55 of 280 files and 37 tests
  failed, the message among their errors. The same without coverage passed every file, with at least 119 of the room
  left at every file's start.

##### WHAT CHANGED

- **`tests/browser/collect.ts`, the browser project's first setup file**, takes #116's collection and its doc out of
  `setup.ts`, and under coverage stops precise coverage before it and starts it again after, with the settings Vitest
  uses. Vitest takes each file's coverage as that file finishes, before the next file's setup, so nothing counted is
  lost.
- **A last-resort collection before coverage starts again.** Stopping precise coverage takes the block counters off
  every compiled function (`Coverage::SelectMode`: "any following coverage recording (without reloads) will be at
  function granularity"), and the next page compiling the same module took those functions from V8's compilation
  cache: the report fell from 97.59 / 92.19 / 98.39 / 98.92 to 96.01 / 89.00 / 98.39 / 97.45 in one run, which the
  floors passed, and to 94.95 / 86.84 / 98.39 / 96.64 in another, which they failed. A last-resort `gc`
  (`Heap::CollectAllAvailableGarbage`, which clears the compilation cache) gives back the stock report, file by file.
- **`sequence.setupFiles: 'list'`** at the config's root, so `collect.ts` finishes before `setup.ts`'s imports from
  `src` begin; Vitest's default imports every setup file at once, and reads this option from the root alone.
- **`tests/browser/global-setup.ts`** hands the pages `coverageOn`, the resolved config's answer, since a page cannot
  read the run's settings and starting precise coverage in a run without it would put the leak back.
- **A guard: a file fails when more than eight pages of earlier files in its tab are still alive after the
  collection**, naming them. Weak references on the orchestrator's page, made with that page's constructors.

##### DECISIONS

Mine:

- **The harness, not CI's settings.** More tabs on the slower runner, or fewer files, would move the point where a tab
  runs out and leave every page alive.
- **A last-resort collection, not `--js-flags=--no-compilation-cache`**, which also gave the stock report: the flag
  would apply to every run, the probes' heap measurements among them, and the collection only to runs with coverage.
- **Eight pages.** At most three were alive at any of 1,260 file starts with the fix's collection; the leak adds one
  a file, so eight trips at a tab's tenth file, on either runner.
- **The guard's list is made with the orchestrator's constructors**, measured: a `WeakRef` of the page's own realm,
  held by the orchestrator, kept every page alive without coverage, and the guard failed files 10 to 12 of 12.

##### THE TESTS

No test file changes; the guard is the check, and three sabotages of the final `collect.ts`, each one edit, fired.
With the restart taken out, a whole coverage run in twelve tabs failed 104 browser files on the guard, every file from
a tab's tenth on. With the last-resort collection taken out, the coverage gate failed at 94.95 / 86.84 / 98.39 /
96.64. With the guard's `WeakRef` made by the page itself, twelve files in one tab without coverage kept every page,
and the guard failed the last three.

**With the fix, the whole coverage gate passed in one tab, with all 210 browser files in a row (607.50 s), in two
(300.65 s), and in three under a CPU quota of one and a half cores (401.07 s)**, each with the stock report, file by
file.

##### WHAT THIS DID NOT CLOSE

- **Nothing has run on the slower runner.** That needs a push. `ef4c9df` has no image, and a rerun of its run would
  meet the same leak.
- **Why three tabs ran out on CI and not here.** Stock `main` in three tabs under coverage passed here, with 6, 10 and
  14 of the room left at the tabs' last files; the runner's own room was not measured.
- **The order of the setup files is held by nothing.** Three runs of the collection with Vitest's default order gave
  the stock report too; `'list'` is what keeps that from resting on timing.
- **A coverage report that falls and stays above the floors would pass.** One run without the last-resort collection
  did.
- **The room for 123 memories was measured on this machine's Chromium**, the one Playwright installs here and on both
  runners.

#### THE PROBE BINARIES SHARE ONE COPY OF MOST HELPERS WHOSE CODE THEY CARRIED IDENTICALLY, UNDER `examples/common/`, WHERE EACH CARRIED ITS OWN, AND THE `FIRST_ORDER_DEMOS` SYNC TEST READS THAT ONE FILE (2026-10-17, branch `probe-support`, `82dc507..a7ae64a`, 6 commits, plus this entry and the two commits that correct it)

**This is PR A of the comments-and-repeats plan.** The probe binaries under `crates/redextape-core/examples/` each
carried their own copies of small helpers. Ten shared files under `examples/common/` now hold one copy of each, and
the probes include them with `#[path = "common/<name>.rs"] mod <name>;` and, except for `allocator.rs`
(nothing names `ALLOC`), a `use` naming the items the probe calls (`inherit_probe.rs` names `median` and reaches
`percentile` through it). No probe was run.

##### WHAT MOVED, AND THE RULE THAT MOVED IT

- **The plan's rule was byte-identical, comments included; the user's rulings changed it to code-identical.** The
  first dispatch found only `line` and `head` byte-identical, so it stopped. The user ruled that identical CODE is one
  copy and doc comments may differ (ruling 1), and after the whole-branch review that the rule covers EVERY
  code-identical top-level item under `examples/`, not only the plan table's rows (ruling 6).
- **`common/demos.rs`**: `FIRST_ORDER_DEMOS`, for concurrency, lambda_sharing, list_reduction and state_cost.
- **`common/text.rs` and `common/text_underlined.rs`**: `line` plus its own `head` each (the `=== s ===` variant for
  blowup, guard_hole and list_reduction; the dash-rule variant for frame_cost, inherit, none and owner). `line` stays
  defined in both, by ruling 4.
- **`common/footprint.rs`** (`peak_rss_kb`, `physical`, `lower_src`), **`common/depth.rs`**,
  **`common/nested_groups.rs`**, **`common/web_budget.rs`**, **`common/tag_census.rs`** (`programs`,
  `count_tagged_apps`, `fmt_pct`), **`common/nearest_rank.rs`** (`percentile`, `median`) and
  **`common/allocator.rs`** (the three-line global allocator, in 12 examples).
- **The doc rule.** The shared file keeps the one doc comment that gives the why. History and measurements from the
  deleted copies' docs moved word for word to `docs/superpowers/notes/2026-10-17-code-history-probes.md`, naming the
  file and line each sat above before the move; docs that only said "COPIED from" were dropped.
- **The sync test.** `tests/three_way_oracle.rs`'s four probe rows became one `examples/common/demos.rs` row, and the
  test is renamed `first_order_demos_stay_synced_across_every_copy`, with every citation outside `docs/` updated.
- **Comments the move left pointing at nothing** got the smallest wording change that names what they meant, adding no
  fact: a prose list of probe files in `guard_counterexamples.rs`, and others found by two sibling searches. Three
  "examples cannot share" claims the move made false were deleted, not reworded: two in `inherit_probe.rs`, which went
  to the notes with their docs, and one in `step_survey.rs`.

##### HOW EACH MOVE WAS PROVEN

- **Identical code.** For every moved item a script extracted the code of every copy (definition line to closing
  line, doc comments excluded, `pub(crate) ` stripped) and compared it with the shared file's; all matched. A later
  enumeration of every top-level item under `examples/` (516 items) found no remaining code-identical group but the
  `mod` include lines, `beta_allocs_fused` and `line`.
- **Each shared file is used in full and is load-bearing.** Renaming one item in each shared file broke the build of
  exactly that file's includers and no other example, with `cargo build -p redextape-core --examples --keep-going`.
  Renaming `ALLOC` built cleanly, since nothing names it, so the allocator was checked another way: the release
  binaries of exactly the 12 includers contain mimalloc's strings and the other 7 contain none. An unused item
  appended to a shared file made clippy fail all its includers.
- **The sync test fires.** A one-character defect in `FIRST_ORDER_DEMOS` in `common/demos.rs` made
  `first_order_demos_stay_synced_across_every_copy` fail; restored, it passes.
- Both results are the implementer's report's, not rerun for this entry.

##### WHAT THIS DID NOT CLOSE

- **Among the items left in place because the code differs** (the report's enumeration table lists the rest): `beta_allocs_fused` (its callee `shift_allocs` differs by an inline
  comment, and its doc names `subst_allocs_today` in one copy); `shift_cost_probe.rs`'s `line` (`.ok()` where the
  shared one has `let _ =`); blowup's `physical` (an inline comment on `continue`); `fmt_count` (each of three prints a
  saturated count differently); `steps_at` and `measure` in step_survey (an expect message, an inline comment,
  different fields); and step_survey's own `FIRST_ORDER_DEMOS` (same literals, plus inline comments, held by the sync
  test). `line` is defined twice under `examples/`, once in each text file, by ruling 4.
- **Comments left for Part C.** step_survey's history sentence about "four" and "the fifth" was moved to the notes;

#### THE TESTS TAKE A HELPER THEY REPEATED FROM ONE SHARED COPY, IN `harness.ts`, 24 OTHER SHARED TEST MODULES OR THE TEST MODULE THAT HELD THE COPIES, WHERE EACH CARRIED ITS OWN, WHEN THE COPIES ARE THE SAME CODE OR DIFFER IN LITERAL VALUES THAT ARE NOT THE WHOLE HELPER; A COPY OF ANOTHER SHAPE, A COPY THAT READS STATE ITS FILE OR TEST OWNS, A COPY INSIDE ANOTHER HELPER AND A COPY THAT WOULD NEED A PRODUCTION ITEM MADE PUBLIC STAY WHERE THEY WERE (2026-10-18, branch `test-helpers`, `1abfdd9..195cf8b`, 109 commits, plus this entry)

**This is PR B of the comments-and-repeats plan.** The browser and node tests under `web/tests/`, the Rust integration
tests and the `#[cfg(test)]` modules each carried their own copies of small helpers. They now take one shared copy
from `web/tests/browser/harness.ts`, from 24 other shared test modules (18 of them new), or from the test module that
held the copies. Outside test code the branch changes two comments, by the user's ruling of 2026-10-18, and adds one
notes file. B4 was run again at `195cf8b`: it lists the same 1,903 Rust and 2,906 web tests as `main` at `1abfdd9`,
and the 93 Rust and 98 web production files `coverage_diff.py` compares on both sides cover the same lines, with
`tm.rs`'s lines 25-460 compared by a separate check (below). The lane record is
`~/temp/redextape-comment-pass-record/` (`R` below); its ledger is `progress-part-b.md`.

##### THE RULINGS THAT SET WHAT COUNTS AS ONE COPY

- **The user's rulings of 2026-10-17** (`b-constraints.md` in the lane record):
  - **Scope (1):** the plan's two tables (B2's 11 Rust clusters, B3's 8 browser clusters) plus every extra helper in
    the lane's list E01-E29, literal differences parameterised.
  - **One copy (2):** the same code is one copy and doc comments may differ; copies that differ in literal values
    share one helper with those values as parameters; a copy whose shape differs stays and is named.
  - **Shape (2, after B3b):** an extra or missing member in an object literal, or an extra statement, is a shape
    difference. Such a copy keeps its own local copy rather than sharing through an override or spread parameter.
  - **Copies against each other (2, after the shape fix wave's re-review):** copies identical to their siblings stay
    shared even where the helper spells out a file-local function every copy called (`drag`, `pressTab`, `compile`),
    copies with `inertEvents`' members share it although they never had its `over` parameter, and a local variable
    against a computed number of the same value is a value difference.
  - **Docs (3):** the shared helper keeps the one doc that gives the why; history and measurements from the other
    copies' docs move word for word to the area's notes file (this branch needed only
    `docs/superpowers/notes/2026-10-17-code-history-web-tests.md`); "copied from" docs are dropped.
  - **Comments the move left false (4)** get the smallest wording change that names what they mean now. All other
    comment trimming waits for Part C.
  - **No production code change (5).** A share that would need a production item made `pub` does not happen, and the
    copy stays.
  - **Proof (6):** a hand-applied defect in each shared helper must fail at least one test from each former copy's
    file. A defect that fails none is a finding to report.
  - **Counts, commits, citations (7-9):** each cluster's test counts equal the baseline's; commits per cluster or file
    with the hooks run; no `file:line` in tracked source.
- **The user's later rulings of 2026-10-17:** share the 39 state-only `idle` copies in this PR; then, for the

##### HOW THE COPIES WERE FOUND, AND THE ENUMERATOR'S KEY FIX

- **The enumerator** (its Method is in `$R/sweep-list.md`; scripts in `$R/sweep-scratch/`) parses every
  `web/tests/**/*.ts` with `@babel/parser` and keys each helper four ways: `exact`; `strip`, without type annotations;
  `id`, with parameters and locals renamed; and `lit`, with literal values abstracted and object keys kept. A free
  name is keyed by what it resolves to. A lexer walks the module-level fns of the Rust `tests/` trees, the
  `#[cfg(test)]` modules and the shared modules. At `00e7970` it listed 193 shareable clusters (187 TypeScript, 6
  Rust) in 9 batches, 9 clusters that read file or test state for a ruling, and 52 families where the literal is the
  whole helper.
- **The key fix.** S8 found that the `id` key never equated a block-body arrow with a `function`, as the Method said
  it did. A `const f = …` helper counted its own name as local `$L0`, so its parameters and locals numbered one higher
  than the same `function`'s; and an expression body keyed as `{ return v.dispatch(…) }` where the statement form
  keyed as `{ v.dispatch(…) }`. That is why `replaceDoc` and `retype` became two exports, and why lsp-format's
  `retype` and parked-view-surfaces' `pinAt` were missed. The fixed key is built from the function node, renames
  locals by first appearance, and counts a final `return call` as `call;`. It adds a call of a `web/tests` helper
  spelled out as its body, `{ a }` as `{ a: a }`, a `lift` key (a file `let` the helper reads becomes a leading
  parameter), an `arg` key (a parameter or constant where a sibling has a literal) and an exported-twin check.
- **The fix was proven before its output was used.** It found 8 of 8 known misses at the commits where each existed,
  and the original key's 21 `id` groups and 91 `lit` groups stay whole under it. At `41cb3a7` it found 20 more
  clusters (33 copies in 20 files), one exported TypeScript twin (`clickShowToggle`), and confirmed the 8 shape
  differences listed below by key.
- **What the twin check missed.** The whole-sweep review found `termEditorCount`, which is `editorsOf` with
  `termEditorsIn`'s body written out; `5872270` deleted it.
- **Nested Rust fns.** The Rust walker read module-level fns only, so a fn declared inside a test was in no list;
  fact-check B found the hole through `viewmodel_contract.rs`'s nested `spin_right`, which B2a had left. A follow-up
  enumerator (`$R/rust-nested-scratch/rust_nested.py`, a copy of the walker) also reads the items declared inside each
  module-level fn of a test file or shared module, and the test fns of each `proptest!` block. At `ae67509` it found
  35 nested non-test fns: 31 in scope, inside a `#[test]` or `#[wasm_bindgen_test]` fn, and 4 out, inside a non-test
  helper. It adds an `id` key, which renames bound names as the TypeScript `id` key renames parameters and locals, and
  `idlit`, which is `id` with literals abstracted. Groups holding a nested fn: none by `exact` or `lit`, and 1 by
  `id`, `unary.rs`'s nested `cmp` with its test module's `cmp`, which `idlit` also groups and to which it adds none.
  At module level `id` joins no rows that `exact` splits, so it finds nothing there the sweep missed. A similarity
  ranking and a hand comparison found the second share: `spin_right` differs from `one_rule_machine` in values alone
  under ruling 2 (`tapes: 1` against `rule.read.len()`, which is 1 here; `"go"` against `name`; the `Rule` literal
  against `rule`), which no Rust key abstracts.
- **How the follow-up was proven.** Its 522 module-level rows are byte-identical to the old walker's output at
  `ae67509`. A completeness check accounts for the `fn` tokens in test-context files, with 11 left over, none in test
  code. In a scratch copy of the tree, a pasted verbatim copy of `one_rule_machine` grouped by `exact` with both of
  its homes, and a copy of `core_of` with its locals renamed and one literal changed grouped by `idlit`. After the two
  shares, core's 1,319 tests with `--features serde` match the baseline per binary, and a defect in each shared helper
  fails a test in the file that newly calls it: `viewmodel_contract.rs`'s
  `the_window_costs_the_same_regardless_of_how_large_the_tape_has_grown` and `unary.rs`'s
  `comparison_trichotomy_sweep`. These are the follow-up's report, not rerun for this entry.
- **The old walker's other blind spot.** Its test-attribute pattern misses `#[wasm_bindgen_test]`, so it counted the
  33 wasm tests in `redextape-wasm/tests/browser.rs` as helpers. None shares an `exact` or `lit` key with another row,
  so the sweep's list did not change.

#### COMMENTS IN `crates/`, `scripts/`, `.forgejo/`, THE GRAMMARS AND THE ROOT CONFIG FILES KEEP THEIR WHY, AND THE HISTORY AND MEASUREMENTS THEY CARRIED ARE IN SIX PER-AREA NOTES FILES OR GONE; EIGHTEEN CODE COMMITS FIX A BLIND TEST GUARD, TWO PRIVATE COPIES OF `lower_program` AND THE PRINTED STRINGS, MESSAGES AND TEST NAMES THAT CARRIED HISTORY OR FALSE CLAIMS (2026-10-20, branch `comments-crates`, `630248f..df71626`, 92 commits, plus this entry)

**This is PR C of the comments-and-repeats plan.** It applies the user's comment rule of 2026-10-17 to the comments in
`crates/`, `scripts/` and `.forgejo/`, and by rulings (w) and (z) to the repo-root config files and the grammars'

changes. History and measurements left the comments. Text a future editor could need moved verbatim into six notes
files, `docs/superpowers/notes/2026-10-17-code-history-<area>.md` for `core`, `core-tests`, `probes`, `wasm-native`,

##### HOW THE COMMENTS WERE CHECKED

The method ran in four stages: keyword-cut chunks with reviews, regex scans for history, a full read, then reviews of
the fix commits. Its limit is that a read is one reader's judgement: reviews kept finding false claims that a fix had
written, a review's own drafted fix among them (`$R/c/F-Bfix-1-review.md` I-1), and the last fix of each lane was
self-checked, not reviewed.

- **Chunks.** Task C0 cut 1,033 flagged blocks into nine chunks; by ruling, `unlisted-01` (150 blocks) and
  `unlisted-02` (105 with process labels) followed. A Sonnet implementer ran `check_comment_only.py 630248f` and
  `check_moves.py` (built in the lane, not committed), then a Sonnet task review. `check_moves.py` checks each moved
  paragraph against the comments at `630248f`, case-sensitive, and flags added comment lines over 120 columns and
  one-word orphans.
- **Whole-PR review.** At `1c97b3a` an Opus review of a 321-block sample found 20 Important defects; 3 of the random
  tenth's 75 blocks were Important, so ruling (d) put Opus on the other 464 changed blocks, which found 36 more. An
  enumerator kept 979 pointer sentences into files whose comments changed; Opus verifiers read the 308 it marked
  LIKELY-DANGLING or UNSURE and 20 of the 671 it marked LANDS: 20 CONFIRMED, 18 PRE-EXISTING, 290 FALSE. Fix wave 3
  took 219 items in seven area commits; Opus reviews of its diff found 7 more Important, and of `unlisted-02` 7.
- **Printed strings.** CODE-10's scan at `2ebc223` matched 483 strings and judged them: 13 LABEL, 28 HISTORY, 1 STALE,
  441 LEGIT.
- **History scans (ruling q).** A regex scan at `855c3be` judged 819 hits: 250 HISTORY and 1 FALSE, in 206 blocks. A
  second scan at `f2bd834`, for forms the first missed, judged 469: 74 HISTORY and 2 FALSE, in 70 blocks. Chunks H1
  `f2bd834`, H1b `6d8998c`, H2 `67787f9`, H3a `68b604b`, H3b `4abbd82` and H4 `abee2d2` fixed them, each with an Opus
  review. The H3a and H3b reviews read their files whole and found about 45 more each that neither scan matched, so
  the class needed a read, not a wider regex.
- **The full read (ruling u).** Ten readers took the files under `crates/`, `scripts/` and `.forgejo/` that had a
  comment line at `abee2d2` (`.rs`, shell, YAML, TOML, text, `.gitignore` and proptest-regressions files) and that no
  chunk review had read whole: 176 files in nine slices, 57 more having been read whole. A tenth slice held the nine
  root config files (ruling w), and one more dispatch read and fixed the eight grammar files (ruling z). The ten
  wrote 709 finding rows (history, measurements, labels, false claims), and the grammar dispatch 28. Not read:
  fixtures (`.rxt`, `.tm`, `.asm`, `.stdout`, `.stderr`), Markdown and JSON under those directories.
- **The fix phase.** Lane A fixed core `src/` and `tests/` in 9 commits, `b96f5ab` to `c7b421c`. Lane B fixed the core
  examples, the other crates, the grammars, the scripts, CI and the root files in 10 commits, cherry-picked as
  `b64557e` to `087f326`. Each of the 34 commits after `2ebc223` has a review in `$R/c/`; `c7b421c` and `087f326`,
  each lane's last, applied a narrow review's drafted fixes and then had a narrow review of their own
  (`$R/c/F-closing-review.md`). The rows that were printed strings,
  messages or test names went to CODE-14.
