##### THE CHECKER

`check_comment_only.py` and its `lexer.py` sit in `.superpowers/sdd/comment-pass/`, gitignored, as the plan decided.
It lexes shell, and it counts a trailing YAML `#` comment as code, so `ci.yml`'s one runner comment is CODE CHANGED.

- **Fence pins.** `ALLOWED_FENCE_EDITS` holds 7 entries: ruling (c)'s `list_reduction_probe` fence (re-pinned by
  (i)), the rewritten `blowup_probe` and `guard_hole_probe` fences, and four removals (`lambda_sharing_probe`'s GATE
  fence, `shift_cost_probe`'s three tables). The real check skips the fence test on a file whose code changed, so
  each pin was proven at `630248f` in a tree whose one change was that fence: exit 0, a one-word change exits 1, and
  the restored copy is `cmp`-identical. The self-test passes 52 of 52.
- **A `.gitignore` reader.** The lexer reads a line whose first character is `#` as a comment, per gitignore(5).
- **The comment-only proof** (`$R/c/proof-final-report.md`). In a scratch worktree at `df71626`, `git revert
  --no-commit` of the 19 code-list commits, newest first, stopped twice, at `aa5f946` (`list_reduction_probe.rs`)
  and `0d873f2` (`outline.rs`). Both conflicts were comment regions, resolved to `df71626`'s comment text, and four
  of `aa5f946`'s comment hunks were set back to it so the pinned fence matches. The live checker run with `630248f`
  then reports 0 CODE CHANGED and 0 fence FAILs; its FAIL lines are the 9 files it has no lexer for. A one-token
  change in `outline.rs` and a one-word change in `guard_hole_probe`'s pinned fence were refused, then restored
  `cmp`-identical. Checked one by one, none of the 73 commits outside the list changes a code token.

**This is PR D of the comments-and-repeats plan, its last.** It applies the user's comment rule of 2026-10-17 to the
comments in `web/` (`web/src/`, `web/tests/`, `web/scripts/` and `web/vite.config.ts`): a comment holds the reason, the
invariant and what breaks if it changes. History and measurements left the comments. Text a future editor could need
moved verbatim into `docs/superpowers/notes/2026-10-17-code-history-web-src.md` and `…-web-tests.md`; the rest was
dropped. The read also reached nine doc comments in four `crates/` files (three by ruling D6, one a code review found
false, and five by ruling D14: `tmText`'s wrapper doc and four `amendment N` citations), the `ci.yml` comment that
pointed at `vite.config.ts`'s cut measurements, and `check-attributions.sh`'s account of the two markers that left

lane record is `~/temp/redextape-comment-pass-record/` (`R` below); its ledger is `R/d/ledger.md`.

##### HOW THE COMMENTS WERE CHECKED

The method ran in five stages: a read of the chunks with a task review each; a dangling-pointer enumeration; a
whole-branch review of a sample and then of the changed blocks it left; three class enumerations, which with the reviews
fed one fix round in two lanes; and a cross-lane check and two citation audits of the result. Its limit is that a read
is one reader's judgement, and fixes write new errors: the D12 audit found 16 citations that the fix round's own
in-place names had made inherit the wrong design, and the review of the commit that fixed them found a sentence it had
named quoting a 5d-i rule that the 5d-iii design reverses. The whole review found 2 Important in the 170 blocks of its
every-tenth sample of changed blocks, the remainder review 29 in 1,112, and most were false at `4687e79` already,
several in text the branch kept; no sample measured the rate in the 4,490 blocks the branch left unchanged.

- **Chunks (ruling D1).** `R/d/cut.py` split the 6,188 comment blocks in `web/` into 29 chunks of up to about 200 KB of
  source: 11 for `web/src/`, `web/scripts/` and `web/vite.config.ts` (lane S) and 18 for `web/tests/` (lane T). An Opus
  implementer read each chunk's files whole and decided its comments; an Opus task review followed each chunk, and each
  lane batched the reviews' findings into fix commits, each but fix T7 (a byte-identical restore) with a narrow review
  of its own. Lane S made 23 commits (11 chunks, 12 fixes), lane T 38 (18 and 20), and lane T's were cherry-picked onto
  `comments-web`, ending at `0b398c2`. For scale: the plan's keyword cut listed 1,340 of the blocks, and Part C's
  history patterns hit 424 it did not list.
- **Dangling pointers.** At `936e63a` (now `0b398c2`) an enumerator kept 1,100 of 3,155 pointer sentences, marking 19
  LIKELY-DANGLING, 401 UNSURE (92 of them crossing lanes) and 680 LANDS, and checked 201 notes headings and 47 twins. A
  first judging found 5 CONFIRMED and 12 PRE-EXISTING; verify batches over the 309 same-lane UNSURE rows and the 37
  twins it left found 4 and 12 more.
- **Whole-branch review.** By call (h), seven Opus reviewers read a reduced sample at `2afc7b7`: every tenth changed
  block (170), every block a fix touched (346) and every block a review named under a finding, 743 blocks; they found 16
  Important. By ruling D8, twelve more read the 1,112 changed blocks the sample did not hold, which with the sample's
  586 changed blocks make the 1,698 the branch changed, and found 29 Important.
- **Class enumerations.** A-B, a pointer that credits another doc with a reason (A) or a test with what it proves (B):
  2,272 candidate sentences, 155 FALSE; a recall pass (calls (j), (j') and (j'')) then read the 976 sentences the
  patterns had dropped, the 157 with no backtick and 9 in a widened possessive form, and found about 10 more FALSE. C-D,
  citations and labels: 1,372 `§` and `decision N` citations and 88 `amendment N` at `2afc7b7`, with 9 WRONG, 125
  inheriting the wrong design and 175 made bare by the branch (ruling D12), and 29 history labels among 44 sightings. E,
  leg counts: 385 lines, 44 FALSE, 36 comment-only and 8 test names or messages (CODE-K).
- **The fix round.** One worklist merged the review findings, the enumerations' rows and the carried rows: 1,117 rows,
  1,107 live, at 523 sites. By call (m) it ran in two lanes, FS in the main checkout (`web/src/`, the root files, the D6
  docs and the web-src notes; 11 commits, `918d7cf` to `1aab3c6`) and FT in a worktree (`web/tests/` and the web-tests
  notes; 9 commits, `3dca394` to `5a30787`, cherry-picked), each commit with a narrow review; from FS3 and FT3 on, each
  group was split into halves of about 20 to 28 sites (call (n)). A comment fix inside a code commit's revert context
  went into that code commit as a fixup (fixups-1, FIXUP-2), and `R/d/fix/revert_check.sh` replayed the code commits'
  reverts with `git merge-tree` after each fix commit.
- **Audits.** `b589b47` (XL) applied the FS-END review's findings and checked 22 cross-lane pointer groups, which all
  landed. The D12 audit re-ran C-D's classifier with the file-doc rule at `dfa14f9`, the FT head that FIXUP-2 and the
  rewords rewrote as `5a30787`: 0 WRONG, 22 wrong-inheritance and 10 made bare, the 32 rows `547d668` fixes. The
  provenance audit asked whether a design a citation now names postdates the commit that brought the citation in: of
  1,537 tokens, 908 named and 412 whose name is new since `4687e79`, 4 meet the date rule and 0 are misnamed (the
  5d-ii-c commit `560d465` rewrote each sentence round them). `f1bb04c` took the D12F review's findings and `10fe9c4`
  code review 4's Minors.
- **Code reviews.** Five reviews (`R/d/code-review-1.md` to `-5.md`) and one of fixups-1 read the code commits at their
  SHAs. The fourth, over FIXUP-2, D12G, CODE-J, L, K and J2, approved with 0 Important and 3 Minor. The fifth, over
  `8a98b6d`, `932c135` and CODE-M, N and O, found 1 Important and 3 Minor, which R5 took (`R/d/fix/R5-report.md`):
  fixups into CODE-N and CODE-O, now `03bd897` and `500ecfa`, and the comment-only `332e5a2`; R5's own review
  (`R/d/fix/R5-review.md`) approved with 0 Important and 0 Minor, and its one note, three bare "spec amendment 13" in
  `crates/`, led to `9f0da7e`.

#### THE WEB-TESTS NOTES HOLD `app.test.ts`'S ENTRIES IN ONE RUN, THE TWO WEB NOTES FILES START AND END EACH PARAGRAPH WHERE ITS SOURCE SENTENCE DOES, AND THE FIVE BARE `spec amendment N` CITATIONS IN `crates/` NAME THEIR SPEC (2026-10-21, branch `notes-and-amendments`, `fc0a8e7..10937ef`, 7 commits, plus this entry)

**This closes two items in Part D's WHAT THIS DID NOT CLOSE** (the `#### COMMENTS IN \`web/\`` entry), "Notes order
(ruling D15)" and "Two `spec amendment N` with no part outside this PR's files", **and the two classes they belong to**:
every bare amendment citation in `crates/`, and every paragraph in the two web notes files that the move cut
mid-sentence. Ruling D15 left the move out of Part D only because it conflicted with a revert check that PR ran; the
user has since asked for it. No commit changes code: four edit the notes, three edit comments.

##### THE NOTES ORDER

- **`1b80f96` moves one entry.** The entry above `app.test.ts`'s `it('reports the absence when a construct emits no
  instructions or machine states', ...` sat after `buffers-quota-restored.test.ts`'s entry; it now follows the
  `app.test.ts` entry above `it('marks the contractum the step produced, and nothing at step 0', ...`, so each source
  file's entries in `docs/superpowers/notes/2026-10-17-code-history-web-tests.md` form one run. The commit is Part D's
  `R/d/fix/X7-work/item6.patch`, applied unchanged.
- **It is a pure move.** Four lines (the heading, its paragraph and two blank lines) left old lines 252-255 and are new
  lines 67-70; the file's lines, sorted, are byte-identical before and after the commit.
- **Nothing points at the entry by position.** The lines outside the notes that name the notes file name an entry by the
  code line it sat above, or name only the file; none gives a line number, and no entry in the file refers to another as
  above or below it.

##### THE CUT SENTENCES

- **`4bf5ce7`, `86d9fe2` and `10937ef` start and end each paragraph of the two web notes files where a sentence of its
  source comment does.** The source is the comment the paragraph was moved from, in the file its entry's heading names,
  at `4687e79`, the commit before #147 (which created the web-src notes and wrote every web-tests entry but the 8 #145
  had), its lines joined. Where the source sentence went on past the paragraph's end, or began before its start, the
  rest is restored word for word, even where the comment still carries that text today. `4bf5ce7` is the first,
  `buffers-quota-restored.test.ts`'s "the SAME assertion the crash would have failed,"; `10937ef` is the five starts
  that followed a colon inside their source sentence (below); `86d9fe2` is every other. Of the 80 paragraphs the range
  changes, 76 were one line at `fc0a8e7` and are one line now; the other 4 were hard-wrapped and keep their lines, each
  with a restored start broken where its source comment breaks its lines.
- **Ends.** At `fc0a8e7`, 22 paragraphs in the web-tests notes and 14 in the web-src notes ended on a comma, a
  semicolon, a dash, a colon or a word. 33 of those 36 ends are restored, each by the text that followed it in its
  source sentence: 29 at the end of a paragraph, and 4 between two paragraphs that the restore joins, where the next
  paragraph of the same entry was the end of the same sentence with the middle dropped (three in web-tests, at "it does
  not, and could not:", "which is structural:" and "That measured almost nothing:"; one in web-src's `colour.ts` entry).
  Web-src's `licences.ts` entry was a clause from a list item, and its sentence is the whole four-item list of toolchain
  licences, restored whole.
- **Starts.** 61 starts are restored: the 48 paragraphs that began with a lowercase letter once the ends were restored
  (52 at `fc0a8e7`, four of them absorbed by the joins above), and 13 that began mid-sentence with a dash, a bracket, a
  backtick, a digit or a capital letter, which a lowercase scan cannot see. Five of the 13 began just after a colon
  inside their source sentence, which an earlier version of the verifier below counted as a sentence end: web-tests'
  `app.test.ts` entry after "FIX 4's REGRESSION GUARD:", and web-src's `base16-adjust.ts`, `colour.ts`, `layout.ts` and
  `scratch.ts` entries after "which then steps over it:", "costs more:", "not of its share:" and "Since then a TM copy
  is:". Where a source sentence opens with a bold or capitalised label (`**WHAT IS HELD IS ...**`, `THROUGH \`settled\`,
  FOR ITS THREE WAITS:`, `FIX 4's REGRESSION GUARD:`), the label is part of the sentence and is restored with it; for
  web-tests' "whole-branch review before merge, finding 5." that is the bold run `**HOW TO RUN IT: \`pnpm test:probe\`.
  IT IS NOT IN THE DEFAULT SUITE, AND THAT IS DELIBERATE — ... finding 5.**`, its closing `**` included.
- **The verifier** (`verify_restored.py` in the record directory) reads each source as its comment blocks only:
  a `/* */` comment, or a run of `//` comments on consecutive lines, each line's marker stripped and the lines joined,
  so code is never read and no match spans two blocks. It checks that every paragraph that differs from `fc0a8e7` occurs
  whole inside one comment block of its source; that every paragraph found in a block starts and ends a sentence at one
  or more of its occurrences there (the text before it ends one at a full stop, a question or exclamation mark, a table
  row, a fence or a list bullet, or at a colon only where the paragraph opens a list, as a paragraph may end on a colon
  only where a list follows it; or it opens the block; and the text after it starts one or the block ends); and that no
  paragraph starts lowercase or ends without a full stop, except a table row and a paragraph that opens the list after
  it. One start is exempt by name, web-src's "**THE READINGS ARE ONE RUN OF THAT COMMAND ...", which follows a command
  line the source sets on its own line. Its `--self-test` checks the block reader on a fixed snippet and corrupts the
  notes five ways, and passes only when each is caught: one word of a restored paragraph changed fails as not verbatim,
  its first word dropped as starting inside a source sentence, its last word dropped as ending inside one, a changed
  paragraph replaced by the end of one comment block of `app.test.ts` joined to the start of the next, which only blank
  lines separate, as not verbatim, and the `app.test.ts` paragraph whose start `10937ef` restores, cut back to the text
  after "FIX 4's REGRESSION GUARD:", as starting inside a source sentence.
- **Three paragraphs still end without a full stop, and stay**: two introduce the numbered lists that follow them, in
  the source too (`buffer-affordability.test.ts`'s "FIXED HERE:**" and "SELF-EVIDENT:**"), and one is a markdown table
  row (web-src, `layout.ts`). None of the web-tests lines the branch removes or changes was in that file at `4687e79`,
  so none belongs to #145's 8 entries.

##### THE CITATIONS

- **`tree.rs`'s "(spec amendment 3)"** was written by `ec79f21` (#106, Plan 7 part 4a). At that commit no part 5 spec
  existed, the 4a plan's head says "The spec is `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-23-plan7-part4-views-design.md` **as
  amended**", and that spec's amendment 3 is "The next redex is found by the arena walk, not by `reduce_step`", the
  sentence the citation ends.
- **`sourcemap_coverage.rs`'s "(spec amendment 14)"** was written by `a4e7c6f` (#107, Plan 7 part 4b). At that commit no
  part 5 spec existed either, the 4b plan's head names the same spec "**as amended** — amendments 8 to 16 are 4b's", and
  that spec's amendment 14 is "The map is built at the width the run fitted, which fixes `tm_owner` as well", the
  premise the test's doc names.
- **`session.rs`'s "(spec amendment 26)" and "(spec amendment 24)"** were written by `18f8225` (#112, Plan 7 part 5c).
  The 5c plan's head says "The spec is `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-27-plan7-part5-asm-design.md` **as amended** —
  amendments 22 to 37 are 5c's". That spec's amendment 26, "A copy's value is computed when it builds", runs the program
  to its end "as `compile` does", which is `asm_scratch`'s "THE WHOLE RUN HAPPENS HERE, ONCE, as in `compile`"; its
  amendment 24, "One byte cap serves both directions", is `MAX_SCRATCH_ASM_BYTES`' "ONE CONSTANT FOR BOTH DIRECTIONS".
  The part 4 spec's amendments end at 18.
- **`viewmodel.rs`'s "(spec §5.3, amendment 13)"**, its number wrapped onto the next line, was written by `e29df3c`
  (#111, Plan 7 part 5b). The 5b plan's head names the part 5 spec "**as amended** — amendments 6 to 21 are 5b's", and
  that spec's amendment 13 says "**§5.3's decimal-string word is required, not only tidy**", because
  `serde-wasm-bindgen` 0.6.5 answers a `u64` above `Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER` with an error: the doc's own argument. The
  part 4 spec's amendment 13 is "The grid's active element is a cell".
- **The other docs with that numbered item after an "Amended" line**, any case, at the commit that wrote each citation:
  for 3, the roadmap, the sharing-aware-decode and counter-machines plans and the cli-config and web-reduced-files
  specs; for 14, the counter-machines plan; for 13, the roadmap, the counter-machines plan and the part 4 spec. None is
  the spec the commit's plan names, and none is about the sentence cited. For 24 and 26 the part 5 spec is the one such
  doc.
- **`ab077e4`, `bac0a0c` and `20e692a` write every amendment citation in `crates/` (twelve, on eleven lines) with "Plan
  7 part N spec"**, the form `session.rs` 263 already had (`viewmodel.rs` keeps its section: "Plan 7 part 5 spec §5.3,
  amendment 13"). `bac0a0c` also drops the comma from `session.rs`'s two "part 5 spec, amendment", and each citation now
  sits on one line, so a search for the whole phrase finds all eleven lines. The part 5 spec has had an amendment 3 of
  its own since it landed at `899c8b2` (#108), and an amendment 13 and 14 since `e29df3c` (#111). Every line these
  commits change stays inside `rustfmt.toml`'s `max_width = 120`.
- **The class was enumerated across line breaks**: every "amendment N" in `crates/`, with the number allowed on the next
  line, checked for a doc named on its line or the line before. At `10937ef` none is bare.

##### WHAT THIS DID NOT CLOSE

- **28 `spec §N` citations in `crates/` name no doc** (27 on one line, 1 with the section wrapped onto the next line),
  among them `viewmodel.rs`'s "(spec §6.3)", `session.rs`'s `lambda_tree` doc, whose "(spec" ends its line and "§4)"
  opens the next, and three that say only "design spec" or "design (spec": `printer.rs`'s "trivia design (spec §4",
  `unary.rs`'s and `tm_bank_invariant.rs`'s "(design spec §4)". This branch was scoped to amendment citations.

Run on 2026-10-21 in the worktree `~/temp/redextape-notes-and-amendments`, every command below with HEAD at the commit
that adds this entry, whose parent is `10937ef`, the last commit before this entry. Six of the scans take their file

#### THE WARM-BUFFER PROBE'S READING (B) COUNTS THE SOURCE SESSION'S ASM RING, RECORDED FULL AND READ FROM THE HEAP, WHERE IT LEFT THAT RING OUT; ITS TM CASE DERIVES READING (B) TOO, 6 AGAINST `MAX_WARM_BUFFERS`' 8, AND REFUSES A COPY WHOSE RING IS NOT FULL, WHERE IT ASSERTED THAT EACH COPY'S RING EVICTED, WHICH A RING WHOSE RECORDING STOPS ON ITS ALLOWANCE HAS NOT DONE SINCE #140 (2026-10-21, branch `asm-ring-measured`, `bdd977d..1c8eb75`, 3 commits, plus this entry)

**`buffer-affordability.test.ts` prices `MAX_WARM_BUFFERS`, and prints two readings of its threshold.** Reading (a)
counts the warm buffers' rings at exhaustion; reading (b) adds the source session's own rings, exhausted at the same
instant. `MAX_WARM_BUFFERS`' doc in `scratch.ts` records which one governs: "**TWO READINGS, THREE INTERCEPT COMPONENTS
APART — THE PROJECT OWNER PICKED THE LITERAL ONE.**", then "**(a) buffers-only-at-exhaustion — GOVERNS, and SHIPS.**"
and "**(b) everything-at-exhaustion — reference only, NOT what ships.**" This branch changes what reading (b) counts and
what the probe's TM case asserts. VERIFICATION names the commit each figure was read at. `MAX_WARM_BUFFERS` stays 8, and
the one change under `web/src` is to its doc comment. The file is a probe: `vite.config.ts`'s `PROBE_FILES` keeps it out
of the browser project unless `REDEXTAPE_PROBE` is set, as `pnpm test:probe` sets it, so `test:coverage` and CI do not
run it.

##### THE ASM RING, AND HOW READING (B) COUNTS IT

- **The source session has three rings, one a leg, and reading (b) counted two.** `main.ts`'s `sessions.add` builds a
  `History` of `HISTORY_BYTES` for each of the λ, asm and TM legs, and `replies.ts`'s `asm-frames` arm pushes each asm
  frame charged `asmFrameBytes`. A ring is bounded by the bytes it is charged, not the heap it holds. It is full when a
  recording spends its `HISTORY_BYTES` allowance and `recordLeg` stops it on `budget`. No shipped example fills the asm
  ring: all 7 `EXAMPLES` entries give `asm: 'ended'`. A user's program that runs long enough does. Before this branch
  reading (b) added the λ ring, read in the file (the n=1 round's ring), and the TM ring, `TM_LEG_RETENTION_RATIO` of
  `HISTORY_BYTES`, a ratio `session-memory.test.ts` recorded; its comment said the asm ring "is not measured, so this
  reading leaves it out".
- **`affordability-asm-worker.ts`, a new worker, records an asm leg as the app's worker does.** It compiles the program
  into a `Session` and steps it as `session-worker.ts`'s `ASM_RECORDING` run by `recordLeg` does, to `HISTORY_BYTES`
  charged. Neither existing probe worker can: one holds a `LambdaScratch`, the other a `TmScratch`. `sourceAsmRing`
  builds the page's `History<AsmState>` from the frames it answers, refuses a ring charged under `HISTORY_BYTES` before
  the reading, and reads the ring after two collections, as `round` reads a λ ring.
- **`ASM_PROGRAM` is `fn main() { let mut i = 0; while true { i = i + 1; } i } main()`**, whose loop never ends. A
  throwaway probe recorded eight programs' asm legs to `HISTORY_BYTES` and read each ring after two collections. This
  loop's ring held 1.5623 heap bytes per charged byte, the most of the eight; the other seven held 1.3173 to 1.5286:

  | Program | Heap per charged byte |
  |---|---|
  | `main-loop` (`ASM_PROGRAM`) | 1.5623, 1.5623 |
  | `spin`, `fn spin(n) { let mut i = 0; while i < n { i = i + 1; } i } spin(1000000)` | 1.5285, 1.5228, 1.5278, 1.5286, 1.5278 |
  | `down`, `fn down(n) { while n > 0 { n = n - 1; } n } down(1000000)` | 1.5171, 1.5230 |
  | `sum_to` | 1.4880, 1.4923, 1.4924 |
  | `idle`, `fn idle(n) { while n > 0 { } n } idle(1)` | 1.4729, 1.4732 |
  | `top`, `let mut i = 0; while i < 1000000 { i = i + 1; } i` | 1.4427, 1.4361 |
  | `fact(3000)` | 1.3182, 1.3181, 1.3181 |
  | `upto(3000)` | 1.3173, 1.3181, 1.3181 |

  The text of `sum_to`, `fact` and `upto` was in a version of the probe that was not kept.
- **Reading (b) for a page of λ copies, before and after**, one whole run of the file each:

  | Tree | Marginal | Intercept (b) | Cap (b) | Cap (a) |
  |---|---|---|---|---|
  | `fc0a8e7` | 16,419,566.67 | 76,583,442.88 | 28 | 30 |
  | `1c8eb75` | 16,419,297.33 | 128,801,543.88 | 24 | 30 |

  The asm ring run 1 at `1c8eb75` read: 52,166,226 bytes for 68,905 frames kept of 68,904 steps, 33,554,827 charged,
  1.5547 heap bytes per charged byte. Cap (b) read 24 in all three runs at `1c8eb75`.

##### THE TM CASE DERIVES READING (B)

- **The TM case printed reading (a) only.** It now adds three source rings to its intercept (a): the λ ring from one λ
  `round(1)`, read as the λ case's n=1 round reads it, since no round of the TM case builds a λ ring; the asm ring from
  `sourceAsmRing`; and the TM ring as `TM_LEG_RETENTION_RATIO` of `HISTORY_BYTES`. The sum is over the TM copy's
  marginal, and the case prints each component and the cap. Three whole runs at `1c8eb75`:

  | Run | TM marginal | Cap (a) | Intercept (b) | Cap (b) | Cap (b) without the asm ring |
  |---|---|---|---|---|---|
  | 1 | 58,537,221.33 | 8 | 131,072,579.88 | 6 | 7.82, so 7 |
  | 2 | 58,537,688 | 8 | 131,071,491.88 | 6 | 7.82, so 7 |
  | 3 | 58,537,688 | 8 | 131,072,611.88 | 6 | 7.82, so 7 |

- **Reading (b) derives 6 for TM copies, below `MAX_WARM_BUFFERS`' 8, and would derive 7 without the asm ring.** It is
  reference only, by the choice `MAX_WARM_BUFFERS`' doc records, so the cap is unchanged and the user was not asked.
- **Both cases print reading (b)'s cap under one label**, `READING_B_LABEL`: "[UPPER BOUND — pageBaseline is a floor,
  each source ring one program's; REFERENCE ONLY, NOT WHAT SHIPS]". The two reasons it is an upper bound: `pageBaseline`
  is a floor, and each source ring is one program's, so a program whose frames hold more heap per charged byte derives
  less. `MAX_WARM_BUFFERS`' doc says the second in its reading (b) paragraph.

##### THE TM CASE'S ASSERTION THAT COULD NOT PASS

- **#138 (`8dc603d`) asserted that each TM copy's ring evicted**: `expect(kept).toBeLessThan((p.steps[i] ?? 0) + 1)`,
  `kept` being the frames the ring holds. Its entry says what that stood for: "each copy's ring evicted, so its history
  filled". The property it wanted is the second half.
- **Since #140 (`7cbac7d`) a recording that stops on its allowance never makes its ring evict.** `History#evict` keeps
  the newest frame past the budget, and `recordLeg` stops at the first frame that reaches the allowance, which equals
  the ring's budget, so the ring keeps every frame recorded: steps plus one. At `fc0a8e7` the case fails with `expected
  69009 to be less than 69009`.
- **It went unseen because the file is a probe**, outside the default suite for the reason its header gives, run only by
  `pnpm test:probe`.
- **The replacement asserts the property.** `tmRound` sums each copy's `tmFrameBytes` and asserts, before the heap
  reading, "precondition: TM copy ${i}'s recording stopped on `HISTORY_BYTES`, so its ring is full", that is `charged >=
  HISTORY_BYTES`.

##### THE SABOTAGES

Each was one edit, with the whole probe file run under `REDEXTAPE_PROBE=1`. Sabotage 4 ran on `1c8eb75`, sabotages 1 to
3 on trees with uncommitted changes besides the sabotage.

1. **The asm worker's loop condition made `false && …`**: the λ case failed with ``precondition: the source asm ring is
   full, its recording stopped on `HISTORY_BYTES`: expected 116 to be greater than or equal to 33554432``.
2. **`ring.clear()` in `sourceAsmRing` before the reading**: the λ case failed with `expected 13898 to be greater than
   3355443.2`, the bound `sourceAsmRingAtExhaustion > HISTORY_BYTES / 10`.
3. **The TM worker's loop bound halved to `HISTORY_BYTES / 2`**: the TM case failed in its warm-up round with
   ``precondition: TM copy 0's recording stopped on `HISTORY_BYTES`, so its ring is full: expected 16777294 to be
   greater than or equal to 33554432``.
4. **`ring.clear()` in `sourceAsmRing` again**: both cases failed on their asm-ring bound, the λ case with `expected
   13818 to be greater than 3355443.2` and the TM case with `expected 2220 to be greater than 3355443.2`.

**Not shown able to fail:** taking the asm ring out of `interceptEverything`, in either case, fails nothing: the file
asserts no figure, for its header's reason, so what reading (b) counts is held by no assertion. The TM case's
`expect(derivedEverything).toBeGreaterThan(0)` and `sourceLambdaRingAtExhaustion > 1_000_000`, and the λ case's
`derivedEverything > 0`, passed in sabotage 4 and were not aimed at. The TM case's precondition was shown failing only
in the warm-up round, on its first copy.

##### THE REVIEW

**A whole-branch review found nothing Critical.** Its Important findings are the asm ring's leftovers below. Its five
Minor are fixed: the two cases' reading (b) labels differed, and neither said reading (b) is reference only (now
`READING_B_LABEL`); `ASM_PROGRAM`'s doc said a loop's frames hold more heap per charged byte than a recursion's, a
general relationship from the eight programs tried (now: this loop held the most of them);
`MAIN_THREAD_WASM_MODULE_BASELINE_BYTES`' doc called it "THE FIFTH INTERCEPT COMPONENT", an ordinal from before this
branch's count of six; the TM case's doc said `MAX_WARM_BUFFERS`' doc reads "the derived cap" where it now prints two
(now: the cap reading (a) derives); and the asm worker's doc said it answers "the leg's status" where it answers
`asmStatus().run`.

**A narrower review found three comments untrue**, now fixed: `READING_B_LABEL`'s doc said both cases print under it at
the two commits where only the λ case does (now: the λ case, until the third commit extends it to both);
`MAX_WARM_BUFFERS`' doc headed its readings "ONE INTERCEPT COMPONENT APART", where reading (b) adds three of the six
printed components to reading (a)'s three; and `ASM_PROGRAM`'s doc said its asm leg never ends, where its loop never
ends and the leg is capped at `DEFAULT_CAPS.steps`, 5,000,000.

##### WHAT THIS DID NOT CLOSE

- **The asm ring holds more heap than it is charged.** `ASM_PROGRAM`'s full ring held 1.5547 heap bytes per charged
  byte, where the λ ring held 0.2354 (this probe's n=1 round; `HISTORY_BYTES`' doc records 0.19451407924488462) and the
  TM ring 0.8744705880483015 (`TM_LEG_RETENTION_RATIO`). At 52,166,226 bytes it is the largest of the source session's
  three rings, over the 33,554,432 of `HISTORY_BYTES`. `ASM_WORD_BYTES`' doc says of its test: "that case fails if a
  word ever costs more than this charges, which is the direction that would let the ring keep more than
  `HISTORY_BYTES`". The ring keeps more anyway.
- **Where the extra heap sits is not established.** A frame of `ASM_PROGRAM`'s ring holds 757 bytes against 487 charged:
  `FRAME_OVERHEAD_BYTES`, 64, plus 8 words at `ASM_WORD_BYTES`, 52, plus 7 written bytes on average.
  `FRAME_OVERHEAD_BYTES` is checked by no test for asm frames; its doc calls it "Approximate and small — it exists so a
  frame is never sized at zero, not to be precise". `frame-cost.test.ts`'s `asm frame cost` case measures a word as the
  heap of `upto(200)`'s frames with their words less the heap without them, at 87.8 words a frame, so a frame's other
  fields are charged to its words there; and it reads frames made on the main thread, where the page's ring holds frames
  structured-cloned from a worker. Among the eight programs, a frame held 761 to 1,356 bytes at 8 to 16 words and 5,747
  to 5,751 at 82.5 words (`upto(3000)`, `fact(3000)`): about 67 bytes more a word from `ASM_PROGRAM`'s frame to theirs,
  against 52 charged. That is a fit through the probe's readings, not a measurement, and it leaves open that the ring's
  words are under-charged as well as the frame's fixed part.
- **A fix changes how long an asm recording runs, so it is the project owner's call.** A larger charge a frame makes
  `recordLeg` stop sooner on the same allowance; `HISTORY_BYTES`' doc declines to re-scale its units for the same reason
  ("would change every recording length in the app").
- **A copy of a user's looping asm program is likely costlier than the TM copy that sets the cap. This is an estimate:
  no asm copy's cost to the page was priced, and `asm-copy-memory.test.ts` prices an asm copy's worker memory, not its
  ring.** If its frames hold what `ASM_PROGRAM`'s do, its full ring alone is 52.17 MB of heap, and its worker's wasm
  module at least 8,454,144 bytes (`SOURCE_WASM_MODULE_BASELINE_BYTES`), 60.62 MB together, against the TM copy's 58.54
  MB marginal. `MAX_WARM_BUFFERS`' doc already names a copy a user writes as one no count prices.
- **`HISTORY_BYTES`' doc gives retention rates for the λ and TM legs only**, and none for the asm leg.
- **The eight programs' rings were read in one throwaway probe**, two to five times each, and the text of three of them
  was not kept.
- **One `test:coverage` run on this machine, at an earlier tree of this branch, stalled after `hidden.test.ts` failed

#### A FOCUS MOVE MADE DURING A POINTER PRESS IS DRAWN ONCE THE PRESS HAS ENDED, AFTER ITS CLICK, SO A FIRST PRESS ON A CONTROL LOW IN ANOTHER VIEW AT A PHONE'S WIDTH LANDS, WHERE THE FRAME THAT FOCUS MOVE DREW MOVED THE CONTROL FROM UNDER THE RELEASE (2026-10-21, branch `tm-maximise-phone`, `349ac8c..55987c6`, 2 commits, plus this entry)

**Part D's entry left the TM view's maximise at Explorer 390×844 open**: CODE-E's probe saw the first press change
nothing. The app was at fault, and the cause is outside the maximise: any first press that moves the focus into
another view can be lost at a phone's width, wherever the frame that focus move draws changes the layout above the
control. CODE-E's probe had pressed the right control with real input and asserted no precondition (at 390×844 its
button was below the viewport, and Playwright scrolled the pane to it); its state table read 120, 120, 0: the first
press lost, the second maximised (dispatch 1's reading of its raw log).

##### HOW A FIRST PRESS WAS LOST

- **The press's `mousedown` moves the focus into the view it lands on, and `hostFor`'s `focusin` drew a frame at
  once**, before the release.
- **Explorer 390×844.** The strip's readout takes three lines for the program (72.6 px) and two for a TM copy (49.1
  px). On a press of the copy's outline maximise, the focus left the source view, the strip shrank 72.6 → 49.1 px, and
  the button moved 633.7 → 657.4 px before the `pointerup`, which landed on `svg.program-gutter`; the `click` went to
  `div.tm-pane`, the nearest element holding both, and the maximise never ran. The copy's outline disclosure the same:
  746.7 → 770.4 px. At 1280×900 the strip is 28.6 px either way, the button stays at 733.3 px, and the press lands.
- **Debugger 390×844.** The inspector stacked under the views shrank 225.3 → 137.6 px on the same focus move, and the
  copy's maximise moved 454.3 → 498.1 px.

##### THE OPTIONS MEASURED, AND THE USER'S CHOICE

- **A. The strip on one line at every width**: the press lands, and every segment of the readout is cut at 390 px
  (`λ 1 · 64 reductions` shows 49 of its 152 px).
- **B. The strip held at its tallest height at narrow widths**: with the height pinned at 72.6 px the press lands; it
  costs the views 23.5 px whenever the copy holds the focus, and the tallest height depends on the readout and the
  width, so no fixed value covers every readout.
- **C. The strip laid over the views' bottom at narrow widths**: the maximise lands, and the strip covers controls:
  at 390×844 its 72.6 px cover the copy's outline disclosure and maximise. It does not reach the stacked inspector, and
  17 tests failed, in 2 of 20 files.
- **D. The focus move's draw waits for the press to end**: on the prototype both first presses landed in Explorer and
  in Debugger at 390×844, and the readout was drawn 10.9 and 19.2 ms after the press's `pointerdown`, where without it
  it was drawn mid-press, 7.6 and 6.3 ms after.
- **E. Leave it**, recorded as a known lost first press.

**The user chose D (2026-10-21), and to ship it with its limit recorded** under WHAT THIS DID NOT CLOSE.

##### WHAT D DOES

- **`focus-draw.ts`'s `createFocusDraw` owns the page's one press state.** `main.ts` builds it once and hands the
  function it returns to the source view's own `focusin` and to `createPaneHost` as `focusDraw`, which `hostFor`'s
  `focusin` calls where it called `draw()`. A focus move during a press owes a draw; the press's end queues it as a task
  of its own (`setTimeout(draw, 0)`), and since the browser fires a release's `pointerup`, `mouseup` and `click` in one
  task, it runs after the click. A focus move with no press around it draws at once. The mark and the focused leaf are
  still written at once; only the draw waits.
- **A press begins at `pointerdown` or `mousedown` and ends at the `pointerup` or `mouseup` after it**, heard on the
  window, capturing. The mouse pair holds a tap's focus move, which a tap makes at the `mousedown` after its
  `pointerup`. The pointer pair holds a focus move that code makes while a finger is held down, before the lift brings
  a tap's `mousedown`, or through a press whose `pointerdown` default is prevented, which no `mousedown` or `mouseup`
  follows.
- **Every press ends**: also at `pointercancel`, at `contextmenu` and at the window's own `blur`, where the release may
  never reach the page; a press left open would leave every later focus move, a keyboard's too, undrawn. Such an early
  end queues the owed draw there, and a release can still follow it.
- **A press on a `<select>` begins none**: its list opens at the press, in a popup that can take the release.
- **`VirtualGrid`'s `mousedown` still takes no focus for a row**, and its comment gives the two reasons left: a press
  ended early queues the owed draw before the row's release, and the prevented `mousedown` keeps a press from starting
  a text selection in the rows.

##### THE TESTS AND THE SABOTAGES

`focus-press.test.ts`, 9 cases on one mount at 390×844, with the source view and the TM view's copy
sharing the bottom row. The 8 cases that press a control in a view first measure their premise (a focus move into the
control's view with no press draws the control more than half its height away) and assert their precondition (the
focus in the view the press leaves, the control in the viewport and what its centre hits). The `<select>` case, whose
press is on the step bar, outside every view, asserts its own, among it that no press is held when it begins: a focus
move made before its press draws at once. Every press is real input: `userEvent` clicks; CDP's
`Input.dispatchTouchEvent` for a tap and for a touch the browser cancels; CDP's `Input.dispatchMouseEvent` for a press
held across the window's loss of the focus, a right press's `contextmenu`, and a press on a `<select>`. Five cases
press a control in another view (the copy's outline disclosure and maximise in Explorer, the maximise from a tap, the
maximise in Debugger, and the source view's disclosure from the copy in Debugger); four end a press some other way
than its release: a cancelled touch, the window's `blur`, a `contextmenu`, and a press on a `<select>`, which begins
none. `harness.ts` gains `pageCentreOf`, the centre of an element in the top-level page's pixels, where CDP's
input lands, and `share-open-clamps.test.ts` takes it where it carried its own.

**RED at `fc0a8e7`'s `main.ts`, `pane-host.ts` and `virtual-grid.ts`, with `55987c6`'s test file and `harness.ts`: 6
of 9 failed**, the five presses on their outcome (`the press maximised the outline: expected false to be true`) and the
window's `blur` case on its precondition that the press has not drawn its focus move. The cancelled touch, the
`contextmenu` and the `<select>` cases pass there, where every focus move draws at once; their sabotages below are
what shows them able to fail.

Sabotages on `fc0a8e7` with this branch's changes to `web/`, each one edit, the whole file run, each restored from a
copy and compared with it.

| Sabotage | Cases failed | First failure line |
|---|---|---|
| `focusDraw` draws at once (no deferral) | 6 of 9 | `the press opened the outline: expected false to be true` |
| no end at `pointercancel` | 4 of 9 | `the copy’s readout, drawn at the focus move: expected 'program' to be 'copy'` |
| no end at the window's `blur` | 3 of 9 | `timed out after 10000ms waiting for the copy’s readout, before any release` |
| no end at `contextmenu` | 2 of 9 | `timed out after 10000ms waiting for the copy’s readout, before any release` |
| the source view's `focusin` draws at once | 1 of 9 | `the press opened the source view’s outline: expected false to be true` |
| a press begins at `pointerdown` alone | 1 of 9 | `the tap maximised the outline: expected false to be true` |
| a press begins at `mousedown` alone | **0 of 9: did not fire** | none |
| no `<select>` guard | 1 of 9 | `the copy’s readout, drawn at the focus move: expected 'program' to be 'copy'` |
| the window's `blur` heard from any target | 6 of 9 | `the press opened the outline: expected false to be true` |

**A sabotage that leaves a press open leaves it open for the cases after it**, so some later failures are that stuck
press: with no end at `pointercancel`, the window's `blur` and `contextmenu` cases failed their premise (`by 0 px`);
with no end at the window's `blur`, the `contextmenu` case did; and with no end at `pointercancel`, at the window's
`blur` or at `contextmenu`, the `<select>` case failed its precondition (`precondition: no press held, so a focus move
draws at once: expected 'program' to be 'copy'`).

**A press begun at `mousedown` alone did not fire**: no case makes a focus move while the pointer pair alone has begun
a press. That is the pointer pair's case: a focus move that code makes while a finger is held down, or through a press
whose `pointerdown` default is prevented. No case holds a finger down while code moves the focus.

##### THE REVIEW'S CALLS

The branch's review found nothing critical:

- **`VirtualGrid`'s `mousedown` comment said a focus taken at the press would lose every first click on a row**: that
  draw is the view's `focusin` draw, which now waits for the press. The `preventDefault` is kept (no behaviour change),
  and the comment gives the reasons left. A row's click does not depend on `focus-draw.ts` holding a draw, which a
  press ended early queues before the row's release. And the prevented `mousedown` keeps a press from starting a text
  selection in the rows, which no rule makes unselectable (in `web/src` only `.term-gutter` has `user-select: none`):
  on a page of two plain rows, a double press by CDP mouse input selected `theta` with no prevented `mousedown` and
  nothing with one. A drag by CDP mouse input selected nothing either way, so a drag's selection is not shown.
- **The window's `blur` listener was registered without capture**, while its check and comment described a capturing
  one. It is registered capturing, as the other six are, and keeps the check; the last sabotage above shows the check
  holding the five presses and the window's `blur` case's precondition.
- **"A press ended early costs only that a focus move later in it draws at once"** left out that an early end queues
  the owed draw there, and a release can still follow it (after the window's `blur`; with two pointers down, the first
  release ends the press while the other is still held), and `hostFor`'s comment said the owed draw runs after the
  release. Both texts now say so.
- **The pointer pair's doc claimed a current case**; it names the case it holds, a focus move that code makes while a
  finger is held down.
- **A press on a `<select>` could stay open**: a press dragged into the speed `<select>`'s popup and released there may
  send the page no release, and none of the early ends. A press on a `<select>` now begins none, and a case holds such
  a press with no release and shows a focus move during it drawn at once.
- **Test text**: the `contextmenu` case names the platforms where a right press fires it before the release (Linux and
  macOS; on Windows it follows the `mouseup`); the source view's disclosure case, named "with the inspector stacked",
  asserts the stacking; the file doc lists every press made with CDP mouse input.

##### WHAT THIS DID NOT CLOSE

- **During playback a press can still be lost (the user's decision).** Only the focus move's own draw waits: a playing
  run's next frame, drawn while the press is held, draws the new focus and moves the control with it.
- **A press ended early can still be lost the same way**: after the window's `blur`, or with two pointers down, the
  owed draw is queued at that end, and a release may still follow it.
- **No case holds a finger down while code moves the focus**, the pointer pair's case, and its sabotage did not fire.
  Code that moves the focus with no press behind it, `notice.ts` focusing its `leaving()` on a repaint among it, was
  not checked against a finger's hold.
- **The `<select>` reasoning is not measured on a real popup.** Headless Chrome's popup is not a desktop's: the case
  reaches the press's `pointerdown` and `mousedown` on the `<select>`, not where a desktop popup sends the release.
- **Touch was driven only by CDP's touch events**, not a device.
- **Only Chromium ran.** WebKit and Firefox did not, and the `contextmenu` order on Windows was not run.
- **`VirtualGrid`'s `preventDefault` on a row's `mousedown` is kept**, though the draw it was written against now waits
  for the press in every case but an early end; a row's first click without it was not measured, and the text
  selection was shown on plain rows, not the grid's.

#### A COPY'S EDIT IS STORED AS THE EDIT SINK SENDS IT, SO A RELOAD BRINGS BACK TEXT THAT DID NOT BUILD, WHERE IT BROUGHT BACK THE TEXT FROM BEFORE THAT EDIT; A COPY THAT HAS NEVER BUILT READS `did not build`, SAYS SO IN ONE NOTICE PER WORKER, AND THE NOTICE ENDS WHEN THE COPY BUILDS (2026-10-21, branch `recompile-persists`, `47c8a40..82364c5`, 9 commits, plus this entry)

**This closes "`recompile` does not persist"** from Part D's WHAT THIS DID NOT CLOSE (the `#### COMMENTS IN \`web/\``
entry). Fixing it showed what a copy whose text has never built does after a reload, and the user chose to fix that in
this branch too. Every file the range changes is under `web/`.

##### THE DEFECT

- **A reload brought back the text from before an edit that did not build.** An edit to a copy reaches
  `ScratchBuffers.recompile` through `transport.ts`'s `editSink`, which writes the text into the buffer and posts a
  build; nothing stored it. A build that lands stored the copy through its compiled arm in `replies.ts`, but a build
  that fails answers `no-session`, which carries no text and stores nothing. So text a user was halfway through typing
  was lost on a reload, on every leg. The 5d-ii-d design's §4.3 schedules a persist at `setText`.

##### THE FIX

- **`editSink` stores the copy when `recompile` answers that it wrote the text**: `if (scratchpad.recompile(session,
  src)) onBuffersPersist()`, in `transport.ts`, which now takes `onBuffersPersist` as a dependency as `replies.ts` does.
  `recompile` answers true on its warm branch and its cold one, and false for an id that is no copy, which stores
  nothing. There is no debounce of its own: the sink is already behind the editor's `EDITOR_DEBOUNCE_MS`.
  `ScratchBuffers.setText`'s doc and `persistBuffers`' and `refreshBuffers`' docs in `main.ts` name the edit among the
  moments the copies are stored.
- **A reload of a stored text that does not build brings it back in the copy's editor**, marked where it is wrong, on
  each leg.

##### A COPY THAT HAS NEVER BUILT

That reload led to a copy whose build fails before it has recorded a frame, on every leg. A probe drove one
(`phantom/zz-phantom-probe.test.ts` in the record, on this branch's first commit's code on `fc0a8e7`): a λ and a TM copy
forked, a failing edit typed, the page reloaded, three more failing key presses, then an edit that builds; and a blank
TM copy shown in a view and edited the same way. "Notices" counts new notice elements drawn; only one is on screen at a
time.

| Step | λ copy, reloaded | TM copy, reloaded | Blank TM copy |
|---|---|---|---|
| before the reload, a failing edit to a built copy | 0 notices, `step 0 of 7` | 0, `step 0 of 405` | made: 2 notices, `TM copy 1 created`, then `the copy did not build — missing \`tapes <n>\`` |
| after the reload, or bound to a view | 1, `building…` | 1, `building…` | 1, `view now shows TM · copy 1`; `building…` |
| each of three failing key presses | 1 each, the same sentence again, `building…` | the same | the same |
| an edit that builds | 0, `step 0 of 7`; the failure notice still up 1.5 s later | the same, `step 0 of 405` | the same |
| a failing edit after that | 0, the run stays | the same | the same |

The step line said a build was coming after the build had been answered; the live region said the same failure again on
every key press, where Plan 7 part 5 spec amendment 27 has an edit to a copy that has built show its diagnostics in its
editor alone; and the notice went on saying the copy did not build over a copy that ran. **The user's decisions**
(2026-10-21): fix all three, in separate commits, for failed forks too; and the step line reads exactly `did not build`.

##### THE THREE BEHAVIOURS

- **`did not build`** (`b41cf8a`). `replies.ts`'s `no-session` arm, on the branch where `ScratchBuffers.noSessionReply`
  answers a copy's first failure, gives the copy's leg the reason `did not build` through `resetLegs`, as the
  `worker-error` arm gives `the copy failed`. The view's step line, the copy's readout and its row in the copies menu
  read it; a build that lands replaces it through its own arm's `resetLegs`. A λ copy's row read `no term yet` for a
  copy with no frame; `main.ts`'s `copyHolds` now hands it the leg's reason while the leg is not available, as
  `tmCopyRow` and `asmCopyRow` do (`building…`, `did not build`, and `the copy failed` after its thread threw), and
  keeps `no term yet` for a leg that is available with no frame yet.
- **One notice per worker** (`7b0b3ab`). `BufferState.reported` is cleared by `#spawn`, which posts a worker's first
  build, and set by `noSessionReply` on the first failure it answers; a later failure on that worker answers `null`, so
  the editor's own diagnostics are the only report of an edit. A reload, a resume or an undone delete gives the copy a
  new worker, so its first failure is said again.
- **The notice ends when the copy builds** (`9e7895c`). `notify` answers a `Notice` whose `dismiss` ends it only while
  it is still the one on the line; `replies.ts` keeps the one saying a copy did not build, with the copy it names, and
  each compiled arm's `built(session)` ends it for that copy.

##### THE REVIEWS' FIXES

Reviews of the branch found nothing Critical; their points are folded into the commit that wrote the text, and the three
on text that predates the branch are commits of their own (`bac6c3c`, `2bb20f5`, `817c033`), as is one comment line's
wrap (`82364c5`).

- **Comments made true or deleted**: `scratch.test.ts`'s note on the cold branch and `ScratchEditor.destroy`'s doc no
  longer say a pause reaches `recompile`'s cold branch (`bac6c3c`: `EditorCustody.flush` sends a copy's typing while it
  is warm); `noSessionReply`'s doc no longer says the wire cannot tell a first build's failure from an edit's;
  `BufferState.reported` points at the doc that has its reason; `ScratchBuffers.fork`'s doc no longer says the failure
  notice is worded for the fork that asked for it (`817c033`); `replies.ts`'s phantom comment lists the undone delete
  among the gestures and no longer names the copies menu as the way out, which an edit that builds also is; the compiled
  arms' comments say their store writes add nothing today; `setText`'s doc says which text each caller stores.
- **`build-reply-fixture.ts` is the one copy of the build-reply recorder**, which `lambda-copy-typed-text.test.ts`
  carried too.
- **`harness.ts`'s `hear` reads each live-region write's own words** from the node the write added, as
  `view-keys.test.ts` does, where it read the region when its observer ran, which gave two writes in one task the
  second's words both.
- **The never-built cases in `tm-buffer-restore.test.ts` use texts no other case in the file uses**, since `answerTo`
  matches a build by its text on any page's worker; comment lines the branch wrote are wrapped at 120.

##### THE FLAKE

- **`tm-buffer-restore.test.ts`'s "warms a restored cold TM buffer onto the tm leg" failed once at `CPUQuota=25%`**,
  `expected 'TM copy 1 · not shown · paused' not to match /paused/` (`d3-q25-tm-buffer-restore.log` in the record), and
  passed on two reruns. The cause is a reading of the code by review, not reproduced: the two cases before it end on
  `settled()`, whose 500 ms quiet period can pass while a reload's build is still running; the page that posted it goes
  on running after the next case's `mountApp` replaces it, and when the build lands its compiled arm stores that page's
  copies into the store the next case has just cleared.
- **`40bce00` makes every case whose reload builds a copy wait for that build's answer before it ends**: the first two,
  and "keeps a forked TM buffer's edited text" and "keeps a pasted blank TM buffer's text", the other two that end the
  same way (the last waits for the paste's build too, since the store holds the paste once the edit sink sends it). A
  print in the wait, run once at 25%, found builds still unanswered when the wait began in three of the four: the first
  case's one, both of the second's, and one of the fourth's two; the third's had landed. Three runs of the file at 25%
  after it: 11 of 11 each time, the slowest cases 9,500, 7,906 and 8,585 ms.

##### THE TESTS

13 cases added: five browser cases in `tm-buffer-restore.test.ts`, two in `asm-copy-restore.test.ts` and one in
`notice.test.ts`, and five node cases in `sessions.test.ts`, `scratch.test.ts` and `replies.test.ts`. `copy-pin.test.ts`
waits on each build's answer, since an edit is now stored when it is sent; `buffer-restore.test.ts`'s wait for a warmed
λ copy's term skips `building…` as well as `no term yet`. The browser cases' waits on a failed build are on its answer
(`build-reply-fixture.ts`).

- **RED.** Before the persist, the three typed-text cases failed at the restored text (λ, TM, asm). Before each
  behaviour, its cases failed: `expected 'building…' to be 'did not build'` (λ, TM, blank and asm); `no notice for an
  edit: expected [ …(4) ] to have a length of 1 but got 4` (all four); `the notice ends when the copy builds: expected
  'the copy did not build — …' to be ''` (λ, TM and asm). The λ row's case failed `expected [ 'no term yet' ] to deeply
  equal [ 'did not build' ]`; the `hear` case, run on the old `hear`, failed with the second notice's words received
  twice.
- **Sabotages, each one edit, each fired at the property it aimed at.** The persist taken out, or moved before
  `recompile`: the three browser cases and the node case fail. The persist without `recompile`'s answer as its guard:
  the node case's second half fails. Aimed at the leg's reason: the step-line assertions fail with `expected 'building…'
  to be 'did not build'`, and, in `readout.ts`, the readout assertions with `expected [ 'λ copy 1 · building…' ] to
  deeply equal [ 'λ copy 1 · did not build' ]`. Aimed at `reported`: `no notice for an edit` fails on all four, `nothing
  said for an edit` on all four, and the node case's warm half with `expected null to deeply equal [ { …(3) } ]`. Aimed
  at ending the notice: `the notice ends when the copy builds` fails on λ, TM and asm, and the node case's `another
  copy’s build` when any copy's build ends it. The λ row hard-coded to `building…`: `expected [ 'building…' ] to deeply
  equal [ 'did not build' ]`.
- **Not shown able to fail**: the error-mark waits after the restored text, which every sabotage of the persist stopped
  before; the count of the reload's notice (1) and of `one notice from each page` (2), which no sabotage made wrong; the
  TM restored case's row in the copies menu, since the λ row's sabotage hard-coded the λ row alone and failed 1 case of
  11; the second step-line check for `did not build`, after the three edits; and the closing waits on `step 0 of`, after
  the assertion that the notice ends.

##### WHAT THIS DID NOT CLOSE

- **A blank copy says two notices for one gesture**, `TM copy 1 created` and at once `the copy did not build — missing
  \`tapes <n>\``; no spec says what making a blank copy announces beyond that it was made. **And a resume, an undone
  delete or a page's restore of a copy that has never built says its failure again**, one notice per worker.
- **`recompile`'s cold branch is reached by no browser test.** A pause's `custody.flush` sends the pending edit while
  the copy is warm (probe `zz-cold-probe.test.ts` in the record, 2 of 2 passed); the node case in `scratch.test.ts`
  holds the branch.
- **The TM and asm compiled arms' store writes store nothing new today.**
- **The bigger fix for the flake is not done**: terminating a replaced page's workers in `mountApp` and `remountApp`,
  which would end every late reply rather than wait for the ones that store. Two cases in `tm-buffer-restore.test.ts`,
  "keeps a forked λ/TM buffer's typed text that does not build", still end with their reload's build running; it fails,
  and a failed build stores nothing.

#### A COMMENT GUARD FORKED FROM TAIYAKU'S FAILS A BRANCH THAT ADDS HISTORY TO A COMMENT, GROWS A COMMENT BLOCK PAST 8 LINES OF TEXT OR RAISES AN AREA'S COMMENT SHARE ABOVE ITS BUDGET; IT RUNS AS THE FOURTEENTH PRE-COMMIT HOOK AND AS TWO STEPS IN CI'S `linear-history` JOB (2026-10-30, branch `comment-guard`, `7da611b..4d1f7a0`, 27 commits, plus this entry's last edit)

**The user asked on 2026-10-29 for taiyaku's comment guard** (taiyaku's #215, `af694710`), so that the comments the
comment pass (#144–#147) left holding their why do not take on history and measurements again.
`scripts/check-comments.mjs` is a fork of taiyaku's script, not a copy shared with it: its lexers, its diff and carry
logic, its base resolution and much of its self-test are taiyaku's; its areas, budgets, retuned history patterns, three
lexers, the moved-block rule and their test cases are redextape's. Its documentation is the spec,
`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-29-comment-guard-design.md`, which the script's header and the README's "Checks" section
point at; the plan is `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-10-29-comment-guard.md`. Of the 27 commits, 13 change only `docs/`:
9 the spec, 1 the plan and 3 this entry. The other 14 change the guard, its budget, its wiring, the README or a comment
in a sibling gate (`check-all.sh`, `check-citations.sh`, `check-doc-figures.sh`). The lane record is
`~/temp/redextape-comment-guard-record/` (`R` below).

##### WHAT THE GUARD DOES

- **It reads** `.rs`; `.ts`, `.js`, `.mjs` and `.tsx` with the TypeScript lexer; `.css`; `.html`, whose `<!-- -->` is a
  comment and whose inline `<script>` and `<style>` bodies go to the TypeScript and CSS lexers; whole-line `#` comments
  in `.sh`, `Dockerfile`, every `.yml` and `.yaml`, `.toml` and `deploy/nginx.conf`; whole-line `;` in the tree-sitter
  `.scm` queries; and whole-line `--` in `.lua`. The HTML, `;` and `--` lexers are new. It does not read Markdown,
  `docs/`, the generated tree-sitter sources or the `.rxt`, `.tm` and `.asm` fixtures.
- **Rule 1, history,** fails a comment on a line the branch adds when it holds a date, a timestamp among them
  (`2026-10-28T09:00`), a commit hash, `PR #N`, `PR N`, `pull request #N` or `pull request N`, their plurals
  (`PRs #12 and #13`) and each with a lowercase letter after its number (`PR 3c`), `pull request` in any case and
  `PR` in capitals, `previously` (not the adjective `previously-`), `originally`, `formerly`, `before this fix`,
  `before the change` or `~~`. A date passes in a file name, after `ruling(s)` or `decision(s)`, before a `§`, and
  after `amended` or `note of` once a `§` has been named; a bare `#N` and a `#N` in backticks pass, and so does a
  lowercase `pr`. A line whose comment text the diff also removes somewhere is carried, not added. Taiyaku's bare
  `PR`, `was/were tried` and `used to` are dropped, for the reasons in the spec's "Rule 1".
- **Rule 2, the block cap,** is taiyaku's: a block of whole-line comments fails when it has more than 8 counted lines
  and the branch grew it, adding more counted lines inside it than the hunks touching it remove. A delimiter-only line,
  fenced code and an `# Errors`, `# Panics`, `# Safety` or `# Examples` section in a doc comment, Rust `//!` module docs
  and a file's leading header are not counted. **The fork adds the moved block:** a grown block is matched with a
  removed run, a maximal run of counted lines inside one block at the base, all of which the diff removes, in any file,
  leaving out the runs that hunks touching the grown block remove, since those already count as its trims. They match
  when the words they share are at least half of the larger one's distinct words, and a matched block fails only when
  it is over the cap and has more counted lines than the run it replaced.
- **Rule 3, the comment share,** compares each area's comment lines ÷ (comment + code lines) with
  `scripts/comment-budget.json` to 4 decimals. The 15 areas are each crate under `crates/` (nine), `web/src`,
  `web/tests`, `web/scripts`, `scripts`, `grammars` and `.forgejo`. A share above its budget fails. A share more than
  0.0050 below it fails as stale when the branch has fewer comment lines in that area than its base. Every budget is the
  share of the tree at `4d1f7a0`.
- **The base** for rules 1 and 2 is the merge base of `HEAD` and `origin/main` locally and in the hook. CI passes
  `--base`: a pull request's `base.sha`; on a push to `main`, `github.event.before`, or `HEAD~1` when that is empty, all
  zeros or not a commit; `HEAD` on a tag push, a dispatch and the schedule. With no base it fails.
- **It runs** as the fourteenth pre-commit hook, `check-comments`, self-test then scan on every commit whatever is
  staged, and as two steps in `linear-history`: `Prove the comment guard still detects`, the self-test, which prints
  `node --version` first, and `Reject history, over-long blocks and share growth in comments`, the scan, which prints
  the base it chose. The README's "Checks" section counts fourteen hooks and describes it.

##### THE USER'S RULINGS

1. A fork, in `scripts/check-comments.mjs`: not a core shared with taiyaku, and not TypeScript.
2. Rule 2 is taiyaku's 8-line cap, unchanged.
3. Rule 3 is taiyaku's exact budget, with its 0.0050 stale arm.
4. A bare `#N` passes, since a comment may point at an issue's record, and Forgejo numbers issues and pull requests in
   one series; `PR #N`, `PR N` and `pull request #N` fail.
5. Dated decision pointers and spec-amendment pointers pass, a decision pointer only after the word `decision` or
   `decisions`: `The user chose this on DATE` fails when a branch adds it, and is reworded to
   `the user's decision, DATE` when a branch edits it.
6. `.html` is lexed, each inline `<script>` with the TypeScript lexer.
7. The moved-block rule matches a run of removed counted lines, not a whole block, leaving out the runs that hunks
   touching the grown block remove, when the shared words are at least half of the larger of the two word counts.
8. The commit-hash marker stays, although 2 of its 7 hits on `main` at `7da611b`, read as if every comment line there
   were added, were legitimate.

On 2026-10-30, after the final review:

9. The self-test's expected `new.ts:1` failure is a plain string ending in the counted `check-citations: allow` marker,
   the third that gate honours, not an interpolated line number.
10. CI's two steps take the `linear-history` job's names: `Prove the comment guard still detects` and `Reject history,
    over-long blocks and share growth in comments`.
11. `scripts/check-doc-figures.sh`'s quoted example `(156 until PR 3 …)` is reworded on this branch.
12. A `####` or `//////` line keeps counting as a line of text, as taiyaku counts it, although a `;;;;` or `----` line
    is delimiter-only.
