#### THE λ VIEW DRAWS EACH MARK ONCE PER NODE: A NODE OVER TWO OR MORE ROWS GETS A BAR IN ITS MARK'S OWN LANE, IN A STRIP THAT STAYS AT THE VIEW'S LEFT, 18 PX WIDE, OR 9 PX IN A TERM WHERE 18 WOULD LEAVE THE LAYOUT AT ITS FLOOR, LINKED COPIES THAT NEST OR MEET SHARE ONE LINE WITH A TICK AT EACH COPY'S ENDS, AND A NODE INSIDE ONE ROW GETS ONE SHAPE ROUND ITS WORDS, WHERE EVERY WORD OF A MARKED NODE WAS BOXED (2026-11-01 to 2026-11-02, branch `lambda-marks`, `29e6a83..ccff474`, 15 commits, plus this entry, `55ea0bd`; then `eabb1ae`, `46d5624`, `1bf93c7` and `4d5a136`, which draw the narrow strip and answer its reviews, and the commit that brings this entry up to date)

**The user raised it on 2026-10-28**, in a bullet under "Deferred beyond v1" that #156 added and this entry replaces:
at step 0 of `sum_to(5)` every token of the λ tree sat in a box of its own, and the tree could not be read. A
prototype was built first and shown running, and the user accepted it before any plan. The design is this entry: by
the controller's call there is no spec file. All 15 commits change `web/` and nothing else; 9 change `web/src/` and 12
change the tests. The 4 after this entry's first version change `web/` alone too, all 4 `web/src/` and 3 the tests:
while the entry was drafted, a measurement in desktop Chrome found the strip pushing the term sideways at 390 by
844 px with the default folds, and the user chose a narrow strip (7 and 8 below). The lane record is
`~/temp/redextape-lambda-marks-record/` (`$R` below).

##### THE DEFECT

The marks belong to nodes but were drawn on tokens. `#marks` in `web/src/lambda-body.ts` gave the mark's class to
every token of every node inside a marked node, and `web/src/style.css` drew `.is-next-redex` as a 1px dashed outline,
`.is-linked` as a wash with a 1px inset edge and `.is-contractum` as a wash with an underline, each round its own token.
A mark on a small node read as one box; a mark on the root read as a box round every word. At step 0 the next redex is
the root, since the outermost `apply` is a β-redex. On `main`, at 1400 by 900 px with the default folds, the view drew
11 boxes on its 2 rows; with the root linked and every fold open, 341 on the 30 rows drawn at the top, each token both
outlined and boxed. At step 1 the contractum is the root, and the whole tree was boxed again.

**The salmon was a link on the root**, which the bullet asked to confirm in the browser first. The investigation found
it to be a pin of the `LetRec` that binds `fn sum_to` round the program, whose one node at step 0 is the root. A click
sets it: on a λ token whose node carries no link of its own, since `LambdaPane` links the innermost linked ancestor
(`lambda-tree.ts`'s `linkedAncestor`), the `λ` of `λsum_to.` among them, or on the TM rule table's `pc0` row. No
click in the source sets it: the function's `Lambda` has the same span, and `link.ts`'s `innermost` keeps the first of
two identical spans. Two more faults sat beside it: every row's first token carried `data-marks`, so every row's
accessible name began "next redex:"; and `.is-contractum` comes after `.is-linked` at equal specificity, so a token
that was both lost the link's wash and box (read from the cascade, never seen in the browser).

##### WHAT CHANGED

- **A node over two or more rows** gets one bar piece on each drawn row it covers, in a lane of its mark's own: in the
  18 px strip, from its left, the contractum a solid line at 3-6 px, the next redex a dashed line at 8-10 px, and a
  link a bracket at 12-17 px, a line with a tick at its copy's first and last rows; the 9 px strip draws the same
  shapes at 2-3, 4-5 and 6-9 px. A bar's first and last pieces stop 3 px short of the row's edge (`--bar-inset`, which
  the dashes' offset reads too), so two marked nodes stacked read as two. The pieces have no text and are
  `aria-hidden`, so the term's text is unchanged.
- **The lanes are a strip** at the start of every row, 18 px (`LANES`) or 9 px (below), always there, so nothing
  moves when a mark comes or goes: the first word is where it was with a mark and without one. `columns()` takes the
  strip off the view's width before it divides by `ch`. The strip is sticky at the view's left and opaque, so a bar
  stays in sight when the term scrolls sideways, over the words that pass under it. Every drawn row is as wide as the
  widest, so each row's strip can stay, and the focus ring is drawn on the active row's strip, which would cover a ring
  on the row; the ring may touch the first lane, not lie over it.
- **In a narrow term the strip is 9 px** (`NARROW_LANES`): where the 18 px strip would leave `columns()` at its floor
  of 24 columns, below a term about 245 px wide in desktop Chrome. `lanesFor` decides from the term's width with the
  18 px strip whatever strip is drawn, so the columns the narrow strip gives back cannot turn it wide again, and
  `columns()` takes off the strip it picks. `#paint` writes that width as `--lanes` on the rows, and the strip's width
  and its lanes' strokes (`--bar-line`, a ninth of it) read it: 2 px strokes in the 18 px strip, 1 px in the 9 px one,
  and the same shapes in both. The paint key holds the width, so a resize across the threshold redraws the rows.
- **Linked copies that nest or meet** share the link lane: one piece on each row any of them covers, a corner where
  the outermost copy starts and ends, and, for a copy inside another, a tick at the top of its first row and at the
  bottom of its last, running through the row's edge (`data-tee`).
- **A node inside one row** gets one run, a `.term-mark` wrapper round its words carrying its marks' classes, which
  the stylesheet's rules for the three marks draw as before; tokens carry no mark class. Two marks on one node are one
  run with both classes, and `.term .is-linked.is-contractum` draws both washes, the link's box and the underline. A
  dashed outline that shares a run's edges with a link's box is drawn 1px outside it, by three selectors: a link on
  the redex, round it and inside it.
- **The words a screen reader hears** are on the node's first token, on its first row only, in `MARKS` order
  ("next redex:", "just produced:", "linked:"), where every row's first token had them.
- **Flat text's contractum** is one run round its tokens, the gaps between them inside it.
- **`markSpans`** finds every node's first and last rows in one pass over the tokens and one back up the tree, so its
  cost is the tokens and the nodes, not the tokens times the marks.

On the branch, at `ccff474` and again at `eabb1ae`, in the state where `main` drew 341 boxes, the view draws none: 30
next-redex pieces and 30 link pieces, one on each drawn row.

##### DECISIONS

The user's, on 2026-11-01:

1. The shape: a bar for a node over two or more rows, and one shape round the words of a node inside one row.
2. Fixed lanes, one per mark, left to right the contractum's solid line, the next redex's dashed line and the link's
   bracket. They were asked for in the existing 2ch margin; the prototype found that margin is the `▸`/`▾` glyph's
   slot, which moves with the indent and which the glyph fills at indent 0, the root's first row, so it drew an 18 px
   strip of its own. The user saw it running and said "yes this seems acceptable".
3. A prototype, shown running before any plan.
4. A review by the `code-review` skill at HIGH.
5. The screen-reader words on the node's first row only, when the review raised it: "First row only, as built", with
   the trade-off listed here for Plan 7 part 7.
6. Linked copies that nest, when the review found them: "One line, a tick per copy".

Then, on 2026-11-02:

7. A narrow strip, when told that with the default folds at 390 by 844 px the term scrolled sideways by 8 px, where
   `main`'s did not scroll: "Narrow strip on phones".
8. Told then that the 174 px term behind that figure is desktop Chrome's, whose classic scroll bar takes 15 px of the
   λ pane's width, and that on a phone the term is 189 px, where the 18 px strip would fit: "Keep it". The narrow
   strip stays, and the 390 by 844 px figures here are named as desktop Chrome's.

The controller's, each told to the user and none overruled: the link on the root is kept, since the link is right
and only its drawing was wrong, and it is drawn once, as a bracket; both marks show where they share a node; the
words once, on the node's first row, which the user then kept (5); the term map's marks and the TM, asm and source
views are out of scope, the views marking once per row already; the design lives in this entry.

The controller's later calls, which the record does not show put to the user: the tests Task 1 moved find a mark by
its class to prove what they proved before, and the rule that a test measures geometry and computed style holds for
the tests of the new drawing; the strip stays at the view's left when the term scrolls sideways (the review's F1);
`67e0c88`'s width test, which pins the right margin `columns()` leaves, is kept; the strip is chosen from the λ term's
own width, narrow where the layout with the 18 px strip would be at its floor, a choice made from the width alone so
that it cannot turn back and forth; the focus ring may touch the first lane but not lie over it (the narrow strip's
review); and the 390 by 844 px app test holds the mechanism, with the 0.625 px desktop Chrome leaves held by no test
(below).

##### THE TESTS

Nineteen new cases, 16 in `lambda-body.test.ts`, 2 in `lambda-tree-app.test.ts` and 1 in `app.test.ts`, and none
removed; 3 of them run in a 640 px body and again in a 174 px one, the λ term's width at 390 by 844 px in desktop
Chrome. A mark's pieces and runs are found by selector, and what is asserted of them is geometry and computed style:

- a term whose root, over 9 rows, carries the next redex and a link, and one of whose nodes is the contractum, has one
  piece per row its node covers in each lane, and no element in the rows draws an outline, a box shadow or a border
  (`harness.ts`'s `wordEdges`), the strip and its pieces aside;
- no piece lies over a word, every word's left is the same with the marks and without them, and every piece lies in
  its row and its lane (`barRows`);
- the link's ticks are on its first and last pieces only, the next redex's pieces are dashed (a gradient with a
  transparent stop, repeated) and the contractum's solid, the three lanes' x ranges are disjoint, the first and last
  pieces are inset, and the first lane starts no nearer the strip's edge than the focus ring reaches, its offset,
  spread and blur together;
- a row laid out as wide as `columns()` allows ends at least 2ch inside the view;
- `columns()` takes the 9 px strip off where the 18 px one would leave the layout at its floor, and keeps the 18 px
  one a column past it; and in a body the 18 px strip would push a first row as long as the default program's past,
  the row does not scroll sideways;
- scrolled sideways, every piece stays in the view's strip and covers the words under it, and the focus ring is on
  the active row's strip at the view's left;
- nested copies draw one line with corners at the outer ends and tees at the inner ones; copies on rows one after
  the other draw two brackets; copies that meet on a row draw one line through it;
- a one-row node's mark is one shape that encloses its words and no other; both marks on one node show both grounds,
  the link's box and the underline; the dashed outline clears a link's box in all three nestings;
- the words are in the accessible name of the node's first row only, before its first word;
- a node longer than the window, scrolled to its end, has a piece on every drawn row and only the last tick;
- in the app, `sum_to(5)` at step 0 with the root linked and every fold open draws a next-redex and a link piece on
  each drawn row and boxes no word, at the top and at the end; `fact(4)` at step 27, sized to 80 columns, reads a link
  to `fact(n - 1)` as two copies, the inner inside the outer; and at 390 by 844 px the default program's first row is
  in view beside the 9 px strip, in a term sized to the widest the 18 px strip would push that row past. The tests'
  headless browser draws the λ pane no scroll bar, so its term is 189 px there and the row fits beside either strip;
  hence the sizing.

The tests that read a mark's class on a token now find it by its bar or its run (`harness.ts`'s `lambdaMark` and
`markStart`); `app.test.ts`'s `markedNodes` reads each marked node's words, from its bar's first row to its last, and
fails on a bar cut off by the drawn rows or a piece with no copy open.

**46 sabotages, each in a scratch worktree, each file restored from a saved copy and checked with `cmp`.** 27 were run
on the tests as Task 2 left them, and 26 failed tests on the first run; per-token marks put back failed 22 of the 84
cases in the three files. The 27th, `columns()` keeping the strip's 18 px for the words, failed nothing in the browser
project: no test drew a row at the width `columns()` returns, and the 2ch right margin its `- 4` leaves hid most of
the 18 px. `67e0c88` adds the width test, which fails under it in 2 runs of 2, with -2 px of room against a bound of
15.5. One more edit was aimed wrong and changed nothing for its fixture, since the token it keyed on, an application's
separating space, belongs to that application; it was aimed again, and fired. Eight sabotages of fix round 2's changes
each failed a test, and a ninth, a tee drawn wherever a neighbouring row holds a copy, failed only the test for copies
on rows one after the other, which round 2b added for it. Ten were run on the narrow strip. Five on `eabb1ae`'s tests
each failed a test on its first run; the strip never turning narrow failed 7 of the 41 cases in `lambda-body.test.ts`.
Of five on the narrow fix round's tests, four failed a test, among them an 18 px narrow strip, which fails the 390 by
844 px app test. The fifth, a 10 px narrow strip, passed it: that test sizes its term to `ceil(LANES + 21ch) - 1`, so
by its arithmetic any strip of up to 17 px passes, and it holds the mechanism, not the 0.625 px desktop Chrome leaves
(below).

##### THE REVIEW

The `code-review` skill at HIGH read the branch at `67e0c88` and did not run it. It reported seven findings, and two
minor points from the task reviews were added. Each fix began by reproducing its finding.

- **F1, a bar scrolled out of sight when the term scrolled sideways.** Reproduced, and fixed by the sticky strip
  (`53ddd91`); its test failed before the fix, on a piece outside the view's strip.
- **F2, linked copies that nest drew two pieces on one row.** Reproduced on shipped programs: in `fact(4)` at step 27,
  code layout at 80 columns, a link to `fact(n - 1)` marks a copy on rows 1-26 and one on rows 23-24, and rows 23 and
  24 each drew two pieces in the link lane, which read as one bracket with stray ticks. A probe found linked copies
  over two or more rows sharing a row in `fact(4)`, `map and fold`, `is_even(6)` and `fact(12)` with the automatic
  folds, and none in `double(1 + 2)`, the review's own example. It went to the user, whose scheme (6) is `ba074f0`.
- **F3, the words on the first row only.** Kept by the user (5).
- **F4, `markSpans` paid a pass over the whole term per mark.** On `map` over 300 elements with every fold open,
  34,896 tokens and a link with 413 copies, `showTree` took 19.6 ms with the link and 1.3 without it; `d984f69`
  brings it to 1.4. The old and new functions gave the same spans on 20,664 inputs.
- **F5 and F6, the strip's width and the bar's inset each written twice.** The width was set from `LANES` alone
  (`a0ba2d8`), as `palettes.test.ts` fails a custom property nothing in `style.css` defines; `46d5624` then made it
  one custom property, `--lanes`, which `lambda-body.ts` sets on the rows and `style.css` declares with an 18 px
  default for that test. The inset is one property (`21199bb`).
- **F7, two test helpers read only the one-row form.** Not reproduced: their fixtures' nodes stay on one row at every
  width the tests reach, so nothing was changed.
- **The two minor points** (`ad1078b`, `2177d91`): a width check without a message, and bounds one test repeated
  from another.

The fixes were reviewed again, three times. The first re-review approved round 1 and raised three minor points:
the focus ring on the strip untested, a comment without its reason and a weak precondition (`81eea20`). The second
found the scheme as the user gave it, and no test for two copies on rows one after the other, which a neighbouring-row
rule passed; round 2b added it, and the ninth sabotage above, and a guard in `markedNodes` with the `fact(4)` app test
(`c2fd87b`). The third found that guard unexercised, and raised comments that claimed too much and an inline size not
restored when the test fails; round 2c fixed those (`ccff474`) and probed the guard (below).

**The narrow strip was reviewed twice.** The review of `eabb1ae` found no app test at 390 by 844 px, the wide side of
the threshold untested, the focus ring touching the contractum's lane in the 9 px strip, a size container and an
inline width on every row where one custom property would do, and comments to fix, and noted that no one had looked at
the narrow shapes. `46d5624` made the width one custom property, and `1bf93c7` added the tests and fixed the comments,
the ring allowed to touch the first lane but not lie over it by the controller's call; a crop of the 9 px strip at 4x
(`$R/nf-s1-strip-x4.png`) was looked at, and every shape reads at that scale. The re-review found that the app test's
title claimed a page scroll bar the test never draws, that the test did not wait for the viewport, that `--lanes`'
default did not say why it is there, and that the ring's reach left out its spread; `4d5a136` fixes those, and this
revision the bullet below on the strip at a narrow width.

##### WHAT THIS DID NOT CLOSE

- **Two nested copies that start, or end, on the same row share one tick,** so counting ticks cannot pair them. The
  code layout can start two nested nodes on one row (`λx. λy. …` prints as one `(λx y.` row). No real link where this
  happens was looked for, so how often it does is unmeasured.
- **Where two copies meet on a row,** counting pairs the next copy's start tick with the first's end tick. The test
  for it merges two rows by hand; the code layout gave no such row for the fixtures tried, and how often a real link
  does is unmeasured. Both limits come with the user's scheme, as the second re-review found.
- **A screen reader hears a mark on its node's first row only.** The other rows say nothing, and where the first row is
  not drawn no drawn row says the mark. The user kept this (5); it is for Plan 7 part 7.
- **The term map tells the next redex from a link by colour alone:** its icicle strokes each as a 1.5px column, in
  `--tok-operator` and `--link-edge` (`web/src/term-map.ts`, `column()`), against the Plan 7 part 1 spec's §11
  (`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-17-plan7-part1-foundations-design.md`). Out of scope by the controller's call.
- **Flat text's contractum has no words for a screen reader;** it had none before.
- **The strip still widens a term with every fold open, and no test holds the 0.625 px the 9 px strip leaves in
  desktop Chrome's 174 px term at 390 by 844 px.** In desktop Chrome at 390 by 844 px, `sum_to(5)` at step 0, the λ
  pane scrolls down and its classic scroll bar takes 15 px of its 189, so the term is 174 px wide. With the default
  folds the term scrolled sideways there by 8 px at `ccff474`, where `main` does not scroll; since `eabb1ae` it scrolls
  by 0, the first row ending 0.625 px inside the view beside the 9 px strip. With every fold open it scrolls by at most
  233 px at `eabb1ae`, where `main` scrolls by 225 and `ccff474` by 242; in desktop Chrome at 320 by 568 px, by 34 with
  the default folds and at most 268 with every fold open, where `main` scrolls by 25 and 260. `columns()` is at its
  floor of 24 there, on `main` and on the branch, so a strip adds to rows the layout cannot narrow. At 1400 by 900 px
  neither scrolls. The 174 px is desktop Chrome's, not a phone's: on a phone, whose scroll bars overlay, the term would
  be the pane's 189 px, as it is in the tests' headless browser, and the 18 px strip would fit the default program's
  first row; no phone was measured. No test holds the 0.625 px: the tests' browser draws the pane no scroll bar and
  measures `ch` at 8.0 px, where desktop Chrome measures 7.82, so the 390 by 844 px app test sizes its term and holds
  the mechanism, the 9 px strip keeping in view a row the 18 px one would push past. A strip of up to 17 px passes it,
  by its arithmetic, and an 18 px one fails it. Task 1's reading, that the branch scrolls only where `main` does, had
  measured every fold open and not the default folds.
- **`#paint` measures `ch` on every paint,** scrolls included, to pick the strip (`#lanesNow`: a `getComputedStyle`
  and a `measureText`). What that costs was not measured.
- **The width test pins the 2ch right margin `columns()`'s `- 4` leaves.** That `- 4` came in with #106 (`ec79f21`)
  with no recorded reason; a change to it is a change to the test.
- **`markedNodes`' guard against a copy cut off at the top is not shown to be needed.** A probe at `ccff474` cut the
  `fact(4)` test's rows above its inner copy's start and above its end: the guard failed the read at the cut both
  times, and a looser guard failed it too, in the first case at the row after the inner copy's end. By reading, not by
  a run, the looser guard is silent only where nothing after the cut needs an open copy: a meet row drawn first, or a
  tee start whose outer copy ends on the inner's last row. `fact(4)` at step 27 has neither.
- **`fact(4)` at step 27 at 80 columns** laid out as 29 lines in a browser drive at `d984f69` and as 33 in the app test.
  Round 2c showed the view's height does not change the layout; why the two differ is not known.
- **One whole-suite run in fix round 1 hung,** after 22:35:44, with four browser files the branch does not touch
  reported skipped; it was killed, and the run after it at the same tree passed. The cause is not known. At `c2fd87b`
  two whole-suite runs failed in files the branch does not touch, one on a 10,000 ms timeout and one in four files,
  where the log shows "Failed to fetch dynamically imported module"; each failing file passed alone, and the gates'
  coverage run that followed passed whole. On the tree committed as `eabb1ae` one more failed in
  `buffers-quota-restored.test.ts`, which the branch does not touch, with the same message, and passed alone. The
  gates' coverage run at `eabb1ae` and the whole-suite runs at `1bf93c7` and `4d5a136` passed whole, which says
  nothing of a fault that comes and goes.
- **Round 2c's commit, `ccff474`, was read by the controller** and by no reviewer. `4d5a136`, written after the narrow
  strip's last re-review, was read by the controller and by no reviewer.

#### `asm` IS RENAMED `rxm` WHEREVER IT NAMED REDEXTAPE'S REGISTER-MACHINE IR, IN THE UI, THE CLI, `.rxm` FILES, THE GRAMMAR, THE LSP, THE NEOVIM PLUGIN AND THE CODE, AND THE `rxm` TOGGLE'S TOOLTIP AND THE HELP PAGE SAY WHAT IT IS; NOTHING READS THE OLD NAME, SO A STORED LAYOUT OR COPY STORE THAT NAMES `asm` IS REFUSED WHOLE AND A SHARE LINK THAT NAMES IT OPENS THE PROGRAM ALONE (2026-11-02, branch `rxm`, `1b305e0..2b9d67c`, 14 commits, plus this entry)

**This answers the bullet "Say what "asm" is, in the UI"** under "Deferred beyond v1", which #153 added on
2026-10-27 and this entry marks closed. It asked for a tooltip on the header toggle, a definition in the help page,
and a decision on whether the label should change, since `asm` was also the name `redextape emit --lang asm`, the
tree-sitter grammar and the `.asm` filetype sniffing used. The toggle did have a title at run time, set by
`viewToggles`' `sync` from `toggleSentence` ("show the asm view"); the bullet's "has no title" holds of the markup in
`web/index.html` only. The user chose to change the name, everywhere (DECISIONS below). Of the 14 commits,
`b72bb16` is a rename script's whole output and the 13 after it are hand fixes. The lane record is
`~/temp/redextape-asm-ui-record/` (`$R` below).

##### WHAT CHANGED

**The names.** Everywhere `asm` named the IR it is `rxm`, in lower case, like `source`:

- **The web page:** the view's toggle, and every label built from `KIND_WORD.rxm` (`web/src/layout.ts`) and
  `LEG_NAME.rxm` (`web/src/legs.ts`): the view headers, the ⋯ and + view menus, the stage tabs, the copies menu, the
  results readout, the link-status and share-position notices and the view-keys hint; the help and about pages. The
  pane kind is `'rxm'`, in stored layouts and links too.
- **The CLI:** `redextape emit --lang rxm` (`Lang::Rxm`), `--form rxm` (`Form::Rxm`) and the `.rxm` extension. The
  emitted listing's first line is ``; rxm listing, read back by `parse_rxm` and run by `redextape run`.``, where it
  was ``; Register-assembly listing, read back by `parse_asm` and run by `redextape run`.``; it is a comment, and
  nothing parses its text.
- **The grammar:** `grammars/tree-sitter-redextape-rxm/`, named `redextape_rxm`, scope `source.rxm`, its parser
  symbol `tree_sitter_redextape_rxm` and its wasm `tree-sitter-redextape-rxm.wasm`, regenerated with the pinned
  tree-sitter CLI 0.25.10 and rebuilt, not edited.
- **The LSP language id and the Neovim parser and filetype:** `redextape_rxm`. The plugin claims `.rxm` by its
  extension and no longer sniffs a buffer's first line (`21a229b`). An upper-case `.RXM` runs but is not coloured,
  as the rxm grammar's README says.
- **The code and its files:** `tm::rxm`, `tm/rxm_syntax.rs`, `lower_rxm`, `trace/rxm_cursor.rs` and `RxmCursor`,
  `web/src/rxm-pane.ts`, `rxm-seed.ts` and `rxm-view.ts`, the wasm crate's `probe-rxm-copy` feature and `pnpm run
  test:probe:rxm-copy`, and the tests and their file names.

Prose that called the IR "assembly" or "register-assembly", in the help and about pages, the CLI's help, the core and
grammar docs and the README, now says rxm or register machine. Where "assemble" means build, and in the crate name
`cranelift-assembler-x64`, the word stays.

**What rxm is, in the UI.** `KIND_GLOSS` in `web/src/app-header.ts` holds a second tooltip line for a kind, and only
`rxm` has one. `toggleTitle` puts it under `toggleSentence`'s words, and the last toggle pressed, which carries its
tooltip as its `aria-description`, carries the line there too. The line, verbatim:

> redextape's register machine: the IR between the source and the Turing machine

The help page, where it names the views, verbatim:

> The rxm view shows redextape's register machine, the IR between the source and the Turing machine: its control flow
> becomes the machine's states, and its registers, stack and heap become the machine's tapes. A software interpreter
> steps it, and it is not x86, ARM, WebAssembly or LLVM output.

The about page says "the rxm view shows the register-machine program the machine is lowered from", where it said an
assembly view showed the register-assembly program.

**How it was done.** `$R/rename.sh <worktree>` runs on a clean worktree whose base still says asm. It rewrites every
`asm` not preceded by `w` or `dis`, in any case, to `rxm` with each letter's case kept, and `register-asm` to `rxm`,
except inside its protect list: dated doc file names, the wasm magic `\0asm`, real assemblers' names (NASM, MASM and
others) and the scratch probes `asmbench` and `asmprobe`. Of `docs/` it rewrites only the IR views groundwork spec
and the `## ` headings of the code-history notes files, which name code files. It moves every path outside `docs/`
that names asm with `git mv`, regenerates the grammar with the pinned CLI rather than editing its generated files,
rebuilds every grammar .wasm in Docker and stops if one of the three it does not touch comes back different, makes the
one exact edit the comment guard needs (a re-added comment that named a commit), and runs `cargo fmt` and biome's
import sort. On `1b305e0` it edited 316 files, replacing 6,320 tokens and 12 phrases, kept 12 spans and moved 48
files; `b72bb16` is that output. Three sets of hand fixes follow, kept in the record as patches:
`$R/fixes-rust.patch` (`21a229b` and `38da964`), `$R/fixes-web.patch` (`41744e7` to `eab8e03`, 4 commits) and
`$R/fixes-docs.patch` (`8ccf42c` to `2b9d67c`, 7 commits).

**The replay.** In a fresh worktree at `1b305e0`, the script and then the three patches, applied with `git apply
--index`, rebuild the branch. At `38da964`, with the .wasm rebuilt, the index matched `b72bb16` and then `38da964`
exactly. At `eab8e03`, `ac571fa` and `2b9d67c`, run with `SKIP_WASM=1`, it matched everywhere but the rxm .wasm and
`grammars/wasm-manifest.json`, which that switch does not rebuild. A rebase of this branch is that replay on the new
base.

**What is still spelled asm outside `docs/`,** at `2b9d67c`: 8 lines. The README's pointer to the roadmap entry
`cli-fmt-tm-asm`, by the name the roadmap gives it; two lines of a doc comment in `trace/rxm_cursor.rs` naming the
probe `asmbench`, the dated plan file it lives in and `run_asm`, that plan's name for `run_rxm`; a dated plan file
named in `tests/rxm_roundtrip.rs`; and four `\0asm` in `scripts/check-grammar-wasm.sh`'s self-test.

##### DECISIONS

The user's, on 2026-11-02:

1. **Rename `asm` everywhere it names the IR**, code identifiers and file names included. The controller had
   recommended keeping the label.
2. **The name `rxm`**, which the user suggested in place of `RM`: "RM reads like the rm remove command". **The
   extension `.rxm`.** The user approved the design with "go".
3. **A clean break:** old share links, stored layouts, `.asm` files and `--lang asm` are not accepted. Told then that
   the loaders refuse a whole store, not only its asm part, the user confirmed it: "nobody is using this so a full
   clean break is fine". No code anywhere recognises `asm`.
4. **A `.asm` file fails to parse, as it is,** with no message of its own.
5. **A review by the `code-review` skill at HIGH** before this entry.
6. **A shorter tooltip line**, "redextape's register machine: the IR between the source and the Turing machine"
   (`8ccf42c`), with the help page unchanged. `41744e7`'s line had gone on to say a software interpreter steps it and
   that it is not x86, ARM, WebAssembly or LLVM output, which the help page still says.

The controller's, each told to the user:

- **Dated history in `docs/` is left as written**: roadmap entries, merged plans and specs record the code as it was.
  Docs that describe the code now follow the rename: the IR views groundwork spec, the README and the notes files'
  headings. This entry is the roadmap's record of the rename.
- **The frozen version 1 share link's promise is its FORMAT**, so its fixture is re-frozen with rxm (`649fc0e`), and
  an asm-era link opening the program alone is the clean break.
- **The Neovim plugin maps `.rxm` by extension,** with no sniff.

The controller's verdicts on the review, which the record does not show put to the user: findings 1-3 and 5-7 are
the user's clean break and get no fix; 4, 8 and 10 are fixed; 9 is recorded below.

##### BEHAVIOUR CHANGES: WHAT THE CLEAN BREAK GIVES UP

1. **A stored copy store with any asm copy is refused whole, so every copy is lost.** `buffers-store.ts`'s
   `validBuffer` checks each record's leg, and one record whose leg is `asm` makes the page refuse
   `redextape.buffers`: every saved copy, λ and TM ones included, and its text, with no notice.
2. **A stored layout with an asm view or an asm key is refused whole, and the page loads the default.** A
   `redextape.layout` workspace holding a view whose pane is `asm` fails `layout.ts`'s `validate`, and an arrangement
   key that spells `asm` fails `arrangements.ts`'s `parseKey`; either refuses the whole envelope, its arrangements,
   panels and preset switches with it.
3. **An old link with asm opens the program alone.** `share-link.ts`'s `readWorkspace` and `parsePositions` refuse
   its workspace and its positions, so the views and positions it carried are dropped. Sabotage S4 below shows it on
   the asm-era frozen fixture.
4. **A `.asm` file is read as `.rxt` and fails to parse, and `--lang asm` and `--form asm` are usage errors** from
   clap.
5. **Old Neovim configs naming `redextape_asm` stop matching,** and a `.asm` listing from an earlier build loses its
   filetype: the plugin's parser and filetype are `redextape_rxm`, and it no longer claims `.asm`. The controller
   checked that the snippets in `grammars/shared/*.md` do not name `redextape_asm`.

##### THE REVIEW

The `code-review` skill at HIGH read `main...rxm` at `ac571fa` and did not run the tests. It found no `asm` token left
outside `docs/` and dated pointers, and nothing like `wasm`, `disasm` or `plasma` mangled. It reported ten findings.

- **1-3 and 5-7 are the clean break**, stated above; 5 asked for one alias step at the storage and link boundary,
  which the user's choice of no code that recognises `asm` declines. No fix.
- **4, the re-frozen fixture's provenance.** Its doc said it was the link as Chrome's `encodeLink` wrote version 1,
  but node's raw deflate wrote it. `459c16e` says so ("Node's raw deflate wrote these bytes, not `encodeLink`") and
  keeps the ruling that the format is what is frozen.
- **8, a coupling claimed but not tested.** `KIND_GLOSS`'s doc said `app-header.test.ts` "holds the two", the gloss
  and the help page, but the test pinned each to a literal of its own, so they could drift apart unseen. `ca6cdcf`
  adds a test that splits `KIND_GLOSS.rxm` at `: ` and asserts that `help.html` holds each clause, and the doc says
  that is what the test checks. A sabotage of the gloss alone fails it (S6 below).
- **10, a comment naming the wrong function.** The doc comment in `trace/rxm_cursor.rs` that points at the frozen
  plan's `asmbench` said the probe measures `run_rxm`, where that plan's probe calls `run_asm`. `2b9d67c` says it
  "measures its effect on `run_rxm`, which that plan calls `run_asm`".
- **9, minor:** rxm is described three times, in `KIND_GLOSS`, `help.html` and `about.html`, and no test reads
  `about.html`'s. Fix 8 ties the first two; the third is in WHAT THIS DID NOT CLOSE.

The ledger records no review of `459c16e`, `ca6cdcf` and `2b9d67c`.

##### THE TESTS AND SABOTAGES

Five new cases and none removed, all in `b72bb16..2b9d67c`:

- `web/tests/node/app-header.test.ts`: `toggleTitle` is the sentence alone for the source, λ and TM toggles; for rxm
  it is the sentence, a newline and the gloss, in each of the three states; the help page holds its definition of
  rxm, as a literal, where it names the views; and the help page holds each clause of the gloss (`ca6cdcf`).
- `web/tests/browser/view-toggle-tooltips.test.ts`, a new file: the rxm toggle, pressed last, has the whole tooltip,
  gloss included, as its title and its `aria-description`.

Changed: `view-toggles.test.ts` and `first-load-views.test.ts` expect the rxm toggle's title to end in the gloss;
`share-link.test.ts`'s frozen version 1 link is re-frozen with rxm's names, its doc says the format is what is frozen
and names what wrote the bytes, and its `describe` is 'the frozen format of a version 1 link'; two sorted literals in
`lsp-protocol.test.ts` and `arrangements.test.ts`, and the ts-rs coverage lists in core's and the wasm crate's
`tests/ts_bindings.rs`, are in alphabetical order again; the CLI's `emit_rxm.stdout` and `fmt_help.stdout` and the
test input in `crates/redextape-grammar-check/src/rxm.rs` carry the new header and help line.

**Six sabotages, each file restored from a saved copy and checked with `cmp`, and each failed a test:**

- **S1**, on `41744e7`'s longer gloss, "a software interpreter" made "an interpreter": 1 of 8 in
  `app-header.test.ts`.
- **S2**, `viewToggles` wired to `toggleSentence` in place of `toggleTitle`: 4 of 20 in the three browser files.
- **S3**, the help page's sentence "A software interpreter steps it, and it is not x86, ARM, WebAssembly or LLVM
  output." dropped: 1 of 8, the help-page definition test.
- **S4**, the frozen fixture put back to its asm-era fragment: 1 of 41 in `share-link.test.ts`, `expected { kind:
  'program', …(2) } to deeply equal { kind: 'whole', …(4) }`. That is the clean break: the old link opens the
  program alone.
- **S5**, on `8ccf42c`'s gloss, "the IR between" made "an IR between": 1 of 8.
- **S6**, the same edit with `ca6cdcf`'s test in place: 2 of 9, the new clause test among them.

##### WHAT THIS DID NOT CLOSE

- **Finding 9: `about.html`'s description of the rxm view is pinned by no test.** A change to the gloss and the help
  page can leave it saying something else.
- **IR views groundwork PR 2 is to follow this rename,** as the lane's design orders it; the groundwork spec already
  names rxm's paths (`ac571fa`).
- **The ir-bumps branch runs in parallel, and whichever merges second rebases;** this branch rebases by the replay.
  At `f4f2172`, ir-bumps' head when this entry was written, `git merge-tree --write-tree rxm ir-bumps` merges
  cleanly, and the one file both branches change is `crates/redextape-wasm/Cargo.toml`. Its plan,
  `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-11-02-ir-views-pr1-bumps.md` on that branch, meets this one in three places: Task 5,
  not yet done at `f4f2172`, modifies `crates/redextape-grammar-check/tests/asm.rs`, which this branch moves to
  `tests/rxm.rs`; Task 9 appends a roadmap entry, as this one does; and its M-browser measurement runs `pnpm run
  test:probe:asm-copy`, which this branch names `test:probe:rxm-copy`.
- **Dated docs still say asm,** by the ruling: this file's earlier entries and the bullet this entry closes, the
  merged plans and specs, and the code-history notes' bodies. Pointers from current text into them keep the old
  names: the README's `cli-fmt-tm-asm`, and the plan file names in `trace/rxm_cursor.rs` and
  `tests/rxm_roundtrip.rs`.
- **The full gates ran at `ac571fa`, before the three review fixes,** and did not run again (VERIFICATION).
- **Nothing has run in CI:** the branch has not been pushed.

#### THE IR VIEWS GROUNDWORK'S DEPENDENCY BUMPS: A `cargo update`, CRANELIFT 0.137.1, INKWELL 0.11 ON LLVM 23, WHERE `Os` AND `Oz` RUN `O2`'S PIPELINE AND KEEP THEIR SIZE ATTRIBUTES, TREE-SITTER 0.27.1, TS-RS 12.0.1 AND WASM-PACK 0.15.1, WITH AN X86-64 LINUX SIZE BASELINE, SO THE NATIVE SIZE GATE CHECKS OBJECT SIZES ON LINUX (2026-11-02, branch `ir-bumps`, `337147d..8c623cf`, 16 commits, plus this entry, `d9c0cc0`; then `369d534`, `741c586`, `c3df447`, `df44a12`, `f4c2654` and `ab40fec`, which answer its review and a gap found while answering it, `7d55814` and `bc455ed`, which answer its final re-review, and the commits that bring this entry up to date)

**Spec §4.1's steps 0 to 4** (`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-27-ir-views-groundwork-design.md`), the groundwork's
first pull request, with three changes the user made on 2026-11-02: ts-rs 10 → 12 and wasm-pack 0.15.0 → 0.15.1 came
in ("Add both"), and the LLVM backend moved to LLVM 23 in place of 22 ("can we bump redextape to use llvm 23
instead?"). The plan is `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-11-02-ir-views-pr1-bumps.md`, written at `e810f70` and amended
for those three at `c787101`; Task 4 amends the spec's §4.1 step 3, whose condition named LLVM 22.1, to 23.1. Of the
16 commits, `e810f70` and `c787101` change only `docs/`, and the other 14 change something outside it. The lane record
is `~/temp/redextape-ir-bumps-record/` (`$R` below).

**The rebase.** After the review the branch was rebased onto `337147d` (#159). This entry names each of the branch's

##### WHAT MOVED, STEP BY STEP

- **Task 1 (spec step 0), `92dba87`: an x86-64 Linux size baseline at the old versions.** `opt_report
  --write-baseline` wrote `crates/redextape-native/baselines/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu.txt` at Cranelift 0.134.2 and
  llvm-sys 221.0.1, against LLVM 22.1.8: 48 rows, 4 programs by 2 backends by 6 levels. `main` has no such file, so on
  Linux the size test prints `NOTE: no size baseline` and passes; from this commit it compares. On an edited copy the
  gate failed three ways, once each: `loop1000000`'s LLVM `O3` row raised from 1,105 to 1,326 B, a row deleted, and a
  row added for a program the corpus does not hold.
- **Task 2 (spec step 1), `16a5cc9`: `cargo update` inside the requirements.** It locked 84 packages, among them the
  `cranelift-*` crates 0.134.2 → 0.134.4, wasm-bindgen 0.2.126 → 0.2.130, js-sys 0.3.103 → 0.3.107, tree-sitter
  0.26.12 → 0.26.13, llvm-sys 221.0.1 → 221.1.2, and proptest 1.11.0 → 1.12.0, which takes `rand` from 0.9 to 0.10.
  `tokio` 1.54.1 joined the lock through `wasm-bindgen-futures`' `rt` feature, under `wasm-bindgen-test`, a dev
  dependency. The wasm crates' floors rose to what the lock holds, `wasm-bindgen` to "0.2.130" in both,
  `wasm-bindgen-test` to "0.3.80" and `js-sys` to "0.3.107", by the controller's ruling that the wasm-bindgen family
  moves together. No size row moved; the baseline's two version lines did. `web/src/third-party-licences.json`
  changed in its `wasm` group only.
- **Task 3 (spec step 2), `31c12ef`: Cranelift 0.137.1.** The six `cranelift-*` requirements went from "0.134" to
  "0.137", and the lock moved 20 packages: 16 `cranelift-*` crates 0.134.4 → 0.137.1, `object` 0.39.1 → 0.40.0,
  `wasmtime-internal-core` and `wasmtime-internal-jit-icache-coherence` 47.0.4 → 50.0.1, and `mach2` 0.6.0, added. It
  built with no source change. 0.137's `JITBuilder::with_flags` sets `is_pic=true` on x86-64, and `JITModule::new`
  asserts `!is_pic || arch == X86_64`. The JIT builds its own ISA with `is_pic=false`, which that assertion accepts on
  every host, and by the controller's ruling it stays `false`: nothing depends on matching `with_flags`, and
  `shared::BYTES_PER_VAR` assumes `false`. The comments on the ISA flags in `jit.rs` and `aot.rs` say what holds at
  0.137 and why, and two comments that named Cranelift 0.134, on `codegen.rs`'s `emit_bin` and on `aot.rs`'s lack of
  a `global_value` instruction, dropped the version, their claims checked again in 0.137.1's source. 13 Cranelift
  rows of the x86-64 baseline moved, each by 8 B.
- **Task 4 (spec step 3, on the LLVM the user chose), `155437c`: inkwell 0.11 on LLVM 23.** `inkwell` went from "0.9"
  with `llvm22-1` to "0.11" with `llvm23-1`, and the lock moved inkwell 0.9.0 → 0.11.0, inkwell_internals 0.14.0 →
  0.16.0 and llvm-sys 221.1.2 → 231.0.2. LLVM 23 removed the `default<Os>` and `default<Oz>` pipelines: with the bump
  alone, 40 tests failed at run time, 22 of 104 under `--features llvm` and 18 of 45 under `--no-default-features
  --features llvm`, 38 on `LLVM ERROR: The optimization level "Os" is no longer supported. Use O2 in conjunction with
  the optsize attribute instead.` and 2 on the same for `"Oz"` and `minsize`. `pass_pipeline` now maps `O2`, `Os` and
  `Oz` to `default<O2>`, and `size_attributes` still puts `optsize` on the defined functions at `Os` and `minsize`
  with `optsize` at `Oz`, the attributes clang 23.1.4 emits at `-Os` and `-Oz` (and neither at `-O2`). CI,
  `scripts/check-all.sh`, the README, the doc comments and the spec name LLVM 23, and `check-all.sh` reads
  `LLVM_SYS_231_PREFIX` and probes `/usr/lib/llvm-23`. All 24 LLVM rows of the x86-64 baseline moved.
- **Task 5 (spec step 4), `771ac87`: tree-sitter 0.27.1.** The lock moved tree-sitter 0.26.13 → 0.27.1 and nothing
  else. 0.27 made `QueryMatch::captures` private, with a `captures()` method in its place, so the two reads of it, in
  `grammar.rs` and `tests/rxm.rs`, call the method. 0.27.1 loads language ABI 13 to 15, and the four grammars'
  `parser.c`, which the pinned 0.25.10 CLI generates, are ABI 15. With the TM parser's `LANGUAGE_VERSION` set to 12,
  16 of the crate's 64 tests failed, on `Incompatible language version 12. Expected minimum 13, maximum 15`.
- **Task 6 (the user's addition), `dd2fbdb`: ts-rs 12.0.1.** ts-rs and ts-rs-macros 10.1.0 → 12.0.1. In 12,
  `TS::export_to_string` takes a `&Config`, so the 29 calls in the two `ts_bindings.rs` guards, 21 in `redextape-core`
  and 8 in `redextape-wasm`, pass one: `Config::from_env()` at this commit, `Config::new()` since `e2b2d33` (below).
  The 29 files `pnpm run build:bindings` writes were byte-identical to ts-rs 10's at this commit.
- **Task 7 (the user's addition), `4bda226`: wasm-pack 0.15.1** at its three install sites, the Dockerfile's `wasm`
  stage and CI's `rust-browser` and `web` jobs. Built with 0.15.0 and then 0.15.1 at the same lock, the 12 files of
  `pkg/` and `pkg-lsp/` were byte-identical. The URLs keep `github.com/rustwasm/wasm-pack`, which redirects to
  `wasm-bindgen/wasm-pack`.
- **Task 8, `bd0079f`: the Mac baseline,** rewritten on the Mac, an aarch64 machine with Homebrew's LLVM 23.1.4 and
  rustc 1.99.1, at `7398103`. First, at `1b305e0` against Homebrew's LLVM 22.1.8, the size test passed there and
  `--write-baseline` wrote `main`'s file back byte for byte; at `7398103` the size test passed against that file before
  it was rewritten.

##### CI'S LLVM

`runs-on: docker` starts `node:22-bookworm`, Debian 12. Run in that image, the job's install step (`llvm.sh 23`, then
an `apt-get install` of `libpolly-23-dev`) installs `llvm-23`, `llvm-23-dev` and `libpolly-23-dev` at
`1:23.1.5~++20261028083858+a738f2737189-1~exp1~20261028203909.94`: a snapshot of LLVM's `release/23.x` branch
labelled 23.1.5, a version not released when the plan was written, on 2026-11-02, the newest release then being
`llvmorg-23.1.4`. `llvm-sys` 231 accepts any 23.1. In that container at Task 4, with `llvm-config` 23.1.5,
`cargo test -p redextape-native --features llvm` passed 104 tests and `--no-default-features --features llvm` 45,
with no `NOTE` line.

**The presence loop reads `--link-static`.** On this LLVM 23, `llvm-config --libnames` prints only `libLLVM-23.so`, so a
loop over it never looks for Polly. llvm-sys 231.0.2's build script prefers static linking when no feature says
otherwise, and inkwell 0.11's `llvm23-1` sets none, so it reads `--libnames --link-static`, which lists `libPolly.a` and
`libPollyISL.a` with the LLVM archives; the loop read the same from Task 4 until `741c586` (below). Since `85d0873` the
step captures the listing before the loop: when a component's static archive is missing, `llvm-config --libnames
--link-static` exits 1 with nothing on stdout, and a loop over its output ran zero times and passed. In
`node:22-bookworm`, with `libLLVMCore.a` deleted after a full install, the step as it was exited 0 and the step at
`8c623cf` exits 1; without `libpolly-23-dev` that step exits 1, naming `libPolly.a`; and with everything installed the
step exits 0.

##### THE SIZE TEST ON LLVM 23

`the_size_attributes_make_oz_ir_strictly_smaller_than_os_o2_and_o3_and_os_smaller_than_o3` counts the instructions
left in `SIZE_FIXTURE`'s IR after each level's pipeline. In the plan's probe, on LLVM 23.1.4 with the `default<O2>`
arm and a print of the counts added, they were `O2` 61, `O3` 61, `Os` 38 and `Oz` 32, the four figures the test's doc
gave at `31c12ef` on LLVM 22.1. With the size attributes suppressed, `Os` and `Oz` measured 61 each and the test failed
at `Oz < O3`; on LLVM 22.1, with the `default<Os>` and `default<Oz>` pipelines still in place, the doc gave 61 and 63.
On LLVM 23 the attributes are what sets the size levels apart from `O2`. The doc's measured margin, "(`Os` 38, `Oz`
32)", came out of the comment in `a211c55` and is here instead.

##### THE §7.2 MEASUREMENTS

The per-task timings the plan names, M-browser before and after Task 2 and M-native before and after Tasks 3 and 4, and
the A/B re-runs the implementers added to them, were taken while other work loaded the machine: the 1-minute load
average at their starts was 22.11 to 42.62, on 32 threads. By the controller's ruling they were redone as one
interleaved A/B of `main`'s build, at `1b305e0`, against this branch's, at `7398103`, and none of their timings is
quoted here but one ratio of Task 4's, below. `bd0079f` and `8c623cf` change nothing either side builds: the Mac
baseline, and `//!` lines in a test.

**The machine.** Davey-Endeavor, the x86-64 Linux development machine, 32 threads, from 19:01:37 to 19:04:17 on
2026-11-02. Three other sessions stopped their Docker builds and an Android emulator for it: their containers had exited
at 18:52:46 and the emulator at 19:00:59, and the controller ended the hold at 19:04. Still running, by the A/B agent's

`git log -S`, at about one core at 19:01:51; and desktop applications, `steamwebhelper` at 90% of a core at 19:04:02.

four samples, against 66% to 71% in the five inside pairs 1 and 2, and its timing figures over 1 ms read a median 1.248

Round 2's flag there, `list30000` Cranelift `O3` `compile`, is 204.5 µs on base, with a spread of 71.3, against 286.1 on

4's frozen `opt_report` binaries, which embed the same `cranelift-codegen` 0.137.1, so a ratio that size comes up on
that row between two builds of one Cranelift.

**What the native spread can and cannot rule out.** The base runs' spread is a median 18.4% of the base median in round
1, quartiles 10.5% and 27.2%, with 22 of the 96 figures under 10%, and 20.6% in round 2. The rule flags a figure only
when final's median is above base's by more than base's spread, so on a figure of the median spread it cannot tell a
slowdown of under about a fifth from noise. With no change at all, three runs against three drawn from one normal
distribution flag 8.77% of figures, 8.4 of 96, in a seeded simulation of 200,000 trials; the rounds flagged 7 and 3, and
no figure in both. A slowdown across the rows would move the median ratios, which over both metrics and both rounds are
1.001 to 1.018 for Cranelift and 0.863 to 0.950 for LLVM.

**M-browser.** The comparer flagged 0 of 124 figures. The 24 that must not vary, the instruction count per text size and
the steps, cap and frames per memory case, were equal across all six runs, and each of the 10 MiB figures read the same
in all six. The six RUN medians were 1.5 to 38.7 ms on base, at final/base ratios of 0.842 to 1.006. The two rows the
review of Task 2 raised from its loaded run read 1.006 for "loop to the step cap" (base 31.8 ms with a spread of 1.3,
final 32.0) and 0.978 for "heap cells" (31.4 with 4.1, final 30.7). The base spread is a median 35.7% of the base median
over the 98 SIZE figures and 36.6% over the 10 MEM `build_ms` figures, so on a typical one of those the rule cannot tell
a slowdown of under about a third from noise; on the RUN figures it is 4.1% to 13.4%, but for "call frames" at 33.3% and
"saved locals" at 105.3%.

**The ruling.** No slowdown reproduced, so by the controller's ruling §7.2's rule is met by the repeat round and the
pooled result. The spec says "A slowdown beyond run-to-run noise blocks the PR until explained or removed", and the plan
reads it as "A slowdown larger than the spread of the three before-runs is a finding: report it, and do not ship it
unexplained". Round 1's 7 native flags are not flagged again in the repeat round, the repeat round's 3 were not flagged
in round 1, the pooled six runs a side flag none of the 96, and M-browser flags none of its 124.

##### THE ONE-BYTE LLVM DIFFERENCE

At Task 4, 18 of the 24 LLVM rows on x86-64 shrank by exactly 1 B, and on the Mac 18 of its 24 did. The byte was never
in the object. inkwell 0.9.0's `MemoryBuffer::get_size` returns `LLVMGetBufferSize(..) + 1`, counting the NUL that
LLVM guarantees after a buffer, and `as_slice`, which `llvm::object_bytes` copies, is that long; inkwell 0.11.0's
returns `LLVMGetBufferSize(..)`. So under inkwell 0.9 every LLVM row read 1 B more than its object. A dump of
`object_bytes` for `loop1000000` at `O0` read 1,377 B under `31c12ef` and 1,376 under `155437c`'s tree, equal in the
first 1,376 bytes and with the same `readelf -S`; the extra byte is a `00` after the section header table, which ends
at byte 1,376. So at `O0` LLVM 22.1.8 and 23.1.4 emitted the same object for that program. The plan's probe had seen
the byte first: inkwell 0.11.0 on LLVM 22.1.8 shrank all 24 LLVM rows by exactly 1 B.

##### WHAT THIS DID NOT CLOSE

- **The size gate on the Mac would not see every LLVM pass stop, and CI runs no job on that triple.** In
  `baselines/aarch64-apple-darwin.txt` at `bd0079f`, `loop1000000`'s LLVM `O0` is 1,008 B against an `O3` row of 928,
  8.62% over it and inside the ±10% band, so an `O3` pipeline that stopped firing for that program on the Mac would
  leave the size test green; in `main`'s Mac file that margin was 15.58%. Set against every level and not `O3` alone,
  `list30000`'s `Oz` row, 1,464 B against an `O0` of 1,520, is 3.83% inside, and it was 3.82% in `main`'s file, so that
  one predates this branch. In the x86-64 file every LLVM row clears the band at every level, the thinnest `list30000`'s
  `O1` at 16.92%. The Mac file is checked only where someone runs the size test on a Mac. Since `df44a12` the header of
  `tests/size_baseline.rs` names no file's margins, and since `bc455ed` it points at no document: it says a row's margin
  is read off its baseline file.
- **The coverage run's "Failed to fetch dynamically imported module" failures, under load.** At Task 6,
  `pnpm run test:coverage` failed twice before it passed: in 2 files at a 1-minute load of 56.53, then in 3 files and
  1 test at 30.02, each failing file on `TypeError: Failed to fetch dynamically imported module:
  http://localhost:63315/src/main.ts`; the third run passed, 281 files and 2,951 tests. Both failed logs carry vite's
  "Re-optimizing dependencies because vite config has changed". The full runs that passed at Task 6's third try, at
  Task 7 and in the whole-branch gate carry none, but Task 2's coverage re-run and Task 6's run of the two failed
  files alone carry it and passed, so the line does not separate the runs. Task 6's change cannot reach what vitest
  loads there: neither wasm build links ts-rs, and the bindings were byte-identical. The cause was not established.
- **The session-memory test failed once, under load.** At Task 2, `test:coverage` failed in
  `session-memory.test.ts`, "measures what a leg of history really costs against what the ring charged it", on
  `expected -1.3466548678574888 to be greater than 0.1`, at a 1-minute load of 31.47; one of its rounds read
  `real=-28090148` against `accounted=6343013`. The file alone passed 3 times of 3, and the whole leg, run again,
  passed, 281 files and 2,951 tests. The cause was not established.
- **The apt cache starts cold.** The `rust-llvm` job's cache key moved from `apt-llvm-22` to `apt-llvm-23`, which no run
  has saved, and its `restore-keys` is the same string, so the first run downloads every .deb. The install step ran only
  in local `node:22-bookworm` containers; that its cold path and the save after it work on the runner is unproven until
  CI runs it. The key is fixed, and the cache action saves nothing after a hit on it, so once a run has saved it and the
  snapshot then moves, every run downloads the packages again.
- **CI's LLVM is whatever `release/23.x` snapshot apt.llvm.org serves that day.** The step requires `23.1.*` (`741c586`)
  and pins no package version. The committed x86-64 baseline came from Arch's 23.1.4, and the 23.1.5 snapshot of
  2026-10-28 already gives 16 of the 24 LLVM rows other sizes, by at most 1.70% (THE SIZE BASELINES), so a later
  snapshot can move rows further on a pull request that changes nothing the size test measures, and a row moved past the
  band fails it.
- **`loop1000000`'s `Os` object is the size of its `O2` object on LLVM 23.1.4,** 1,136 B each on x86-64 and 904 on
  the Mac, where on LLVM 22 x86-64 gave 1,097 against 1,105; on the Mac they were equal on LLVM 22 too, at 873. CI's
  23.1.5 snapshot gives 1,128 against 1,136. Nothing asserts that a size level's object is smaller than `O2`'s: the
  size test counts instructions in `SIZE_FIXTURE`'s IR.
- **No box builder in `measure::CORPUS`.** Spec §7.2 asks for list and box builders; the corpus holds `loop1000000`,
  `sum30000`, `list30000` and `map30000`, so the A/B measures list builders and no box builder. PR 2, whose heap core
  needs box measurements, is where one comes in.
- **`cargo deny check advisories` was not run here,** as cargo-deny is not installed; the advisories workflow runs it
  on this branch's pull request, since the workflow's `pull_request` paths include `Cargo.lock`.
- **`redextape-cli`'s `toml = "1.1.4"` floor is behind the lock,** which Task 2's `cargo update` took from
  1.1.4+spec-1.1.0 to 1.1.8+spec-1.1.0. It was left alone by the controller's ruling: floors rise here only for the
  wasm-bindgen family.
- **The nullability gate fails some `optional_fields` shapes that keep the null** (`ab40fec`): a container carrying the
  bare key and `= nullable` in two `ts(...)` lists, in either order, or in one list with `= nullable` after the bare
  key, or the bare key and then `= false`, in one list or in two; an `Option<Option<T>>` field, from which ts-rs strips
  one `Option`; a field with `ts(skip)`; and a variant whose own `type` replaces its payload. In each ts-rs 12.0.1
  writes `| null` or no field at all, so there the gate fails where it need not, and asks for `optional = nullable` or
  `= false`. In one list ts-rs keeps the later key, so `optional_fields = nullable, optional_fields` writes `field?: T`,
  which drops the null, and the gate is right to fail it.
- **A cargo `[env]` table can still set the three variables the bindings scripts drop.** `369d534` takes
  `TS_RS_IMPORT_EXTENSION`, `TS_RS_LARGE_INT` and `TS_RS_USE_V11_HASHMAP` out of the environment cargo starts with, and
  cargo sets an `[env]` entry of a `config.toml` it reads for the processes it runs when that variable is absent: in a
  scratch crate whose `.cargo/config.toml` sets all three, a test run under `env -u` on each read each one set. ts-rs
  12.0.1's `Config::from_env`, which the derived export tests build, reads all three, so under such a table the written
  bindings can differ from what both guards check, and the guards, which build `Config::new()`, still pass. The repo's
  `.cargo/config.toml` sets only `RUST_MIN_STACK` in `[env]`, and `$CARGO_HOME/config.toml` has no `[env]` table. Since
  `7d55814` the comment in `redextape-core`'s `ts_bindings.rs` says that the table can still set them.
- **Nothing has run in CI:** the branch has not been pushed. Its first `rust-llvm` run is the first CI run in which the
  size test reads a baseline.

#### WEB'S DEPENDENCY BUMPS: EVERY PIN TO THE NEWEST RELEASE OF ITS CARET RANGE, `web-tree-sitter` 0.27.1, BIOME 2.6.4 AND PLAYWRIGHT 1.64.1 AMONG THEM, WITH TWO BROWSER TESTS MOVED TO REAL GESTURES FOR CHROMIUM 156, AND VITEST 5 LEFT OUT (2026-11-03, branch `web-bumps`, `14621b1..d337369`, 13 commits, three of them this entry's earlier versions, `1b7a47a`, `e7eaa39` and `57286d2`, plus this rewrite)

**Spec §4.1a** (`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-27-ir-views-groundwork-design.md`), the user's decision of 2026-10-27:
`web/`'s pnpm dependencies move as far as they safely go, within their ranges first and then each major on its own,
with the full checks green, and a bump that fails is left out and recorded. The controller ruled pnpm's and Node's
own versions out of scope. Biome 2.6.4 and Playwright 1.64.1 are in their caret ranges and failed the checks at first;
the user's decision of 2026-11-03, on the branch's first review, was that both go in, with whatever test and lint
config changes they need. The lane record is `~/temp/redextape-web-bumps-record/` (`$R` below); its `plan.md` holds
the inventory, taken against the live npm registry on 2026-11-02, the breaking changes of vitest 5 against this tree's
usage, and each failure's first lines. The Chromium investigation's record is `~/temp/redextape-chrome156-record/`
(`$C` below).

##### WHAT MOVED

- **Within range, `ca269f2`.** Every direct dependency in `web/package.json` is an exact pin, so "within range" here
  means the newest release a caret range on the pin would allow: the same major, or the same minor for a `0.x`
  package. CodeMirror's `commands` moved 6.10.4 → 6.11.1, `language` 6.12.4 → 6.13.1, `state` 6.7.1 → 6.7.6 and
  `view` 6.43.8 → 6.43.15; `@types/node` 26.1.2 → 26.6.6; Vite 8.2.1 → 8.3.5; vitest and its three `@vitest/*`
  packages 4.1.10 → 4.1.12; and `web-tree-sitter` 0.27.0 → 0.27.1. `pnpm update` then moved the transitive packages
  inside their own ranges. Biome 2.5.7 → 2.6.4 and Playwright 1.62.1 → 1.64.1 follow in their own commits, below.
  Over the branch the lock goes from 149 packages to 153: 70 change version and 4 are new,
  `@codemirror/streamparser` 6.0.0, a dependency of `language` 6.13.1, `@rolldown/binding-android-arm-eabi` 1.2.16,
  and Biome's `@biomejs/cli-android-arm64` and `@biomejs/cli-android-x64` 2.6.4.
- **`third-party-licences.json`**, regenerated by `node scripts/licences.ts`: 13 packages differ, all in its `code`
  group. They are the four CodeMirror packages, `@codemirror/streamparser`, which is new, three `@lezer/*` packages,
  `@marijn/find-cluster-break`, `style-mod`, Vite, rolldown 1.2.3 → 1.2.16 and `web-tree-sitter`. Biome and
  Playwright are dev dependencies and ship nothing.
- **`web-tree-sitter` 0.27.1 loads the grammars the pinned CLI builds.** The four committed grammar `.wasm` come
  from `parser.c` files headed `@generated by tree-sitter v0.25.10`, and `scripts/check-grammar-wasm.sh` holds each
  to its `parser.c`. On 0.27.1, `web/tests/browser/grammar-differential.test.ts`, which loads all four through the
  app's `createGrammarRegistry` and compares their captures with `grammars/capture-golden.json`, passed 6 of 6, and
  `web/tests/node/colour.test.ts`, which loads them through `Language.load`, passed 34 of 34. With the TM grammar's
  `.wasm` cut to its first 4,096 bytes, the differential failed 2 and the colour file failed at load, each with
  `CompileError: ... section (code 10, "Code") extends past end of the module`; the file was then restored from a
  copy, and `cmp` found it equal.
- **Comments that cite a version name the installed one, `fed76d2`.** `colour.ts` and
  `grammar-differential.test.ts` cite `web-tree-sitter` 0.27.1, `pane-host.ts` `@codemirror/view` 6.43.15 twice,
  `harness.ts` Vitest 4.1.12, and `licences.ts`'s `TOOLCHAIN` list `web-tree-sitter` 0.27.1. Each claim was read
  again in the installed source first, and holds: 0.27.1's `ts_query_captures_wasm` passes `start_index` to
  `ts_query_cursor_set_byte_range` unconverted while `ts_node_start_index_wasm` returns `byte_to_code_unit` of the
  byte offset (`lib/tree-sitter.c`, embedded in the package's `.wasm` source map); 6.43.15's `readSelectionRange`
  keeps its 200 ms check and `observers.focus` its scroll reset; 4.1.12's `setIframeViewport` resolves one animation
  frame after the resize. The Emscripten licence text stays at 4.0.15: tree-sitter's
  `crates/loader/emscripten-version` reads 4.0.15 at `v0.27.1`, and its release workflow builds the npm package's
  `.wasm` with `cargo xtask build-wasm`, which runs `emcc` from the `docker.io/emscripten/emsdk` image of that version.
  The committed `LICENSE` is byte-identical to Emscripten's at its `4.0.15` tag.
- **Biome 2.6.4, `da3081f` and `d337369`.** 2.6 deprecates `linter.rules.recommended` for `linter.rules.preset`, whose
  default is `recommended`, and `biome migrate --write` rewrites `"recommended": true` as `"preset": "none"`, which
  enables no rule, so `web/biome.json` is edited by hand and names no preset. `biome rage --linter` lists 178 enabled
  rules on 2.5.7 with `"recommended": true`, 181 on 2.6.4 with no preset named, the same 181 with `"preset":
  "recommended"`, and 0 under `"none"`. The 181 are all 178 and the three 2.6 adds to its recommended set,
  `complexity/useMathMinMax`, `correctness/noDuplicateFieldDefinitionNames` and `performance/useDomNodeTextContent`;
  they stay on, since the recommended set is what the config asks for. A file with a `debugger` statement and a
  `document.body.innerText` read fails `biome lint` with `suspicious/noDebugger` and `performance/useDomNodeTextContent`
  with no preset named and under `"recommended"`, and passes under `"none"`. The one new diagnostic on the tree is
  `useDomNodeTextContent` on `label.innerText` in `web/tests/browser/base16-remove.test.ts`, which reads `innerText` on
  purpose: the label is `text-transform: uppercase`, and the rule's fix, `textContent`, reads the text before the
  transform. A `biome-ignore` for that rule alone says so on the line above.
- **Playwright 1.64.1, `918115d`, and with it Chromium 156.** Playwright 1.62.1 drives Chromium 151.0.7922.34,
  1.63.0 Chromium 153.0.8010.12 and 1.64.1 Chromium 156.0.8078.4, and CI installs the Chromium of the Playwright the
  lock names. Two browser tests failed on 1.63.0 and on 1.64.1 and passed on 1.62.1:

  ```
  FAIL  browser (chromium)  tests/browser/extend-focus-probe.test.ts > focus when a frontier control is withdrawn > hiding or disabling the focused frontier control strands focus on body
  AssertionError: expected <button type="button" …(3)></button> to be <body>…(8)</body> // Object.is equality
  FAIL  browser (chromium)  tests/browser/virtual-grid.test.ts > a virtual grid > follows again on attach after a link, though the frame it draws has not changed
  Error: timed out after 10000ms waiting for a user scroll to detach following
  ```

  Both come from how the tests drove the page, and from two Chromium changes. With real gestures, the app ends the
  same in Chromium 151, 153 and 156: `◀` pressed at step 1, by the mouse or by Enter, leaves the focus on `<body>`,
  and Tab then reaches `▶`; and the rule table detaches on a wheel and returns to the same row on attach.
  - **Chromium `e939057f7a`**, flag `AvoidSynchronousBlurOnDisabledAttributeChange`: a focused form control that
    becomes disabled keeps the focus until the next rendering update, where the HTML spec's focus fixup rule moves
    it to `<body>`. On 156, `document.activeElement` read in the task that disables the control is the control, and
    `<body>` two animation frames later; with the flag off, it is `<body>` at once, as on 151. A control that becomes
    `hidden` still loses the focus at once, on 151 and on 156. The probe disabled a focused `▶` in code and read the
    focus in the same task. It now clicks a button of its own, fixed at the page's corner, whose click disables it,
    checks that the click focused it, and waits for the focus to reach `<body>` (`6ef5ab7`). `918115d` pressed the
    app's `◀` at step 1 instead, which asserted the `◀` defect under WHAT THIS DID NOT CLOSE, so that version would
    have failed its fix; with `◀` given a hand-off like `⏭`'s, the probe now passes 3 of 3. No app code reads the
    focus after disabling a focused control and expects `<body>`: `step-controls.ts` hands `⏭`'s focus on before it
    disables `⏭`.
  - **Chromium `678107367b`**, flag `EventTimingMatchingHTML`: a scroll made inside a scroll event's dispatch gets its
    own event in the next frame. The grid case set `scrollTop = 0` to stand for a user's scroll, and ran on from the
    previous case's await of a scroll event, so inside its dispatch. On 153 and 156 the new box's first resize report
    then ran first, `Follow.onResize(0)` made following expect a scroll to 0, and the event read as its echo, so
    following never detached; with the flag off, 156 detaches again. Made from a plain task, the same write detaches
    in every build. On 1.64.1 the case fails both in the whole file and run straight after "holds a link's row…", and
    "centres the row it follows…", which used the same write, fails run straight after it. The same change blinded
    "reads no scroll as the user's while its panel is closed", which follows a case that ends on a scroll event's
    await and stands for the late echo of the grid's own scroll: with the grid's closed-panel guard removed, it passed
    in file order and failed alone. The test side's cause is the harness's `scrolled()`, which resolved from inside
    the event's listener, so the code after its await, the next case included, ran inside the dispatch. It resolves
    from a task after the event now (`1fe4fb1`), and with that alone the old write passes straight after "holds a
    link's row…", and the closed-panel case fails in file order without its guard and with no yield of its own. The
    files that use `scrolled()` pass: `lambda-follow` 9, `focus-scroll` 11 and `virtual-grid` 23. The grid file's
    three user scrolls are a wheel all the same (`70f2dc9`, `1fe4fb1`): `wheelToTop` waits two frames for the grid's
    first resize report, turns the wheel, and waits until the box's `scrollTop` holds for six frames, and `steady`
    throws, naming what it watched, when it does not. In headless Chromium 156 the wheel moves the box in one scroll
    event, straight to 0. Each passes alone, straight after "holds a link's row…" and in file order, and fails when
    the grid's scroll listener no longer calls `Follow.onScroll`. The two that had no wait before the wheel passed 10
    runs of 10 at a 25% CPU quota both before the wait was added and after.
- **`style.css`'s note on a transparent select's open list names Chromium 156, `6f12be0`.** In a headed Chromium
  156.0.8078.4 under Xvfb, with the dark scheme, a transparent select's open list is white, `#FFFFFF`, under the
  palette's light text, and with an `option` rule it is the rule's colour; 151.0.7922.34 gives the same.
- **`grammars/tree-sitter-redextape/README.md`, `e273aab`**: its note on an earlier CLI pin to "0.27.0" said no such
  release exists; 0.27.0 came out on 2026-08-30, so it now says none existed yet.

##### WHAT WAS LEFT OUT

- **vitest stays at 4.1.12; 5.1.0 and 5.0.5 fail.** Its three `@vitest/*` packages move with it, as each requires
  the same version. On 5.1.0, with no change to the config or the tests, three browser tests:

  ```
  FAIL  browser (chromium)  tests/browser/lambda-follow.test.ts > a λ view whose box changes size under it > stays following when the WINDOW grows and its clamp is reported before its resize
  Error: timed out after 10000ms waiting for the window to grow
  FAIL  browser (chromium)  tests/browser/panel-boundaries.test.ts > a drag of a boundary > stops where a neighbour would go under its floor of five rows
  TimeoutError: frame.dragAndDrop: Timeout 14893ms exceeded.
  FAIL  browser (chromium)  tests/browser/view-keys-focus.test.ts > the focus after a view key > on a header control > stays on share
  AssertionError: precondition: the toggles are shown: expected true to be false // Object.is equality
  ```

  Every other step passed. Run alone, the three fail on 5.1.0 and on 5.0.5. Two causes were ruled out. v5's inline
  projects inherit the root config, but with `extends: false` on both, as in v4, all three still fail and a fourth
  joins them. And `page.viewport` sizes the page as before: a probe test read the same `innerWidth` by `innerHeight`
  after `page.viewport` at 1280×896, 600×400 and 1600×1200 on 5.0.5 as on 4.1.12. What is left points at v5's
  reworked browser orchestrator (vitest's #9745, "Iframe scale", and #10212, locators serialized as objects):
  `lambda-follow.test.ts` resizes the window by restyling the element round vitest's iframe and resizing the top
  window over CDP, a lever into vitest's own page; "stays on share" runs after its file's own window-narrowing case and
  finds the toggles still hidden at 1280 px; and the drag resolved its target and then stalled in Playwright's
  `dragAndDrop`, "waiting for scheduled navigations to finish". This was not taken further.

  Pinning 5.1.0, released on the day of the inventory, made pnpm 11.20.0's `pnpm install` write an untracked
  `web/pnpm-workspace.yaml` with 9 `minimumReleaseAgeExclude` entries, its exemptions from pnpm's minimum release
  age. Nothing here commits that file.

##### WHAT THIS DID NOT CLOSE

- **vitest 5**, for the user to decide: the three tests' levers. That commit also needs `.vitest/` in `.gitignore`,
  as v5 writes failure screenshots to `web/.vitest/attachments/failure-screenshots/`, and `.gitignore` lists
  `.vitest-attachments/` and `**/__screenshots__/`.
- **For a PR of its own on the step buttons' focus, queued after this one and not yet begun:**
  - `◀` pressed at step 1, and `▶` at a finished run's last step, drop the focus to `<body>`; neither has a hand-off
    like `⏭`'s. It is on `main` and not caused by this branch: for `◀`, Chromium 151, 153 and 156 all end on
    `<body>`, and Tab recovers to `▶`. The focus probe no longer depends on it.
  - `↺` and `⏵` have no hand-off either, and since the probe's disabled half clicks a button of its own, no test
    holds the hazard on the app's step buttons.
  - **This branch's move to Chromium 156 blinds a test.** "hands the focus to ◀ when ⏭ goes off under it", in
    `web/tests/browser/step-controls.test.ts`, holds `step-controls.ts` to calling `handOff` before it disables `⏭`.
    On 156 a disabled button keeps the focus until the next rendering update, so with the two lines swapped the file
    still passes 7 of 7. On 151, where the blur is synchronous, the swapped call would find the focus already on
    `<body>` and hand nothing on.
- Seven pins were already the newest release: TypeScript 7.0.2, `@codemirror/lint` 6.9.7, `@codemirror/search`
  6.7.2, `@fontsource/inter` 5.3.0, `@replit/codemirror-vim` 6.4.0, `dom-accessibility-api` 0.7.1 and `hack-font`
  3.3.0.
- Nothing has run in CI.
