#### FIREFOX PR 1: AN OPT-IN `firefox` BROWSER PROJECT, `pnpm test:firefox`, RUNS THE BROWSER TIER IN PLAYWRIGHT'S FIREFOX, WHERE THE 16 TESTS THAT NEED WHAT ONLY CHROMIUM HAS ARE SKIPPED WITH THEIR REASONS, `collect.ts` COLLECTS THROUGH PLAYWRIGHT'S `page.requestGC()` AND THE SYNTHETIC POINTER EVENTS CARRY THE ID A REAL MOVE REPORTED; THIS PR LEAVES CI AS IT WAS, AND THE FIREFOX RUN'S FAILURES ARE LEFT TO PRS 2 TO 5 (2026-11-03, branch `firefox-local`, `e9bbf67..9040ffa`, 13 commits, plus this entry, `362d3e2`, and the two commits that correct it, `964a038` and the one that records the user's ruling on base16-remove's cases)

**The first of five Firefox PRs.** On 2026-11-03 the user asked "Can you add Firefox to CI", and ruled its scope to
be the web browser tier, less the files that use APIs only Chromium has, and the wasm boundary. Measured at `e9bbf67`
in a scratch worktree, Chromium passed the tier's 1,540 tests in
212 files. With `$R/firefox-measure.patch` applied to `collect.ts` and `vite.config.ts`, so that Firefox could run the
tier at all, Firefox failed 145 of them with 19 unhandled errors in one run, and 139, again with 19, in a second, made
with `firefox-measure-diag.patch`, the same plus a print of `document.hasFocus()` per file. The wasm boundary passed
33 of 33 in Firefox. The user chose to fix every failure before Firefox runs in CI, in five PRs (THE USER'S
DECISIONS below). PR 1 is there to give the later PRs a Firefox run whose failures are Firefox's own: one command
runs it, `collect.ts` works there, the tests that need what only Chromium has are skipped there with their reasons,
and no synthetic pointer event throws there. The spec is
`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-03-firefox-pr1-local-project-design.md` and the plan
`docs/superpowers/plans/2026-11-03-firefox-pr1-local-project.md`. The lane record is
`~/temp/redextape-firefox-ci-record/` (`$R` below): the base measurement is `$R/measure-report.md` with its logs in
`$R/logs/`, this PR's runs are in `$R/logs/pr1/`, and the task reports and reviews are in `$R/tasks/`.

##### WHAT CHANGED

- **The spec and the plan.** `be23df0` is the design, `719aa58` applied the user's three decisions to it, and
  `c6e72ba` is the plan, in 5 tasks. A read-only pre-flight of the plan made thirteen findings; `acb67fd` (the spec)
  and `f31f943` (the plan) answered them, with the user's rulings on three of them (F3 to F5 below).
- **Task 1, `68b88a4`: `until.ts`, `engine.ts`, the Firefox project, and `collect.ts` in every engine.**
  - `until`, with `sourceOf` and `MAX_SOURCE_CHARS`, moved from `web/tests/browser/harness.ts` to a new
    `web/tests/browser/until.ts` that imports nothing. `harness.ts` imports it and re-exports it, so none of its
    importers had to change its import. `tests/node/browser-timeout-invariants.test.ts` reads the default bound from
    `until.ts`, and its alias check matches an import from either module, with a new case for that.
  - `web/vite.config.ts` builds each browser project with one function, `browserProject(name, browser, provider,
    commands)`. The `firefox` project is among the projects only when `REDEXTAPE_FIREFOX` is set, which
    `pnpm test:firefox` (`web/package.json`) does. It registers one browser command, `requestGC`, which calls
    Playwright's `page.requestGC()`. With the variable unset, the projects are `node` and `browser`, whose fields
    are the base project's plus an empty `commands` (the whole-branch review).
  - `web/tests/browser/engine.ts` exports `CHROMIUM`; `chromiumOnly(ctx, reason)`, a test's first statement, which
    skips the test outside Chromium with its reason; and `mousePointerId()`, which on its first call hovers a
    temporary element at two points and resolves with the `pointerId` of the last `pointermove` it heard, waiting
    with `until` at its default bound, and keeps that answer in a module-scoped variable for later calls.
    `engine.test.ts` holds the gate to `server.browser` in an `afterAll`, and checks that the capture of a synthetic
    press carrying the reported id does not throw.
  - `collect.ts` collects as before in Chromium. In any other engine it calls `commands.requestGC()` in place of
    `gc`, under the same pages-alive guard.
  - The README's Checks section names `pnpm test:firefox`. Comments the change made inexact were corrected: one line
    for one, the four that named `harness.ts` as `until`'s home, in buffers-quota, buffer-cool-warm,
    tm-reduced-buffer and tm-blank-buffer, and five in `vite.config.ts` (spec §4); and two lines for two,
    `vite.config.ts`'s v8 coverage comment, which said that `instances` is Chromium-only.
- **Task 2, `4d3d21c`: the gates and the finger.**
  - The 15 tests that need CDP, `performance.memory` and `gc`, or an AltGraph press, which Playwright's Firefox
    cannot send, start with `chromiumOnly` and their reasons: focus-press 5, frame-cost 2, session-memory 2,
    share-popover 2, view-keys 2, lambda-follow 1 and share-open-clamps 1. view-keys' modifier table became
    `it.for`, so that its AltGraph row can take `ctx`. share-open-clamps' two cascades are not gated: they pass in
    Firefox once the case before them is skipped.
  - share-popover's `afterAll` resets the browser's permissions only when a case set one, through a flag the two
    gated cases set before their first CDP call, so in Firefox it sends nothing.
  - panel-boundaries' "leaves a finger’s press alone, which the boundary itself takes" (U1) sends a real touch
    through CDP's `Input.dispatchTouchEvent` in Chromium, where it had dispatched synthetic `PointerEvent`s, and is
    the 16th gated test. A `finally` lifts the finger, and focus-press's `tap` lifts its own in a `finally` too.
    `fire` lost its `pointerType` parameter.
- **Task 3, `1b09226` and `87feecf`: the reported pointer id.**
  - `1b09226`: panel-boundaries' file doc no longer counts the cases that make their own pointer events or says
    that each gives its reason, which Task 2's review found false (its Important 1): five cases do, one for a
    reason the doc did not name and one with none.
  - `87feecf`: divider-drag, layout-view, panel-boundaries, panel-regions and pane-floor await `mousePointerId()`
    once, in a top-level `beforeAll` before any mount, and every synthetic pointer event that carried `pointerId: 1`
    carries that id. In Firefox, `setPointerCapture` throws for a synthetic id until real mouse input has reached the
    tab and then takes 0, never 1 (spec §3.5, probe P2), so no fixed id serves both engines. `separator.ts`'s comment
    and pane-floor's say that capture throws for an id the browser holds no active pointer for.
- **The whole-branch review's fixes, `dce5c96`, `2149bfb`, `fc9edad` and `9040ffa`, text only**
  (`$R/tasks/whole-branch-review.md`).
  - `dce5c96`: `style.css`'s comments on two of its `position-area` fallbacks said the browser tier runs Chromium
    only; they say that Chromium and the opt-in Firefox both have `position-area`, so the fallback fires in neither
    (the review's probe, cited in spec §4). `session-worker.ts`'s "needs Chrome" became "needs a browser".
  - `2149bfb`: `until.ts`'s doc said the invariant test fails for "any call site under `tests/browser/`"; it says a
    call site in a `.test.ts` file there, which is what the test scans. panel-boundaries' doc lost "with `fire`",
    which the held case's hand-built release made false. lsp-hover's "Playwright injects keys through CDP" is scoped
    to Chromium.
  - `fc9edad`: the README says that `--reporter=verbose` prints every skip's reason, where the default reporter
    leaves some out, and that the run still has known failures.
  - `9040ffa`: the spec's A3, §3.1, §3.5, §4 and §8 say what was built.

##### THE USER'S DECISIONS

All on 2026-11-03, from the Log of `$R/progress.md`:

1. **Scope:** the whole web browser tier, less the files that use APIs only Chromium has, and the wasm boundary
   (`rust-browser`, wasm-bindgen-test) in Firefox.
2. **Approach B:** every failure fixed first, then Firefox switched on in CI, with no expected-to-fail marks and no
   advisory job. Not chosen: A, Firefox on at once with marks; C, an advisory job first.
3. **Five PRs, one at a time:** (1) this local project with the Chromium-only tests gated, (2) tab contention, (3)
   engine-difference test fixes, (4) the caret bug, after step-focus merges, (5) Firefox in CI; Playwright's Firefox
   in both tiers, and geckodriver pinned.
4. **U1 = (b):** the finger case becomes a real touch through CDP in Chromium, and is gated in Firefox.
5. **U2 = (a):** real gestures through Playwright commands, as a follow-up after PR 5, recorded under WHAT THIS DID
   NOT CLOSE.
6. **U3 = (a):** a CI check that the Chromium run skips nothing lands in PR 5; in PR 1 it was checked by hand.
7. **On the plan's pre-flight:** F3, `until` moves to a module free of `src` and `engine.ts` waits with it at its
   default bound (one bound, still under browser-timeout-invariants); F4, panel-regions takes its id in its file's
   `beforeAll`, as the plan had it, and the spec was amended to match; F5, a `finally` lifts the finger, in the new
   helper and in focus-press's `tap`.
8. **base16-remove's chained cases,** ruled on 2026-11-03 when the question was asked again: the file keeps its
   design, one mount with its cases run in order, each on what the one before left, and for a file whose cases are
   chained that way, T3's alone check re-runs a case together with the cases before it. Not chosen: redesigning the
   file, in PR 1 or in its own PR. This superseded a first answer, to fix the case in PR 1, given before it was known
   that 11 of the file's 15 cases failed alone (VERIFICATION).

The controller's and the reviewers':

- Task 2's review found a false count in panel-boundaries' doc, which the plan had told the implementer to write.

- Spec §3.5 at `acb67fd`, and the Log's line for the pre-flight's answers, said that under F3 `until` "moves
  unchanged"; the user's F3 ruling in the Log does not say "unchanged". The whole-branch review read the words as

##### WHAT THIS DID NOT CLOSE

- **The Firefox run fails.** At `87feecf`, `pnpm test:firefox` failed 129 of its 1,542 tests in one full run and
  141 in a second. The spec's figures for those counts were 128 and 122, the two base runs' 145 and 139 less
  cluster (a)'s 17, to be recorded and not asserted (spec §5.2, T4): run 1 was 1 above its figure, and run 2 was 19
  above its figure. Of run 1's 129, 18 lie outside the base union, and 7 tests did not run, skipped behind its two
  lost `beforeAll` clicks (below), so the nearness to 128 is not the base less cluster (a). The README at `9040ffa`
  says that the run still has known failures.

**For U2's follow-up, after PR 5:**

- Playwright commands over `page.mouse` (a press held, one move at a time), `page.setViewportSize` and the
  context's clipboard permissions. They could bring 6 gated cases to Firefox, focus-press's 3 held presses,
  share-open-clamps' held press, lambda-follow's window and share-popover's copy, and turn the synthetic pointer
  sites into real input in both engines, except panel-boundaries' "keeps its ratio" and pane-floor, whose points
  lie outside the window, and divider-drag's move with no displacement. The driver could carry three sites at
  `9040ffa`: divider-drag's "never moved" and "across a reload", and layout-view's fraction case (spec §3.5's
  table). They wait for U2's follow-up because converting them changes what Chromium runs (spec A4), and whether
  real Firefox input is dependable is PR 2's question.

**For PR 2, tab contention:**

- **Firefox's tab count or file parallelism.**
- **T3's 37 cases.** 18 tests in run 1 and 16 in run 2 failed outside the base union, 2 of them in both runs, and the
  one-tab re-run failed 5 more outside it. 36 of the 37 passed when run alone in one tab, which the spec's T3 rule lists
  as contention for PR 2. T3's case 2, base16-remove's "is undone exactly: …", failed alone; it is in a file whose cases
  run in order by design, so under the user's reading (THE USER'S DECISIONS, 8) T3 re-runs it with the cases before it,
  and it passed that way (VERIFICATION), so it is listed here too. Task 4 read every first error as a real gesture that
  did not land or a focus that moved, and T3's case 2's in run 2 as the cascade of T3's case 1, the removal before it in
  the file: a menu, dialog or popover a click should have opened that was not open, the focus on `<body>` or on the
  wrong view, a drag or press that did nothing, or an element an earlier press should have made that was not there. They
  lie in copy-editor-mount, default-views-gestures, panel-sizes-stored, view-keys-focus and other files; the table is
  `$R/logs/pr1/t4-t3-table.md`.
- **The one-tab split.** Of run 1's 129 failures, 88 failed again in one tab, all of them in the base union, and 41
  passed, among them all 18 of run 1's T3 cases. The one-tab run failed 12 tests that run 1 had not failed: 7 that
  run 1 passed and 5 that it skipped behind a lost `beforeAll` click. 5 of the 12 are outside the union.
- **Run 1's two lost `beforeAll` clicks.** tm-view-narrow's "the program level’s counts, on 'fact(4)'" (5 tests)
  and view-keys-format-on-blur's "a view key from an editor, with format on blur on" (2 tests) skipped their tests
  when the menu or the dialog their click opens did not open, so run 1 skipped 26 tests. The spec expects 19, the 17
  skipped by design and share-open-deep's 2, and 23 more if tm-view-narrow's `beforeAll` times out, as it did in
  base run 1 (spec §5.2, T4): tm-view-narrow's 5 are 5 of those 23, and view-keys-format-on-blur's 2 are outside
  what the spec named. Both hooks passed in the one-tab run.
- **The base's contention.** `$R/scripts/cluster.py` counts 16 drags that did not move under 12 tabs and 27 tests
  that passed in one tab, in base run 1; `document.hasFocus()` was false at the start of all 212 files in base run
  2; and two waits for `view.hasFocus` never came true, in storage-blocked and view-keys-focus.
- **Memory at the slower runner's 3 tabs** (`$R/measure-report.md`, question 5), and **whether real Firefox input
  is dependable**, which U2's follow-up needs.
- **T3's alone rule in a file whose cases are chained.** Spec §5.2's T3 text still states the alone rule without the
  chained-file reading; PR 2's spec carries the ruling (THE USER'S DECISIONS, 8). Only base16-remove was searched
  for chained cases; the other 36 T3 cases passed alone.
- **A popover asserted open straight after the click that opens it.** At `9040ffa`, share-popover's `openShare` and
  header-menus-narrow's `openAt` read `:popover-open` after `userEvent.click` with no wait, so a failure there cannot
  tell a menu that closed from one not yet open. `openAt` failed in T3's cases 17 and 18. share-popover's popover
  cases failed outside the union in each of Task 2's three nine-file Firefox runs with the gates in place (3, 1 and
  4 cases: two runs of its tree before its commit, and S1's, whose throws the gates skip in Firefox), in neither of
  its two runs without them, and in neither of Task 4's full runs.
- **Focus failures in one tab.** The one-tab re-run's 5 failures outside the union are all focus losses, at a
  1-minute load of 30.83 when it started and 27.56 when it ended.
- **panel-boundaries' "skip a closed region, and are drawn beside it again once it is open"** failed in Task 3's
  five-file Firefox mix, in 3 of 3 runs at `87feecf` and in 3 of 3 with S4's throwing captures, on assertions about
  the boundaries drawn, which Task 3 read as one real click that did not toggle its panel; it passed in one tab.
  Task 3's capture instrument and its cross-tab probe (VERIFICATION) found no synthetic capture held. It passed in
  both of Task 4's full runs.
- **The timeout invariant's scope.** At `9040ffa`, `tests/node/browser-timeout-invariants.test.ts` scans `.test.ts`
  files only, so nothing but reading holds the 9 other modules under `tests/browser/` that call `until` to its
  default bound: `engine.ts`, `harness.ts`, `lambda-deep.ts`, `lambda-text.ts` and the fixtures
  `build-reply-fixture.ts`, `editor-view-fixture.ts`, `format-on-leave-fixture.ts`, `share-open-hashchange-fixture.ts`
  and `user-event-fixture.ts`. F3's premise, one bound "still under browser-timeout-invariants", holds for the default
  the invariant reads; `engine.ts`'s call passes no timeout, which only reading shows. The scope predates this
  branch. It is placed with PR 2, which works on the waits, since a numeric timeout added to one of these modules
  would pass the invariant.

`REDEXTAPE_FIREFOX` unset, `vitest run --project firefox` exits 1 on `No projects matched the filter "firefox".`;
with it set, `pnpm run test:coverage` exits 1 on `@vitest/coverage-v8 does not work with`; and `git diff --stat
e9bbf67 9040ffa -- .forgejo scripts` is empty. G2 and T1: cluster (a)'s 17 were as specified in both full runs, the
15 skipped and the 2 cascades passed. G3 and T2: neither full run printed an `Errors` line, an `[Unhandled error]` or
`BLOCKED`. T5: neither printed "pages this tab ran before this file are still alive". G4: Chromium ran 213 files
and 1,542 tests, all passed, `numPendingTests` 0, and coverage read the same four figures at `87feecf` and at
`e9bbf67`. T3 did not hold: 37 cases failed outside the base union. 36 of them passed alone in one tab, which the spec's
rule lists as contention for PR 2. T3's case 2, base16-remove's "is undone exactly: …", failed alone in one Firefox tab
at `87feecf`, and alone in Chromium at `362d3e2`, whose `web/` is `9040ffa`'s, it failed in both of two runs, on the
first error it failed on alone in Firefox. It is in a file outside the branch's diff whose cases run in order by design:
its doc says "ONE MOUNT FOR THE FILE, and the cases run in order, each on what the one before left". At `964a038`, whose

the same 11 in Firefox, the file's 2nd, 4th and 7th to 15th, of which T3's case 2 is the 4th. Under the user's reading
(THE USER'S DECISIONS, 8), T3 re-runs a case of such a file with the cases before it. Run that way in one Firefox tab at
`87feecf`, it passed: with T3's case 1, the removal before it in its `describe`, both passed, and the whole file passed
15 of 15. T4's failure counts are under WHAT THIS DID NOT CLOSE.

#### THE STEP BUTTONS HAND THE FOCUS ON WHEN THEY GO OFF UNDER IT, AND A ▶ OR ⏭ THAT A RECORDING TURNS OFF UNDER THE FOCUS WAITS FOR IT, FOCUSED AND OFF BY `aria-disabled`, SO THAT THE ENTER AT A `capped` OR `budget` STOP RECORDS FURTHER; THE WAIT HOLDS THROUGH A REBUILD THAT GIVES THE FOCUS BACK, AND ENDS ONCE ITS BUTTON IS TAKEN OFF THE PAGE (2026-11-03, branch `step-focus`, `1b2f0cb..940295c`, 17 commits, plus this entry and the commit that corrects it; then `f2ad034`, which corrects when `offPage`'s comment says the guard reads the focus, and the two commits that bring this entry up to date)

**A PR of its own after web-bumps.** At `1b2f0cb`, ◀ pressed at step 1, and ▶ pressed onto a finished run's last step,
disable themselves under their own click or Enter with no hand-off, so the focus drops to `<body>`. Web-bumps' review
3 added that ↺ and ⏵ have no hand-off either, and that on Chromium 156, which defers the blur of a disabled focused
button, the test of ⏭'s hand-off no longer catches its call order (its findings 4 and 3, as
`~/temp/redextape-step-focus-record/progress.md`'s opening lines record them, and WEB'S DEPENDENCY BUMPS, WHAT
THIS DID NOT CLOSE).
The lane record is `~/temp/redextape-step-focus-record/` (`$R` below): `$R/progress.md` holds the user's rulings and
every round, `$R/design.md` the hand-off map and the three choices it put to the user, `$R/reviews/` the reviews, the
delta reads, their fix reports and the rebase report, `$R/try-it.md` the script for a try by hand, and `$R/logs/`
every log named below. The branch began on web-bumps' `2f6d787`. It was rebased onto `e9bbf67` once #161 merged, its
trees unchanged, and onto `1b2f0cb` once #162 merged, with no conflict and its 16 patches unchanged, and `940295c`
followed. A figure from before the second rebase names the commit it ran at and the commit that commit is now, as
"`530e44e` (now `3c5cd28`)"; the map is `$R/rebase-map-1b2f0cb.txt`.

##### WHAT CHANGED

Over the range, 14 files change, with 1,147 lines added and 76 removed.

- **Every step button hands the focus on, `92102c5`, `c0ce50e` and `1ad67ee`.** At `1b2f0cb`, of the five, ⏭ alone
  handed the focus on, to ◀, ↺, ▶, ⏵ and the speed select. At `940295c` `step-controls.ts`'s `buttons` table, built
  once, gives each of the five the `ControlState` field that keeps it live and its hand-off list, and `update` reads
  it against the focus (`1ad67ee`, review 1's findings 4 to 7):

  | goes off | the focus goes to the first live of |
  |---|---|
  | ↺, under a state change only | ▶, ⏭, ⏵, ◀, the speed select |
  | ◀ | ▶, ⏭, ⏵, ↺, the speed select |
  | ▶ | ◀, ↺, ⏭, ⏵, the speed select |
  | ⏭ | ▶, ◀, ↺, ⏵, the speed select |
  | ⏵, under a state change only | ⏭, ▶, ◀, ↺, the speed select |

  ⏭'s list starts at ▶ since `3c5cd28` (THE USER'S DECISIONS, 5). The button holding the focus takes its state after
  the other four, so its hand-off reads the strip as the update leaves it, and it hands the focus on before its own
  `disabled` is set, so the focus never rests on a disabled control, whenever the browser blurs it. `c0ce50e` makes
  the call-order tests name the control that held the focus when the button was disabled.
- **The hand-off's tests, `92102c5`, `2f17d10` and `d85f226`.** Each button by click and by Enter, the focus read
  once it settles and the call order read inside the `disabled` setter. ◀, ▶ and ⏭ are also turned off by a state
  change under a focus a real gesture put there: playback reaching the end for ▶ and ⏭, and for ◀ a recording's
  evictions, through a real `History` moved as `transport.ts`'s handlers move it (`d85f226`). ↺ and ⏵ are turned off
  by an unavailable leg and by a new run.
- **A ▶ or ⏭ that a recording turns off under the focus waits for it, `41b2b28`, `3c5cd28` and `0cc3dd5`.** Review
  1's finding 1: with the hand-off, Enter on ▶ at a `capped` or `budget` stop started a recording that turned ▶ off
  under the focus, the focus went to ◀, and the next Enter stepped back. Before the branch the focus went to `<body>`
  and that Enter did nothing. Review 1's fix round showed ▶'s case to be a regression and ⏭'s to be older
  (`$R/reviews/review-1-fixes.md`). At `940295c`:
  - The focused ▶ or ⏭ that a recording turns off keeps the focus and waits, off by `aria-disabled`, while
    `ControlState`'s new `recording` holds, which is while frames still arrive and the readout's count carries `…`
    (`controls.ts`). A click or Enter on a waiting button runs nothing. At a `capped` or `budget` stop ▶ is live
    again with the focus on it, and a waiting ⏭ hands the focus to it, so the next Enter records further; at a
    finished run's end either hands to ◀. Only the focused button waits, and a waiting button the focus leaves is
    disabled at its `blur` (`41b2b28`). It waits only while a recording runs, read from the state and the focus
    alone, so no wait outlives the leg it waited on (`3c5cd28`, review 2's findings 2 and 6).
  - The continue button (`[keep recording]` at a `budget` stop, `[continue — raise the step cap]` at a `capped` one)
    going away under its own press hands the focus to ▶, which waits, where it had handed it to ⏵ and the Enter at
    the next stop played (`3c5cd28`, review 2's finding 5). `0cc3dd5` makes that hand-off run before the buttons take
    their state, and reads the waiting button from the focus afterwards, so a ▶ the focus did not reach is disabled
    rather than a dead Tab stop (review 3's findings 1 and 5).
  - `style.css` draws a waiting button as faint as a disabled one by its colours rather than by `opacity`, so its
    focus ring stays whole (`41b2b28`), and in `GrayText` under forced colours (`0cc3dd5`, review 3's finding 3).
- **The wait and the page, `efb3f92`, `ccf8ded`, `a96edf9` and `468ce1a`.**
  - `efb3f92`, the user's guard: while a ▶ or ⏭ waits, a `MutationObserver` on `document`'s child lists ends the
    wait at the next microtask checkpoint after the script that took the button off, if the button does not hold the
    focus then, as Firefox sends a focused button taken off the page no `blur` (review 3's finding 2). The `blur`
    comment no longer says that a strip off the page is sent the recording's updates (the round-3 delta read's M1).
  - `ccf8ded`: `focus-handoff.ts`'s `keepFocusOn(el, rebuild)` and `focusHolder()`. `pane-host.ts`'s `keepingFocus`
    runs its rebuild under `keepFocusOn`, naming the element it will give the focus back to, and the strip, its
    `blur` and `handOff` read the focus through `focusHolder`. So a divider's drag (`resized`) and a view key
    (`switchViews`) leave a waiting button focused and waiting, where the drag had dropped the focus to `<body>` and
    the view key had moved it to the view's title (the round-3 delta read's I1 and M2).
  - `a96edf9`: the strip test of such a rebuild runs it without drawing the strip as well as drawing it. `468ce1a`,
    comments only: `keepFocusOn`'s and `keepingFocus`'s docs say that the rebuild must defer nothing, and the
    `focusin` comment says that the guard reads `focusHolder` (the round-4 delta read's m1 and m2).
- **The tests in the app, and the helpers, `41b2b28`, `3393f02`, `4fa7a4c`, `0252408` and `e245324`.**
  `step-focus-recording.test.ts` is new. It runs the app with its worker and holds the session workers' replies, so
  that a gesture lands inside a recording at a chosen point, which ⏭'s case cannot reach by hand (WHAT THIS DID NOT
  CLOSE). Its waits are `historyFills` and stages of 37,000 steps, each within `until`'s one bound (`4fa7a4c`). It
  holds only the session workers' replies (`0252408`, review 2's finding 1), with one listener of its own on each, and
  gives the page its `Worker` back after its cases (`e245324`, review 3's finding 7). `harness.ts` gains
  `controlName`, `settledFocus` (`0252408`), `legView` and `pressable` (`e245324`). The helpers in `app.test.ts`,
  `extend-during-recompile.test.ts`, `extend-focus-probe.test.ts` and `share-positions.test.ts` that wait for a step
  button to be live ask `pressable`, which a waiting button is not (review 3's finding 4).
  `tests/node/controls.test.ts` tests `recording` and builds its legs with `legView`.
- **`940295c`, after the rebase onto `1b2f0cb`.** Two step-control tests start with Firefox PR 1's `chromiumOnly` and
  their reasons: "a waiting ⏭ taken off the page with the focus is disabled, so it is no Tab stop when it is back",
  which reads the button straight after taking it off, before the guard's observer runs, and so needs Chromium's
  `blur` (the no-`blur` case beside it runs in Firefox), and "looks off in forced colours as a disabled step button
  does, and keeps its focus ring", which sets forced colours through CDP.
- **`f2ad034`, comments only, after this entry.** `step-controls.ts`'s comment on `offPage` said that a waiting
  button taken off the page stops waiting "ONCE THE TASK THAT TOOK IT OFF IS DONE", "Read after the task". It says
  that the button stops waiting at the next microtask checkpoint, and that a rebuild that gives it the focus back in
  the same synchronous call leaves it waiting, as `keepFocusOn`'s doc says; a give-back left to the task's end would
  find it disabled. `step-focus-recording.test.ts`'s doc of a view key that hides the TM view said that the watch
  ends the wait "once the key is done", and says the next microtask checkpoint too (the entry check's M7, its code
  half; `$R/reviews/comment-fix.md`).

##### THE USER'S DECISIONS

All on 2026-11-03, as `$R/progress.md` states them:

1. On web-bumps' review 2: "Separate PR after" for the step buttons' focus hand-off; then "Start now on web-bumps",
   the branch made from web-bumps' head and rebased once it merged.
2. `$R/design.md`'s three choices, each the pick: ↺ and ⏵ covered; ▶ at the end hands to ◀; ⏵ hands leftwards along
   the strip, the speed select last.
3. Reviews: the built-in `code-review` at HIGH, each round, as web-bumps had; each finding reproduced before it is
   fixed; "fix all".
4. Review 1's finding 1 = option C: the button keeps the focus, off by `aria-disabled`, while the recording its own
   press started runs, Enter doing nothing; live again when the recording stops; handing to ◀ only if the run ends;
   for ▶ AND ⏭.
5. ⏭ at a stop: "hand to ▶ when live". ⏭'s hand-off tries ▶ first, so ⏭ pressed during a recording that stops and ⏭
   pressed at a stopped run both land on ▶; at a finished end ▶ is off and ⏭ hands to ◀.
6. The round-3 delta read's I1 and M2: the focus stays on the waiting button through a rebuild that gives it back, a
   divider's drag and a view key.
7. Review 3's finding 2, Firefox's missing `blur` on removal: "add a guard", so that a waiting button no longer on the
   page stops waiting, though Firefox is not in CI.
8. His try on 5181, at `4567370` (now `468ce1a`): "ok overall seems to work". His two further asks are new work for
   another lane (WHAT THIS DID NOT CLOSE).

The lane's own calls: round 3's fixer added no guard for finding 2 and said why (`$R/reviews/review-3-fixes.md`),
which decision 7 reversed; after three HIGH rounds, one read-only reviewer read each later round's delta, round 3's
(`$R/reviews/round-3-delta-read.md`) and round 4's (`round-4-delta-read.md`), in place of a fourth and a fifth HIGH
round. The round-4 read found two Minors and no Important or Critical finding, and `468ce1a` fixed both. The wait
was built on `ControlState`'s `recording`, which holds for any recording that carries the head, wider than decision
4's "the recording its own press started": a ⏭ pressed into a recording already running waits (`41b2b28`), and so
does the ▶ that the continue button's press hands the focus to (`3c5cd28`).

##### WHAT THIS DID NOT CLOSE

- **A Firefox leak victim, for the Firefox CI lane's PR 2 (tab contention) or PR 3 (engine-difference test fixes).**
  `step-focus-recording.test.ts`'s "⏭ at a `budget` stop hands the focus to ▶, which by Enter keeps it while it
  records; Enter at the stop records further" fails in one Firefox tab when it runs after
  `extend-focus-probe.test.ts`, whose failing case's body is as at `1b2f0cb`, on ``where the focus settles after ⏭ at
  the `budget` stop: expected 'BODY' to be 'one step forward'``, and passes alone, before the probe and at default tabs
  (VERIFICATION). The lane reads it as the class of `step-controls.test.ts`'s "still hands the focus on when nothing
  in the strip is live", whose body is `1b2f0cb`'s plus `recording: false`, and which fails on `1b2f0cb` as on
  `940295c` in one tab, after `app.test.ts`, and
  passes at `940295c`'s default tabs: a focus moved after a neighbour file in the same Firefox tab that does not land
  (`$R/reviews/rebase-report.md`, cause 3). `app.test.ts`'s sub-pixel `scrollTop` and the probe's "hiding the focused
  continue button, or disabling a focused button, strands focus on body" fail on both commits too; that case's body is
  as at `1b2f0cb`, but it failed at a different check on each (VERIFICATION).
- **The guard's Firefox proof runs only by hand.** Its strip test, "a waiting ⏭ taken off the page with no `blur`
  stops waiting there, and is no Tab stop when it is back", passes in `pnpm test:firefox` at `940295c` at both tab
  counts. CI runs Chromium alone until Firefox PR 5. Chromium blurs a focused button taken off the page, so in
  Chromium the test stops that `blur` at a capturing listener and asserts that it did, leaving the guard alone to
  end the wait.
- **⏭'s wait during a recording cannot be checked by hand** (`$R/try-it.md`). A recording that a ⏭ press can join
  ends within half a second of starting, and no program or setting found makes it slower. In the try-it drive at
  `4567370` (now `468ce1a`), ⏭ waited 219 ms with the gestures 150 ms apart, 111 ms at 250 ms, and not at all at
  400 ms. The tests and the drives that hold the worker's replies are what see it.
- **Round 4's concerns, which the round-4 delta read judged and which stay as they are:**
  - A rebuild that gives the focus back must stay one synchronous call: a `keepingFocus` rebuild that awaited would
    let the guard end the wait before the give-back. No caller is async, and `keepFocusOn`'s and `keepingFocus`'s
    docs say so since `468ce1a`, and `offPage`'s comment since `f2ad034`, but the types do not hold it, as
    `rebuild: () => void` accepts an async function.
  - While a ▶ or ⏭ waits, the observer watches every child-list change on the page. The read's probe, from a
    release to a `budget` stop, counted 36 callbacks over 152 records, and the watch disconnected at each of the four
    exits it drove. The callback time it read, 0.10 ms in all and 0.100 ms for the longest call, is at the floor of
    headless Chromium's coarsened `performance.now()`, the read says, not a measurement. No test holds the
    disconnection, which the read counts as a cost, not behaviour.
  - `main.ts`'s `focusKept` and `focus-handoff.ts`'s `kept` both answer whether a rebuild that gives the focus back
    is running. No reachable read sees them disagree; folding the first into the second is left undone.
- **The user's two asks from his try** (`~/temp/redextape-history-restart-record/progress.md`): "the restart button
  after pressing 'history is full' doesn't go back to step 1, and there doesn't seem to be a way to do so", and "there
  should be a way to do 'keep recording' forever and just let it execute while ejecting old history from memory".
  They became the history-restart lane. Its design, the hidden recording, is a separate design that the user approved
  on 2026-11-03, with a PR A, ↺ back to step 0, and a PR B, the hidden recording, both after this branch merges. It
  changes the step bar this branch builds on, `[keep recording]`, ⏭ and the waiting rule among it. Its decisions are
  that lane's, in its `progress.md` (Q1 to Q8 and §1 to §4), and this entry does not restate them.
- **What the reviews left:**
  - `style.css`'s forced-colours comment says that forced colours replace the waiting button's colours with "the
    live button's", which is true of the glyph only (the round-3 delta read; not counted).
  - `pane-host.ts`'s "THE FOCUS IS `within`'s FOR THE REBUILD'S LENGTH" holds for `focusHolder` only while the focus
    is on `<body>` (the round-4 delta read; read as shorthand, not counted).
  - On a `blur` with no draw, `stop` does not disconnect the observer; the focus move's draw or the next child-list
    change does (the round-4 delta read; a cost, not behaviour).
  - Review 2's finding 2, a ⏭ waiting on one leg that kept waiting on another, and review 3's finding 1, a ▶ left
    waiting when the continue button's hand-off missed, were reproduced and fixed at the strip; no app route to

#### FIREFOX PR 2: `pnpm test:firefox` RUNS TWO FIREFOX PROJECTS, EACH IN A FIREFOX OF ITS OWN: `firefox-capture` RUNS THE EIGHT FILES WHOSE REAL PRESSES TAKE A POINTER CAPTURE AND THE TEST THAT THE PROJECTS HAVE TWO BROWSERS, ONE AT A TIME, AND `firefox` THE REST AT 6 TABS; A GUARD FAILS A CAPTURE OUTSIDE THE LIST, TWO CHECKS HOLD THE SPLIT, AND IN FIREFOX THE TEST FRAME IS GIVEN THE FOCUS AT EACH FILE'S START AND BEFORE A `focus()` IT WOULD IGNORE; CI IS AS IT WAS, AND WHAT IS LEFT GOES TO PRS 3 TO 5 (2026-11-04, branch `firefox-contention`, `ec4f11a..10c3560`, 26 commits, the last that changes code `6f19fe8`, plus this entry, `5a555c6`, and the commit that corrects it)

**The second of five Firefox PRs** (PR 1's entry above, its THE USER'S DECISIONS, 3). PR 1 left `pnpm test:firefox`
running the browser tier in one Firefox at Vitest's default tab count, 12 on this machine, with failures beyond what
fails in one tab. PR 2 is about those. Its measurements before the spec (M1, `$R/pr2/measure-report.md`; M2,
`$R/pr2/measure-2.md`) found two causes. Cause 1: Playwright synthesises every page's mouse in one Firefox's one
browser process, so a pointer capture that real input takes in one tab takes the clicks of every other tab of that
Firefox (spec §3.1). Cause 2: a `focus()` made while the test frame lacks the focus leaves its element unfocused and
fires no event (spec §3.4). The plan's Task 2 found a third. Cause 3: that one process carries every tab's real input,
and on a loaded machine it ran on about half a core, so a case of many real clicks could cross its 15,000 ms bound
(spec §3.8). The spec is `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-04-firefox-pr2-tab-contention-design.md` and the plan
`docs/superpowers/plans/2026-11-04-firefox-pr2-tab-contention.md`, in 11 tasks. The lane record is
`~/temp/redextape-firefox-ci-record/` (`$R` below): this PR's runs are in `$R/logs/pr2/`, the R6 probe's in
`$R/logs/pr2-r6/`, the measurements in `$R/pr2/`, and the task reports, the reviews and the record of failures outside
R (`outside-r.md`) in `$R/tasks/pr2/`. `$W` is the worktree `~/temp/redextape-firefox-contention` and `$S` the
sabotage worktree `~/temp/redextape-firefox-contention-sab`. R, the one-tab set, is the failures of three one-tab
runs, `tabs1-1` (M1), `focusobs-1` (M2) and `t1-base-1tab` (Task 1), by file and name, with the files that fail as a
whole in them (spec §6.2).

##### THE USER'S DECISIONS

Each ruled on 2026-11-04, and worded as the Log of `$R/progress.md` has it:

1. **Approach "D: split by capture":** two Firefox projects with separate browsers, the capture files one at a time in
   their own Firefox beside the rest at the default tab count, and a guard that fails when a file outside the list takes
   a real capture. Not chosen: A, a Firefox per tab (Vitest internals); B, one tab. **Cause 2 → "PR 2":** the
   frame-focus step for the five focus failures M2's step cleared, and the other four worked out in PR 2 (the ruling's
   count: spec §4.6 and §8 make them five, with live-views-bound-switch's "65 of 63" case, which M2's join had left
   out).

   (2) "Add a permanent check": a test that fails if two capture files run at once, the deprecated
   `browser.fileParallelism: false` kept; (3) "PR 3": an engine difference in focus that §4.6 finds is recorded in PR
   2 and fixed in PR 3; (4) "Yes, every one": the step arms for every `focus()` made while the frame lacks the focus;

##### WHAT THIS DID NOT CLOSE

**For PR 3, engine differences and tolerances:**

- **Two engine differences in focus** that Task 8 recorded (`$R/tasks/pr2/t8-focus.md`), each still failing with Task
  9's fix in place (`t10-16`; `t10-leak-1` to `-3`):
  - view-keys-focus's "goes to + view when the window is narrowed past 40rem, …" ("the focus is not on + view in the
    narrow window, at once: expected `<body>`"). `style.css`'s `@media (max-width: 40rem)` rule hides the views toggles
    at the style update, and Firefox blurs the focused toggle (`focusout button.view-toggle rel=null`) before it
    dispatches the media query's `change` event (`media-change matches=1 … active=body`), on which `main.ts`'s
    `placeToggles` calls `handOff`, which then finds `<body>` and moves nothing (the trace of
    `t8-alone-view-keys-focus-none`). It failed in every Firefox run of Task 8, alone included, and passes in every
    Chromium run of the record; Chromium's order, which lets the listener see the toggle focused, is inferred from that
    and was not traced. It would be user-visible in Firefox if a top-level window's resize orders the two as the test
    frame's does, which is unmeasured: a user who narrows the window with the focus on a toggle would be left on
    `<body>`. Its fix is in `web/src` (A3).
  - extend-focus-probe's "hiding the focused continue button, or disabling a focused button, strands focus on body":
    right after `extend.hidden = true`, `activeElement` reads `expected <button …(2)> to be <body>`, and the frame's
    `focusout` comes later. Firefox keeps a just-hidden focused element as `activeElement` until a later style update,
    where Chromium answers `<body>` at once. The file probes the engine, so no app path is shown wrong by it.
- **PR 1's list for PR 3,** the menus' gutter among it (header-menus-narrow's 9, spec §7).
- **Two cases another lane's gate failed alone at `ec4f11a`,** in its alone runs, one per file with `-t` set to the
  file's failing titles (the history-restart lane, `~/temp/redextape-history-restart-record/tasks/task-6-report.md`),
  with no cause-finding in PR 2: base16-import's "forgets a check when the text is edited" (`locator.fill: Timeout
  14897ms exceeded`), which is in the failure tables of two runs of PR 2's record, `t1-base-default-1` and M2's
  `e2-serial-1`; and state-diagram's "keeps a runtime box's focus while the run moves, …", whose file passed alone (THE
  CONTROLLER'S CALLS, 10). base16-import is one of spec §3.6's chained files, which the alone rule runs whole, and PR
  2's record has no run of that file alone, so it is not shown that the case fails alone.

**For PR 4, the caret bug:**

- Cluster B, the view-keys caret test included ("a key held down > acts once with Ctrl held through a held ], and its
  repeats are not the editor's", spec §3.5), which runs in `firefox-capture`.
- `targets.py`'s `R_BY_SHAPE` rule, which holds view-keys' failures with the caret at offset 0 in R until PR 4 (spec
  §6.2), leaves when PR 4 lands. Over the 361 runs of the record that `targets.py` reads, the gate's at `5a555c6`
  included (every JSON report but the six `.split.json` re-cuts), it holds 10 failures: the held-key case's 4 and "ends
  on a key it does not know, …"'s 6, `gh-r6-1`'s among them.

**For PR 5, CI:**

- Both Firefox projects in the `web` job; memory and wall time on the runners, measured on this machine only (the rest
  at 6, and at 3 + 1); Firefox as root, unmeasured.
- Chromium's wall time: the tier loads one more setup module per file. `run.sh`'s `WALL` was 108 s for `t1-chromium` at
  the base's `web/`, 90 s for `t10-chromium` at `55c712e` and 64 s for `gh-chromium` at `5a555c6`, each under other
  lanes' load, so the three do not measure the module's cost.

**For U2's follow-up, after PR 5:** a file that holds a press across `page.mouse` commands joins the capture list.

**What holds each premise, and what does not:**

- The projects together and the rest at 6: C4, in `targets.py`'s exit status since fix round B. One browser per
  project: two-browsers. One file at a time: the one-at-a-time check (C9). C4 cannot see an overlap that check
  catches: it fails a file before its first case, and the JSON gives such a file the run's start as its start and end,
  so under S8 C4 read a peak of 1.
- The setup call's presence: `frame-focus.test.ts`'s first case (S11), in every `firefox` run of the file, and not in
  `firefox-capture`, where the file does not run. Its sufficiency, a focused start letting a real click's or a popover's
  `autofocus` focus reach its element after a file whose frame ended focused, is held by runs alone: F1's 16 files hold
  about-menu, lambda-display, live-views-bound-switch and view-toggles; F2's full one-tab run (`t10-1tab`, a tab in each
  of the two Firefoxes) those, add-view-floor, follow-kept and view-header; F3 the leak's victim. `e305ab5` is the tree
  without the call. There Task 8's `none` runs fail the other six and the victim (`t8-16-none-1` and `-2`, the `none`
  pairs of add-view-floor and follow-kept, `t8-leak-1` to `-3`); view-header passed in its `none` runs, and fails in
  `t8-1tab` and in Task 9's `t9-pair-view-header-after-active-pane-base`. A two-file pair for it needs the record's
  untracked `Ordered` sequencer (`vite.focus.config.ts`): Vitest orders files by cached duration and size.
- The per-call step: `frame-focus.test.ts`'s step cases alone, since with the setup call it fired on 0 of 257 calls in
  Task 8's `t8-16-win-1`. Its `SVGElement` half and its reach into a file's own hooks are held by the code's shape, a
  two-prototype array and no per-case state, not by a case: no `focus()` in `web/src` targets an SVG element at
  `085874c` (Task 6's review, M2).
- The guard sees a `setPointerCapture` that holds in the frame's realm, and only that. Whether a native HTML drag
  session or a pointer lock takes the shared mouse the same way is unmeasured; neither is in `web/src` or `web/tests`
  at `fb73350`. The guard relies on three Vitest defaults, `'stack'` hooks, a page per file and cases one at a time
  (spec §4.3).
- The capture list's third direction is unchecked: a listed file that no longer captures (spec §8).
  `browser.fileParallelism` is deprecated and stays, held by the one-at-a-time check at each Vitest bump.
- two-browsers needs a file of `firefox` beside it: a run that names it among capture files alone fails it by design,
  as fix round A's `--project firefox-capture` run did.
- C8 and C9 read every error of a failure since fix round B; C1 says nothing of R's 127 tests, which `errdiff.py`'s
  DIFF lines cover.

**Recorded, with no ruling:**

- **The coverage check's lost results.** Under `--coverage` in Firefox a file loses its last results: the JSON has 111
  cases `pending` in `frb-coverage`, 219 in `t10-coverage`, 251 in `t10-coverage-2`, 289 in `t10-fix-cov-1` and 262 in
  `gh-coverage`, and the check's C1 judges none of them. Whether those cases ran and their results were dropped, or did
  not run, is not shown.
- **F2's four DIFFs** against `t1-base-1tab` (`t10-1tab.errdiff.out`), each in R, where `t10-1tab` ran a tab in each of
  the two Firefoxes and `t1-base-1tab` one project in one tab: view-keys' "is over after one action …" and "runs ahead
  of vim …", from the caret read to the typed text at offset 0, the same caret state read by the case's other assertion;
  extend-focus-probe's first case, from `expected <body> to be <button>` to `expected <button> to be <body>`, the engine
  difference above, which shows once the frame has the focus; virtual-grid's "moves the active row by index …", from
  `'g-0' to be 'g-999'` to `'g-8' to be 'g-10'`, the base's own first error in its default runs.
- **The scroll-event window.** The product reads a user's scroll of a following grid only from its `scroll` event, so
  a redraw that lands between a real wheel scroll and its event could take the scroll back; a key that scrolls
  detaches at once and has no such window. It was seen only as state-diagram-no-machine's test race (`6f19fe8`);
  whether a real gesture can land in that window is unmeasured. Where it goes is the user's call. The other
  `scrollTop` writes under `tests/browser/` (52 in 25 files) were not audited one by one.
- **The two test fixes' sabotages.** `81d3758`'s race was not made to fire on demand, so no run shows the unfixed case
  failing beside the fixed one passing. For `6f19fe8`, the forced-order runs do (3 of 3 failed without the fix, 3 of 3
  passed with it), but under emulated load the unfixed file passed 20 of 20, as the fixed one did.
- **Memory:** `t10-r6-1` peaked at 7.13 GiB, within C6 but above M3's R6 runs (5.30 and 5.25 GiB).
- **parked-copy-editor-mount under R6** took 6,422 and 4,702 ms in M3, against 1,344 and 1,522 ms under D: two runs
  each, unexplained.
- **The full runs at `6f19fe8`'s code,** all with the rest at 6 tabs: `t10c-fix-r6-1`, and at `5a555c6`, whose code is
  `6f19fe8`'s, `gh-r6-1` and the coverage check `gh-coverage`. The 3-tab and one-tab full runs are at `55c712e`;
  `81d3758` and `6f19fe8` change one test file each.
- **`collect.ts`'s page guard in `firefox-capture`:** it trips at a tab's tenth file, and that project's one tab runs 9,
  so it cannot fire there until the list grows, as U2's follow-up may make it (the whole-branch review's "Checked"
  list).
- **Firefox's events on a frame given back its focus:** whether Firefox fires `focus` and `focusin` again on the frame's
  remembered `activeElement` when the step's `window.focus()` gives the frame its focus back is unmeasured; if it does,
  the app's handlers on that element run once more (Task 6's review).
- **`pnpm test:firefox --project firefox` cannot narrow,** since the caller's flags append to the script's two
  `--project` flags; it is undocumented (the whole-branch review).
- **`$S` is not removed** (`~/temp/redextape-firefox-contention-sab`).

#### HIDDEN RECORDING PR A: ↺ GOES BACK TO STEP 0 OF ITS OWN VIEW, A SEEK WHILE STEP 0 IS KEPT AND OTHERWISE A REWIND OF THAT VIEW'S LEG ALONE, WHICH RECORDS THE LEG'S FIRST FILL AGAIN UNDER A NEW EPOCH WHILE THE OTHER VIEWS KEEP THEIR STEPS; DURING A RECOMPILE, OR ON A COPY WHOSE LAST EDIT DID NOT PARSE, IT STAYS A SEEK, AND ITS NAME IS `back to step 0` (2026-11-04, branch `hidden-recording`, `92f2b55..b36a102`, 19 commits, then `caee6db`, which brings the plan and the spec up to the last of them, plus this entry)

**PR A of the hidden-recording design.** At `ec4f11a` ↺ is `hist.seek(0)`, named "back to the oldest kept step": once
a recording has dropped step 0, ↺ goes to the oldest step the ring keeps, and only a recompile, which resets every
view, records from step 0 again (`$R/facts.md`). The user's try of step-focus on 5181 asked for a way back (THE STEP
BUTTONS HAND THE FOCUS ON …, WHAT THIS DID NOT CLOSE, the user's two asks). The design he approved splits the answer
in two (spec §9): PR A, this branch, takes ↺ back to step 0 on today's recording UI, and PR B, the hidden recording,
gets a plan of its own after PR A. The spec is `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-03-hidden-recording-design.md`, the
plan `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-11-04-hidden-recording-pr-a-rewind.md`, whose plan calls P1 to P8 and sabotage rows
this entry names.
The lane record is `~/temp/redextape-history-restart-record/` (`$R` below): `$R/progress.md` holds the user's rulings
and every dispatch, `$R/tasks/` the briefs, the reports and the reviews, `$R/logs/pr-a/` (`$L`) each log named below
without a directory, `$R/scripts/pr-a/` the scripts that ran them, and `$R/sab/` the copy each sabotage saved before it
changed a file. The sabotages ran in a scratch worktree, `~/temp/redextape-hidden-recording-sab` (`$S`), with its own
target dir and copied `web/node_modules`, `pkg`, `pkg-lsp` and `web/bindings`.

**The branch was rebased twice.** Before its first code commit, its two spec commits, `1646438` and `5af1333` on
`1b2f0cb`, were rebased onto `ec4f11a` once step-focus merged as #163, and two fix rounds that ran on branches of their
own were cherry-picked onto it: the plan's pre-flight fix round's `88a5a2f` and `3f75dbc`, and Task 1's fix round's
`139a7cc` and `a367e92`. After this entry was written, the whole branch was rebased onto `92f2b55` once Firefox PR 2
merged as #164. Every SHA this entry gives a commit of the branch is that commit after the second rebase, and
`$R/rebase-map.txt` pairs each of the 22 with the commit it replaces. The six above are now `edd1d86`, `d64353a`,
`806270c`, `f324bd6`, `1404763` and `1fc5ff0`, each with the patch-id of its original. Of the 22, each has the patch-id
of the commit it replaces but `3bf0e69`, the entry's first commit, whose added lines are the same and whose context
lines are #164's entry where they were `ec4f11a`'s last lines; and each one's files differ from that commit's in the
17 files #164 changes alone, which outside `README.md` and the roadmap differ by #164's diff, byte for byte. A run, a
sabotage, a review or the gate this entry places at a commit ran before the second rebase, at the commit the map pairs
with it; what ran again after it is in VERIFICATION, **After the rebase**.

   pressed twice.

   chosen: a rerun of the whole session.

   line reads `step 0 of 0…` and ↺ waits, greyed with its focus kept. Not chosen: `step 0…`; the old window kept shown.
5. 2026-11-04, ⏸ while a playing leg rewinds, "Grey it out": ⏸ is off until the first reply, then play carries on from
   step 0. Not chosen: ⏸ live, cancelling the held play.

#### THE IR VIEWS GROUNDWORK'S PR 2: ONE LOWERING WALK DRIVES BOTH NATIVE BACKENDS, NATIVE-RT AND THE RXM INTERPRETER SHARE ONE HEAP CORE IN `redextape-core`, AND A SNAPSHOT GATE HOLDS THE GENERATED CLIF, MACHINE CODE AND LLVM IR TO THE FOUR OF §8'S CHANGES THAT ARE THIS PR'S (2026-11-06, branch `ir-lowering`, `18c5272..73dc741`, 37 commits, plus this entry)

**Spec §4.2 and §4.3** (`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-27-ir-views-groundwork-design.md`), the groundwork's second
pull request in §6's order, gated by §7.1 (generated code changes only as §8 names) and §7.2 (no hot path slows). The
plan is `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-11-02-ir-views-pr2-lowering-heap.md`, written at `f69779f`. The user decided D1 to
D4 on 2026-11-03 and revised D1 the same day, after Task 1's container run (THE SNAPSHOT GATE); on 2026-11-03 he also
added Task 8b, the LLVM load rename, as its own commit. D5, a quiet machine for §7.2, was his word: "I'll tell you
when", then "can we work on this: ir-lowering Task 13" and "is it possible to run now" on 2026-11-05, and "Targeted
re-measure" for what the first rounds left undecided. Of the 37 commits, 7 change only `docs/` and 30 change something
outside it. The lane record is `~/temp/redextape-ir-lowering-record/` (`$R` below); its ledger is `$R/progress.md`.
`$F` is `$R/task14a/figures.log`, the output of `$R/task14a/figures.zsh`, which re-reads the figures below that git, a
baseline file or a Task 13 or rebase log gives.

**The rebases.** The branch was built on `14621b1`. After Task 12 it was rebased onto `e9bbf67` (#161), 30 commits,
`273520f` → `50710a8` (`$R/rebase-map.txt`), and after every §7.2 round but the browser 8-pair round and the
code-placement test onto `18c5272`, 37 commits, `7670b52` → `73dc741` (`$R/rebase-map2.txt`). This entry names each
commit by its SHA after the second rebase, but where it names a side of §7.2 as it ran. Each rebase brought in main's
change and nothing else: `git diff 273520f 50710a8` is byte-identical to `git diff 14621b1 e9bbf67` (16 files),
`git diff 7670b52 73dc741` to `git diff e9bbf67 18c5272` (87 files), and `git range-diff` marks all 37 of the second
rebase's commits `=` (`$R/range-diff2.txt`). So what this entry says ran at a commit ran at the commit it replaces:
Tasks 1 to 12 and their reviews on `14621b1`, and the whole-branch review, its gate, the fix rounds and §7.2 on
`e9bbf67`. Only what VERIFICATION places after the second rebase ran at `73dc741`, and its final gate at `9c45e4c`.

##### WHAT SHIPPED, TASK BY TASK

- **The plan, `f69779f`.**
- **Task 1 (§7.1), `016de34`, `dcc32e9`, `c7ff52d` and `ab3faef`, then `a21ec0b` and `0e11ae4`.** `016de34` moves the
  oracle corpus into `crates/redextape-native/tests/common/corpus.rs`, which `native_oracle.rs` and the snapshot test
  share. `dcc32e9` adds `src/codegen_snapshots.rs` with `every_build_prints_the_same_clif`, which failed first, and
  imports a function's callees in declaration order (D3, THE GENERATED-CODE CHANGES). `c7ff52d` adds the compare and
  write machinery, its three compare tests and 211 files under `crates/redextape-native/snapshots/`. `ab3faef` corrects
  two comments the corpus move made wrong. After the review, `a21ec0b` is D1 as revised, and `0e11ae4` puts it in the
  plan's gate, which now opens with an `llvm-config --version` check against `llvm-version.txt`.
- **Task 2, `d8f9862` and `c76ebe2`.** `d8f9862` makes the plan's gate block a `( set -e … )` subshell, so a STOP exits
  1 where the old block exited 0. `c76ebe2` adds `box30000` to `measure::CORPUS`, with 12 rows in each size baseline
  and three snapshots (THE BOX BUILDER). It is §7.2's base.
- **Task 3, `5f0da58`.** `codegen::define_all` is the one driver loop for the JIT, the AOT emitter and the snapshot
  test, and `codegen::jit_flags` the one flag set that `jit::host_isa` and the snapshots' fixed ISAs take.
- **Task 4, `2de3249` and `80a7d6d`.** One runtime import table for both backends. After the review one `rt_imports!`
  macro list generates the `RtFn` enum, its `ALL` list, each symbol (by `stringify!`) and each address, so a misspelt
  or missing row fails to build.
- **Task 5, `b334cd4`, `c6888e3` and `18b00c8`.** `lower::lower_subroutine` walks a subroutine once and drives a
  `LowerSink`; `codegen::ClifSink` is its first sink, and the arm-by-arm Cranelift body is gone. The plan's sabotage,
  the `Jz` tick moved after the register read, did not fire: the corpus's 68 `jz` were all forward. `c6888e3` adds
  `rxm-backward-jz`, a hand-written rxm loop with a backward `jz`, to the snapshot corpus alone, its snapshots recorded
  by `80a7d6d`'s code, and the sabotage then fails `rxm-backward-jz.clif`. `18b00c8` changes comments.
- **Task 6, `aca2333`.** `llvm::LlvmSink` is the walk's second sink, and LLVM's `translate_subroutine` is one
  `lower_subroutine` call. The trait's `missing_entry` keeps each backend's own error text for a missing entry block.
- **Task 7, `b2f62d0`.** Cranelift off `dyn Module`. `module_free::build_clif` builds CLIF with no `Module`, and
  `module_free_clif_equals_the_module_paths` holds it to the `Module` paths' CLIF. A `clif` feature, which `cranelift`
  (the default) turns on, builds for wasm32, checked by check-all's `base|wasm|-p redextape-native --lib
  --no-default-features --features clif` leg.
- **Task 8, `3f06b63`.** LLVM's register slots take the rxm printer's names, `a{i}`, `r{i}` and `rr`, from
  `tm::reg_str`, which becomes public.
- **Task 9, `61b3c93`.** Each CLIF instruction carries its rxm pc as a source location, and
  `each_instruction_carries_its_pc` checks it.
- **Task 8b, `1b3bbb7` and `9e62986`.** LLVM's loads take their slot's name, `S.v`, with LLVM numbering a repeat.
  `9e62986` lists the rename in the spec's §4.2, §7.1 and §8 and adds Task 8b to the plan.
- **Task 10, `b4f446a`.** `redextape_core::heap`: `Heap<R>` over a `Tags` recorder, the 8 fault texts once in
  `HeapFault`, `HeapCapped` for an allocation past the cap, and two recorders, the zero-sized `NoTags` and `VecTags<W>`.
  The rxm interpreter's cursor holds a `Heap<VecTags<WordTag>>`.
- **Task 11, `ecac1ba` and `8ae0f9c`.** native-rt's `Runtime` holds one private `Heap<NoTags>`, and each runtime import
  `RtFn` lists other than `rt_is_empty` is a thin wrapper over an `#[inline]` `Runtime` method; `rt_is_empty` calls
  the core's `heap::is_empty`.
  native-rt's tests pin all 8 fault texts, the JIT and LLVM `agree` helpers compare fault texts, and check-all gains a
  `base|wasm|-p redextape-native-rt --lib` leg. `8ae0f9c` brings the plan's heap lines up to the code.
- **Task 12, `050b1d7` and `e772257`, then `b90ce37`, `5e033ab`, `464512e` and `cf1dfed`.** The native crate's doc
  says where the two machines differ, and why: steps, the memory cap, the stack cap, registers across a call, malformed
  programs, and what follows a fault (§4.3's "not unified"). After the review the register, memory-cap and stack-cap
  items say what the code does; `codegen.rs`, `llvm.rs`, `native_oracle.rs`, `measure.rs`, the spec's §2.2 and the plan
  say a call counts depth, not a step; two JIT tests run where the machines' registers differ across a call; and the
  heap doc excepts the test-only `tags_mut` from "everything is `#[inline]`".
- **The whole-branch review's answers, `1533790`, `a395948`, `4b8b3bd`, `183cb24` and `084fff6`, then the re-read's,
  `0fad3d9` and `73dc741`.** The review's Important finding (the JIT and LLVM drivers promised `run_rxm`'s outcome on
  every program, which the crate doc contradicts), its 5 new Minors and the 12 carried Minors it marked to fix; then the
  re-read's Important finding (an `OPT_LEVELS` doc said every test that pins an outcome sweeps it) and its 4 Minors.
  `183cb24` adds a test that `build_clif` refuses a register index of exactly `MAX_REGISTERS`, and `084fff6` makes the
  heap's out-of-range test probe `(1 << 32) + 1`, which a 32-bit `as` cast would wrap onto a live cell. The rest change
  docs and comments, and `1533790` also renames `llvm.rs`'s `set_host_target` to `set_target`.

##### THE GENERATED-CODE CHANGES

§8 names five; four are this PR's, each in a commit of its own (the fifth is whatever PR 1's bumps changed).

- **D3, the import order, `dcc32e9`.** `translate_subroutine` imported a function's callees by iterating a `HashMap`.
  The plan's probe (its fact V5; `$R/probe-out/run-a1.log` and `run-s1.log`) found two builds in one process differing
  in as-built and optimised CLIF in 17 of 18 multi-subroutine configurations, in vcode text in 8 of the 9 x86-64 ones
  and in none of the aarch64 ones, and in machine-code bytes in none; in declaration order, 0 of 18 differ, and two
  processes' dumps are byte-identical (`cmp $R/probe-out/clif-s1.txt $R/probe-out/clif-s2.txt`). No snapshot predates
  the fix. `every_build_prints_the_same_clif` failed before it, on `first-order-11`, and its declaration-order assertion
  fires on a reversed sort (`$R/tasks/task-1-report.md`, B2 and sabotage B-ii).
- **The alloca rename, Task 8, `3f06b63`.** 124 snapshot files, 72 `.ll` and 52 `.opt.ll`, no `.clif`, 27,932 lines
  in and 27,932 out (`$F`). `$R/task8-logs/names-only-check.py` masks every value name and label definition and also
  requires the renaming to be one-to-one within each `define`: 124 equal, 0 not-equal. In the new `.ll` files' 489
  function bodies the 4,707 allocas are named `a0`…, `r0`… and `rr`, none renamed by LLVM
  (`$R/tasks/task-8-report.md`).
- **The source locations, Task 9, `61b3c93`.** 72 files, every `.clif`, no `.ll` or `.opt.ll`, 61,805 lines in and
  61,805 out (`$F`). `$R/task9-logs/srcloc-only-check.py`, on the tree before the commit and on its pair of commits:
  72 equal, 0 not-equal, each file's 6 machine-code sections byte-identical, hash lines and vcode included, and every
  `@` the one leading annotation of its line (`$R/tasks/task-9-report.md`).
- **The load rename, Task 8b, `1b3bbb7`.** 124 files, the set Task 8 changed, 19,689 lines in and 19,689 out (`$F`).
  `$R/task8b-logs/names-only-check.py`: 124 equal. Across the 72 `.ll` files, 5,556 loads, 4,623 named `S.v` and 933

##### THE SNAPSHOT GATE

**Where.** `crates/redextape-native/snapshots/` holds 217 files at `73dc741`: for each of 72 corpus keys a `.clif`, a
`.ll` and a `.opt.ll`, and `llvm-version.txt`, which reads 23.1.4; 8,240,032 bytes by `git ls-tree -l`. At `c7ff52d`
it held 211 files and 6,196,430 bytes (`$F`). By D2, decided before Task 1, the user kept all of the text the plan put
to him, about 6.1 MB in about 210 files; the ledger, `$R/progress.md`, records no decision on the growth to 8,240,032
bytes. The keys, in order: `first-order-NN`, `lambda-limitation-NN`, `beyond-field-width-NN`, `saturation-NN`,
`fault-NN`, `example-<stem>` for each `web/src/examples/<stem>.rxt`, `measure-<name>` for each `measure::CORPUS` entry
and `rxm-<name>` for each hand-written rxm program. A `.clif` holds the CLIF as built, then for
`x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu` and `aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu` at Cranelift's `none`, `speed` and `speed_and_size` the
optimised CLIF and each function's code size, fnv1a64 hash and vcode, on ISAs looked up by name with the JIT's flags and
no host CPU feature. A `.ll` holds the LLVM module as built, for `x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu`; a `.opt.ll` the module
after each of `O1` to `Oz`'s passes. The tests are in `crates/redextape-native/src/codegen_snapshots.rs`: 7 under
`--features llvm`, 3 under `--no-default-features --features llvm`.

**Regenerating.** On LLVM 23.1, `REDEXTAPE_WRITE_SNAPSHOTS=1 cargo nextest run -p redextape-native --features llvm
--lib codegen_snapshots`, then `git diff --stat -- crates/redextape-native/snapshots`. Under the variable each compare
test rewrites its own files and deletes its own orphans.

**The per-commit gate** is the block in the plan's "The snapshot gate": it stops unless `llvm-config --version` equals
`llvm-version.txt`, runs both test sets, and fails on a dirty `snapshots/`. It ran after each task's commits, and last
at `73dc741`; at `9c45e4c` the final gate's `check-all.sh` ran both test sets, 7 and 3 passed (VERIFICATION).

**D1 as revised.** The user's first D1 compared post-pass IR only on the release `llvm-version.txt` names. After Task
1's container run he revised it on 2026-11-03: `.opt.ll` is compared on every release; on 23.1.4, the recorded one, a
difference fails; on any other a difference prints `NOTE: this is LLVM <running>, the post-pass IR snapshots are LLVM
<recorded>'s, so <n> differing file(s) pass:` with the files, and the test passes; a missing or orphan `.opt.ll` fails
on every release. `.clif` and `.ll` fail on any difference everywhere. **So CI fails on post-pass IR only on the
recorded release.** The `rust` job's `check-all.sh --no-llvm --no-browser` runs the Cranelift half in its
`base|test|--workspace` leg; the `rust-llvm` job's `check-all.sh --llvm-only` runs the LLVM half in its `llvm|test|-p
redextape-native --features llvm` and `--no-default-features --features llvm` legs (`$F`). CI's LLVM is apt.llvm.org's
`release/23.x` of the day (C4 drew `1:23.1.5~++20261028083858+a738f2737189-1~exp1~20261028203909.94` from
`llvm-toolchain-bookworm-23`, `$R/task1-logs/c4-container.log`), and nextest hides a passing test's stdout, so a `NOTE:`
there reaches no log; it shows under `--no-capture` (`$R/tasks/task-1-report.md`, sabotage C2(d)).

**On the Mac.** At `c76ebe2`'s pre-rebase commit the gate ran on `davids-macbook-pro`, aarch64-apple-darwin, with
Homebrew's LLVM 23.1.4: 5 passed, 3 passed, `snapshots/` clean, so the 71 programs' files then matched there
(`$R/task2-logs/mac-logs/gate-mac-2.log`; the host, LLVM release and commit, `$R/tasks/task-2-report.md`, "The Mac
session"). It has not run there since.

The whole-branch review asked for these to be recorded: Task 5's sabotage could not fire on a corpus with no backward
`jz`, and the plan's gate section did not name the rxm program that answered it until `4b8b3bd`; Task 12's mandated
`>=`/`>` wording read as an off-by-one; and D3's and Task 8b's sentences went false as later tasks landed, until
`4b8b3bd`.

##### WHAT THIS DID NOT CLOSE

- **CI's LLVM has not run the snapshots added or renamed since Task 1's container run:** box30000's and
  `rxm-backward-jz`'s 6 files, and the 72 `.ll` and 52 `.opt.ll` that Tasks 8 and 8b renamed. A `.ll` fails on any
  difference on every release, so the PR's first `rust-llvm` run is their first check on whatever `release/23.x`
  snapshot apt.llvm.org serves that day. And on CI's LLVM a post-pass difference only prints a `NOTE:` that nextest
  hides, so CI fails on post-pass IR only on 23.1.4.
- **No gate runs core's tests on a 32-bit target.** check-all and CI only `cargo check` wasm32, so `084fff6`'s `(1 <<
  32) + 1` probe shows a 64-bit host only a pointer past the end, and the wrap it is there for was shown only by an
  emulation (`$R/tasks/whole-branch-fixes-review.md`).
- **9 rustdoc warnings in core's `tm/`, all from before the branch:** an unresolved link to `reduce` in `tm/header.rs`,
  and public docs linking the private `refused`, `pads` and `StateTable` in `one_way.rs`, `reduced_file.rs`,
  `reduction.rs`, `single_tape.rs` and `two_symbol.rs` (`cargo doc -p redextape-native -p redextape-native-rt -p
  redextape-core --no-deps` at `8e9ca0c`, `084fff6`'s pre-rebase commit, `$R/fix-logs/final-doc.log`;
  `$R/tasks/whole-branch-fixes.md`).

#### THE IR VIEWS GROUNDWORK'S PR 3: THE EIGHT WIRE TYPES, THEIR HELPERS AND `to_value` MOVE TO A NEW CRATE, `redextape-wire`, AND `web/bindings/` CHANGES IN JSDOC ONLY; CORE'S RXM `Program` GAINS SERDE; A COMPILE LOWERS CORE TO RXM ONCE FOR THE SOURCE MAP, THE TM RUN AND THE RXM LEG, WITH ONE TM STATUS MAPPING AND ONE COPY PROLOGUE; THE WEB'S FRAMES, RECORDINGS, SCRATCH REQUESTS, REPLIES AND SESSION FIELDS ARE KEYED BY `Leg` THROUGH TABLES; AND A `wasm-opt` SETTING, HELD BY A NODE TEST, KEEPS THE DEFUNCTIONALIZER OUT OF THE `compile` EXPORT (2026-11-07, branch `ir-wire-legs`, `783af0e..4065424`, 53 commits, plus this entry)

**Spec §4.4 and §5.1** (`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-27-ir-views-groundwork-design.md`), the groundwork's third pull
request in §6's order, gated by §7.2 (no hot path slows) and §7.3 (the app behaves the same, with a walkthrough in a
browser). The plan is `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-11-06-ir-views-pr3-wire-legs.md`, committed as `daafd4c` and
`bc068d1`. The user started the lane on 2026-11-06 ("resume the next IR step is PR 3 of the groundwork spec") and
decided Q1 the same day: `redextape-wire`'s comment budget is its measured share after the verbatim move, and the trim
of the moved docs is a later comment pass. On 2026-11-07 he accepted the amend of `ab0e8ee`'s message and the
controller's rulings that the first two handoffs list ("amend is fine and the rulings you made are fine"), said to wait
for the `ra-gui` session's CI job before the quiet-machine hold, to "try the `#[inline(never)]` split first", to land
the `wasm-opt` setting that trial found "with a guard", and to leave the check of upstream binaryen's `wasm-opt` to CI.
Later that day, after a fact-check of this entry, he decided to amend it with the check's corrections and to have the
record probe's cases (e), (f) and (h) measured again at the head under a quiet-machine hold. On 2026-11-08, when that
round flagged (b)'s `compiled` ms, he decided to run both a four-side diagnosis of (b) and the rule's repeat round in
one hold, then to test the mechanism before choosing, and then to keep WOPT's setting, this entry recording (b)'s cost
at the head, with the diagnosis, the mechanism and their limits, as an open item. Of the 53 commits, 2 change only
`docs/` (the plan's two) and 51 change something outside it. The lane record is `~/temp/redextape-ir-wire-legs-record/`
(`$R` below); its ledger is `$R/progress.md`. `$V` is `$R/z4/verify`: `$V/figures.zsh` re-reads the figures below that
git, a record file or a log gives, and re-runs the comparers of the window's rounds, the heap rounds, the trace and the
split trial, and the two module comparisons, comparing each output with the stored one by `cmp`, into `$V/figures.log`;
`$V/heavy.zsh` rebuilds `web/bindings/` and runs the leg count at the head, into `$V/heavy.log`. A row that names a
report gives the figure as that report states it. `figures.zsh` runs none of the commands in the rows for the re-run,
the diagnosis and the mechanism.

**The amend.** On 2026-11-07 a scripted rebase from `3b2bfa7` corrected `ab0e8ee`'s message, which had left 2 renamed
setup lines in `sessions.test.ts` out of its count. `ab0e8ee`, `88bca6f` and `3930912` became `7b7e974`, `e8dd37f` and
`0e1f5ac`; `git diff --quiet 3930912 0e1f5ac` exits 0, and the ledger's range-diff changed the message line only. This
entry names those three commits by their new SHAs.

##### WHAT SHIPPED, TASK BY TASK

Each task was its implementers' commits, then a review; the commits after "then" answer that review.

- **The plan, `daafd4c` and `bc068d1`.** `bc068d1` names a new `web/src/copy-build.ts` as the home of the copy build.
- **W0 (§7.2's base point), `6c11fe6`, then `7e2bbe8` and `eb1d954`.** A new probe,
  `web/tests/browser/record-cost.test.ts`, times recording through the real session worker: (a) fact-12 and (b)
  `sum_to(2750)` through all three legs, (c) and (d) two rxm copies, (g) a TM copy, (e) and (f) stepping the program's
  and a copy's views in the strip and the inspector, and (h) a replay of fact-12's captured replies through `onReply`.
  It prints each timing as a `RUN` line and each count that must not vary as a `FIXED` line. W0 changes no Rust.
- **R1, `f883480`, then `83a66a9`.** Serde for core's rxm `Program`, its instructions, registers, operators and caps,
  behind core's `serde` feature, with a round trip over the web app's corpus.
- **R2, `35def12`, then `23c63a1` and `b958906`.** One lowering dispatch, `tm::lower_program_mapped`, which keeps each
  instruction's origin, for `lower_program`, the source map and attribution. `b958906` sends 17 test and example helpers
  that wrote the dispatch by hand through `lower_program`; its message says 15.
- **R3, `4286fc8`, then `fc0bb83`.** The TM run (`run_tm_described_program`) and the source map (`sourcemap::Prepared`,
  `build_prepared`) take a lowering their caller hands them.
- **R4, `3f1afbf` and `e1fd2c1`, then `b64341b` and `219c9ce`.** One lowering per compile: `compile_with_caps` builds

##### THE GENERATED TYPESCRIPT

`web/bindings/`, rebuilt at the head by `bash scripts/build-web-bindings.sh`, differs from the baseline W0 regenerated
at `783af0e` (`$R/bindings-783af0e/`, 29 files) by R7's JSDoc alone: `diff -r` names `Decoded.ts`, `RxmCap.ts` and
`TmScratchStatus.ts`, its output is byte-identical to `$R/bindings-r7.diff`, and with each `/** … */` block stripped
every file equals the baseline's. `pkg/redextape_wasm.d.ts` is another matter: wasm-bindgen carries the exports' doc
comments into it, and R7's `36384e0` and `7acfc3c` and R8's `0ac62bf` replace 48 of its lines, all JSDoc, with 48
others. With JSDoc stripped, the head's `redextape_wasm.d.ts`, `redextape_wasm_bg.wasm.d.ts` and `redextape_wasm.js`
equal `783af0e`'s (`$R/r9/pkg-base/`). So no export, signature or import changed, and the d.ts's doc text did.

##### THE LEG COUNT

Spec §5.1's "Done when". The method is the plan's "The leg count": T is the sites `tsc` names once a fourth member,
`'probe'`, joins `Leg` and `PaneKind`, by `$R/leg-count/tsc-sites.zsh <worktree> <outdir>`, and N is the (file, family)
pairs in which one file of `web/src` spells a leg-named token for two or more legs, by `cd web && python3 -I
$R/leg-count/leg-names.py src --list`. W0 ran both at `783af0e` (`$R/leg-count/base/`), Z1 at `9e05912`, the last commit
of both halves before WOPT (`$R/leg-count/final/`, every site named in its `Z1-table.md`), and `heavy.zsh` at the head.

| figure | `783af0e` | `9e05912` | `4065424` |
|---|---|---|---|
| `tsc` error lines in the edited tree (the unedited tree: 0) | 80 | 163 | 159 |
| T sites, unique `file:line` | 78 | 155 | 151 |
| T in `web/src`: sites / files | 46 / 15 | 65 / 21 | 65 / 21 |
| T in `web/tests`: sites / files | 32 / 7 | 90 / 12 | 86 / 12 |
| N: sites / files / families / lines | 101 / 21 / 43 / 536 | 51 / 17 / 28 / 311 | 51 / 17 / 28 / 306 |
| files with T-`src` and N sites; with either | 10; 26 | 11; 27 | 11; 27 |

By Z1's reading of each site at `9e05912`, T's 65 `web/src` sites are 26 table entries, 5 switches and 34 cascades,
where the base had 19, 14 and 13; one of the 5, `programFork`, is new and not on the plan's list of switches that stay,
with W8's reason (the leg an arm narrows does not survive into a closure inside an inline spread). Of the families of
per-leg names, 15 went, every one the plan expected to go among them, and none is new; `<L>program`, `<L>state` and
`<L>leg` stayed in more than one file, each for a reason Z1 names (among them the wasm method names the Rust half keeps,
the ts-rs re-exports, the type maps).

**T rose.** The plan expected T to move "toward table entries (TS2741) and away from cascades (TS2536, TS7053)". Tables
went 19 → 26 and switches 14 → 5, but cascades went 13 → 34, so T in `src` rose 46 → 65 (TS2536 10 → 28 error lines).
The W tasks used the plan's typing pattern, a `<K extends Leg>` that indexes a per-leg type map, and the 8 maps
(`LegFrame`, `LegResult`, `LegStatus`, `LegReading`, `LegPane`, `ScratchOf`, `Made`, `CopyCompiled`) list their legs as
literal keys: `tsc` names each generic index into a map that lacks the key, and not the map. What a new leg must touch
in `src` is, by Z1's count, the 26 table entries, the 5 switches and one line in each of the 8 maps, which clears the 34
cascades; a leg that compiles a program also needs its key in `LegProgram`, and only then does `tsc` name `TELL`; since
`a0f3904` a key in `LegReading` likewise makes it name `CLEAR_READING`. T in `web/tests` rose 32 → 90 at `9e05912`, 46
of the 58 more being fixtures for `ResultLegs` and `ProgramRecording`, which `a99fd10` keyed by leg; `0269591` removed 4
(86 at the head).

**Against §2.4.** §2.4 counted "about 60 sites in about 20 files" by hand. T counts `tsc` error sites and N (file,
family) pairs, neither of them §2.4's unit, so only the file counts compare: at the base T's `src` sites lie in 15 files
and N's in 21, 26 in either; at `9e05912` and at the head, 21, 17 and 27.

**What neither instrument sees.** A bare leg comparison, `leg === 'tm'`: 15 code lines in `web/src` at the base, at
`9e05912` and at the head. The branch removed 3 in `pane-host.ts` and spelt three of the base's `'tm-scratch'` and
`'rxm-scratch'` checks in `session-worker.ts` as `kind === 'scratch' && leg === …`, one in its negated form, so part of
N's drop in `<L>-scratch` is a re-spelling into a form N does not count (`Z1-table.md`). And `TELL`, keyed by `keyof
LegProgram`: a leg added to `Leg` alone does not make `tsc` name it.

above in 16 of 16 and every split run above every final run; head/split 0.999, 10 of 16; and head/base 1.055, flagged,
