is WOPT's `5fac6ac`, not the commits after it.

**The mechanism, as far as it was found** (`$R/z3/mech-report.md`). The experiments ran without a hold, at 1-minute
loads of 2.6 to 22.8, final against split, (b) alone, each run's figure the median of its 5 fresh workers, in the
browser vitest drives, Playwright's `chrome-headless-shell` 156.0.8078.4. The hypothesis tested first, that split's
separate `defunc_mapped` stays in V8's baseline tier, Liftoff, is wrong: `defunc_mapped` never runs in (b) nor in its
warm-up, and no V8 trace compiles it. The cost sits in the Liftoff code of the `compile` export, on a compile that is
not the worker's first and runs before the export tiers up. It holds with `--liftoff-only`, +5.85 ms, split above in 6
of 6. It goes when that call runs TurboFan code: −1.40 with `--no-liftoff` (2 of 6), and a worker's second
`sum_to(2750)` compile, after the first has tiered the export up, reads −3.85 and −4.70 in two variants of the probe,
final above in every run. A worker's first `sum_to(2750)` compile reads −2.00, split above in 3 of 12. binaryen
re-optimised the whole export, which uses 60 locals in split and 73 in final, so its Liftoff code differs throughout.
The cost is fragile: four timestamps added to the worker's `onRun`, one field on its `compiled` message and one print on
the page, touching no wasm, took it from +6.60 ms (8 of 8) to +0.20 (4 of 8) in one interleaved round. By the report's
reading at most one compile in a worker's life pays it, a heavy one that is not its first. Not identified: the
lowest-level cause, for which code or data placement is the report's inference, not a measurement; nor was the cost
shown in the app, whose `main.ts` drives the worker differently. Tiering the export up eagerly, measured only through
V8's `--wasm-eager-tier-up-function` flag, removes the Liftoff call, −2.05, but costs a worker's first compile about 11
ms on split (29.25 ms against 18.1). On 2026-11-08 the user kept WOPT: the head ships `5fac6ac`'s setting, and (b)'s
cost is open (WHAT THIS DID NOT CLOSE).

**The warm-buffer heap: 40 B a copy.** Every TM round read final's JS heap above base's in every window round, by +160,
+200, +280, +560 and +360 B at 1, 2, 4, 8 and 9 copies, with a spread of 0 B on each side; the λ rounds did not differ
beyond a side's spread. The cause is the probe's own `entries` literal in `tmRound`, which mirrors `SessionEntry`:
`7b7e974` took it from 3 objects a copy to 5, two more `{ rxm, tm }` wrappers of 20 B each, and the rest of each round's
figure is V8's metadata for the new shape (`$R/trace-heap.md`). Base's probe file run on the final worktree read base's
figures to the byte in all 6 TM rounds, twice. The app's `SessionEntry` gained the same two wrappers in place of four
flat fields, so its net change per entry is roughly 40 B less the flat fields' slots, not measured (`$R/trace-heap.md`,
5); nothing in the figure grows with frames, steps or rings. The probe's "main-thread wasm module" and "source session
fixed cost" lines are constants in the test file, and its "wasm growth over module baseline" line comes from the λ
worker, which calls no `compile`, so nothing in it measures what `compile` allocates in wasm memory
(`$R/z3/cmp2-report.md`, 2).

**The module's size**, no gate: base `783af0e` 898,207 B raw and 318,020 B gzip; the window's final 896,735 and 317,251,
−1,472 B (−0.164%) and −769 B (−0.242%); the head 896,914 and 317,364, −1,293 B (−0.144%) and −656 B (−0.206%) against
base. gzip is `gzip -c <dir>/redextape_wasm_bg.wasm | wc -c`, whose header holds the file name.

The walkthrough drove the app at `4065424` in a headless Chrome, 1440×1000 at desktop width, by real CDP input through

##### WHAT THE PLAN STATED THAT NO GATE HELD

- **W5's sentence** "a new leg that compiles a program still has to say so in `LegProgram`, where `tsc` then reaches
  every reader" was false at `3c382ab`. With a probe leg added to `Leg`, `PaneKind`, `LegProgram` and `LegReading` (the
  web review's probe B), `tsc` named `TELL` but none of `replies.ts`' four places that set programs and cleared readings
  by a literal key. `a0f3904` made those places loop over `TELL`'s and `CLEAR_READING`'s keys; at `d08e21d` probe B
  names 69 `src` sites, 67 before, the two new ones `CLEAR_READING` and an `UnseenViews` cascade. The fix round checked
  those four places and no other reader.
- **§4.4's "one lowering per compile"** is held by `Prepared`'s private fields and `into_parts`, and by review, not by a
  test: `the_rxm_leg_and_the_map_index_one_lowering_through_defunc` passes a `compile` that lowers a second time, as
  `lower_program` is a pure function of its `Core`, and so does `3c382ab`'s guard. The Rust review argued this and did
  not probe it.
- **The leg count** went the other way from the plan's expectation (THE LEG COUNT).
- **Sabotages that did not fire:** R3's skip of `sized`, since `lower_tm_all` refuses the same programs, so `sized`'s
  checks are an early exit (`fc0bb83` says so) and its slot count is what a sabotage reaches; R4's frame-bank pre-check,
  until `219c9ce` tested `sized` itself; W8's `EDITOR_ON_LEAVE.tm = 'hold'` in the two files the plan named, where the
  whole browser tier fails 9 tests in 4 files; and the fix round's skip of the TM reading's clear alone, until
  `4065424`. The ones the plan's Z4 asked after fired: R8's `serialize_missing_as_null(false)` in `to_value`, and R2's
  and R5's.
- **The `CopyBuild<M>` of W3's brief did not tie a copy build to its leg.** With it, a `<K extends Leg>` body paired
  `BUILD[leg]` with another leg's `RECORDINGS` at `tsc` 0; `fe2e858`'s `CopyBuild<K, M>` refuses all four mismatches.
- **The R tasks' gates ran no web tier,** so `wasm-vocabulary.test.ts` failed from `9e85993` until W1.

##### WHAT THIS DID NOT CLOSE

- **Links, displays and pane construction stay per leg, for PR 4:** `draw.ts`'s focus links, `link-wiring.ts`'s pin
  fan-outs, `applyLayout`'s pane construction, and the `<L>display` family, λ's and TM's persisted view settings, whose
  shapes differ (λ layout, vars and map; TM level and edges; rxm none).
- **`PaneKind` is still a literal union,** not derived from `Leg`.
- **T sites with no reason, all from before the branch:** `main.ts`'s scratchpad `legs`, three `freshLeg` calls under
  one rule that `mapLegs` would build, and uniform fixtures in `examples.test.ts`, `protocol.test.ts`,
  `record-loop.test.ts` and `share-positions.test.ts` (`Z1-table.md`, "T sites with no reason").
- **What `tsc` does not name when a leg is added to `Leg`:** `TELL`, keyed by `keyof LegProgram`; the 15 bare leg
  comparisons; and a union leg argument, which defeats the per-leg tables (`setLegProgram`, `onScratch(req.leg, req)`,
  and `main.ts`'s `readingOf`, which has the same shape).
- **Holes a cast or a hand-built value still opens:** a `TmProgram` widened to `RxmProgram` first, or cast, passes as
  the rxm program (closing it needs a ts-rs discriminant or a brand); a hand-built entry passed to `seedPane` compiles
  with no cast; `tsc` does not stop a `RecordLeg<Leg, …>` from being built; and a TM pane built with an rxm slot's
  events compiles, which `applyLayout` never does (a phantom `LegEvents<K>` would close it).
- **Unheld behaviour, from before the branch:** nothing holds `BUILD.tm.free`'s `value?.free()` (removing it leaks a
  value run), and `copy-edit-leaving.test.ts`'s header claim that the typing is "sent as the view leaves" has no
  assertion.
- **The probe's case (h) does not time `LinkPositions.onReply`.**
- **The Rust half's leftovers:** the later comment pass that trims the history in `redextape-wire`'s moved docs (Q1),
  whose bindings difference will be JSDoc only and with which the crate's budget falls; each compile still builds the TM
  machine twice (`lower_tm_guarded` in the run, `lower_tm_mapped` in the map's TM half) and lowers λ twice
  (`lambda::lower`, `lambda::lower_mapped`), where §4.4 asked only for Core → rxm once; no test holds that it is once
  (WHAT THE PLAN STATED THAT NO GATE HELD); `to_value` refuses a `u64` above 2^53 − 1 (serde-wasm-bindgen 0.6.5 with
  bigints off), which `Instr::Li`'s immediate and native-rt's `Caps { mem: u64::MAX }` can hold, untested, and core's
  `Program` doc gives no caveat; the CLI's `emit.rs` emits rxm for first-order programs only; `b958906`'s message says
  "Fifteen helpers" where 17 are meant; and grammar-check's `src/rxm.rs` keeps the name `lower_via_program_template` for
  what is now `lower_program(core).ok()`.
- **The guard is a size, the profile a name.** A rename of `defunc_mapped`, a move or a `wasm-opt` that ignores the pass
  each fail `3c382ab`'s test, but its 36,000 B bound needs a human when `compile` or the defunctionalizer legitimately
  changes size, and it misses an inlined defunctionalizer under about 13 KB while some other function reaches the bound
  (`$R/tasks/WOPT-report.md`, 5). `build:wasm:dev` runs no `wasm-opt`, and the guard is inert there.
- **CI's `wasm-opt` has not run the pass:** by the user's decision of 2026-11-07 that check is CI's. The guard has run
  only on local builds, with Arch's binaryen 130; CI's `web` job runs it against its own build, by wasm-pack 0.15.1 and
  the upstream binaryen `version_130` it downloads. The gate's Docker image, built that way, served a module of 896,121
  B against the local 896,914 B, and nothing tests the image's module.
- **What §7.2 left unexplained:** the split's cold residual over base, +0.55 [−0.10, +1.30]; the trace's
  `--liftoff-only` residual of +1.0 ms; which commit merged the lowering into `compile` (not bisected); base's 36 B
  wobble in the TM warm-up round; the λ warm-up round reading about 10,000 B low on two of three runs at `3c382ab`;
  rxm-copy's 7 clean-pairs flags; and the outside loads, from about 16:35 in the window, 00:02 in r1 and 00:57 in r2,
  and the I/O pressure, whose sources were not traced.
- **(b)'s cost at the head is kept, not closed.** With WOPT's module, (b) `sum_to(2750)`'s `compiled` ms reads 1.047
  head/base in r1 and 1.052 split/final in the diagnosis, every run of the one side above every run of the other; pooled
  over r1 and r2 the rule clears it only through r2's wider base spread. Its limits: it was read only in the record
  probe's worker, where edits to the worker's and the page's JS that touch no wasm take it to +0.20 ms in one round and
  +2.15 ms in another; it was not shown to pay in the app; its lowest-level cause is not identified; and eager tier-up
  of the export, measured only through a V8 flag, costs a worker's first compile about 11 ms on split. To close it, a
  later change would have to read (b) beside a variant of the worker's JS that changes no wasm, as the control
  (`$R/z3/mech-report.md`'s p3), and read (b)'s sequence, a small compile and then a `sum_to(2750)`-sized one in one
  worker, as the app's `main.ts` and session client drive the worker, which no run here did.
- **Two strip behaviours the walkthrough saw, which comments at `783af0e` describe** (not re-driven at the base): the
  strip keeps the λ count from before a rewind until the next result, and keeps "stopped after 5,000,000 … at a cap"
  after a raise. And F1 and F2 (§7.3).
- **The gate differs from CI:** its local wasm-pack was 0.15.0, where CI and the `Dockerfile` pin 0.15.1, and it built
  the image with `docker build`, where CI runs `docker buildx build` on a `docker-container` builder.
- **Nothing has run in CI:** the branch has not been pushed.

#### RUST 1.100.0 TURNS `main` RED TWICE WITH NO CHANGE OF ITS OWN: THE STANDARD LIBRARY'S REGISTRY CRATES NOW LEAVE `/cargo/registry/<hash>/` PATHS WHERE THE TOOLCHAIN TEST LOOKED FOR `/rust/deps/`, AND CLIPPY FLAGS FIVE SITES `main` HAD NOT CHANGED; THE TEST READS THE NEW PATHS BY THEIR 16-HEX SEGMENT, THE RUST LICENCE TEXTS, BYTE-IDENTICAL, ARE NAMED AT 1.100.0, AND EACH SITE SATISFIES ITS LINT, ONE WITH A SLICE WHERE CLIPPY OFFERS `.take()` (2026-11-14, branch `fix/toolchain-1-100-licences-scan`, `101f1eb..b8277e3`, 3 commits, plus this entry)

`rust-toolchain.toml` tracks `stable`, and on 2026-11-12 rustup's stable channel moved to 1.100.0 (`0ef1bc386`,
committed 2026-11-09). `main` at `101f1eb` passed run 654, its push on 2026-11-08 under 1.99.1, and under 1.100.0 it
fails CI two ways at once: the web job's toolchain test no longer finds the standard library's registry crates in either
build, and clippy fails `-D warnings` on lines `main` had not changed. Three commits mend it: `4b8dc0f` changes the
test's regex, `303ff6a` names the Rust licence texts at 1.100.0 once they are compared, and `b8277e3` satisfies each
lint at five sites, one with a slice where clippy offers `.take()`, and raises one comment budget by 0.0002. No
behaviour changes, and no licence text or `web/src/third-party-licences.json` changes.

##### WHAT FAILED, AND WHY

- **Run 656, #168's CI on `fc1caba` on 2026-11-14, installed 1.100.0 and failed `rust`, `rust-llvm` and `web`**, and
  `gate` on them; `detect`, `linear-history`, `rust-slow` and `rust-browser` passed, and `rust-scoped` and `docker` were
  skipped. `fc1caba` is one commit on `101f1eb` that changes the README, three files under `docs/`, a grammar's README
  and `scripts/check-doc-figures.sh`, and nothing under `crates/` or `web/`, so the run tested `main`'s code. Run 654,
  `main`'s push of `101f1eb` and the `ci.yml` run before 656, installed 1.99.1 and passed every job it ran.
- **`rust` and `rust-llvm` stop at their first clippy leg on the same 3 errors**, all `clippy::map_unwrap_or`, whose
  message is "called `map(_).unwrap_or_default()` on an `Option` value", all in `redextape-core`'s lib. Those 3 were all
  CI could see: once a crate fails clippy, no crate built on it is linted. `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets` on
  `101f1eb`, without `-D warnings`, reports nothing under 1.99.1 and 6 warnings at 5 sites under 1.100.0:
  `map_unwrap_or` at those 3 and at 1 in `redextape-lsp`'s lib, which is reported twice, and `needless_range_loop` at 1
  in `redextape-core`'s `tests/tm_comments.rs`. With `-A clippy::pedantic` added, only the last is left:
  `map_unwrap_or` comes in through `clippy::pedantic`, which the workspace `Cargo.toml` enables as written, and
  `needless_range_loop` through `clippy::all`.
- **`web` fails 2 of its 3,092 tests, in 1 of its 288 files**: `licences-scan.test.ts`'s "names every registry crate of
  the standard library %s carries", once for each build, `pkg/redextape_wasm_bg.wasm` and
  `pkg-lsp/redextape_lsp_wasm_bg.wasm`, at its precondition: "the build carries some: expected 0 to be greater than 0".
  The test read those crates from `/rust/deps/<crate>-<version>` paths, and 1.100.0's standard library leaves none. The
  registry crates that 1.99.1's `x86_64` std rlibs name, 11 of them, are all under `/rust/deps/` (its `wasm32` std is
  not installed here); those that 1.100.0's name, `wasm32` and `x86_64` alike, 11 again, are all under one directory,
  `/cargo/registry/25cdd57fae9f0462/`, and no `/rust/deps/` path is left. The crates did not change: 1.100.0's
  `library/Cargo.lock` names `compiler_builtins` 0.1.160, `dlmalloc` 0.2.14 and `hashbrown` 0.17.1, the versions
  `licences.ts` already gave, and both builds carry `dlmalloc-0.2.14` and `hashbrown-0.17.1`, the two crates
  `TOOLCHAIN` lists.

##### WHAT CHANGED

- **`4b8dc0f`: the test reads `/\/cargo\/registry\/[0-9a-f]{16}\/([a-z0-9_-]+?)-\d+\.\d+\.\d+/g`.** Its one directory
  between `/cargo/registry/` and the crate, 16 hex digits, keeps the project's own dependencies out. A release build
  carries their paths too, two directories down, under `<CARGO_HOME>/registry/src/index.crates.io-<hash>/`, and where
  `CARGO_HOME` ends in `/cargo`, as this machine's `~/.local/share/cargo` does, those read `/cargo/registry/` as well.
  The census compared it with a loose form that puts any run of directories in the segment's place,
  `/\/cargo\/registry\/(?:[^/\0]+\/)*?([a-z0-9_-]+?)-\d+\.\d+\.\d+/g`, which finds `console_error_panic_hook`, `js-sys`
  and `serde-wasm-bindgen` in this machine's `pkg/` build and six such crates in its `pkg-lsp/` build, none of them in
  `TOOLCHAIN`, so the test would fail here with it. The web job, where the test runs, has `/root/.cargo` for its
  `CARGO_HOME`: `ci.yml` sets neither `CARGO_HOME` nor `RUSTUP_HOME`, the job's rustup install puts cargo's bin
  directory under `$HOME/.cargo`, which the job adds to `GITHUB_PATH`, and its `rustup show` prints
  `rustup home:  /root/.rustup`. `/root/.cargo/registry/` does not read `/cargo/registry/`, so on CI the loose form
  misses the project's crates by that dot alone. With both crates rebuilt under `--remap-path-prefix` from this
  machine's `CARGO_HOME` to `/root/.cargo`, and again to `/usr/local/cargo`, the new regex finds `dlmalloc` and
  `hashbrown` and nothing else in all six builds; the loose form finds only those two under `/root/.cargo`, and the
  project's crates again under `/usr/local/cargo`.
- **`/rust/deps/` is dropped, not kept beside the new form.** 1.100.0's std leaves no such path, and CI installs the
  newest stable on every run, as `rust-toolchain.toml`'s `channel = "stable"` asks, so no CI build leaves one now. A
  local build with an older stable, whose std leaves no `/cargo/registry/<16 hex>/` path (1.99.1's `x86_64` rlibs leave
  none), fails the precondition. The test's doc and `licences.ts`'s doc name the new form where they named
  `/rust/deps/`.
- **`303ff6a`: the Rust repository's licence texts are named at 1.100.0.** `licences.ts` gave them as at the commit of
  Rust 1.99.0, under "the versions that built the shipped files". The committed `COPYRIGHT`, `LICENSE-MIT` and
  `LICENSE-APACHE` are byte-identical to those at the `1.100.0` tag, as they are to those at `1.99.0`, and
  compiler-builtins' `LICENSE.txt` is byte-identical to the `1.100.0` tag's and to 1.100.0's `rust-src` copy. No text
  is replaced. The doc now reads "at Rust 1.100.0's release tag" and names no commit, since the comment guard's history
  rule rejects a commit hash in an added comment.
- **`b8277e3`: each of the 5 sites satisfies its lint, one with a slice where clippy offers `.take()`**, 4 files under
  `crates/`, 8 lines in and 11 out.
  - **`map_unwrap_or`, 4 sites.** `rxm.map(owners).unwrap_or_default()` in `build_over` becomes
    `rxm.map_or_default(owners)`, and the `listing` and `labels` fields in `TmProgram::of` and the diagnostics in
    `redextape-lsp`'s `publish` change the same way. `Option::map_or_default` gives `f(x)` for `Some(x)` and the
    default for `None`, as the chain did, and has been stable since 1.98.0, so the change builds with 1.99 too.
  - **`needless_range_loop`, 1 site, in `tm_comments`' `render`.** `for i in 0..spec.n_states` with
    `let st = &spec.states[i]` becomes `for (i, st) in spec.states[..spec.n_states].iter().enumerate()`. Clippy offers
    `spec.states.iter().enumerate().take(spec.n_states)`, which stops quietly at the vector's end where the index
    panicked; the slice panics there as the index did, and reads like `&st.rules[..st.rule_count.min(MAX_RULES)]` below
    it. The generator makes `states` `MAX_STATES` long and draws `n_states` from `1..=MAX_STATES`, so the two forms
    agree on every generated spec.
  - **`redextape-lsp`'s comment budget goes from 0.3077 to 0.3079, the user's call on 2026-11-14.** The rewrite of
    `publish` makes the crate 2 code lines shorter, 2,194 to 2,192, and no comment changes, 975 lines before and after,
    so the share goes from 975 of 3,169 lines, 0.30767, to 975 of 3,167, 0.30786, which the guard reads at the budget's
    four places as 0.3077 and 0.3079. At 0.3077 the guard fails the commit.

##### WHAT THIS DID NOT CLOSE

- **The sibling case, "carries no crate from the Rust tree but alloc, core and std", is partly blind on this machine.**
  It reads `/rustc/<40 hex>/library/<crate>/` paths, and on this machine, which has the `rust-src` component
  installed, a build also names the Rust tree's crates under `<sysroot>/lib/rustlib/src/rust/library/<crate>/`; no
  build without `rust-src` was compared. Both of this machine's builds name `alloc`, `core` and `std` in each form
  today, so nothing is hidden now, but a crate named only in the second form would pass here. Neither `ci.yml` nor
  `rust-toolchain.toml` adds `rust-src`; what CI's builds leave was not measured.
- **The toolchain test's precondition cannot see a partial move.** It fails only when a build carries no
  `/cargo/registry/<16 hex>/` path at all, so if a later standard library left some of its registry crates in a third
  path form while `dlmalloc` and `hashbrown` kept this one, the test would pass without reading the others. Each
  toolchain leaves one form today: of the `/<crate>-<x.y.z>` strings in 1.99.1's `x86_64` std rlibs, 0 sit anywhere
  but `/rust/deps/`, and of those in 1.100.0's, `wasm32` and `x86_64`, 0 anywhere but
  `/cargo/registry/25cdd57fae9f0462/`. The test is unchanged here.
- **Cargo 1.100.0 warns of an unused dependency** on `redextape-native` built `--no-default-features`, with or without
  `clif`: `redextape-native-rt`, through `cargo::unused_dependencies`, which is `warn` by default. It fails no gate:
  each of the five `check-all` legs that print it exits 0. 1.99.1's cargo gives no such warning on the same build of
  `101f1eb`. Making the dependency optional, or keeping it, is left for its own change.
- **The class search leaves 9 sites of `map_unwrap_or`'s shape as they are.** A scan of every tracked `.rs` file for
  `.map(..)` followed by `.unwrap_or`, `.unwrap_or_default` or `.unwrap_or_else` finds 9, each where `clippy::pedantic`
  is allowed: 4 in 3 of `redextape-core`'s examples and 3 in `redextape-test-support`'s `ts_derive_scan.rs`, each file
  allowing it at its top, and 1 each in `redextape-core`'s `tm/rxm_syntax.rs` test module and `redextape-native`'s
  test-only `codegen_snapshots`, under each crate's `cfg_attr(test, allow(clippy::pedantic))`. The scan for
  `needless_range_loop`'s shape, a `for` over a range that indexes by its variable, finds 14, none in a file that allows
  the lint and none flagged by 1.100.0's clippy.
- **`rust-toolchain.toml` still tracks unpinned `stable`**, as its own comment chooses, so the next stable can do this
  again, as 1.99.0 did on 2026-10-01.

#### MATERIAL AS THE DEFAULT PALETTE AND GRAYSCALE AS AN OPTION, WITH `match style` REMOVED: TWO BUILT-IN PALETTES FROM TINTED THEMING'S BASE16 SCHEMES, `material`, MATERIAL DARKER DARK AND MATERIAL LIGHTER LIGHT, FIRST AMONG THE BUILT-INS, AND `grayscale`, GRAYSCALE DARK AND GRAYSCALE LIGHT, LAST, EACH ADJUSTED TO THE CONTRAST FLOORS BY THE APP'S OWN `adjustVariant`; MATERIAL IS WHAT A VISITOR WITH NO STORED PALETTE CHOICE GETS AND WHAT `style.css`'S FALLBACK PAINTS, WHILE INSTRUMENT STAYS THE DEFAULT STYLE AND A STORED BUILT-IN CHOICE STILL WINS; `match style` LEAVES THE PALETTE MENU, A STORED `match` READS AS NO CHOICE, AND A CUSTOM PALETTE'S HALF NOT IMPORTED IS MATERIAL'S UNDER EVERY STYLE, SO NO PALETTE FOLLOWS A STYLE CHANGE; THE LICENCES PAGE CREDITS THE SCHEMES, MIT, IN ONE ENTRY UNDER A NEW COLOUR SCHEMES HEADING (2026-11-14, branch `feat/tomorrow-palette`, `13bc049..e2d3fef`, 21 commits, four of them this entry's, `a218f1f`, `c4ddaa1`, `e85c264` and `8b4976a`, plus this update)

The design's intent: Instrument's teal accent and blue-grey surfaces are not a good default, so the site gets a
classic palette, one built-in palette with a dark and a light half, and a visitor who never chose a palette gets it.
That palette is Material: the base16 schemes Material Darker for the dark half and Material Lighter for the light, by
Nate Peterson, from Tinted Theming's `tinted-theming/schemes`. Grayscale, the same repository's Grayscale Dark and
Grayscale Light by Alexandre Gavioli, joins the menu as an option. With #170 open, the user had `match style` taken
out of the palette menu, so the style and the palette are two independent choices. The design is
`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-14-tomorrow-palette-design.md`, whose three amendments of 2026-11-14 make the palette
Material, add Grayscale and remove `match style`, and the plan `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-11-14-tomorrow-palette.md`,
written for the design's first scheme, Tomorrow; both keep their names. `13bc049` is `main` with #169, the Rust 1.100
fix, and the branch was rebased onto it. The range counts every commit on the branch, as recent entries do: the
design's `6c75656`, the plan's `123b797` and the design's three amendments, `2edcbbd`, `b1435b5` and `235bd49`;
`c9e3bfd` and `383d79f`, which correct the design's first Colours table and the count below it; this entry's four,
its first draft, `a218f1f` and `c4ddaa1`, its rewrite for Material, `e85c264`, and `8b4976a`, which noted `aedc832`;
and the ten that change files outside `docs/`, `ce48d88`, `4e7823b`, `ea23ec3`, `4bbe19e`, `f464300`, `59864b8`,
`dd1bec4`, `e1a22aa`, `aedc832` and `e2d3fef`. Of those, `aedc832` changes only wording, Grayscale's doc comment in
`palettes.ts` and the design's text on it and on its amendments: from `e1a22aa` to `e2d3fef` no line of `palettes.ts`,
`contrast.ts` or `style.css` outside a comment changes. The figures below are `e2d3fef`'s.

##### DECISIONS

The user's:

- **Material, in place of Tomorrow.** The design's first scheme was Tomorrow Night Eighties dark and Tomorrow light,
  which he picked from mockups of published schemes mapped onto the app's slots. On 2026-11-14, with it built and
  #170 open, he tried its dark half live on the dev server and did not like it. He was shown nine dark base16 schemes
  as screenshots of the real app, each mapped onto the slots by the same roles and adjusted to the floors,
  `tomorrow-night`, `default-dark`, `grayscale-dark`, `material-darker`, `darcula`, `gruvbox-dark-medium`, `monokai`,
  `onedark` and `twilight`; he then tried Material Darker with Material Lighter live and kept them.
- **Grayscale as an option, not the default**, asked for after he chose Material: "can we actually also add the
  greyscale one as an option? (not default)". He had seen Grayscale Dark among the nine.
- **It follows the system's light or dark setting, with each scheme's own light half**, adapted, not Instrument's.
- **A default palette of its own, not a fourth style.** With nothing stored the palette choice reads as `material`
  where it read as `match`; `match style` stayed in the menu, meaning the style's own palette, until the decision
  below removed it. The way not taken, a style made the default, would have put a near-copy of Instrument in the
  style menu and changed every page's `data-style`.
- **With nothing stored, a style change keeps the default palette's colours**, which the user accepted with the
  design; only `match` followed the style, and with it gone no palette does.
- **2026-11-14, after the whole-branch review: a custom palette's half not imported keeps the style's own palette**,
  as on `main`. **Superseded the same day** by the next decision, which closes what this ruling left open.
- **2026-11-14, with #170 open: `match style` is removed.** "I think 'match style' is kinda confusing and we should
  probably remove it. people can just choose a style and palette that they like." His answers to the three questions
  it raised: **in #170**, not in a follow-up PR; **a stored `match` resets to Material**, reading as nothing stored,
  with no migration to the style's own palette; and **a custom palette's half not imported comes from the default
  palette, Material**, not from the style's own, and so does a token an imported half lacks. The design's third
  amendment, `235bd49`, records them and names the earlier text they supersede.
- **2026-11-14: the Rust 1.100 licences-scan failure, which predates this branch, is mended in a PR of its own
  first.** That is #169, `13bc049`.

The design's and its amendments' own calls, which they leave open to correction: the names and ids, Material and
`material`, Grayscale and `grayscale`; the menu order, Material, Paper, Terminal, Instrument, Grayscale since the
third amendment, so the default comes first and the option last; one PR; the one-time flash accepted, with no
cache versioning; `style.css`'s fallback block standing for the default palette, its test holding
it to `PALETTES[DEFAULT_PALETTE]` rather than to a palette by name; the slot roles, each slot drawn from one base16
colour; Material's light text and comment colours, under WHAT CHANGED; and one credit entry for the repository both
palettes come from, under its one licence.

One ruling made during the build, which the amendments keep: **`tok-binder` is the scheme's green, base0B, not its
red.** The design's first table gave it red, which is `error` too, and `contrast.ts`'s `binderClashes` holds
`tok-binder` at least `BINDER_APART`, 24, from every other token in some channel, `error` included. Material's
mapping keeps base0B for it, and Grayscale takes Material's roles; set to `error`'s value, `tok-binder` is 0 from
`error` in each Material half. `c9e3bfd` and `383d79f` correct the first table and its count.

##### WHAT CHANGED

- **The palettes, `ce48d88`, `59864b8` and `dd1bec4`.** `ce48d88` added the palette as `tomorrow`, `59864b8` renames
  it `material` with Material's values, and `dd1bec4` adds `grayscale`. `web/src/palettes.ts`'s `PALETTE_IDS` is now
  `material`, `paper`, `terminal`, `instrument`, `grayscale`, 19 tokens a half, and `skin.ts` labels the two Material
  and Grayscale. Each doc comment names the schemes, their author, the repository and MIT, and points at the design's
  amendment for each slot's source; the values are the amendments' tables'. Each slot takes one base16 colour by the
  roles the Material amendment lists, then `base16-adjust.ts`'s `adjustVariant`, which a base16 import's
  `apply adjusted` runs, moved each colour that fell below a floor.
  - **Material dark** is Material Darker as published but for base03, `#4a4a4a`, which `adjustVariant` moved to
    `#979797` in its three slots, `fg-dim`, `tok-neutral` and `tok-punct`.
  - **Material light.** The base16 port's base05 is `#80cbc4`, a teal, so the light half takes `#546e7a` as base05
    and `#90a4ae` as base03, which the amendment gives as Material Lighter's own text and comment colours;
    `adjustVariant` then moved 13 slots. `rule` is `#ccd7da`, the port's base03, not base02's teal, `#cceae7`.
  - **Grayscale** has no hand change; `adjustVariant` moved 8 dark slots and 11 light ones. Its tokens are told apart
    by brightness, not hue, and the floors leave most of them on one grey: in the light half six of the eight `tok-`
    slots, neutral, keyword, nat, bool, operator and punct, are `#656565`, with ident `#464646` and binder
    `#2e2e2e`; in the dark half four, neutral, keyword, operator and punct, sit within one step of `#8c8c8c` in each
    channel, nat and bool are brighter at `#999999`, ident is `#b9b9b9` and binder `#d1d1d1`. Its accent is its
    error colour in both halves, `#8c8c8c` dark and `#656565` light.
  - As committed, no half of either palette falls below any of `contrast.ts`'s 35 floors, and `binderClashes` finds
    nothing in any; `palettes.test.ts`'s *meets every contrast floor in every variant* and *keeps tok-binder apart
    from every other token* run over every built-in.
- **The default, `4bbe19e`, then `59864b8`.** `skin.ts` exports `DEFAULT_PALETTE`, `'material'`, beside
  `DEFAULT_STYLE`, which stays `'instrument'`, and `readPaletteChoice` returns it where it returned `match`: with no
  stored choice, with one it cannot read, and with a stored `custom` and no half imported. Removing the last imported
  half, which turned a `custom` choice into `match`, turns it into `DEFAULT_PALETTE` and stores `material`.

##### WHAT THIS DID NOT CLOSE

- **A visitor who had stored `match` sees Material on their next load, by the user's choice.** The stored `match`
  is not migrated to the style's own palette but read as nothing stored, so a visitor who kept `match` under any
  style, Instrument included, moves to Material, and chooses that style's palette again to get it back. **And a
  custom palette no longer follows a style change:** its half not imported is Material's whatever the style, where
  on `main` it was the style's own.
- **A one-time flash for a returning visitor.** The pre-paint script applies the palette `main.ts` cached under
  `redextape.palette.css` on the last load. A visitor with no stored palette choice, or with a stored `match`, has
  the style's own palette there from before this change, Instrument's under the default style, and one with an
  imported half has the style's own for the half not imported: their first page after it paints that palette until
  `main.ts` applies Material and rewrites the cache. The about, help, licences and privacy pages do not run
  `main.ts`, so they keep the old cache, and its palette, until the app is next opened. The design accepts the flash
  and versions no cache; its third amendment, which adds the stored-`match` and imported-half cases, does not
  mention it.
- **No text or button touching a pane's or the window's edge.** The user asked for this on 2026-11-14, his examples
  the TM pane's x button and the `source` title; it is a separate PR, not this one.
- **The view-switcher buttons.** The mockups' bordered source, λ and TM buttons are a separate change, later, as the
  user asked; the design lists them as a non-goal.
- **#168's README screenshot shows the old default**, and is to be retaken once this merges.
- **The deferred minors of the reviews before Material, re-checked at `e2d3fef`:**
  - `palettes.test.ts` asserts 4 of Material's 38 values and 4 of Grayscale's 38 directly, and no test holds the
    rest to the amendments' tables: the floor and binder cases hold properties, and the fallback case holds
    `style.css` to `palettes.ts`. The tables and `palettes.ts` agree at `e2d3fef`.
  - In `skin-switcher.test.ts` the two nothing-stored cases read the computed `--bg`, which `style.css`'s fallback
    block now gives alone, so they would pass if `main.ts` applied no palette. Its case that relied on the style an
    earlier case left, with a stored `match` held only in node, went with `match`: *switches the style, and a chosen
    palette stays* passes whatever style it starts from, and `skin-stored-match.test.ts` reads a stored `match` back
    at start-up in a browser.
  - `skin.test.ts`'s *keeps a stored choice over the default* repeats the loop of *reads a stored palette choice,
    and anything else as the default palette*, and since `e2d3fef`, which took out its `resolvePalette` assertion
    and made `PALETTE_CHOICES` `PALETTE_IDS`, adds nothing to it.
  - `web/scripts/licences.ts`'s `colourSchemes()` repeats `toolchain()` but for its group and directory.
  - `web/about.html`'s "The libraries and fonts it ships keep their own licences" names neither the colours nor,
    as before this branch, the toolchain runtimes.
  - `commitCustom`'s doc comment in `web/src/main.ts` gains a 121-character line, over biome's `lineWidth` of 120,
    which `biome ci` passes; the file had 11 lines over 120 before this branch and has 12.

#### `main` FAILS ITS 90% COVERAGE FLOOR AT 89.31% WITH NO RUST CHANGE: A CACHED `target` THAT RUST 1.99.1 BUILT KEEPS INSTRUMENTED TEST BINARIES IN CARGO'S OLD LAYOUT, WHICH `cargo-llvm-cov`'S PRE-RUN CLEAN NO LONGER REACHES UNDER CARGO 1.100 AND ITS REPORT STILL READS; EVERY CARGO CACHE KEY NOW CARRIES THE TOOLCHAIN'S VERSION, AND THE `rust` JOB CLEARS `cargo-llvm-cov`'S WHOLE BUILD TREE BEFORE THE COVERAGE RUN (2026-11-15, branch `fix/coverage-stale-cache`, 3 commits on `e65b164`: `d5e9c15`, the clean step; `3efa0ba`, which moves this entry's record to `~/temp`; and the one that keys the caches on the toolchain, which carries this text)

`main` at `e65b164` failed run 668's `rust` job at `Test + coverage`, where `cargo llvm-cov nextest --workspace
--fail-under-lines 90` measured 89.31% of lines. Run 659, the push of `13bc049`, passed the same step at 95.67%, and
between the two commits nothing changes outside `web/` and `docs/` but `README.md` and `scripts/check-licences.sh`. Two
changes mend it. Every cargo cache key in `ci.yml`, and every `restore-keys` prefix, now carries the toolchain's
version, so no job restores a `target` another toolchain built. And a step before the coverage run, `cargo llvm-cov
clean --verbose`, deletes all of `target/llvm-cov-target`, as defence in depth; `.forgejo`'s comment budget rises from
0.4973 to 0.4991 for that step's comment. No code, test or coverage floor changes.

##### WHAT FAILED, AND WHY

- **Run 668 restored a `target` that Rust 1.99.1 built.** Its `rust` job ran on runner `450440e2` and restored
  `cargo-v2-72c3afe5…` at 2,543,718,768 bytes: the entry that run 654, `main`'s push of `101f1eb` on 2026-11-08, saved
  on that runner under 1.99.1, the last time `Cargo.lock` changed. Run 659 ran on the other runner, `4360ddec`,
  restored `cargo-v2-slow-72c3afe5…` through the `cargo-v2-` fallback, and saved a `cargo-v2-72c3afe5…` of its own at
  3,016,195,101 bytes, which run 668 did not see. A hit on the primary key saves nothing, as `ci.yml`'s header comment
  on the `v2` salt says, so under the old keys run 654's entry is what a `main` run on runner `450440e2` restores
  until `Cargo.lock` or the salt changes. Nothing in it was reusable under 1.100.0: run 668's coverage step compiled the same 172 crates
  as run 659's, which started with no coverage tree at all.
- **Cargo 1.100 moved where test binaries go.** Its changelog
  (https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/cargo/CHANGELOG.html, Cargo 1.100, 2026-11-12): "Cargo now uses a new directory
  layout for intermediate build artifacts. … Tools that inspect the build directory may need to use Cargo’s JSON
  messages to locate build artifacts instead of relying on the build directory layout." In the reproduction below,
  1.99.1 writes the coverage test binary to `target/llvm-cov-target/debug/deps/stalecov-<hash>` and 1.100.0 to
  `target/llvm-cov-target/debug/build/stalecov/<hash>/out/stalecov-<hash>`.
- **`cargo-llvm-cov` 0.8.7's pre-run clean misses the old layout, and its report does not.** Its README
  (https://github.com/taiki-e/cargo-llvm-cov/blob/v0.8.7/README.md): "`cargo llvm-cov`/`cargo llvm-cov run`/`cargo
  llvm-cov nextest` cleans some build artifacts by default to avoid false positives/false negatives due to old build
  artifacts." `src/clean.rs` at v0.8.7 lists them, "build artifacts of crates to be measured for coverage", profdata,
  profraw, doctest bins and old reports, the first through `cargo clean --package` for each workspace member.
  `src/report.rs` at v0.8.7 makes the report's object list by walking `<target>/llvm-cov-target/debug` and keeping
  every executable named like a workspace package or target, hash or not, to "pass all compiled executables". Under
  Cargo 1.100.0 that `cargo clean --package` leaves a binary at the old layout's path, so the report reads it.
- **Everything the report gained is missed.** From run 659 to run 668, 85 of 104 files gain lines and none loses any;
  lines grow by 2,302 and missed lines by 2,302, functions by 117 and missed functions by 117, and the warning "N
  functions have mismatched data" goes from 1 to 68. `redextape-lsp/src/lib.rs` reads 1,039 lines with 6 missed in
  run 659 and 1,786 with 753 missed in run 668. A line that only the old binaries map has no counts in this run's
  profile, so it counts as missed.
- **A one-file crate reproduces it** with `cargo-llvm-cov` 0.8.7, building under Rust 1.99.1 first, as run 654 did,
  and then under 1.100.0, as run 668 did. Version B of its `lib.rs`, alone under 1.100.0, measures 13 lines, 0
  missed. Over a coverage tree that 1.99.1 left from version A, the same functions higher in the file and one with
  another body, version B measures 30 lines, 17 missed, 43.33%, and `--fail-under-lines 90` exits 1; `cargo llvm-cov
  report -v` lists both test binaries as `-object`s, and 1.99.1's survives the run's own clean. Over a tree that
  1.99.1 left from version B itself, version B measures 14 lines, 1 missed, 92.86%: the two compilers map the same
  source a line apart, so a file need not change to grow. From `101f1eb` to `e65b164` only 4 files under `crates/`
  change, against run 668's 85 that grew.
- **`clean --workspace`, the README's advice, would not have fixed it.** The README: "When using these flags, it is
  recommended to first run `cargo llvm-cov clean --workspace` to remove artifacts that may affect the coverage
  results." That runs the same per-package `cargo clean` (`src/clean.rs`), and in the reproduction 1.99.1's binary
  survives it and version B still measures 43.33%. `cargo llvm-cov clean` without `--workspace`, which the README's
  help gives as "Remove artifacts that cargo-llvm-cov has generated in the past", deletes `<target>/llvm-cov-target`
  and `<target>/llvm-cov` whole (`src/clean.rs`) and nothing else of `target`; after it version B measures 13 lines,
  0 missed, exit 0.
  Neither the README nor the CHANGELOG says anything about caching `target`; the README's CI examples do not cache it.

##### WHAT CHANGED

- **Every cargo cache key carries the toolchain's version, in the primary key and in every `restore-keys` prefix.**
  The five jobs with a cargo cache, `rust-scoped`, `rust`, `rust-slow`, `rust-llvm` and `rust-browser`, key it as
  `cargo-v2-<version>-<lockfile hash>`, with the job's tag after the version (`scoped-`, `slow-`, `llvm-`,
  `browser-`; `rust` has none), and their prefixes as `cargo-v2-<version>-` and `cargo-v2-<version>-<tag>-`.
  `<version>` is `rustc -V`'s release and commit hash, `1.100.0-0ef1bc386` today. Each job gains a step, "Read the
  toolchain's version for the cargo cache key", `id: rustc`, which writes it to `$GITHUB_OUTPUT` as `version`, the
  way `detect` and `docker` pass their outputs; it runs after the job's install step, whose `rustup show` installs
  the toolchain `rust-toolchain.toml` names, and before its cargo cache, and every step runs from the checkout's root,
  where that file selects the toolchain. `set -eu` and a separate `rv=$(rustc -V)` fail the step if `rustc` does.
- **Why the prefixes carry it too, and ahead of the tag.** A key without the version hits exactly on another
  toolchain's entry, which the cache action then never saves over: run 654's entry is that case. A prefix without it
  falls back to another toolchain's `target`, as the old `cargo-v2-` prefix did. With the version ahead of the tag,
  `rust`'s prefix and `rust-scoped`'s second one still fall back across jobs, as before, but only within one
  toolchain. A new header block in `ci.yml` gives the reason.
- **The `v2` salt stays.** A new version makes every key new by itself, so a toolchain release needs no bump; the
  salt is still for a change that alters `target` without changing `Cargo.lock` or the toolchain.
- **What a toolchain release costs now.** Each job's first run under a new version restores nothing, builds cold and
  saves under the new key. The build is cold on a release either way: run 668's coverage step, over 1.99.1's tree,
  compiled the same 172 crates as run 659's over none. What the old fallback did spare is the registry download,
  which each job now pays once per release. The merge is such a release for all five jobs.
- **`ci.yml`'s `rust` job gains a step, "Clear cargo-llvm-cov's build tree", `cargo llvm-cov clean --verbose`,**
  between the feature matrix and `Test + coverage`. `--verbose` prints a `Removing <path>` line for each directory it
  deletes, so a run's log shows whether its cache carried a coverage tree. The step's comment gives the reason, why
  not `--workspace`, and the cost.
- **The clean step is kept as defence in depth, and is redundant for this failure once the keys carry the version.**
  Within one toolchain, the pre-run clean already removes a test binary left under another hash: in
  `$S/same-toolchain.log`, a run at another package version leaves its binary, and the next run's report lists only
  its own. Only a tree another Cargo built escapes that clean, and the keys now keep such a tree out. The step holds
  the report if one gets in anyway, by a key or restore this change did not foresee. Its cost is the cold
  instrumented build of the dependencies on every run: run 659's coverage step, with no tree to start from, logged
  `Finished` at 14.21s on runner `4360ddec`, and run 668's at 48.00s on runner `450440e2`. The workspace members
  were already rebuilt on every run, since the pre-run clean removes them.
- **`scripts/comment-budget.json`: `.forgejo` 0.4973 → 0.4991**, the value the comment guard gave for the clean step's
  comment, 561 comment lines against 563 code lines. The key change adds 6 comment lines and more code lines, and the
  guard passes at 0.4991 with no new value to write.
- **Not taken: dropping `target/llvm-cov-target` from the cached paths.** It would also stop carrying the tree in the
  cache, but it changes the cache's paths and so its version, whose matching on this Forgejo's cache server was not
  checked.

##### WHAT THIS DID NOT CLOSE

- **The entries under the old key forms stay on both runners' cache servers until they are evicted**, run 654's
  among them. No run restores them: none of the new keys or prefixes is a prefix of an old key.
- **The cache still carries `target/llvm-cov-target`**, which the new step deletes after each restore; the transfer
  is unchanged.
- **This PR's own CI cannot run the failing case.** Run 666, PR #170's `pull_request` run on runner `450440e2` after
  run 654's save, restored `cargo-v2-slow-72c3afe5…` through the fallback rather than run 654's `cargo-v2-72c3afe5…`,
  and run 668 did not restore the 3,273,638,517-byte `cargo-v2-72c3afe5…` that run 666 saved, so on that runner
  `pull_request` runs and `main` pushes do not share these entries. After the merge no run can restore run 654's
  entry either, so the failing case is gone by construction; the reproduction is what shows the clean step at work.
  What the PR's run can show is the keys: each job's new step should print its version, its cache step should miss
  `cargo-v2-1.100.0-0ef1bc386-…` and save under it, and a second push should hit it.
- **`rust-toolchain.toml` still tracks unpinned `stable`.** A release still changes clippy's and rustfmt's verdicts
  with no change here; the keys only stop it from mixing toolchains in `target`.
- **The class search finds no other reader of Cargo's build layout, and no other cache of Rust output.** `git grep`
  outside `docs/` for `/deps/`, `debug/deps`, `release/deps`, `llvm-cov-target`, `target/debug/build` and
  `.fingerprint` finds nothing; the paths under `target/release` that `plugin/redextape.lua` and two examples' doc
  comments name are final artifacts, which Cargo 1.100.0 still writes there. `ci.yml`'s other caches, `apt-llvm-23`,
  `apt-chrome` and `pnpm-<lockfile hash>`, hold downloaded packages, not a build, and `advisories.yml` caches nothing.

requires no step between the first and the last to run `rustup` or set `RUSTUP_TOOLCHAIN`, and requires the key
and every `restore-keys` line to begin `cargo-v2-${{ steps.rustc.outputs.version }}-`. It prints each job's step
indices and the `ci.yml` lines of the three, which were read against the file. Then it runs the version step's
script, the same text in all five jobs, from the checkout's root with `GITHUB_OUTPUT` pointing at a file.

    page's end edge. Where neither the base option nor a flip fits, that fallback is taken, nothing overflows, and

    `position-area` the percentage is of the room the menu opens into, so a menu longer than the room below its button

##### WHAT THIS DID NOT CLOSE

- **The TM tape label `BOX` at the TM pane's bottom.** In the sweep at 390 × 844 with source and TM, its bottom is
  2.6 px above the pane's bottom edge, where the pane, its content taller than it, cuts its tapes; the rows above it
  grew, which moved the cut. The plan has the guard skip a pane's bottom, since a pane scrolls, and ruling R24 has this
  entry state `BOX` as that case. It is the sweep's one row against a pane's edge left.
- **`linesShown` in `inspector-phone.test.ts` counts a panel header's label as a line of content**, so Debugger at
  320 × 500 with the notice gone keeps its open-inspector check on a label.
- **Two 1-px header bands.** `◐` at 10 px is 0.94 px wider than this machine's system face drew it, so `settings`
  takes an extra header row at 587 px in all three presets and at 372 px in Stage. No pinned width sits on either; the
  guard's settings scan steps through 372 and picks its width at run time.
- **83% is tuned to Chromium's rounding.** Chromium as the browser tests run it sets the shrunk face on a whole pixel,
  15 px × s to 12 px for every s from 76.67% to 83.33%; Firefox draws it unrounded, at 83% of STIX's advances. Firefox
  kept Debugger's header on one row at 1280 px with full-size STIX too.
- **Paper and Terminal draw `→ ↗ ▾ ◐ ⚠` from system fonts, by design**: the face is in Instrument's stacks only, and
  their headers wrap where each machine's fonts put them.
- **`help.html`'s six other glyphs**, `↺ ◀ ▶ ⋯ ✕` in its `<strong>`s and `⌘` in a `<kbd>`, are system-drawn: the
  range names the app's list. STIX has five of the six, not `✕`.
- **The face has no preload.** On a first Instrument visit the header draws its carets and `◐` in a system face until
  the file arrives (`font-display: swap`), and can shift when it swaps in. The shrunk glyphs sit on the baseline,
  lower against the text than full-size STIX's.
- **The wrapped-actions case at 320 × 844 runs in the default style only**, and the tally of `⚠` rows was not
  sabotaged again at 83%.
- **The guard's pane edges come from `clientWidth` and `clientHeight`**, which Chromium rounds to whole pixels, so a
  pane's right-side gap is good to under 1 px; its rows sit 8 px in against a 4 px threshold. The panel-header cases
  read their rules from the border box.
- **Measuring an open menu against the viewport, `52a0617`, was not sabotaged**, so whether the earlier measure, the
  document's scroll size, was ever blind at the guard's windows is not known. A menu taller than the whole window was
  not measured; the cap is of the room below its button.
- **About's guard case runs below 320 px.** In Instrument in Chromium no window from 320 to 1280 px wide, 844 px
  high, puts about's button where its menu fits beside it with under 4 px to spare, so the case finds 303 to 306 px
  and holds about at 305; there, with its gutter, about fits neither way, and in Firefox only its fallback keeps the
  gutter.
- **Settings and the add-view menu have no fallback against the page's edge**; in the scans neither fits neither way.
- **Paper's about menu on CI's fonts was reproduced in Chromium here only by moving its button.** Before the fix,
  Firefox here put it 2.47 px from the window's left edge in Paper at 488, 496 and 944 to 1040 px, and 0.93 px in
  Instrument at 488, 496 and 952 to 1048, by the same leftward fit; it now opens rightward there, 120.27 and 118.9 px
  from the left edge.
- **Firefox, which CI does not run, for the Firefox lane, whose next is its PR 3:**
  - `header-menus-narrow.test.ts`'s "the workspace menu, open > lies under its button at a desktop width, each row on
    one line" fails in Firefox before `a989d13` and after: Firefox sizes that menu at 320 px, its `20rem` minimum, in
    Paper and at 321.35 px in Instrument, against Chromium's 368 to 370, and a row wraps.
  - `view-keys-focus.test.ts`'s "in Stage > leaves the caret in the source editor, and the key chooses the tabs" and
    "on a views toggle > leaves the focus alone when the window is narrowed with the focus elsewhere" pass in some runs
    and fail in others; the first failed at `c6b4d68` too, and passes run alone.
  - Of the 15 files that open the workspace, examples or share menu, 12 cases fail in Firefox both at `c6b4d68` and
    after `a989d13`: controls-gate 1, follow-kept 1, header-menus-narrow 1, scroll-kept 5 and view-keys-focus 4. The
    15 were last run at `8e8b7b5`, twice, with 13 and 12 failures, and not on the final tree.
  - `inspector-phone.test.ts` fails 11 cases in Firefox, the same 11 at `52a0617` and at `30dcb96`: Debugger and Stage
    open at 320 × 568, 390 × 844 and 480 × 800, Explorer with the inspector open at 390 × 844, and the stage-strip
    short pages at 320 × 320 and 320 × 400 with the notice up and gone. The figures this branch re-derives are
    Chromium's.
- **The README screenshots** are to be retaken once this merges, as the design's "After it merges" says: Material

- **The design's non-goals:** the TM tape cells, whose glyphs sit 1.7 px from the cell borders; `help.html`'s `kbd`

#### README ACCURACY: THE README READS AS AN INTRODUCTION, WITH "HOW IT WORKS" IN PLACE OF THE BUILD TOOLING, THE PROJECT'S NAME IS LOWERCASE IN PROSE, THE ARCHITECTURE, DEVELOPMENT AND CONVENTIONS DOCS AND THE CLI AND GRAMMAR READMES SAY WHAT THE CODE DOES, AND THE CLI REFUSES WHAT IT CANNOT RUN, AMONG IT A `.tm` THAT HALTS IN ITS `overflow` STATE, WHICH IT DECODED TO A WRONG VALUE AT EXIT 0 (2026-11-15, branch `docs/readme-accuracy`, `9e0c229..75f0f6c`, 26 commits, plus this entry)

The user, 2026-11-15: review every README against the code for accuracy. The top README should read
less like AI and more like a good introduction, and its "How it's built" was padded with what does
not matter to its reader, CI, nginx and Docker; the CLI and grammar READMEs may stay technical; and
nothing is edited until he has seen the findings. Five read-only agents fact-checked, at `85b987f`,
the top README, the CLI README, the mini-language and λ grammar READMEs, the rxm and TM grammar
READMEs, and the four grammar READMEs' editor-install sections, and found 75 problems; among them
were three bugs in the CLI, not mistakes in its README. The lane's record is
`~/temp/redextape-readme-review-record/`, `$R` below: `ledger.md` holds the user's decisions and the
order of the work, `top.md`, `cli.md` and the three `grammars-*.md` the fact-check, and the
`*-report.md` files beside them the work, the review and the fixes. The CLI commits were made on a
branch of their own, `fix/cli-readme-bugs`, in a second worktree, and cherry-picked onto this one in
the order `ledger.md` lists their first SHAs; they are `c0f0f36..63bac76` here, and the review's
grammar fixes, made on `fix/readme-review-grammars`, are `a3f5fdd`. The reports name commits by the
SHAs they had where they were made, before the branch was rebased onto `9e0c229`; `sha-map.txt`
pairs each of the branch's SHAs from before the rebase with its SHA now.

##### DECISIONS

The user's, all on 2026-11-15:

- **The CLI's bugs and the stale `docs/architecture.md` and `docs/development.md` are fixed here, in
  one PR**, so that he can read the README rendered on the forge and on GitHub. The leftover
  `grammars/tree-sitter-redextape-asm/parser.so`, which no commit tracked, was deleted.
- **The README draft is "pretty good", and the name is lowercase in all prose in this PR:** the
  READMEs, the `tree-sitter.json` descriptions, the header comments of the CI, Docker, nginx and
  compose files and of the rxm and TM `grammar.js` and `highlights.scm`, core's crate doc and the
  example programs' banners. `Language::Redextape`, the lines that name it, and the `"camelcase"`
  fields stay.
- **The overflow fix keeps its reach into core and the web app**, and `emit` and `lint` refuse a
  `.tm`, `.rxm` or `.rxlambda` file up front at exit 2, as `run` refuses a `.rxlambda`.
- **`emit --lang rxm` refuses a function-typed result at exit 2, as `--lang tm` does**, where the
  first fix wrote a listing with no `result` line at exit 0 that `run` then refused. Asked whether
  such a result is "categorically wrong" or could be shown in "a more interesting way", he kept the
  second as a follow-up, below.

The controller's:

- **`fmt --form <form> q.rxlambda` skips the refusal**, because `--form` overrides the extension
  wherever `fmt` reads one; the CLI README says so since the review.
- **`docs/conventions.md`'s four wrong statements about CI**, found while the development doc was
  corrected, went in with the lowercase pass as a commit of their own, `f085cbc`.
- **The rxm and TM READMEs' seed-dependent span ranges were deleted, not widened**, once four more
  runs of the TM leg put three totals outside the ten-run range the README quoted.

##### WHAT CHANGED

- **The top README, `9c2f3b3`, then `3c0a2d2` and `f3deb33`.** It opens with what the language
  compiles to and the link to redextape.com, then the screenshot. "What it does" is corrected: the
  λ, rxm and Turing machine views step, and the source view does not; a long run pauses at the step
  cap or when its recording fills, two stops, either of which it can be told to carry on past; a
  share link holds the program, the layout of the views and the step shown for each machine. "How it
  works" replaces "How it's built", which described CI, nginx and Docker, and said that
  `redextape-core` holds all the backends and that wasm-pack compiles it: the front end, the λ
  backend's encodings and why its term must reduce in normal order, readback by the program's type,
  rxm and the dispatcher for functions used as values, the five tapes and their fixed-width fields,
  the reductions, the source map behind linking, and the web worker. Since the review it says the
  compiler turns *a* program into a λ-term, and that a few programs that use `mut` have none, for
  which the λ view shows the reason.
- **The name, `2fc8e56`.** 35 lines in 24 files go from `Redextape` to `redextape`. The 24 lines
  outside `docs/superpowers/` that still say `Redextape` are the ones the decision keeps: 18 in
  `crates/redextape-lsp/src/language.rs`, the four `tree-sitter.json` `"camelcase"` fields,
  `scripts/check-lua.sh` and `web/tests/browser/lsp-diagnostics.test.ts`. Regenerated with the
  pinned tree-sitter 0.25.10, each grammar's `src/parser.c`, `grammar.json` and `node-types.json`
  are byte-identical, since `generate` writes neither the description nor `grammar.js`'s comments.
- **The docs, `0de5a6b` and `f085cbc`, then `3c0a2d2`.**
  - `docs/architecture.md` describes four kinds of pane, with the λ tree, linking, the copy editors
    and the state diagram built, where it said the λ pane had no tree and lacked click-linking; LSP
    hover served; the TM reductions, the universal machine and the counter machines; "ten exported
    functions", the module's `start` function, `init`, not among them; and a core with no
    dependencies at default features, `serde` and `ts-rs` being optional dependencies behind the
    `serde` and `ts` features. Its three 2026-08 measurements are dated.
  - `docs/development.md`'s web setup runs `pnpm run build:lsp-wasm` beside `build:wasm`. Followed
    as written in a fresh worktree, the old setup left `typecheck` failing with TS2307 on
    `../../pkg-lsp/redextape_lsp_wasm.js`, `test:node` failing 2 of 1,482, and the dev server
    answering the LSP worker with a 500. The CI jobs are described as `ci.yml` has them, and
    `rust-scoped` as scoped to the branch's whole diff against `main`.
  - `docs/conventions.md`: `rust-browser` joins `rust` and `rust-llvm` in covering every
    configuration and in skipping a draft PR; an edit to a PR's title or body re-runs CI; and
    `linear-history` never sees a push to `main` that changed only `docs/`.
- **The CLI.** Each fix and refusal has a test, and each report says its new tests failed with the
  fix reverted:
  - `c0f0f36`: `emit --lang rxm` lowers through `tm::lower_program`, which falls back to
    defunctionalising, where it called `lower_rxm` alone. `closure.rxt` and `map-fold.rxt`, which
    `emit --lang tm` and `run --backend tm` took, failed with "no rxm lowering" at exit 2; they now
    emit and run back to 42 and 9.
  - `85d66e7`: `--backend` is an `Option` with no default, so `--backend reference` on a `.tm` or
    `.rxm` file is refused at exit 2, as `lambda` and `tm` were, where it was accepted silently.
    Omitted, it still means `reference` for a `.rxt` program.
  - `be5abeb`, then `92f89ae`: every overflow under `run` exits 2. `run --backend tm` answered 1.
    Worse, a `.tm` that halted in its non-accept `overflow` state had its truncated tapes decoded:
    `40 + 2` built at width 4 printed `0` at exit 0. The check is in core, where `value_of_run`
    returns a new `RunFailure::Overflow` keyed on `build::OVERFLOW_STATE`, because that function is
    the one decision the CLI and the web app's TM buffers share; so a TM copy in the web app that
    halts in `overflow` shows a fault where it showed a wrong value, through a new arm in the wasm
    crate's `failure_value`. `emit`'s overflow refusal says `run` would find no value and exit 2,
    where it said `run` would print a wrong answer at exit 0.
  - `a0cbde4`, `3f8aa36` and `ddf7aaa`: `run`, `emit`, `lint` and `fmt` read a file's kind from its
    extension in any letter case and refuse one they do not take before reading it, at exit 2,
    naming what the file is: `run` a `.rxlambda`; `emit` and `lint` a `.tm`, `.rxm` or `.rxlambda`;
    `fmt` a `.rxlambda`, unless `--form` names a form. Each lexed the file as `.rxt` and blamed the
    program, at exit 1, or at exit 2 under `fmt`. `Form::is_lambda_term` matches as
    `Form::from_extension` does, and `Form::compiled_noun` builds on both, so there is still one
    extension table.
  - `2baf2b5`: `emit --lang rxm` refuses a result type no `result` line can name, a function's, at

- **The CLI README, `63bac76`, then `3c0a2d2` and `aba3c20`.** It is rewritten against the CLI after

  - What uses them, `711f304` and `bd6281a`: the web app colours its source editor and each copy

  - History phrasing, `aba3c20`, then `97a720c` and `75f0f6c`: sentences in the CLI and grammar

##### WHAT THE REVIEW CAUGHT

Three reviewers read the branch at `a220feb`, one the code and two the prose, and a fourth read the
history pass at `aba3c20`; they found 28 problems, and every one was fixed.

- **The overflow fix's own false positive.** `be5abeb` keyed the overflow on the state's name alone,
  so a `.tm` whose accept state is named `overflow` was refused at exit 2: `list_1_2.tm` with
  `overflow` renamed `ovf` and `halt` renamed `overflow` printed `[1, 2]` on `main` and was refused
  on the branch. `54f9b26` adds `!s.accept`; `Builder::state` always makes the guard non-accept.
- **An order no test held.** `run`'s `.rxlambda` refusal test used only files that exist, so a
  refusal moved after the read stayed green; `6d5eab2` adds a missing file, as the other three
  commands' tests have.
- **A wrong reason.** A list nested past `MAX_TY_DEPTH` was refused with "this type has none", which
  `1982f9d` replaces.
- **A claim the branch made wrong.** The λ README said no committed file has a `.rxlambda`
  extension, and the branch's own CLI fixtures added four.
- **A correction that was wrong.** The first editor pass said Zed's `rev` takes a tag. Zed runs
  `git fetch --depth 1 origin <rev>` and then `git checkout <rev>`, and a tag fetched by name stores
  no tag ref, so the checkout fails; replayed with git 2.56.1 against a `file://` remote.
- **A tense that made a claim false.** The history pass turned "nothing downstream could have caught
  it" into "nothing downstream would catch it", which a test over `lambda::CORPUS`, holding
  `f λx. x`, disproves.
- **The rest:** `rust-scoped`'s scope in `docs/development.md`; the CLI README's `--form` exception;
  the TM span range; `tree-sitter test` counted as a layer of the crate when `check-all.sh` runs
  it; and imprecisions and history phrasing in the README, the docs and the grammar READMEs.

##### WHAT THIS DID NOT CLOSE

- **Function-typed results**, the follow-up the user kept. `emit --lang tm` and `--lang rxm` refuse
  them; the λ backend could print the normal form, and every backend could agree on an opaque
  `<fn>`.
- **A hand-written `.tm` whose non-accept halt is named `overflow`** is still read as an overflow
  and refused at exit 2, since the header does not record which state is the guard.
- **A reduced, `version 2`, `.tm` that halts in a state named `overflow`** goes through `NotAccept`,
  exit 1, "not an accept state". An emitted reduced file cannot reach it, since `reduce` refuses a
  reduced run that does not halt in an accept state.
- **Stdin, `-`, has no extension**, so `emit -`, `lint -` and `run -` read it as `.rxt`, and a
  machine or a λ term on stdin is blamed as a program at exit 1.
- **`--help` for `emit`, `lint` and `fmt` names none of the refusals.** `run`'s message for a
  `.rxm` with no `result` line, `crates/redextape-cli/src/run.rs:327`, says `emit --lang rxm`
  "writes a header whenever the program's result type can be expressed", and not that it refuses
  otherwise; and the CLI README's `--field-width` sentence, line 239, still says "today's
  behaviour".
- **`fmt --form rxt q.rxlambda`** reads the term as `.rxt` and prints a lexer error for each `λ`,
  exit 2, as `--form` is meant to override the extension.
- **`fmt` has no printer for a λ term**; it could format `.rxlambda` the way the LSP does.
- **The editor checks that did not run:** the `master` proof ran on Neovim 0.13.0-dev, outside
  `master`'s 0.10 and 0.11, and on no supported version; a Zed tag `rev` was reasoned from Zed's
  source and replayed with git, not run in Zed; and the Helix `indent` values were not run in Helix.
- **The rxm and TM `grammar.js` header comments still call an accept-less divergence "a defect"**,
  though both READMEs now list accept-less divergences that reproduce, and the TM one's item 4
  still describes the `two-symbol` comma ERROR that the README lists as accept-less.
- **`plugin/redextape.lua`'s comment on `.tm` sniffing** names a TeXmacs document in its measured
  corpus, history in a comment.
- **The λ backend's limitations:** the 4 programs of `LAMBDA_LIMITATION_DEMOS` in
  `crates/redextape-core/tests/three_way_oracle.rs`, each with a `let mut`, still have no λ-term;
  the README now says so.
- **`docs/architecture.md`'s dated figures**, the 1,156-test count, 7.48 s, 105,607 steps and the
  Firefox run's known failures, were not measured again.

#### λ EXPAND ALL: THE λ VIEW'S `⋯` DISPLAY MENU HAS *expand all*, A CHECKBOX BEFORE *reset folds* THAT TURNS ON A MODE IN WHICH EVERY SUBTERM BUT A NUMERAL OR BOOLEAN CHIP OPENS, WHAT A LATER STEP BUILDS OPENS TOO, AND THE MODE HOLDS THROUGH STEPS, JUMPS, REBUILDS AND REBINDS; A CLICK STILL FOLDS ONE NODE, AND *reset folds*, OR THE ITEM AGAIN, TURNS IT OFF; THE FOLDS LOOK UP NO PATH WHILE NONE IS MADE BY HAND, SO A STEP UNDER THE MODE ON A DEEP TERM NO LONGER PAYS THE SUM OF ITS NODES' DEPTHS (2026-11-16, branch `lambda-expand-all`, `1d40a4e..42a0436`, 9 commits, plus three docs commits: this entry, then the fact-check's corrections to it and the design, then a last touch-up to this entry)

The user, 2026-11-06: an "expand all" control for the λ view, where a subterm over `AUTO_FOLD_NODES`, 200 nodes,
starts folded unless the next redex is inside it, and the only bulk action on folds was *reset folds*. The design is
`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-16-lambda-expand-all-design.md`: the decisions, each call with its reason, and the
cost figures. The lane's record is `~/temp/redextape-lambda-expand-all-record/`, `$R` below: `brief.md` holds the
decisions as the controller passed them on, `progress.md` the work, `review-1.md` the review, and the logs named
below sit beside them.

##### DECISIONS

The user's, 2026-11-16:

- **It lives in the λ view's `⋯` display menu, next to *reset folds*.** No new header button.
- **It is a mode, not a one-time action:** everything opens and stays open as the run steps, including the
  subterms a step creates. A click on a node still folds that node, and *reset folds* turns the mode off.

The controller's:

- **A chip, a Church numeral or boolean, stays closed under the mode**, since its value is its readable form; a
  click still opens one.
- **The item is a toggle:** choosing it again turns the mode off, as *reset folds* does.
- **The mode survives a jump, a rebuild after an edit (`setBuild`) and a rebind (`setBindings`)**, and the
  folds made by hand still clear where they cleared before. It is not saved to the workspace or a share link.

The implementer's, each with its reason in the design:

- **Turning the mode on clears the folds made by hand**, or a node folded before the choice would stay folded.
- **The item is a `button` with `role="checkbox"` and `aria-checked`, not a `menuitemcheckbox`:** the popover is
  not a `role="menu"`, which is why the display settings are `radio`s.
- **It is drawn checked with a checked choice's cue**, heavier and with the `--accent` bar at its leading edge,
  **and choosing it leaves the menu open**, as a setting's choice does; *reset folds* stays an action that closes
  it. It sits directly before *reset folds*.
- **A view made by a split starts with the mode off**, as it starts with no folds made by hand: folds are per view.

The fix round's:

- **The cost probe times each turn-on on a new `Tree`**, the first turn-on a user meets on a step. It had toggled
  on one `Tree`, so every turn-on sample but the first reused the paths the first had built.
- **`Folds.isOpen` looks up no path while there is no fold made by hand**, below.

##### WHAT CHANGED

- **`Folds` holds the mode, `480561c`.** In `web/src/lambda-folds.ts`, a node's default under the mode is open
  unless it is a chip, in place of `autoOpen`. The overrides sit on top of either default, so a click folds one
  node under the mode as it opens one without it, and `advance` needs no change: a step drops the overrides under
  its contractum, and what it built takes the default. `reset` turns the mode off and clears the overrides;
  `newTerm` clears the overrides alone.
- **The menu item, `43d436e`.** `DisplayMenu.expandAll` and its item in `viewMenu`, `web/src/view-header.ts`,
  wired in `web/src/lambda-pane.ts`, whose `setBuild` and `setBindings` call `newTerm` in place of `reset`; the
  checked cue in `web/src/style.css`.
- **The cost probe, `d26698a`, and `6c3e1b1`.** `pnpm test:probe:lambda-expand-all`,
  `web/tests/browser/lambda-expand-all-cost.test.ts`, kept out of the default run by `vite.config.ts`'s
  `PROBE_FILES`. It finds the largest term an example's recorded λ history draws as a tree, sum-to's at step 460,
  17,831 nodes, builds three terms of 19,999 nodes, seeded random, an `f x … x` spine and an `a (a (… z))` chain,
  and times turning the mode on and a step with it off and on. The design's cost table holds the figures; none is
  over the brief's ~100 ms, past which a cap or a fallback would have been the user's call.
- **No path without an override, `42a0436`.** `isOpen` looked up a path for every node it was asked about. Under
  the mode the layout asks about every node of each step's new `Tree`, whose path cache is empty, and a path is as
  long as its node is deep, so on the chain a step paid the sum of those nodes' depths. On the chain, in the
  probe's first run before and after, the turn-on fell from 15.2 / 25.9 ms, median / max, to 2.9 / 3.2 ms, and the
  step with the mode on from 35.1 / 43.6 ms to 2.3 / 2.6 ms; the design has both runs of each. One fold by hand
  brings the lookup back for every node the layout asks about.
- **Tests.** 8 node tests in `web/tests/node/lambda-folds.test.ts` under expand all, among them the fix round's,
  which spies on `Tree.key`. 3 browser tests in `web/tests/browser/lambda-display.test.ts` drive the real menu with
  `userEvent`: the mode opens what the policy folds and what a step builds, a click folds one node, and *reset
  folds* turns it off; Tab reaches the item and Space toggles it; the mode outlives a new build and a new binding.
  The file's Tab order gains the item.

##### WHAT THE REVIEW CAUGHT

`$R/review-1.md`: 0 Critical, 0 Important, 4 Minor, all four fixed.

- **M1, a path looked up for every node with no override to match**: `42a0436`, above. Before the fix the new
  node test saw `Tree.key` called 407 times on its term.
- **M2, the design's turn-on median was a warm figure, and the design did not say the term map was closed**:
  `6c3e1b1`.
- **M3, two `console.error` lines left in the expand-all browser test**, printing values the next lines assert:
  `3169b8f`.
- **M4, `viewMenu`'s doc named one exception to "every item closes the menu", and expand all is a second**:
  `4842c06`.

##### WHAT THIS DID NOT CLOSE

- **`share-positions.test.ts`'s *reaches fact(4)'s λ step 3,000 after two continues* races on `main`.** The lane's
  full browser run before review failed it, `the run: expected 3 to be 2`, its one failure of 1,745 tests.
  `resultsReach` waits until the count of `result`s reaches `n`, then asserts it equals `n`; the count advances by
  itself, since each continue's `result` posts the next, so under load a continue that lands inside one of
  `until`'s 20 ms polls overshoots the `===`. The branch touches nothing on that path, and expand all is off until
  a user turns it on. Run alone, the file passed 17 of 17 tests in each of seven runs: three by the lane, two by the
  review and two at `42a0436`. A sibling race in the same file was closed by holding `result`s back
  (`holdingResults`); this one needs a fix on `main`.
- **A view made by a split starts with expand all off**, the implementer's call; the user has not been asked.
- **The term map's cost under the mode has no committed probe.** The review measured it with the probe edited to
  open the map, `$R/review-probe-minimap.log`, and the design quotes it.
- **Where the view scrolls when the mode adds lines above it** is what *reset folds* does on `main`, by the
  review's reading of `LambdaBody`'s paint; it was not changed.
