#### THE VIEW SWITCHER'S TOGGLES ARE FOUR BORDERED BUTTONS APART: A PRESSED ONE EDGED AND UNDERLINED IN THE ACCENT, ONE THAT IS NOT EDGED IN THE RULE WITH DIM TEXT, EVERY CORNER AT THE STYLE'S `--radius`; IN FORCED COLOURS ONE THAT IS NOT PRESSED IS DASHED AND A PRESSED ONE EDGED IN `Highlight` (2026-11-16, branch `view-switcher-style`, `f6666e9..38b6fb0`, 8 commits, plus four docs commits)

The user, 2026-11-14 and 2026-11-16: the header's `views` toggles, `source`, `rxm`, `λ` and `TM`,
should look like the bordered buttons of his palette mockups, because in the joined strip `main`
drew the pressed state was hard to see. The design he approved, and the controller's and the
implementer's calls, are in `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-16-view-switcher-style-design.md`. The
lane's record is `~/temp/redextape-view-switcher-style-record/`, `$R` below: `brief.md`,
`progress.md`, `review-1.md`, and the logs this entry names.

##### DECISIONS

The user's, 2026-11-16:

- **Four separate buttons, a `--space-*` gap apart, every corner rounded**, with no joined edges and
  no negative margin. Not pressed: a solid `--rule` border, `--fg-dim` text and no background.
  Pressed: an `--accent` border, a 2px accent underline drawn inside by an inset shadow, and `--fg`
  text, the panel radios' cue but at normal weight, so that a press does not widen the bar.
- **Only the toggle-specific rules change.** The base rule every header button shares, and
  `index.html`, stay; so do the focus ring, the hiding at 40rem and below, and the last pressed
  toggle that cannot be turned off.
- **The toggles' inline padding is `0.2em`, down from `0.3em`.** As first built, in `f480ae5`, the
  header took two rows at 1280px in Instrument's Debugger preset, which `inspector-phone.test.ts`
  caught. The controller put three options to him: the narrower padding, which it recommended,
  accepting the second row, or 2px gaps. He chose the padding.

The controller's:

- **The corners take the style's `--radius`**, 2px in Instrument, 5px in Paper and 3px in Terminal,
  and not the brief's 3px, so that the toggles match the header's other buttons in every style.
- **The rule that draws the focused toggle over its neighbours stays**, held by a case at a 12px
  root, where the gap of `--space-1`, a quarter of a rem, is 3px and the ring reaches 4px.
- **After review, in forced colours only, one that is not pressed is dashed and a pressed one solid
  in `Highlight`**: `main`'s solid/dashed cue, brought back for that mode alone, with a case that
  fails without the rule. The look everywhere else stays as the user ruled. The review's four minor
  findings were fixed as it proposed them (below).

The implementer's, in the design doc's "My calls":

- **The pressed state has no background.** `main`'s `--bg-raised` fill went: the mockup has none,
  and neither do the panel radios.
- **The gap is `--space-1`**, the smallest spacing token, as far as the ring reaches outside a
  button at a 16px root.
- **No new contrast floor.** `accent` on `bg-chrome`, the header's surface, is already held at 3:1
  for every built-in palette, and `--rule` stays the faint edge it is elsewhere.

##### WHAT CHANGED

- **`web/src/style.css`.** The `.views-shown` and `.view-toggle` rules draw the look above. The
  corner rules for the first and last toggle, the negative margin, the dashed border, the raised
  fill and the pressed toggle's `position: relative` are gone. A `@media (forced-colors: active)`
  rule draws one that is not pressed dashed and a pressed one in `Highlight`. The focus rule's
  comment gives its reason now that the toggles are apart.
- **`first-load-views.test.ts`** asserts the look: each side's style and colour against the resolved
  `--accent` and `--rule`, the inset underline, a gap between neighbours, and, under forced colours
  emulated through CDP (Chromium only, as the step buttons' case is), solid `Highlight` against
  dashed. Its last case now asserts that the load left the focus on `<body>`.
- **`view-toggle-focus-ring.test.ts`** reads every toggle's ring at a 16px root in every style, with
  its top on the ring's pixel row nearest the button; reads both of the ring's pixel columns beside
  each neighbour at a 12px root; and holds every toggle's four corners to `--radius` in every style.
- **The harness has `token(name, property, where)`**, the probe that resolves a token or a system
  colour, in place of the copies `focus.test.ts`, `term-map.test.ts` and `first-load-views.test.ts`
  each had.
- **The view layouts spec's §6** describes the new look and points at the design doc. §6.1's widths,
  measured on the joined buttons, stay as written, with a pointer.

**What it costs the header.** The four toggles are 3.0px wider in all in each style than on
`f6666e9`: 152.6px in Instrument, 149.0 in Paper and 152.1 in Terminal. With the widest workspace
label, `Debugger`, and the appearance button at its default, `system`, the header keeps one row with
8.9px to spare at 1280px in Instrument and 22.2px in Paper, and in Terminal 22.9px at 1280px, at its
half gap, and 15.9px at 1361px, at its full gap.

##### WHAT THE REVIEW CAUGHT

`review-1.md` found no Critical, 1 Important and 4 Minor findings, all fixed in this branch:

- **I1, forced colours.** Forced colours put a system colour in place of each of the page's and draw
  no shadow, so the accent edge, the dim text and the underline all went and the four toggles looked
  alike. `4acbc0c` adds the media rule; without it the new case reads all four `solid` in the edge
  forced colours give a header button.
- **M1, the ring's top.** To keep clear of Paper's 5px corners on `λ`, the ring check had narrowed
  every side's sample and dropped the top's floor to more than 2 pixels. `846a588` reads the top on
  the ring's inner pixel row, where a round corner's curve stays in the ring further along the side,
  which restores the middle half and the floor of more than 5. A red bar over the ring's top in Paper
  fails it, `λ`'s top `0 of 7` where `7 of 7` was expected.
- **M2, the first-load page.** The every-style corner case chose a style in the first-load file,
  which left the focus on `settings` and a style stored, so the last case's "a load takes no
  keyboard focus" was false. `7953ded` moves the case to the focus-ring file, and the last case now
  asserts it; with the corner case still in the file, that assertion fails.
- **M3.** The view layouts spec's §6 still described the joined strip; `38b6fb0`.
- **M4.** A third local copy of the token probe; `b2d7975` makes it one harness helper.

##### WHAT THIS DID NOT CLOSE

- **`--rule` has no contrast floor on `--bg-chrome`**, so the edge of a toggle that is not pressed is
  as faint as the user ruled it: the review put it at about 1.3:1 in Material dark, and a base16
  scheme whose rule equals its chrome would leave `rxm` and `λ` no edge at all. They are still found
  by their words.
- **Forced colours in Firefox were not checked.** The new case emulates them through CDP, so it runs
  in Chromium alone.
- **The header's room at 1280px in Instrument with `Debugger` is 8.9px**: anything that widens the
  header by more takes a second row there, which `inspector-phone.test.ts` would catch.
- **The gap is in rem and the ring in px**, so under a root smaller than 16px the ring lies over the
  neighbour's edge and the focus rule's `z-index` keeps it whole. A gap of
  `max(var(--space-1), 4px)`, which would not need that rule, was the review's alternative; it was
  not taken.
- **The view layouts spec calls the rxm view `asm`**, in §6's list of the toggles among other
  places: the name it had when the spec was written. Seen while §6 was edited, and left as it was.

#### TM ANSWERS THAT WERE WRONG: A BINARY CALL'S RETURN TAG THAT DOES NOT FIT THE FIELD WIDTH GOES TO THE OVERFLOW GUARD INSTEAD OF RESUMING AFTER ANOTHER CALL SITE, A TM RUN CONTINUED PAST ITS CAP INTO `overflow` REPORTS A FAULT NAMING ITS WIDTH INSTEAD OF A VALUE, EVERY OVERFLOW MESSAGE SAYS A NUMBER THE MACHINE STORES (A VALUE, AN ADDRESS OR A CALL'S RETURN TAG) OUTGREW ITS FIELD, AND A TM OR rxm RUN A RAISED CAP CARRIES FURTHER REPORTS HOW FAR IT HAS GONE, NOT THE CAP (2026-11-16, branch `tm-return-tag`, `649fd0f..b01ba64`, 15 commits, the code ending at `31be292` but for a test's comment in `c644009`, and this entry's earlier versions, `479b45e`, `09641ed` and `b01ba64`, among them, plus this update of the entry)

Two wrong TM values and one wrong length, found on 2026-11-16. The lane's record is
`~/temp/redextape-tm-return-tag-record/`, `$R` below: `brief.md` holds the two wrong values and the
user's rulings on them, and its ADDENDUM 2 the user's ruling on the steps row and the controller's
calls; `progress.md` holds the work, `review-1.md` the review, and the logs the runs this entry
quotes. The controller's ledger, `~/temp/redextape-ui-lanes-ledger.md`, records the user's ruling
that the return-tag fix ship as its own PR first.
The design doc is `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-16-tm-return-tag-design.md`, which holds the
enumerations in full.

##### WHAT CHANGED AND WHY

- **A binary return tag that does not fit.** Under binary auto-fit, `fn f(x) { x } let c = 1; if c
  == 0 { f(0) + …sixteen calls… + 7 } else { f(3) }` answered `10` where the reference answers `3`,
  with no overflow. The `else` call is call site 16; `Binary::push_frame` wrote its return tag cut to
  four bits, as 0, and `dispatch_tag` resumed after call site 0. `push_frame` now sends a tag that
  does not fit to the overflow guard, as `write_literal` does a literal, so auto-fit widens (to 8)
  and a pinned width 4 halts in `overflow`; `dispatch_tag` compares only call sites whose ordinal
  fits, so a cut ordinal can never shadow a real tag. Unary is not affected: its tags are unbounded
  mark runs. The design doc enumerates every number derived from the program's structure, in both
  encodings, and found no other.
- **A continued run that halts in `overflow`.** Auto-fit keeps the narrowest width whose attempt did
  not overflow, and an attempt the step cap stopped has not overflowed yet. In the web app a raised
  cap then carried the cursor into the guard, and `tm_value` decoded its cut fields: binary `let a =
  9; let b = 9; a + b` under a ten-step cap answered `0`, and with the real 5,000,000-step cap `fn
  g(n) { if n == 0 { 1 } else { g(n - 1) * g(n - 1) } } g(13) + 20` answered `1` where the answer is
  21. `tm_value` now answers a fault that names the width and, below 64 cells, points at a wider
  one; at 64, the widest, it names the encoding's limit instead.
- **The overflow words (review findings M2 and M3).** The fault said "a value outgrew", but a
  return tag can be what outgrew; and a copy of the session's machine said "this is the encoding's
  limit" at every width, false below 64. Checking the class found a third kind: every value of
  `head(tail([0, …twenty zeros]))` is 0, yet `emit --field-width 4` refused it with "a value does not
  fit" (twenty cells need a five-bit address), and seventy zeros under unary were refused at the
  64-cell ceiling the same way. One phrase, `tm::OVERFLOWING_NUMBER`, "a number the machine stores (a
  value, an address or a call's return tag)", is now in every overflow message: the web app's fault
  and decline reason, `redextape run`'s two and `redextape emit`'s refusal. `overflowed_at(width,
  from)` is the one place the web app words the fault, for the session's leg and every copy, and
  below 64 both say "it needs a field wider than N cells".
- **A continued run's length.** After a raised cap carried a TM run to a halt, the `steps` row (the
  strip and the inspector) showed the cap, 5,000,000 under the default caps, as the run's length,
  because `TmStatus::total_steps` was always `compile`'s count; after a continue that stopped at a
  cap again it said `stopped after <compile's count> at a cap`, a stop the cursor had gone past. The
  rxm row did both. While `compile`'s run was capped, each leg's `total_steps` is now the larger of
  `compile`'s count and the cursor's: at a halt or a fault the run's length, beside the value read
  off the cursor, and at a later cap where that cap stopped the run. A rewind puts it back to
  `compile`'s count with the value.
- **The review's other findings:** `Builder::overflow`'s doc names the return tag among what reaches
  it (M1); `tm_value`'s doc names the fault (M4); `stack_push_literal` and `branch_on_equals` state
  that their constant must fit and `debug_assert!` it, with two unit tests compiled only with debug
  assertions, since a release build drops a `debug_assert!`: `check-slow.sh --all` runs the whole
  suite in release, though by default, and in CI, the script runs only the `#[ignore]` slow tier
  (M5).

##### DECISIONS

The user's, all on 2026-11-16:

- **The return-tag fix ships as its own PR first, and a tag that does not fit goes to the overflow
  guard**, the way a literal does, rather than any other repair.
- **The continued-overflow fix is in this PR, and its behaviour is "say it overflowed"**: a TM that
  halts in `overflow` never reports a value; its status names its width and points at a wider one,
  with no automatic re-fit or re-run.
- **The steps row's cap is fixed here too.**

The controller's:

- **The rxm leg's twin of the steps row is fixed with it**, as the same mistake, and so is a
  continue that stops at a cap again, which this entry's first version listed as not closed. The
  controller's dispatch asked for the steps-row fix test-first, and for every other place a run's
  length is shown, λ included, to be checked.
- **Review 1's findings are all fixed**, M2's and M3's overflow words among them; the words
  themselves are the implementer's.

The implementer's:

- **`dispatch_tag` trims `exits` to the fitting prefix before the chain**, so its defensive last
  exit is a site a frame can name.
- **The overflow travels as the value's `Fault`**, the shape a `.tm` buffer already used, not as a
  new `TmStatus` field; the rows already show the width beside it.
- **The words for M2 and M3**: one phrase that names addresses as well as return tags, from the
  probes above, as one constant in core that the CLI and the web app share; and one function,
  `overflowed_at`, that words the session's fault and a copy's alike. Help text that describes what
  binary holds ("a far larger value") or what auto-fit does ("until the values fit") is unchanged.
- **The length is how far the run has gone**: while `compile`'s run was capped, the larger of its
  count and the cursor's, so at an end the length is the one beside the value read off the cursor,
  and the figure never falls back to `compile`'s while the cursor is past it, after a second
  `[continue]` for instance.
- **`tm_value`'s doc was shortened to make room** for the fault's paragraph, since the comment
  guard does not let an over-cap block grow. The measurements it quoted were dropped, and so was its
  paragraph on the two producers of `HitCap` (the step budget and the live-cell budget, which no
  test can tell apart); `results.ts`'s TM comment, beside the count it is about, still makes that
  point.

##### WHAT THIS DID NOT CLOSE

- **The narrow-window strip cuts the width part of the overflow message** (review 1, extra item 3).
  `.results .segment` is `nowrap` with an ellipsis and the full text in its `title`, so a narrow
  window loses " · width 4" and then "wider than 4 cells"; the inspector wraps and shows all of it.
  The new phrase makes the fault longer, so the strip cuts it sooner.
- **The fault says "this run was fitted to"**, true while the width is always auto-fitted. The
  `tm-width` lane, stacked on this branch, adds a pinned width and a third wording to
  `overflowed_at`; whichever lands second keeps the words true.
- **The pointer to a wider width is words only**: `main` has no width control (the `tm-width` lane's
  job), and nothing re-fits a continued run.
- **`TmStatus` carries no overflow**: `run` reads `Ended` beside the fault, and only the value says
  why.
- **A recording stopped on its history budget past `compile`'s count still reads "stopped after N
  at a cap"** in the TM and rxm `steps` rows (found by reading): N is now how far the run has gone,
  but no cap stopped it there, and the rows cannot tell that stop from a cap's without a web change.
- **A corrupted binary STACK with a tag no site compares falls through to the last fitting site**,
  as on `main` (review 1, extra item 1); no lowered program can produce one.

#### A RECOMPILE SWAPS EVERY VIEW TO THE NEW PROGRAM'S STEP 0 IN ONE FRAME: THE BUILD REPLY CARRIES EACH VIEW'S STEP-0 PICTURE AND THE λ TERM'S STEP-0 TREE, FOR THE PROGRAM AND FOR A COPY, SO NO FRAME BETWEEN THE OLD PROGRAM AND THE NEW ONE SHOWS AN EMPTIED PANEL, THE λ TERM AS FLAT TEXT OR `not run`, AND A HEADERED TM COPY'S VALUE LINE KEEPS ITS ROOM UNTIL ITS VALUE RUN REPORTS (2026-11-17, branch `recompile-flash`, `486df8d..9d9796f`, 15 commits, then this entry, `fd41186`, then `808c11e`, which corrects two code comments, then `1e6c0c4`, `33a4f97` and the commit after them, which correct this entry and the design: 20 commits in all)

The user, 2026-11-17: "after the program recompiles, there's a bit of a flash as the panels are
rebuilt, can we eliminate that?" He saw it on the `notice-float` branch; the lane reproduced it on
`main` at `486df8d`. The design he chose, and the controller's and the implementer's calls, are in
`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-17-recompile-flash-design.md`. The lane's record is
`~/temp/redextape-recompile-flash-record/`, `$R` below: `brief.md` (his words, his decision and the
controller's calls, in three addenda), `progress.md`, `review-1.md`, the frame captures in `frames/`
and `shots/`, and the logs this entry names.

##### WHAT CHANGED AND WHY

- **The cause.** At each recompile the lane captured on `main` (a typed edit, an example, the
  encoding, an example's undo and a shared link's open in the Explorer preset; a typed edit and an
  example in Debugger) the page painted at least one frame of emptied views. `replies.ts`'s
  `compiled` arm emptied every leg's ring (`sessions.ts`'s `resetLegs`) and drew at once: the TM
  view lost its status line and tape rows, so its rules panel and state diagram moved up; the rxm
  registers, call stack and heap emptied; in Explorer the rxm and TM step lines read `not run` (at
  the encoding change the λ one too, and at a shared link's open TM's, the only one shown), and
  Debugger's one step line never did. Each leg waited for its first `frames` chunk, TM's behind the
  λ and rxm legs' whole first recordings, and the λ view drew the term as flat text until its
  `lambda-tree` reply.
- **`compiled` carries every leg's step-0 frame and the λ term's step-0 tree** (`first`,
  `lambdaTree`), and the worker records each leg from step 1 (`record-loop.ts`'s `recordBuild`). The
  page resets the legs, puts each step 0 in its ring and the tree in `LambdaTrees` under the new
  generation, and draws once.
- **A copy's build reply does the same for its leg**: `scratch-compiled`, `tm-scratch-compiled` and
  `rxm-scratch-compiled` carry `first`, the λ one `lambdaTree` too, and `copy-build.ts` records from
  step 1, so an edit in a copy's editor swaps the copy's view in one frame.
- **A leg whose recording waits behind another's** reads `step 0 of 0…` from `compiled`, where it
  read `not run`, and ⏭ is off until its first chunk.
- **↺ on a view still waiting for its first chunk leaves it on step 0** (`History.toStart`), where
  `seek(0)` on a ring of one frame followed the recording to its newest step.
- **A shared link's step line leaves the link's tail off while its leg holds only the build's step
  0**, so the waiting line is no longer than the line it turns into and wraps no header; a link's
  position of step 0 is spent at `compiled`.
- **A headered TM copy's value line keeps one line's room while its value run has not reported**
  (`TmPane`'s `has-value-run`, `min-height: 1lh`). The run's first `tm-value` comes after the copy's
  whole first recording, and until then the empty line took no room, so the rules panel stood one
  line higher.
- No Rust changed.

##### DECISIONS

The user's, 2026-11-17: of three options the controller put to him (swap in one frame; the same,
with the old content dimmed while an edit waits; hold every view until all are ready), the first,
"Swap in one frame". The option's description is the controller's text: "The worker sends each
view's step-0 picture together with 'compiled', and the page switches every view to the new program
in a single frame. No blank frame and no jump."

The controller's, in `brief.md`'s second and third addenda:

- **Copies are in scope** (review 1's I3): "The user asked for the flash after a recompile to go,
  and a copy's edit is a recompile."
- **↺ on a waiting view leaves it on step 0, not following** (I1), as a press of ↺ does anywhere
  else.
- **A TM copy's value line keeps its room while it waits, its settled height, empty**, with no new
  wording: the smallest visible change. The controller applied here what the user said of the page's
  banners on 2026-11-17: "I don't want anything like this that shifts the page unexpectedly".

The implementer's, in the design doc's "Calls made in the build" and the two sections after it:

- **The pictures ride `compiled` itself**, not replies after it: each message from a worker is its
  own task, and a browser may paint between two tasks.
- **λ's tree is sent whether or not a λ view is open**: an open λ view asks for it at once, and it is
  bounded by `LAMBDA_TREE_NODES`.
- **The link's tail goes while the leg waits** (I2), rather than the header reserving the room,
  which would change every view's header at every step.
- **The value line's room follows the build, not the reading**: a pane showing a copy whose status
  says `header` (which is when the build makes a value run) keeps one line's room, reading or not.
  Keeping the previous reading's exact height would need a layout read in the reply's draw and would
  still move the panel whenever the new value's line count differs.

##### WHAT THE REVIEW CAUGHT

Review 1 (`$R/review-1.md`), on `d4d0615`: 3 Important and 3 Minor findings, all fixed. I1, ↺ on a
waiting view jumped to the newest step. I2, in Firefox a shared link with every view past step 0
wrapped the TM header while λ and rxm recorded, moving the rules panel from 230 to 261 px and back.
I3, an edit in a copy's editor still flashed. M1, `test:probe:record`'s pins: its tally now counts
the step 0 a build reply carries, and the pins are unchanged. M2, three stale docs; M3, an orphaned
doc comment. The fix round left a TM copy's value line moving its rules panel from 487 to 459 px and
back, which the controller ruled on (above).

##### WHAT THIS DID NOT CLOSE

- **↺ on a view whose step 0 was dropped (`rewindLeg`) still empties the leg's ring** until the
  rewound recording's first chunk: a designed wait (hidden-recording spec §6), held by
  `restart-rewind.test.ts`, left for the user to decide.
- **A view's header that wraps as its step line grows can still move the view's body once**, the
  open TM header-wrap item; a link position past the first chunk shows the link's tail from that
  chunk on, as on `main`.
- **A TM copy's value that wraps onto more than one line** still grows the line by the extra lines
  when it arrives; the room kept is one line's.
- **From the keystroke to the new build, every view shows the old run at its old step, undimmed**,
  and the strip and readout keep the old run's values, dimmed, until the new `result`, both as on
  `main`: the option that dims the old content was not the one chosen.

#### NOTICES FLOAT OVER THE HEADER AND MOVE NOTHING: A NOTICE AND THE RESTING SENTENCE SIT IN THE HEADER'S EMPTY RUN BEFORE `share` WHERE THEY FIT, AND AT THE HEADER'S INLINE END ON `settings`'S ROW WHERE THEY DO NOT, THEIR WORDS PASSING A CLICK THROUGH TO THE CONTROL UNDER THEM; THE RESTING SENTENCE OFFERS `hide`, AND THE STRIP KEEPS ONE HEIGHT ACROSS A RUN (2026-11-17, branch `notice-float`, 16 commits: `846bb78..cf2bd2b`'s 12, then this entry, `1d4dffd`, two that correct it and the design doc, `14e2b34` and `debd976`, and the last, which updates its SHAs and figures for the rebase onto `846bb78`)

The user, 2026-11-17: "also the message that shows up for 'opened the example...' all these sort of
banner messages which shift the page should be removed. I don't want anything like this that shifts
the page unexpectedly". The notice line (Plan 7 part 2 spec §11) sat in the page's flow under the
header, so a notice pushed everything below it down a line and its end pulled it back; the resting
sentence (*… not being saved*) did the same. The decisions, round by round, and every call with who
made it are in `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-17-notice-float-design.md`; spec §11 points there. The
lane's record is `~/temp/redextape-notice-float-record/`, `$R` below: `brief.md` with its five
addenda, (2) to (6), `progress.md`, `review-1.md`, `review-2.md` and the logs this entry names.

##### DECISIONS

The user's, 2026-11-17, in four rounds:

- **Float them**, over removing the notices (and the four undos) or keeping an empty line under the
  header: first drawn at the window's bottom inline-end corner.
- **Above the bottom bars, with words a click passes through**, after the first build covered the
  step bar's controls at phone widths. The placement went in the next round; the click-through
  words stayed. The sweep of everything else that moves the page waits for a separate, measured PR.
- **At the top, as an overlay, in an empty spot to the left of `share`**: "if it needs to draw over
  on small screens it can".
- **"Over the right buttons"** where it does not fit that spot: review 2 found that at 1280 px the
  example's notice covered `examples ▾` and the encoding select, and a press on the select's arrow
  ran its undo. A notice wider than the run now ends at the header's inline end and covers `share`,
  the appearance button, `about` and `settings`, its undo over `settings`.

The user's verdict on the top placement, after trying its build at `6d43f88` and before the fourth
round (the controller's record of when): "banners looks good".

The controller's:

- **Drawn as the app's menus and popovers are**, by their tokens, above the panes and below modal
  dialogs (the brief).
- **The resting sentence floats where a notice does, and gets a `hide`** (review 1) that keeps it off
  until the condition says something else, since it can last a whole session.
- **The notice stays at the top when it does not fit** rather than dropping over the views, no wider
  than the window less a 16 px gutter, wrapping down; where `share` begins a row of its own (bands of
  widths within 850-964 px, and 354-402 px on the Stage), it follows the run.
- **Review 2's I1 and M1**: an undo pressed over the resting sentence leaves the focus on its own
  fallback, not on `hide`, which ignores a double-click's second click; Tab reaches the action where
  it is drawn.
- **The strip's link-sentence line is fixed here**: it grew the strip 3.3 px mid-run and moved the
  workspace above it.
- **After the fourth round's build**: a notice too wide for the run ends on the row of the header's
  last control, `settings`, wherever that row is, since at 414 px `share` ends its row and `settings`
  sits below it, and the undo lay over `share`; and a notice drawn in place of one whose action was
  just pressed takes clicks on its words for 500 ms, since a double-click on the example's undo ran
  it and its second click opened `settings` through the next notice's words.

The implementer's, each with its reason in the design doc: `floatInRun` places the notice from the
header's measured boxes, observing the header and every control in it for size and the notice only
for its words; "fits" is the notice's width against the run's, decided for new words and kept while
the same words' element is redrawn (Plan 7 part 6a spec §5.5's kept button); it is `position: fixed`
at `z-index: 10`, the view keys' hint's, which the top layer's menus and dialogs paint over, with the
menus' `1px solid var(--rule)` and `var(--bg)`, no radius and no shadow; its first line is
centred on its row with the action at that line's end; the notice element moves after `settings`
when it ends there so Tab reaches its action as drawn; and a caught press on the words moves no
focus.

##### WHAT CHANGED

- **`web/src/notice.ts`**: `floatInRun(line, run)`, called from `main.ts`, sets `--notice-end` and
  `--notice-row`; `createNotices` gains the resting sentence's `hide`, the press's catching
  (`SECOND_CLICK_MS`) and the focus rules above.
- **`web/index.html`** (and the test harness's `SHELL`): `#notice` moves into the header, after its
  `.bar-spacer`.
- **`web/src/style.css`**: `.notice` is fixed over the header, its words `pointer-events: none` and
  its action `auto`, `.notice-catching` while it catches; `.strip .link-status` sets
  `line-height: 1.2`.
- **Tests**: `notice-float.test.ts` is new (nothing moves when a notice or the resting sentence comes,
  changes or goes; the place at 1280, 414, 1600, 1920, 375, and in the bands; the header followed on
  resize and preset; `hide`; a notice with no action; the select's arrow at 1280; Tab order; real
  clicks on the undo and through the words; a double-click's second click; the strip's height across
  a run). `notice.test.ts` gains the focus and double-click cases; `inspector-phone`, `follow-kept`
  and `header-menus-narrow` were updated for the line leaving the page's flow, each with its reason
  in its commit message.

##### WHAT THE REVIEWS CAUGHT

- **Review 1** (`review-1.md`, at `1010ab1`): 0 Critical, 2 Important, 5 Minor. I1, the undo moving
  under a held press as the bars changed height, was made moot by the move to the top; I2 became the
  resting sentence's `hide`; the five minor findings were fixed.
- **Review 2** (`review-2.md`, at `6d43f88`): 0 Critical, 2 Important, 4 Minor, all fixed: I1 in
  `08aeeb6`, I2 by the user's fourth-round decision, M1 in `08aeeb6` and `e2e1fc8`, M2-M4 in
  `01be15b` and `08aeeb6`.

##### WHAT THIS DID NOT CLOSE

- **The sweep**, everything else the app shows or hides in the page's flow on its own (the readout's
  worker-error banner, the readout's segments mid-run, the step bar's `extend`, the TM status and value
  lines, the reattach buttons), is listed in the design doc's *Not closed here*, read from the code and
  not measured, for the follow-up PR the user chose.
- **`footer.strip` is drawn while `hidden`** (`display: flex`, no `[hidden]` rule), empty, in the
  debugger and stage presets; and **an open inspector can lengthen the page at a desktop
  width**: both measured by the lane, neither changed.
- **A notice redrawn with longer words keeps its place**, so a kept undo does not move under a press:
  such a redraw that no longer fits the run grows over the controls before it until the next notice or
  a change of the header.
- **Firefox's open list**: Firefox under the test driver reports no `:open` on the encoding select
  after a press at its arrow, so that check is Chromium's alone.
- **Firefox failures that are not this branch's**: 10 `inspector-phone.test.ts` cases (Chromium's
  boxes pinned against Firefox's font metrics), `controls-gate.test.ts`'s toggle walk, two
  `focus-scroll.test.ts` cases and `header-menus-narrow.test.ts`'s workspace-menu case fail in
  Firefox here and at `846bb78` alike, with one more `inspector-phone` case failing there.

#### THE STATE DIAGRAM'S LOCAL LEVEL CUTS A LONG NAME IN THE MIDDLE SO THE END, WHERE ONE LEVEL'S NAMES DIFFER, SHOWS, SETS EVERY LABEL CLEAR OF THE BOXES, LOOPS, LINES AND OTHER LABELS AND A FAN'S LABELS BY THEIR OWN LINES, WRITES ONE TAPE OF ONE RULE A LINE IN GAPS AS WIDE AS THEIR LABELS, CENTRES ITSELF IN ITS PANEL, KEEPS EVERY STATE IN A PANEL TOO SMALL FOR IT, MOVES WITH A MOUSE DRAG AT ANY SIZE, AS A MAP DOES, WHILE A STEP TO A NEW STATE CENTRES IT, AND ZOOMS WITH THE WHEEL (2026-11-16 and 2026-11-17, branch `state-diagram-tidy`, `7085aa2..d02504c`, 37 commits: 21 to `233e4ac`, four docs commits, `30b365f`, the crop and drag, `58c1f35`, its docs, `d6b7073`, the drag at any size, `ab26085`, its docs, `f7d5c59`, the zoom, `426730f`, its docs, `7a49354`, review 6's fixes, `bc68049`, their docs, `d8b9439`, two of their tests' waits, `eb4c819` and `f43f1e5`, docs that bring this entry to `d8b9439` and correct it after a fact-check, and `d02504c`, a fan's label along its row by its own line; then two docs commits that bring this entry to it, the second naming the new browser file among the tests, and one after a fourth fact-check that also narrows `MOST_APART`'s comment and a node test's name to a rule that moves, and one that gives the design doc's rise in a gap 0.75 px wider as its log has it, and one after a fifth fact-check that also cuts `MOST_APART`'s comment to its first sentence and renames a node test, and one that updates this entry for the rebase onto `7085aa2` and deletes a clause from the design doc; 43 commits in all)

##### DECISIONS

The user's, 2026-11-16:

- **Fix all four.** Cut a long name in the middle, not at its end, with each box sized to its measured
  name up to a cap and the full name kept in the node's `title`; set each self-loop's label clear of
  its loop; write one rule a line instead of a `, `-joined line, with the gap between two columns as
  wide as its longest label; and centre a diagram shorter than its panel vertically, still scrolling
  when it is taller and centring again when the panel's height changes.
- **One tape a line, and one rule each way where two do not fit.** With gaps sized to their labels,
  37.5% of the 24,428 local levels of the seven examples were wider than the 844 px panel and
  scrolled sideways. The user chose to write a rule that touches several tapes a tape a line
  (`REG:0 R` over `WORK:0/0 R`), and to draw a level still wider than its panel at two rules each way
  at one (±1 state), decided against the panel's real width and decided again when it changes. The
  second half is replaced by crop and drag, below.
- **A fan's labels by their own lines, in this PR.** After review 1's fixes, `is_even(6)` at step
  11,827 stood the four `*` labels of a fan into `bdt35.n0` in one column, and the three of a fan
  out of `bdt35.q1.e0` in another, so which line each belonged to was a guess. The user ruled that
  a sloping edge's label sit beside its own line. The implementer measures that as no other edge's
  drawn line nearer the label; the labels that miss it are under WHAT THIS DID NOT CLOSE.
- **Keep the scroll bar's room**, `scrollbar-gutter: stable`, the option the lane called A, rather
  than lay rows out at their natural width and only spread them sideways. Its cost: where scroll bars
  take width (Chrome on Linux and Windows), an 844 px panel lays its level out over 829 px, and more
  levels are wider than their panel. Overtaken by the drag at any size, below: the level draws no
  scroll bar, so there is no bar's room to keep.
- **A fallen-back level says so in a tooltip only**: the level's `title` reads `states within 1 rule
  each way: the panel is too narrow for 2`. Nothing is drawn; three columns in place of five are
  what a reader sees. Gone with the fallback.
- **Crop and drag** (2026-11-17, after trying the branch: "I can't freely drag the diagram around",
  and a narrower panel "just alters the diagram by combining states"). Chosen over shrinking to fit
  with drag and zoom, and over the fallback with drag added: a narrow panel cuts off the diagram's
  edges without changing what is in it; a drag on the background moves it any way, with an open and
  a closed hand as over the panel divider, and a click on a state still links it, since a drag starts
  only once the pointer has moved a few pixels; touch keeps its own scrolling; a step to a new state
  centres the diagram on it, and while the run stays on one state the dragged position stays put.
- **"I can't move it around at all"** (2026-11-17, after trying `d1e14a6`: "am I supposed to drag
  the state diagram? I can't move it around at all"). As built, a level its panel fits ignored
  presses, and at an ordinary width most levels fit. The controller's answer, that a drag always
  moves the diagram, is below. After trying it at `5c17348`: "dragging works".
- **The wheel zooms the diagram** (2026-11-17, asked about the wheel after review 5 found that in
  Firefox the wheel over a level moved it and no longer scrolled the TM view: "I think scrolling over
  the diagram should actually zoom it if possible").

The controller's:

- **The same reason in the level's group name**, its `aria-label`, which a screen reader says as the
  focus enters the level. Gone with the fallback.
- **Crop and drag's details** (2026-11-17): a drag starts past about 4 px; it pans both ways with the
  pointer captured; mouse only, so a pen and a finger keep native scrolling; the open hand only while
  the level is larger than its panel, the default pointer when there is nothing to pan; a press that
  panned neither links nor moves the roving focus; and the scroll bar's room stays unless a test
  shows the loop cannot occur. The open hand's condition and the scroll bar's room are replaced by
  the next.
- **A drag always moves the diagram, like a map** (2026-11-17, the answer to the user's "I can't
  move it around at all"): a drag moves the level both ways whatever its size,
  the open hand over the whole level; it cannot be lost, since it moves until any point of it reaches
  the panel's middle and no further, by half the panel's width and height of room on every side of
  the drawing in the level's own scroll, whose scroll bars are hidden; a new state centres it, and so
  does a resize, a font load or a skin change with no drag since the last centring (review 4's I1),
  while after a drag a redraw around the same state keeps the user's offset; a pen and a finger
  scroll natively, which the room now gives a level that fits too; and review 4's M1 and M2 fixed as
  no ring for a focus a pointer gives, and a click on the level's background taking the focus into
  the level, with no ring.
- **The zoom's design** (2026-11-17): the wheel over the level, and Ctrl with it, as a trackpad's
  pinch comes, zoom the drawing about the pointer, with no page zoom over the diagram and the TM view
  left unscrolled; about ×1.1 a notch, scaled by the delta; from where the whole level fits, or 50%
  if that is smaller, never below 5%, up to 300%, the drawing scaled rather than a bitmap; the zoom
  kept through steps and resizes, a new state centred at it; a double-click on the background, or
  `0` with the focus in the level, back to 100% and centred, `+` or `=` and `-` about the panel's
  middle; no indicator; a drag at any zoom with its clamp in zoomed terms; phones unchanged; review
  5's fixes as listed under WHAT THE REVIEW CAUGHT, with its I1 as its option (a) and its M1 as
  `tabIndex = -1` on the level.
- **Review 6's fixes** (2026-11-17, after the user tried the zoom: "yes zoom works well"): M1, `0`
  during a drag moving the drag's start as `#zoomAt` does; M2, the zoom keeping its scroll as a
  float of its own; M3, a press whose release never comes ended at `lostpointercapture`,
  `pointercancel` and the window's `blur`; M4, a double-click resetting only if neither of its
  presses moved past the drag's threshold; each test-first in both engines where it applies; M6 and
  M7 in the docs; and M5, the pinch's rate, left as it is with its figure recorded under WHAT THIS
  DID NOT CLOSE, since the user judged the zoom by feel.
- **Every review finding fixed**, six reviews, under WHAT THE REVIEW CAUGHT, but review 6's M5
  (above). For review 1's M3 and M4 the controller set the fix: text measured again when a web font loads or the style or palette
  changes, and two names whose cuts clash cut longer only until they differ, still capped where
  possible, rather than shown whole.
- **The implementer's last resort accepted** (review 3's M1): a label with no clear place near its
  line moves from whichever of its places it moves least from to be clear, not from its best place
  alone. The review's suggested fix on its own, weighing each label's best place past the cap, moved
  none of the labels it was aimed at.
- **The fan labels the sweep found, fixed in this PR** (2026-11-17, on the user's decision "fan
  labels: fix in this PR"): the ten `WORK:1 R` labels the sweep at `ca21e4e` found by the wrong line
  in `fact(12)`'s `bmul17.sN.up31` levels, which fell back to one rule until the crop and drag, by
  their own line at 844 and 829 px, test-first, with the sweep run again. The way, a higher
  `MOST_APART` rather than a wider gap, is the implementer's (`Where each label goes`, below).

The implementer's, each with its reason in the design doc's "My calls":

- **The cut.** A name over the cap keeps its first dotted segment, then `…`, then as many whole
  trailing segments as fit: `bpf31.l2.r1.rw2` shows as `bpf31…r1.rw2`. A name whose first and last
  segments do not fit is cut by characters, two thirds of them from its end. Clashing cuts (the
  controller's fix, above) grow by a character's room at a time, and only a pair that no cut tells
  apart is shown whole. The CSS ellipsis stays as a safety net.
- **The cap is 14 characters** of the node's font, the width of fourteen `0`s. Text is measured with
  canvas `measureText` in the node's computed font at the current node's weight. It is measured
  again (the controller's fix, above) on `document.fonts`' `loadingdone` and on a change to
  `data-style` or `style` on `<html>`, and the level is laid out again only if sample texts measure
  differently.
- **Columns size to what they hold, and the fixed 750 px floor goes.** A column is as wide as its
  widest box or self-loop label, in place of `floor(width / 5)`, and a gap, as wide as its widest
  label by the user's decision, keeps a margin either side of it. Spare width is shared by the gaps,
  so a level still spans its panel, and the width is rounded to the nearest pixel.
- **The rules of a stacked label stand 4 px apart** (`RULE_GAP`), and **different edges' labels at
  least 8 px** (`LABEL_GAP`).
- **Where each label goes.** A self-loop's label sits over its arc, right-aligned to its box, and
  moves right along the arc past a line up its column. A backward edge's sits under its curve, kept
  inside the drawing. A sloping edge's goes by the end where its line is apart from the others, on
  the side the line turns away from. A line along a row between a rising and a falling sibling has
  its row set apart from the rising one, by up to five node heights (`MOST_APART`, 120 px), and its
  label goes up against its target. A moving rule `<tape>:1 R` was measured for `REG`, `WORK`,
  `STACK`, `HEAP` and `BOX`, needing up to 109 px in a gap its width and two `LABEL_MARGIN` wide; a
  rule that writes, such as `STACK:0/1 R`, was not measured. Each label takes
  the cheapest of its places that is clear of the nodes, the arcs, the other lines and the labels
  placed before it, with its own line nearer than any other by `NEARER` (1 px), searching up to
  `SEARCH` (24 px) from each place. Failing that, it takes the clear place where it is least behind,
  and failing that, the last resort above, found in one pass (`firstClear`).
- **A level weighs at most `WEIGHED_PLACES` (2,000) places** beyond each label's best one.
- **A `browser-scrollbars` vitest project**: Chromium without Playwright's `--hide-scrollbars`, for the
  one test that needs classic scroll bars. `test:browser` runs it with `browser`.
- **Crop and drag's mechanics.** A press on a level that can pan has its default prevented, so it
  neither selects text nor moves the focus, and a click focuses its node itself; the pointer is
  captured when the drag passes the threshold, so the release's click goes to the level and a pan
  links nothing, while a plain click still reaches its node. The level is centred on a new state, and
  also when it is shown afresh (switched to, a recompile, its panel reopened), since a dragged
  position belongs to a view the user left. The fallback's reach parameter, `Local`'s `reach` and
  `fitLocal` go with it.
- **The drag at any size's mechanics.** The room is CSS: `.local-content`'s margins are `50cqh
  50cqw` of the level, a size container, so a resize leaves the drawing where it was against the
  panel's middle. A centring keeps the clamp it had, so a level its panel fits is shown whole rather
  than shifted to put its current state at the middle. A scroll since the last centring, by a drag,
  the wheel, a finger or a focus, is the user's move, and a redraw then keeps the current node's
  offset from the panel's middle. No `scrollbar-gutter`: beside hidden bars it keeps no room. A click
  on the background (review 4's M2) focuses the level's tab stop rather than its group, since the
  arrows move from a node; the empty outer columns' gaps are taken in first in a narrow panel; and an
  emptied level has no size left.
- **The zoom's mechanics.** A transform: `.local-drawing` holds the drawing at its laid-out size,
  scaled from its top left, and `.local-content` takes the scaled size, so the scroll's range is the
  drawing as shown and the drag's clamp holds at any zoom. A layout at the zoomed size would rearrange
  the drawing, and CSS `zoom` sets text at a scaled font size that a cut name can outgrow. A notch is
  100 px, 3 lines or a page of delta, ×1.1 each, continuously; a key press is one. A zoom already past
  an end, as a step or a resize can leave it, is kept and moved no further past it. `0` is the
  double-click's reset. A zoom counts as the user's move, as a drag does. An emptied level leaves the
  wheel to the view. While a mouse press is on the level, a draw that would lay it out or place it
  waits, and the release draws it a frame later, after the release's click. A `mouse` command in
  every browser project holds a press in Firefox too.
- **Review 6's mechanics**, on the controller's fixes above. A wider rule for M1, that a move
  finding the scroll changed by anything goes on from it, made three drag tests' drags end about
  330 px out in both engines and was dropped. The next zoom starts from the scroll the last asked for
  only while the level is within a pixel of it. A press also ends at a move with no left button held.
  The level keeps whether each of the last two presses panned (`#panned`). The `mouse` command takes
  the system's click count, which Playwright does not work out.

##### WHAT CHANGED

- **`web/src/local-level.ts`.** An edge carries its rules' labels as a list, each rule a list of its
  tapes' parts. What a screen reader is told of an edge is unchanged.
- **`web/src/local-layout.ts`**, new, pure and free of the DOM: the cut and the rule that keeps
  names apart, the layout (columns, gaps, rows, loops, lanes, every label's places and the search),
  and `firstClear`. A level wider than the width it is given keeps its own width, and one narrower
  takes in the gaps past its outermost occupied columns before it is wider than its panel.
- **`web/src/state-diagram.ts`.** The local level measures its text, lays out on each change of
  state or width, and draws a label's lines as `<tspan>`s. A mouse drag moves a drawn level at any
  size (`#panLocal`), `data-pans` marks one, and `#place` centres a new state, or a redraw around the
  same one that nothing has moved since, and keeps the user's offset after a move. Its resize
  observer watches the border box, and any change of size places the level again. One pair of font
  and style listeners serves the page. The wheel, Ctrl with it, a double-click and the keys zoom the
  level (`#zoomLocal`, `#zoomAt`, `#unzoom`, `#sizeLocal`); nothing moves it while a mouse press is
  on it; the level is no tab stop of its own (`tabIndex = -1`). A press ends without its release at a
  move with no button held, a lost capture or the window's blur; a zoom or `0` during a drag moves
  the drag's start with the level; a double-click after a drag leaves the zoom.
- **`web/src/style.css`.** `.local-level` is a flex column and a size container with no scroll bar
  (`scrollbar-width: none`), an open hand while it holds a drawing (`data-pans`) and a closed one
  while it moves (`data-dragging`). `.local-content`, the drawing's box at its zoom, has half the
  level's width and height of room on every side (`margin: 50cqh 50cqw`), and holds
  `.local-drawing`, the nodes and edges at their laid-out size, scaled from its top left.
- **`web/vite.config.ts` and `web/package.json`.** The `browser-scrollbars` project; its one file is
  left out of `browser` and of Firefox's project. `state-diagram-local-pan.test.ts` and
  `state-diagram-local-layout.test.ts` are in `CAPTURE_FILES`, since their drags hold a pointer
  capture. A `mouse` command in every browser project (typed in `tests/browser/engine.ts`), with
  a click count.
- **Tests.** New: `tests/node/local-layout.test.ts`, and `tests/browser/state-diagram-local-layout`,
  `state-diagram-local-fans`, `state-diagram-local-fan-row`, `state-diagram-local-scrollbars`,
  `state-diagram-font-listeners` and `state-diagram-local-pan` (each `.test.ts`). `tests/node/local-level.test.ts` pins the parts;
  `tests/browser/state-diagram-local.test.ts` finds nodes by their full names and holds the drawing
  to the level's width in place of the 750 px floor; `tests/browser/state-diagram-no-machine.test.ts`
  holds an emptied local level to nothing to scroll or drag.

In all, at `7a49354`, 18 files change against `7085aa2`, with 4,955 lines added and 127 removed
(`git diff --shortstat 7085aa2..7a49354`, which counts this entry and the design as `426730f` left
them).

##### WHAT THE REVIEW CAUGHT

Review 1, `$R/review-1.md`, at `58fe5f1`: no Critical, 2 Important and 7 Minor findings.

- **I1.** A level whose height depends on its width laid itself out again every frame as a classic
  vertical scroll bar came and went: 60 times a second at `is_even(6)` step 11,827 in a 1690 × 613
  window. Fixed by the gutter, by one width for both the fallback and the spread, by the border-box
  observer, and held by `state-diagram-local-scrollbars.test.ts` under real scroll bars.
- **I2.** The labels of different edges were nudged into one stack and read as one edge's: 819
  levels had two of them under 3 px apart. Fixed by `LABEL_GAP`, then by the user's decision on fans.
- **M1 to M7.** Labels of edges along an outer column cut off at the drawing's side; a label nudged
  onto another edge's line; no new measurement when a web font arrives or the style changes; names
  shown whole without a cap; two gaps in the tests; a fallback that hid no state saying the panel
  was too narrow; three comments holding history. All fixed.

Review 2, `$R/review-2.md`, at `3592f88`: no Critical, 2 Important and 3 Minor findings.

- **I1.** In `fact(12)`'s `bmul17.s31.up31`, the label of the flat edge `need → wr1` sat over the
  rising `need → wr0`, so a reader would predict the wrong next state. The row is set apart and the
  label goes up against its target. The sweep run again at `ca21e4e` found it back in ten `fact(12)`
  levels that the crop and drag brought to two rules, which `d02504c` fixes (DECISIONS).
- **I2.** A self-loop's label under a line up its column (`hs.dc.n` in `closure` and `map-fold`) was
  pushed past the next node onto that node's loop label. It now moves right along its arc, in a
  column widened for it.
- **M1**, the search's cost, per level about ten times what it was at `6b5c999`: each line is cut
  into points once, and the cap. **M2**, a scroll-bar test that saw a layout loop only indirectly:
  it now fails on any `ResizeObserver loop` error and checks that the width the level is laid out
  for is the same overflowing as fitting. **M3**, the font and style listeners added again once every diagram was
  collected: a module flag, and a test.

Review 3, `$R/review-3.md`, at `5605426`: no Critical, 1 Important and 2 Minor findings.

- **I1.** The last resort moved 2 px at a time and checked every box at each step, which took
  seconds a layout on a hand-written 30-way fan. `firstClear` finds the same place in one pass, and
  no level of the examples lays out differently.
- **M1.** The labels left when the cap ran out lost their place search. Each label's best place is
  now weighed past the cap, and the last resort tries every place. In `fact(12)`, the `*` label
  furthest from its own line in `pc20`'s level went from 617.5 px from it to 44.3, and the
  `overflow` level from 7,421 px tall to 6,522.
- **M2.** Ten levels a fraction of a pixel over 829 px fell back: the width is rounded, not ceiled.

Review 4, `$R/review-4.md`, at `d1e14a6`: no Critical, 1 Important and 5 Minor findings.

- **I1.** A panel narrowed with nothing dragged kept the scroll at (0, 0), so the current state
  went off screen at the right (`s` at x 220 to 239 of a 185 px view). A redraw around the same
  state now centres it again unless the level was moved since.
- **M1.** A click on a node of a level that could pan drew the keyboard's focus ring wherever the
  keyboard was last used. Focused with `focusVisible: false`.
- **M2.** A click on the background of such a level left the focus in the editor, so typing edited
  the program. It now focuses the level's tab stop, with no ring.
- **M3.** Three fallback sentences outside what the design marked historical. Reworded or marked.
- **M4.** A level with nothing two rules away spent 40 px on each empty outer column's gap, so it
  was wider than a panel its states fit. Those gaps are taken in first in a narrow panel.

  sized to nothing, and the open hand goes; the SVG's old size, which alone kept half a panel of
  scroll, was found by the new test.

- **M3.** Three failures in `pnpm test:firefox`, in two files this branch adds: two label tests

- **M4.** In a panel of a couple of hundred px, a backward edge's label wider than its columns hung
  past the drawing's left edge. The drawing is now never narrower than such a label and its margins.
- **M5.** The PR draft's review count, its scroll shares and its Firefox line had gone stale.

Review 6, `$R/review-6.md`, at `f26fe9c`, in Chromium and Firefox: no Critical, no Important and 7
Minor findings.

- **M1.** `0` during a held drag centred the level, and the next 2 px move set the scroll from the
  press's: the level jumped about 300 × 950 to 1,080 px. `0` now moves the drag's start with the
  level, as a zoom did.
- **M2.** A trackpad's run of small wheel events moved the point under the pointer: each zoom's
  scroll was rounded and the next started from the rounded one. In the new test, 60 events of −4 px,
  the old code moved it 11.4 px across in Chromium and 5.8 px down in Firefox. The zoom now starts
  from the scroll it asked for.
- **M3.** A press whose release the page never heard kept the level following a pointer with no
  button held, and every draw that waited for the press waited on. It now ends at a move with no
  button held, a lost capture or the window's blur.
- **M4.** Two drags from one spot, counted a double-click by the system, put the zoom back to full
  size. A double-click either of whose presses was a drag now leaves it.
- **M5.** The pinch's rate has a figure: ×1.07 for a pinch that doubles the fingers' spread, by
  Chromium's convention. Recorded, not changed (WHAT THIS DID NOT CLOSE).
- **M6.** At the drag's reach the clamp wins over the point under the pointer staying put, which the
  docs did not say. They do now.
- **M7.** The PR draft and the design said every zoom test failed first and was sabotaged in both
  engines, named the wrong logs for Firefox's passing run, and called the text sharp at any zoom
  from Chromium's 200% screenshots. Each now says what was checked.

##### WHAT THIS DID NOT CLOSE

- **Phones zoom the page, not the diagram.** One finger moves the diagram natively, and a pinch
  zooms the page, as before decision 12 (its point 5).
- **How far a real pinch or wheel notch zooms is not measured.** No trackpad or mouse was tried:
  the tests send Playwright's pixel deltas. A pinch comes as Ctrl and the wheel and zooms at the
  wheel's rate, ×1.1 for 100 px of delta. By Chromium's convention a pinch that scales the fingers'
  spread by `s` arrives with `deltaY = −100·ln(s)` (Chromium review 250923004, and its PDF viewer's
  `gesture_detector.ts`), so the level zooms by `s^0.095`: ×1.07 for a pinch that doubles the
  spread (review 6's M5, computed, not measured). If a pinch proves slow, a rate of its own for Ctrl
  would make Ctrl and a mouse's wheel jump instead (×2.7 for a 100 px Chromium notch), which is the
  user's choice.
- **Keys under a held drag** (review 6's M1 siblings, older than the zoom): an arrow key's focus, and
  Home, End, Page Up and Page Down, scroll the level while the mouse holds a drag, and the next move
  undoes them.
- **A lost capture in Firefox is untested.** Firefox fired no `lostpointercapture` for a capture the
  page released while the button was held, so the case runs in Chromium alone; a move with no button
  held is sent through CDP, Chromium's alone.
- **The panel moved up the page in Chromium** by 4.75 px during the test's run of 60 wheel
  events, which the zoom does not do; not looked into, and the test measures the point under the
  pointer from the panel.
- **Home, End, Page Up and Page Down on a focused node scroll the level** (review 5), as a scroller's
  keys; the arrows move between nodes.

- **Labels still nearer another edge's line**: 144 of 156,485 labels at 844 px, in 5 of the 24,428
  levels (143 at 829 px), as `51d3a73` lays them out. 103 of them (102 at 829 px) are in `overflow`
  levels, where up to 65 edges converge from rows far apart and cross every gap. There, 62 of the
  103 (61 of 102 at 829 px) sit nearer a line whose text differs from their own
  (`$R/fan/fix-mis3h-844.log` and `fix-mis3h-829.log`, `ovfDiff`). The 41 outside `overflow` sit
  nearest a line whose label has the same text, the `*` fans into `bdt25.n0` in `fact(12)`'s `pc20`
  and `bdt25.n0` levels, so they mislead no one. Outside `overflow`, none sits nearer a line whose
  label differs from its own. That 0 is asked of the levels outside `overflow` only, by the
  controller's ruling, 2026-11-17.
- **A big program's `overflow` level is tall.** `fact(12)`'s, 131 states, is 6,522 px tall at 844
  px, 2.25 times `main`'s 2,898 (`fact`'s, 1,752 px against 786), and takes about 0.13 s to lay
  out. Few of its labels have a clear place near their own lines, and hiding a label rather than
  moving it far is a question for the user, as review 3 put it. A hand-written 30-way fan with
  six-rule loops (review 3's probe) takes 159 to 185 ms a layout and draws 110,927 to 154,588 px
  tall.
- **The scroll-bar test's height change comes from where labels sit.** With no reach to turn, its
  level is taller at one spread than at a scroll bar's width less only because its labels' places
  change with the spread (324.3 px over 319 px, 322.4 px over 324 px, 309.2 px over 358 px in
  `$R/pan/scrollbars-2.log`), which other font metrics may move. With the level's scroll bars shown
  again and no gutter, the loop test passes and only the no-bar test fails
  (`$R/map/sab/s6-bars.log`): the border-box observer alone stops the loop.
- **Text selection by a drag is untested.** The nodes' layer lies over the labels, so a press never
  lands on a label's text; the press's prevented default is tested through the focus it no longer
  moves. A copy's nodes link nothing, so `state-diagram-local-pan.test.ts` tests a click by the tab
  stop and focus it takes, and `state-diagram-local-layout.test.ts` links a node in a 600 px panel.
- **The cap's accounting alone is untested.** Weighing a label's best place past `WEIGHED_PLACES`
  moves one label in the examples, in `map-fold`'s `overflow` level, by 4 px, and every node test
  passes without it.
- **A sabotage that does not fire.** A self-loop's label put back at `main`'s place, centred 30 px
  left of its box's right edge with its baseline 8 px above the box, passes every node test and the
  five local-level browser files: the place search lifts it clear of its arc. The tests hold the
  property, clear of its loop, not the place.
- **A fan's rows grow.** The row set apart under a rising line makes `fact`'s `bmul17.s7.up7` level
  159 px tall at 844 px instead of 122 (`fact(12)`'s `bmul17.s31.up31`, 131 instead of 130), and
  `fact(12)`'s ten levels `bmul17.s0.up31` to `bmul17.s9.up31` 184.0 px tall instead of 123.3, at 844
  and 829 px. Widening the gap instead would make those levels wider.
- **Wider than their panel**: 1,911 of the 24,428 levels (7.82%) at 844 px, as `ca21e4e` and
  `51d3a73` lay them out, the widest 902 px. Over 829 px, 4,576 (18.73%), but the level draws no scroll bar now, so an
  844 px panel lays it out over 844.
- **Only Chromium is tested with classic scroll bars.** Firefox's project leaves the scroll-bar file
  out, and Firefox's scroll bars were not checked.
- **A level wider than its panel shows part of itself**, which a drag, a pen or a finger moves and
  the wheel zooms out, and nothing drawn says there is more of it.

#### THE CLI'S GOLDEN TESTS RUN ON SNAPBOX, NOT TRYCMD: `tests/cli.rs` IS A SMALL HARNESS THAT READS THE SAME 41 `tests/cmd/*.toml` CASES AND CHECKS THEM AGAINST THE SAME GOLDENS, UNCHANGED, AND `Cargo.lock` LOSES `trycmd` AND, WITH IT, THE UNMAINTAINED `humantime` (RUSTSEC-2026-0542) THAT FAILED `main`'S ADVISORIES JOB (2026-11-17, branch `drop-trycmd`, `0230e6b..fe907ca`, 6 commits, the second this entry's first version and the fourth and fifth its updates for review 1 and for the rebase onto `0230e6b`, plus a third update, after fact-check 1, and a fourth, after fact-check 2)

After #180 merged, `main`'s `advisories.yml` run (Forgejo run 720, job `cargo-deny`) failed:
`error[unmaintained]: humantime is unmaintained`, RUSTSEC-2026-0542, "No safe upgrade is available!",
reached as `humantime v2.4.0 ← humantime-serde v1.1.1 ← trycmd v1.2.1 ← (dev) redextape-cli` and
through `trycmd` directly. redextape uses no time crate itself, and trycmd 1.2.1, the latest release
(2026-07-21), still requires `humantime ^2` and `humantime-serde ^1`. The lane's record is
`~/temp/redextape-drop-trycmd-record/`, `$R` below: `brief.md` (the user's decision), `progress.md`,
the sabotage scripts in `sabotage/` and the logs this entry names.

A SHA this entry gives for a run, a measurement, a sabotage or a review from before the rebase is
that commit's SHA before the rebase onto `0230e6b`, measured before the rebase, on `846bb78`;
`$R/rebase1/sha-map.txt` maps each to its SHA after it, and the local branch
`drop-trycmd-pre-rebase-1` keeps them. The runs after fact-check 1, whose logs are in `$R/fc1fix/`,
are on `423fa4e` with `tests/cli.rs` changed but not committed, on `fe907ca`, or on `3d46a5f`, the
commit that adds the update after fact-check 1. A SHA that names what a commit changes, a range or
a count of commits is its SHA after the rebase.

##### WHAT CHANGED AND WHY

- **`snapbox` replaces `trycmd`** in `redextape-cli`'s dev-dependencies: 1.2.2, the latest release on
  crates.io when checked on 2026-11-17, with its default features off and `cmd`, `dir` and `diff` on.
  snapbox is the engine trycmd runs on, and none of its normal dependencies is a time crate. `cmd`
  runs the binary, `dir` makes the sandboxes and compares `.out` files, and `diff` prints a failure
  as a unified diff through `similar` 3, which `redextape-cli` already depends on.
- **`Cargo.lock` loses ten packages and gains none**: trycmd 1.2.1, humantime 2.4.0, humantime-serde
  1.1.1, rayon 1.12.0, rayon-core 1.13.0, crossbeam-deque 0.8.8, crossbeam-epoch 0.9.21, either
  1.19.0, glob 0.3.4 and shlex 1.3.0 (shlex 2.0.1 stays). snapbox 1.2.2 was already locked, under
  trycmd.
- **`tests/cli.rs` is a harness that reads `tests/cmd/*.toml`** and does for each case what trycmd
  did: the same argv and stdin (the `stdin` key, or else a `<name>.stdin` file, which trycmd also
  read); the same working directory, a fresh temp sandbox holding a copy of
  `<name>.in/` for the 30 cases with `fs.sandbox = true` and the crate's directory for the other 11;
  the exit code (`status.code`, or 0); stdout and stderr against `<name>.stdout` and `<name>.stderr`
  through the same snapbox filters (line endings, and `\` to `/` on both sides) and redactions
  (`[CWD]`, `[ROOT]`, `[EXE]`); and every file under the four `<name>.out/` directories against the
  sandbox's file at the same path. It runs every case and then fails once, naming each case that
  differed and how. No file under `tests/cmd/` changed but `.gitignore`, which is gone (below).
- **An entry in `tests/cmd/` that is not part of a `.toml` case fails the run, naming it** (`fe907ca`),
  before any case runs: anything but `<name>.toml` and the `.stdin`, `.stdout`, `.stderr`, `.in` or
  `.out` beside it. That covers a `.trycmd` or `.md` case, which the harness does not read, and a
  golden or `.in/` whose `.toml` is missing. trycmd's `tests/cmd/*.toml` glob never ran such a file
  and said nothing.
- **`SNAPSHOTS=overwrite`** rewrites each `.stdout`, `.stderr` and `.out/` golden whose content
  differs. It never writes a `.toml`, so a changed exit code stays a failure until `status.code` is
  edited by hand, and an `.out/` file the binary did not make also stays a failure. `SNAPSHOTS` takes
  no other value: any other fails the run before a case runs.
- **The `.git` marker that stops `config::discover` at the sandbox root is written into each sandbox
  after the copy**, no longer into the working tree's 30 `.in/` directories for the copy to carry. The
  sandbox the binary runs in is the same; a test run no longer writes into the working tree, and
  `tests/cmd/.gitignore`, whose one pattern named those markers, is deleted.
- Two comments that named trycmd now say what they mean: `config.rs`'s "so a CLI transcript golden
  stays legible", and `scripts/check-citations.sh`'s "a file `SNAPSHOTS=overwrite` regenerates". The
  plans and specs that name trycmd are history and stay.

##### DECISIONS

The user's, 2026-11-17: a PR of its own for the advisory. He said "we should move to jiff"; told that
only a trycmd release could change the time crate trycmd uses, and offered three fixes, he chose
**"Drop trycmd for snapbox"**: port the CLI's golden tests to snapbox, keeping the golden files.

The controller's, after fact-check 1 found a `.trycmd` or `.md` file in `tests/cmd/` skipped where
this entry said it failed: change the code, so that any entry there that is not part of a `.toml`
case fails the run, naming it.

The implementer's calls:

- **A harness that reads the `.toml` cases, not 41 Rust tests.** The case files stay byte-identical,
  so each case's command line and exit code are the same by construction rather than by checking 41
  transcriptions, and adding a case is still adding its files. What it costs: nextest shows one test,
  `cli_transcripts`, for 41 cases, and its failure message is what lists the failing cases.
- **Strict reading.** Every table in a case refuses a key it does not declare
  (`serde(deny_unknown_fields)`), so a trycmd key the harness does not act on fails its case instead
  of being ignored; a case with a `.in/` or `.out/` and no `fs.sandbox = true` fails; a case missing
  either golden fails, where trycmd skipped a stream that had none; and `bin.name` must be `redextape`.
- **The path filter stays on both sides.** snapbox's `Assert` filters only the captured stream; the
  harness filters each golden too, as trycmd did, so no golden changes. The module doc's note on
  `fmt_check_dirty.stdout`'s `/` trailer is kept and reworded: the filter can now be turned off
  (`Assert::normalize_paths(false)`), and doing so would need that golden to hold the binary's `\`.
- **The `.git` marker is kept and moved into the sandbox.** snapbox still sandboxes under the system
  temp directory, so the upward walk the marker bounds is still there to bound.

##### WHAT THE REVIEW CAUGHT

Review 1 (`$R/review-1.md`), on `6f26d9c`: 0 Critical, 0 Important and 4 Minor findings, all fixed
in `add0ae9` as the controller called them.

- **M1, `SNAPSHOTS=skip` or `ignore` passed every stream.** snapbox reads both as "pass whatever the
  stream holds". The harness now takes only `overwrite`, or `SNAPSHOTS` unset; any other value,
  `verify` and the empty string included, fails the run (`snapshots_takes_only_overwrite_or_unset`, and
  `snapshots_ignore_fails_the_run`, which runs the test binary's own `cli_transcripts` under
  `SNAPSHOTS=ignore`).
- **M2, a `<name>.stdin` file was ignored**, where trycmd read it as the input of a case with no
  `stdin` key. The harness now reads its bytes; a case with both fails, naming its two inputs
  (`a_stdin_file_is_the_input_of_a_case_without_a_stdin_key`,
  `a_case_with_a_stdin_key_and_a_stdin_file_fails`). No case in `tests/cmd/` has one.
- **M3, "a case without either fails"** (the module doc) and "a case without both goldens fails"
  (this entry) read as "a case with neither"; the harness fails a case missing either one, and both
  now say so (`a_case_missing_either_golden_fails`, which holds it for each golden in turn).
- **M4, under `SNAPSHOTS=overwrite` an `.out/` file the binary did not make counted as fixed.**
  snapbox's overwrite of that difference copies the golden into the sandbox and returns `Ok`, so the
  run passed and the stale golden stayed. Only a content mismatch now counts as fixed
  (`overwrite_rewrites_a_differing_out_file_and_fails_on_one_the_binary_did_not_make`, which also
  checks that a differing `.out/` file is still rewritten). trycmd counted it fixed the same way.

##### WHAT THIS DID NOT CLOSE

- **`fmt_check_dirty.stdout` still holds `/` where the binary prints `\`.** Turning snapbox's path
  filter off on both sides and putting the real `\` in that golden would make it what a terminal
  shows; it is left so that this change touches no golden.
- **One test for 41 cases.** nextest names `cli_transcripts`, not the case that failed.
- **A checkout that ran the trycmd test keeps its `.git` markers in `tests/cmd/*.in/`.** Git skips any
  entry named `.git`, so `git status` does not show them; the copy into a sandbox brings one along,
  and the harness writes the same marker over it. Deleting them is safe.
- **trycmd's other case keys** (such as `env`, `fs.cwd`, `fs.base`, `timeout`, `stderr-to-stdout` and
  `binary`)
  **and its multi-step `.trycmd` and `.md` files are not modelled.** No case uses one. A case with
  such a key fails on it as unknown; a `.trycmd` or `.md` file in `tests/cmd/` fails the run, naming
  it (`a_file_that_is_not_part_of_a_toml_case_is_named_and_refused`,
  `a_stray_file_in_tests_cmd_fails_the_run`).
- **26 of the 30 sandboxed cases have no `.out/`, so nothing checks the files they leave**:
  `fmt --check dirty.rxt` rewriting `dirty.rxt` would still pass `fmt_check_dirty`. trycmd checked no
  more; a sandbox file no `.out/` names is not checked in the other four either.
