#### TM FIELD WIDTH: EACH TM VIEW'S HEADER BAR HAS A `width` BOX, EMPTY FOR `auto` OR A WIDTH FROM 1 TO 64 CELLS, THAT RE-RUNS THE PROGRAM AT EXACTLY THAT WIDTH; A PINNED RUN THAT OVERFLOWS KEEPS ITS TM, WHICH STEPS TO ITS HALT IN `overflow` AND SAYS IT OUTGREW THE WIDTH CHOSEN; THE WIDTH IS STORED AND SHARED BESIDE THE ENCODING, AN EXAMPLE RESETS IT TO AUTO, AND THE RESULTS STRIP MARKS A PINNED WIDTH; THE TM VIEW'S STEP COUNT MOVES TO THE LINE UNDER ITS BAR, WHICH KEEPS ONE ROW (2026-11-16 and 17, branch `tm-width`, `538b211..9bd8a4d`, 34 commits, ten of them this entry's earlier versions, plus this rebuild of it, its correction and its update for the rebase onto `538b211`, 37 in all)

The user asked for a live control over the bit width of a TM program's numbers, for teaching: a narrow
width makes a run small enough to follow by eye, and lets you watch a value run out of bits. The lane's
record is `~/temp/redextape-tm-width-record/`, `$R` below: `brief.md` holds the user's decisions and the
controller's calls, `progress.md` the work and its logs, `review-tasks12.md`, `review-tasks34.md` and
`review-branch.md` the three reviews of the plan's work, `review-hb.md` the review of the header round and
`review-box.md` that of the width box's rounds. The design doc is
`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-16-tm-width-design.md`, whose decisions 1 to 33 this entry cites as D1 to D33; the
plan is `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-11-16-tm-width.md`.

The lane's first step probed a suspected wrong value on `main` and found it: under binary auto-fit, a program
whose values fit four bits but which has more than sixteen call sites ran at width 4, and a return tag cut to
four bits resumed after the wrong call. The user ruled that its fix ship first, as its own PR, and put a second
fix in that PR: the fault a run continued into `overflow` reports. Both shipped as #179 (`486df8d`, branch
`tm-return-tag`, which has its own entry); this branch was rebased onto it, and then onto `538b211`.

A SHA this entry gives for a run, a measurement, a screenshot, a review or a trial of the user's is that
commit's SHA before the rebase onto `538b211`, measured before the rebase, on `486df8d`, and
`$R/rebase2/sha-map.txt` maps each to its SHA after it (the local branch `tm-width-pre-rebase-2` keeps them);
a SHA that names what a commit changes, the branch's range or a count of its commits is its SHA after it.

##### WHAT CHANGED AND WHY

- **The width box.** Each TM view's header bar has `width` and a box at its end, right before `⋯`: empty for
  `auto`, the default, where `auto` stands in grey, or a width from 1 to 64, the range `fieldWidths()` lists. A
  width typed applies on Enter or on leaving the box; a step of ↑/↓ or of the box's arrows applies 400ms after the
  last, through one plain order, auto, 1, 2, ..., 64, so ↑ from auto is 1 and ↓ past 1 is auto (D32); Escape puts
  the box back, and an entry that is not a listed width is put back (D29). The arrows are the box's own, an up half
  over a down half inside its border at its end, drawn as `icons.ts` chevrons (D30). The box is a text field that
  is a spin button, so each entry is judged on the text it shows (D33). The control started as a select in the
  rules panel's header, moved to the bar after the title when the user tried the branch (D24), to the bar's end
  when they tried it again (D27), became a number box the third time (D29), drew its own arrows the fourth (D30),
  went down to 1 under the plain arrow pointer the fifth (D31), stepped from auto to 1, not from the width auto
  fitted, the sixth (D32), and became a text field on the review of those rounds (D33). wasm's new `fieldWidths()`
  export and the `compile` export's third argument (`null` for auto) share one range, `session::FIELD_WIDTHS`. An
  entry recompiles once however many TM views show it, and every view's box follows; a view showing a TM copy has
  none, since a copy runs at the width its own header records (D19). The box's accessible description says what the
  bare word leaves to the eye: "tape field width in cells for the program’s TM, shared by every TM view; empty for
  auto". Its last words are how a screen reader in Chromium learns what the empty box means: Chromium hands on no
  native input's `aria-valuetext`, which in Firefox makes `auto` the empty box's value as well (D33).
- **A pinned width runs at exactly that width.** Core gains `run_tm_described_program_at` for an already-lowered
  program, with the range check and the one build site `run_tm_described_at` already used. `auto` is unchanged,
  its decline at 64 included (D4).
- **Widths under auto's 4.** What held the floor at 4 was the pinned entry points' range check alone (D31): auto's
  first rung, `MIN_FIELD_WIDTH`, is no limit of the encodings, which already ran at widths 0 to 3 under test. Pinned
  at 1, 2 and 3, the seven examples halt in `overflow` in 41 runs of 42 and answer `true` in the other (`is-even`
  under binary at 3), and no run gives a wrong value. Core names the range `PINNED_FIELD_WIDTHS`, `1..=64`, which
  the pinned entry points and the `.tm` header reader both check and wasm's `FIELD_WIDTHS` takes; `MIN_FIELD_WIDTH`
  stays 4, so auto is unchanged.
- **A pinned run that overflows keeps its TM.** Where auto would widen, a pinned run's `overflow` halt is kept:
  the TM view steps to it, and its value is a fault from the moment `compile` returns: "a number the machine
  stores (a value, an address or a call's return tag) outgrew the 4-cell tape field chosen for this run; try a
  wider width, or auto". At 64 it names the encoding's limit instead. `tm_value` never decodes the tapes of a run
  that halted in `overflow` (D11, D12). A copy of a kept overflow halts there too, in its header's words.
- **Stored and shared beside the encoding.** `StoredProgram` and share links carry `width` only when pinned, so an
  auto payload has no `width` and no version is bumped (D14). A width this build does not list reads as auto,
  checked in the web code as an integer `fieldWidths()` lists (D15). A link carries the width because its TM
  position is a step of one run, and another width is another run (D16); a link's width is always its own, never
  the stored program's (D22). A whole link whose width this build does not list opens at auto **without its TM
  position**, which belongs to the run at the width it named (D15, the branch review's M3).
- **An example resets the width to auto**, as it resets the encoding, since the example manifest's outcomes hold
  under auto; the pick's undo puts back the width it replaced.
- **The results strip marks a pinned width**: `let x = 2; x + 3` pinned at 4 reads
  `TM 5 · 233 transitions · width 4 (pinned)` where auto's fit stays `width 4`, and the inspector's row reads
  `4 cells (pinned)` (D23). With no TM view open there is no box, so the strip is all the page says of the
  width. The mark comes from the `result` reply's new `pinned`, set by the worker from whether the `run` request
  carried a width, so a result still on screen while a new width compiles is marked as its own compile ran.
- **The TM view's step count is on the line under its bar** (D25). With the select on the bar, the bar wrapped at
  1280px in Explorer at every step count; now the bar holds the title, the step buttons, the speed select, the width
  box and `⋯ ✕`, one row at every count in each style, and the status line reads
  `pc0 · step 0 of 12,976 · width 4`. On a phone the line stays one row by cutting the state's name with an
  ellipsis, its whole name in a tooltip; the step text and the width are never cut. The step text takes the room it
  needs at the run's newest step, so where the line wraps, in Explorer's two columns on a phone, its rows do not
  change while a run plays (D28). The λ and rxm views keep their step text on their bar. In a copy's view too the
  line sits directly under the bar, above the copy's text panel (D26).

##### DECISIONS

The user's, on 2026-11-16 (`$R/brief.md`, and the controller's dispatches after it, which its ledger
`~/temp/redextape-ui-lanes-ledger.md` records):

- **A width select**, `auto` (the default, today's behaviour) and every width from 4 to 64.
- **A pinned width runs at exactly that width.**
- **A pinned run that overflows keeps its TM**, steppable to its halt in `overflow`, and the status says it
  overflowed at width N, with a pointer to a wider width or auto. This is the demo.
- **The select lived first in each TM view's rules panel header**, not the top bar beside `encoding`: at 1280 the top
  bar had no room for it (Task 3's probe, `$R/task3-room-probe.log`). On 2026-11-17, after trying the branch: "I
  think the width should be on the same bar as TM - program not in the rules section" (D24). After trying `bfae654`:
  "I think width should be on the right side next to the ... button" (D27).
- **A number box instead of the select** (2026-11-17, after trying `7b61933`, the "Number box" of three controls shown;
  D29 quotes its description): type a width or step it, empty for auto, applied on Enter or on leaving the box.
- **The box's own arrows** (2026-11-17, after trying `f921888` in Firefox: "the arrows look bad, they go outside the
  box. they do work but we should probably draw our own"), D30.
- **A plain pointer on the arrows, and widths down to auto past 1 or 2** (2026-11-17, after trying `b149c7a`: "can we
  make it use a regular pointer instead of the hand pointer? can we also make it go down to "auto" after 1 or 2?
  whatever makes sense (even though 1 and 2 will overflow most programs, it's good for demo)"), D31.
- **Auto is the bottom of one plain order** (2026-11-17, after trying `036a198`: "it's confusing that after you go to
  auto it jumps back to up to 9 or 7 depending on what you press. it should just go up to 1 in this case"), D32.
- **The step count leaves the TM view's bar for the line under it** (2026-11-17, option B of three measured and
  shown to the user, D25 quotes it), so that the bar keeps one row; λ and rxm unchanged.
- **The strip marks a pinned width** (after the branch review's M4), "width 4 (pinned)"; auto stays "width N".

The controller's:

- From the brief: `auto` exactly as today; the floor stays 4 (until D31); the width stored and shared the way the
  encoding is, a payload without it reading as auto; picking an example resets it to auto; TM copies keep their own
  header width.
- **The pinned fault's pointer reads "try a wider width, or auto"** (the Tasks 1-2 review's M2): the controller's
  wording of the user's pointer.
- **The inspector's width row marks a pinned width too**, `4 cells (pinned)`: the controller's extension of the
  user's strip ruling, in its dispatch.
- **No version bump (D14), and a width this build does not list read as auto (D15)**, both proposed in the plan.
  D14's cost is named there and below: an older deployment opens a pinned link at auto.
- **Integers only** (the Tasks 1-2 review's M4): the web code accepts a width only as an integer `fieldWidths()`
  lists, because wasm-bindgen's `u32` glue turns `16.7`, `2 ** 32 + 16` and `"8"` into 16, 16 and 8 before Rust's
  range check runs. One function, `field-width.ts`'s `listedWidth`, is the check (D15).
- **D21 and D22**, the implementer's proposals, kept: writers may leave the width out (a width left out is auto),
  so the test files that store or encode a program for other reasons pass none, while `main.ts`'s three writers
  always pass it; and a link's width is always its own.
- **A link whose width this build does not list drops its TM position** (the branch review's M3), test-first.
- **The select right after the title** on the bar (D24), until the user's D27; **the step text between the state and
  the width, its endings with it, and the name cut at its end** (D25), a middle cut's helper being then on the unmerged
  state-diagram branch, since merged as #182.
- **A copy's status line under its bar too** (D26), following the user's D25: under the copy's text panel it sat
  237px below the bar at 1280, a whole editor away from the step buttons.
- **The box's behaviour** (D29): a step applies after a 400ms pause, so stepping 8 to 12 runs once; Escape puts the
  box back; an entry that is not a listed width is put back on Enter or leave, with no notice; from auto the first
  step started at the width auto fitted, until the user's D32.
- **The arrows' terms** (D30): each half steps as ↑/↓ do, out of the Tab order, the focus kept in the box, nothing
  drawn outside it, 3:1 or more in every style and theme and visible in forced colours; the box as tall as the speed
  select in both engines; letters put back in both; an entry kept through a playing run's frames. The implementer's
  calls: chevrons at stroke 3 in `--fg-dim`; no hover or pressed look, as `⋯` has none; a TM view's speed select held
  to the box's height, 2px shorter in Chromium, its bar no shorter; Chromium's refused letters read from
  `beforeinput` (until D33); a 1.1em column.
- **A text field that is a spin button, its description ending "; empty for auto"** (D33, on `review-box.md`'s I1,
  I2 and M1): the text field judges each entry on the text it shows and has no browser step to leave the plain
  order by. The controller's first call was the text field alone, its `aria-valuetext` saying `auto`; measured over
  AT-SPI, Chromium hands on no native input's `aria-valuetext`, text or number, so on that measurement the
  controller added the description's last words, the name staying `width`.
- **The step text sized by the run's total** (D28, on review-hb's I1), under the user's rule that nothing moves the
  page on its own: in Explorer's two columns on a phone the line gained rows as a playing run's count gained digits,
  pushing the tapes 39px down mid-run. A line that gains a row when the total itself grows is accepted.

The implementer's, each with its reason in the design doc: the kept overflow recorded as one field, `run_end`
(`Halted`, `Overflowed` or `NoHalt`), beside `width_from`, which only picks the words (D12); `tm_status` and the
wire types unchanged (D13); a pinned `TooLarge` keeps the generic words (D18); the width as `main.ts` state handed
to every view as the speed is (D20); the strip's mark carried on the `result` reply rather than read from the page
(D23); the select a child of the bar between the heading and the step slot, in the speed select's chrome (D24); the
TM-only status line built by `TmPane` from the readout `stepControls` hands it rather than scoped by `data-kind`,
the line dropping the readout at the `steps` switch's `bar`, and the step and the width taking another row rather
than being cut where the two alone outgrow the line (D25); the select first among the view's own actions, at their
`var(--space-1)` before `⋯`, and the actions wrapping on the right where they do not fit one row (D27); the room
reserved by drawing the readout at the newest step unseen in the step part's grid cell, not by a width in `ch`, which
would not hold the part's rows where it wraps (D28); the box applying on Enter's `keydown` and `focusout`, not on
`change`, which both browsers fire at every step; ↑/↓ handled by the box and a step of its arrows from empty moved to
the fitted width (until D32), since both browsers step an empty box to its `min`; the wheel's default prevented
over the focused box, which Chromium would step (until D33); an entry kept through the run's frames;
`aria-valuetext` `auto`; the box's line and width (D29); a number written in digits, with a fraction if any, so
`1e1`, `+3` and `0x10` are put back; `autocomplete` off and `spellcheck` false; Ctrl, Alt and Meta with ↑/↓ left to
the browser, which steps no text field (D33).

##### WHAT THE REVIEWS CAUGHT

- **Tasks 1-2** (`review-tasks12.md`, 6 Minor): the fault said "a value outgrew" when a return tag had; "pick a wider
  width, or auto" promised a remedy where no width fits, so it reads "try" by the controller's ruling; a copy of a
  kept overflow claimed the encoding's limit at width 4; the export took widths the caller never sent (the
  integers-only rule above); stale doc pointers; no test of a width off auto's ladder.
- **Tasks 3-4** (`review-tasks34.md`, 1 Important, 4 Minor): D22 had no test on any open path (I1), now one browser
  file, `share-open-width-own.test.ts`; a width choice withdrawing a link's undo was untested; the select's handler
  was a second copy of `listedWidth`'s rule; D14's cost was unnamed; the select had no description.
- **The branch** (`review-branch.md`, 4 Minor, all fixed in the last four commits): `check-doc-figures.sh`'s ordinal
  comment said "the tenth" (M1); the no-bump comments told history rather than the reason (M2); an unlisted width's
  link kept its TM position (M3); with no TM view open, a pinned width could not be seen (M4, the strip's mark).
- **The header round** (`review-hb.md`, `e054a38..bfae654`, 1 Important, 5 Minor, all fixed): in Explorer's two
  columns on a phone the status line gained rows while a run played (I1, D28); `#rulesPanel`'s doc still named the
  width (M1); a style comment gave a TM reason that no longer held, and now gives the λ and rxm strips' reason,
  which holds: at `.controls button`'s padding, λ's bar wraps at a five-digit count in Instrument and rxm's at three
  digits in Paper and Terminal, all one row as built (M2, `node r5/m2.mjs` in `$R`, `r5/m2.log`); the PR draft
  lagged D26 (M3); the line at the `steps` switch's `bar` had no test (M4); comments ran past 120 columns (M5).
- **The width box's rounds** (`review-box.md`, `7b61933..ec2348e`, 2 Important, 3 Minor, all fixed in `be683e9` and
  `9bd8a4d`): in Chromium a screen reader heard the empty number box as a spin button with no value, where the
  select said "auto", and D29's claim and the tests read only the DOM attribute (I1, D33); one refused character
  made every later entry refuse until a deletion, so `16` typed over `1x` put the width back, in both engines (I2);
  Ctrl+↓ at auto pinned 1, past the plain order (M1); two comments still said "select" and a style comment held a
  measurement (M2); D9 and D29 still gave the floor as 4 (M3). The review's own property test, run and deleted, had
  every one of 2,005 generated programs at widths 1 to 4 in both encodings give the reference answer or `overflow`.

##### WHAT THIS DID NOT CLOSE

- **At 1280 the strip cuts a pinned overflow's fault with an ellipsis, and the `(pinned)` mark with it.** With the TM
  view off, `let a = 9; let b = 9; a + b` pinned at 4 draws its mark from x 1495.2 to 1557.9 in a segment that ends
  at 1264. The full text is in the segment's `title` and the inspector; a short value's mark is drawn whole.
- **With no TM view open the width can be seen but not changed**: turning a TM view on, or picking an example
  (which resets it to auto), is the way back.
- **D14's cost**: a tab still on an older deployment opens a pinned link whole at auto and applies its TM position,
  a step of the pinned run, to the auto run. Writing pinned links alone at a new version would avoid it.
- **`keep recording` and `continue — raise the step cap` still wrap the TM view's bar** at 1280 in Explorer: with
  either shown, the bar is two rows, three with the longer label (`$R/hb/ext-B.log`). They stay where they are;
  their room belongs to a later change to the page's layout.
- **The state's name is cut at its end**, where a middle cut would keep the part that differs between two names; the
  helper for that, `middleCut` in `local-layout.ts`, came to `main` with #182 and is not used here.
- **In a TM view narrower than the step text and the width** (Explorer's two columns at 320 to 390px, 154 to
  189px), the status line takes more than one row: the width, and there the readout too, wrap rather than being cut.
  Its rows are those of the run's newest step from step 0 (D28), 78px at 375 and 390px where at step 0 the readout
  needs 39, and blank room follows a count shorter than the total wherever the line is.
- **A held press on the width box's arrows steps once**, where the browser's arrows repeated while held (D30).
- **In Chromium the empty box has no value**: a screen reader hears a spin button named `width` with no value text,
  and `auto` only at the end of its description; in Firefox `auto` is its value too (D33). Only an element that is
  not a native input would carry `aria-valuetext` in Chromium.
- **A step from text that is no number**, ↑ to 1 and ↓ to auto (D32), has no test.
- **In Firefox's forced colours over dark content** the box's text, its `auto` and its focus ring come out
  near-white on white, as the speed and encoding selects' do (the box review, which left it as not this branch's).
- **The CLI pins 4 to 64 only**: `--field-width` and `emit.field-width` still check `MIN_FIELD_WIDTH`, the CLI being
  a non-goal of this lane, where the app pins down to 1 (D31).
- **A copy's status line and its text panel are 16px apart**, the line's 8px under itself and the panel's 8px above
  itself added in the view's flex column (D26). Closing it to 8px would raise everything under the text panel by
  8px, so it was left.
- **A pinned run continued past its cap into `overflow` is held only by a session test**,
  `a_pinned_run_raised_past_its_cap_into_overflow_answers_the_pinned_fault`. The branch review drove a counter
  through the page at width 16, raising the cap, and stopped before the run reached the overflow.
- **A pinned `TooLarge` says "too large to build"** whatever the width (D18), though a narrower width can help a
  state-ceiling refusal; telling the refusals apart needs plumbing nothing else needs.
- **A pinned 64 compiles more slowly than auto** on programs auto fits narrow; Task 5's timing is in
  `$R/t5/measure/RESULTS.md` (not re-run for this entry, so no figure here).
- **No test sees a map built wider than its run.** In the Tasks 1-2 fix round, a sabotage rounding a pinned width
  of 13 up to 16 for the map failed nothing (`$R/fix-sabotage2.log`): a narrower width's state names all appear in a
  wider width's map, so the billed-state check cannot tell, and no observable effect of the wider map was found.

#### A CLICK ON EMPTY SPACE IN A VIEW, A COPY'S INCLUDED, OR ESCAPE WITH THE FOCUS IN ONE, CLEARS THE LINK AND LEAVES LINKING ON; A CLICK THAT LINKS, ON A CONTROL OR A VIEW'S CHROME, ENDING A DRAG, CLOSING A MENU OR WITH SHIFT HELD CLEARS NOTHING, AND NO LIST MOVES ON THE CLEAR; THE LOCAL DIAGRAM'S DOUBLE-CLICK RESETS NOTHING, *LOCAL* PRESSED WHILE IT SHOWS PUTS IT BACK AT FULL SIZE, AND A FIRST DRAW OR A RESET CENTRES WHAT IT DRAWS, AND A PAN STOPS WITH SOME OF IT IN THE PANEL (2026-11-17, branch `link-clear`, `2cdf0b0..280cb35`, 18 commits, this entry's first and three updates of it among them, plus the commit that updates it and the design doc for review 2, the one that adds the full gate's figures, one that changes a code comment and three that correct this entry, 24 in all)

The user, 2026-11-17, trying the state diagram's drag: "we should also make it so if you click outside it deselects
that code section". An edit clears a pinned link (Plan 5b's click-linking design, decision 6), and
that clear turns linking off until the next compile. The decisions and every call, with who made it, are in
`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-17-link-clear-design.md`. The lane's record is `~/temp/redextape-link-clear-record/`,
`$R` below: `brief.md`, `design-draft.md` (the recon),
`progress.md`, `review-1.md`, `review-2.md` and the logs this entry names.

A SHA this entry gives for a run, a measurement, a sabotage, a review or a trial of the user's from before the rebase
onto `2cdf0b0` (`30d5228`, `de25908`, `74bfdab` and `d7f2049`) is that commit's SHA then, measured before the rebase,
on `0230e6b`, and `$R/r6/sha-map.txt` maps each to its SHA after it (the local branch `link-clear-pre-rebase-1` keeps
them). Every other SHA is one after the rebase: review 2's and those of the runs from it on (`523bfd4`, `280cb35`,
`0e21c07` and `7e5c36f`), and a SHA that names what a commit changes, the branch's range or a count of its commits.

##### DECISIONS

The user's, 2026-11-17:

- **"Empty space, any view"**, put to him as: a click on empty space in any view clears the highlight (the diagram's
  background, blank rows of the rules list, the tapes panel, the λ and rxm views), and Escape clears it too.
- **"ok" to the short design**: a click on anything in a view that does not link clears (the tapes, the diagram's
  background, the blank beside a λ line, rows that link nothing); a press that moves more than 4 px is a drag and
  clears nothing; Escape clears with the focus in a view, not in the code editors and not with a menu or dialog open;
  a click on empty space in a copy's view clears the program's highlight too; the source editor works as before.
- **"clear highlight seems good"**, after trying `30d5228`.
- **"Stay put"**, after review 1 found that the clear sent the rule table and the rxm listing back to the run's row:
  "The lists stay where they are when the highlight clears; they pick up following the running state again on the
  next step. Nothing moves on the click itself."
- **"Keep the highlight"**, asked whether a double-click on the diagram's background should both reset the zoom and
  clear the highlight: "A double-click only resets the zoom; the highlight the first click cleared comes back."
- **"the blink bothers me, it shouldn't do that"**, after trying `de25908`, whose double-click took the highlight off
  at its first click and put it back at its second.
- **"Shorter wait"**, after trying the half-second wait: "half a second is way too slow, how does something like
  youtube handle double clicking to full screen the video". Told that YouTube acts on the first click and lets the
  second undo it, the blink already turned down: keep the highlight through a double-click, but wait about a quarter
  of a second instead of half; a quick double-click keeps it, a slow one clears it on its first click, without a blink.
- **"drop the double click"**, which overtakes the three before it, after trying the quarter-second wait: "ok I don't
  like it, I think I wuld rather drop the double click, and we can actually make pressing "local" after it's already
  highlighted reset the view"; and of the local level, "when it's "reset" it would be nice if it was centered and not
  right aligned".
- **"yes looks good"**, after trying what that asked for, at `d7f2049`.

The controller's: the rows that link nothing and the blank beside a λ line counted as empty space, the copy's clear,
and the editors' Escape (all three shown to the user inside the design he approved); after review 1, no clear for a
press with a menu or popover open, a copy's diagram node and runtime box left to the gesture count as rows are, the
double-click ruling applied to a word selected on the tapes and to a Shift-click, the Escape listener returning at
once for other keys, and a test for a row that links nothing. After "drop the double click": every click clears at
once; the local diagram's double-click reset goes, and the tapes' word selection stays the browser's; a press of
*local* while the local level shows puts it back at full size where a first draw places it, by keyboard too, and
clears no link; and the centring rides in this branch. After review 2: one Escape does one thing, the innermost first,
so a TM view's width box keeps the Escape that puts back a width typed there; and the pan's reach follows what is
drawn, fixed in this branch, being the same blank room the centring met. At the finish, on review 2's M2, which
asked for the zoom and the place: a press of *local* from the program level keeps the zoom and centres the current
state again, as `setLevel` does on `main`, because a change of level shows the level afresh. Measured after review 2:
zoomed to 1.5 and moved 57 px off the middle across, the state came back at 0 in Chromium (59.1 and 0 in Firefox;
`r7/red-chromium.log`, `r7/red-firefox.log`).

##### WHAT CHANGED

- **`web/src/link-clear.ts`**, new: listeners on `#views` (a `pointerdown` and a `click` in the capture phase, a
  `click` in the bubble phase) and a `keydown` on the document. A click clears at once unless it linked, landed on something
  `KEEPS` names (a control, a widget role, a popover, an editor, a view's or panel's header, the λ term map and its
  fold and open toggles), ended a press that went more than `DRAG_THRESHOLD` (4 px) from where it began, followed a
  press made with a menu open, or had Shift held. Escape's rule is a pure function, `escapeClears`.
- **`LinkWiring.unpin()`** (`web/src/link-wiring.ts`): the user's clear. Nothing pinned, every mark redrawn with no
  scroll, and linking left on, where `clearLink` (an edit's) turns it off. `gestures` counts `setLinkTo`'s link
  gestures: read around a click's own handlers, it says whether the click linked, which only the view knows.
- **`DRAG_THRESHOLD`** replaces the state diagram's `PAN_THRESHOLD`, so a press that pans never clears.
- **The local level** (`web/src/state-diagram.ts`): a double-click on its background resets nothing; `resetLocal()`
  puts it back at full size where a first draw places it, which a press of *local* while it shows does
  (`web/src/tm-pane.ts`) and the `0` key does; and `#place` centres `LocalLayout.inked` (`web/src/local-layout.ts`),
  the part of the drawing anything is drawn in, not the drawing's box, which in a panel wider than the level also
  holds the spread of the gaps past its outermost columns.
- **A `hint` on a `radioGroup` choice** (`web/src/view-header.ts`): what a press does beyond choosing, its `title` and
  `aria-description` while it can be made. *local* says "press again to reset the view" while the local level shows.
- **A TM view's width box** (`web/src/field-width.ts`): the Escape that puts back a width typed there is prevented,
  and the clear passes over a prevented Escape, as it does an editor's; with nothing typed the box uses no Escape, and
  the link clears.
- **The local level's reach**: `.local-content`, whose room in the panel is the pan's reach (`web/src/style.css`), is
  the part of the drawing anything is drawn in, at the zoom, with the drawing set in it and clipped to it
  (`#sizeLocal`), so a pan ends where a corner of what is drawn reaches the panel's middle; `#place` centres that box.
- **The help page** (`web/help.html`): a row for Escape clearing the link, and the local level's row names `+`, `=`,
  `-`, `0` and a second press of *local*.
- Tests: `web/tests/browser/link-clear.test.ts` (in `CAPTURE_FILES`) and `web/tests/node/link-clear.test.ts`; for
  the local level, `web/tests/browser/state-diagram-local-pan.test.ts`, `web/tests/browser/state-diagram-local.test.ts`
  and `web/tests/node/local-layout.test.ts`; `state-diagram-local-layout.test.ts` and
  `state-diagram-local-scrollbars.test.ts` read the whole drawing from `.local-drawing` now that `.local-content` is
  its inked part.

The implementer's calls, each with its reason in the design doc: whether a click linked is read off the gesture
count rather than a list of rows that link; a click is classified by its `composedPath()`, because a grid's click
can redraw the rows under it before the event reaches `#views`; no guard for a scroll bar (no engine measured sends a
click for a press on one); Escape with the focus on the body counts as in a view; "Stay put" is `unpin` drawing with
no scroll; a Shift-click clears nothing, because the clear's redraw would take away the selection it extends; a later
click of a run that cleared needs no rule of its own, finding nothing pinned; a press of *local* reads what shows
before it picks, so one that brings the level in from the program level keeps its zoom; the first draw's placing is
tested through a resize, which places a level not moved since by the same function; and, after review 2, the reach's
box is the inked part, clipped, rather than a margin less the blank, which would leave the drawing's own box in the
scroll's range on the far side.

##### WHAT THE REVIEW CAUGHT

Review 1 (`review-1.md`, at `30d5228`): 0 Critical, 4 Important, 2 Minor, all fixed. I1, a click that closed a menu
also cleared, and I3, a copy's diagram node kept the pin while a row of the same copy cleared it, with M1 and M2, in
`f31afeb`; I4, the lists moving on the clear, by the user's "Stay put", in `62ce45c`; I2, the double-click, by his "Keep
the highlight", in `560f629`, and, after he had tried two ways of keeping it, by his "drop the double click", in
`4526dc3`.

Review 2 (`review-2.md`, at `523bfd4`): 0 Critical, 1 Important, 6 Minor, all fixed. I1, Escape in a TM view's width
box put back a width typed there and cleared the link too, in `85355a4`, with the tests M1 (the box, its label and
arrows keep the link) and M6 (the lists stay put after a clear of a pin made outside the rxm listing) and M4's
leftover; M3, a pan could leave a zoomed level's drawing wholly out of the panel where the level holds blank room on
one side, in `0c09901`, with M2's test (a press of *local* from the program level keeps the zoom); M5, the help page,
in `280cb35`.

##### WHAT THIS DID NOT CLOSE

- **A view off the page whose link row was still waiting for a draw** keeps that row after the clear, and scrolls to
  the block it names when it is next shown, as after an edit's clear (by reading `VirtualGrid.scrollToRow`, not
  measured).
- **A selection in the tapes, the registers, the call stack or the heap goes on any redraw**: each draw rebuilds
  those nodes (`replaceChildren`), so a link made in another view, a step or a clear drops it. Read from the code. A
  double-click's word is kept: its first click's clear redraws before its second press selects the word (the browser
  test).
- **A Shift-click clears nothing** whether or not there is a selection for it to extend.
- **No test clicks an rxm label row**: the test's program has none. Review 1 checked the rule by reading the code.
- **A press on a scroll bar**: no test. Review 1 measured that no click reaches `#views` in Chromium and in Firefox,
  headed under Xvfb with classic and overlay bars.

#### THE HEADER'S VIEWS TOGGLES READ SOURCE, λ, TM, RXM; THE `1` TO `4` KEYS, THE LAYOUT CYCLE AND THE LIVE REGION'S SENTENCE FOLLOW THEM, AND THE DEFAULT FOUR-VIEW GRID AND STORED WORKSPACES STAY AS THEY WERE (2026-11-17, branch `view-button-order`, `eb12e11..fbc573f`, 4 commits, plus this entry and one commit correcting it and the design doc)

The user, 2026-11-17: "we should make the order of the buttons at the top 'source, lambda, tm, rxm'". The toggles read
source, rxm, λ, TM. The design is in
`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-17-view-button-order-design.md`. The lane's record is
`~/temp/redextape-view-button-order-record/`, `$R` below: `brief.md`, `progress.md`, `review-1.md` and the logs this
entry names.

##### DECISIONS

The user's, 2026-11-17:

- **The order**, in the words above.
- **"yes keep"**, on the layout cycle. Following the new order changes what `]` does from a first load, the source
  beside the TM view (review 1's table, read from the running app by real key presses at 1280 x 896). The controller
  asked "should the `]` key follow the new button order? It currently does", showing that table, and said
  "I recommend keeping it, so the buttons, keys and cycle all share one order". The user answered "yes keep". The cycle
  goes on reading `HEADER_ORDER`.

| press of `]` | on `eb12e11` | on this branch |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | all four | the source beside rxm, the TM view hidden |
| 2 | the source beside rxm | all four |
| 3 | the source beside λ | the source beside λ |
| 4 | the source beside TM | the source beside TM |

The controller's, in the lane's brief: the `1` to `4` keys, the layout cycle and the live region's sentence follow the
new order, since they read `HEADER_ORDER` on purpose; the default four-view grid does not move; `KIND_ORDER` does not
change, since stored workspaces are keyed by it.

The implementer's, each with its reason in the design doc: a test about a view keeps its view and changes its key,
while a test whose subject is the digit keeps the digit; `step-focus-recording` presses `2` where it pressed `]`; the
focus ring case presses the source and rxm, where it pressed the source and TM; and a stored workspace is pinned as
written text in a file of its own.

##### WHAT CHANGED

- **`HEADER_ORDER`** (`web/src/layout.ts`) is source, λ, TM, rxm. What reads it follows: key `2` is λ, `3` TM and `4` rxm,
  the hint says so, the cycle's stops are the source beside λ, beside TM, beside rxm, then all four, and the live region
  says "showing source, λ, TM and rxm".
- **The lists written by hand**: the four toggles in `web/index.html`, their copy in `SHELL` in
  `web/tests/browser/harness.ts`, and in `web/help.html` the views sentence, the keys table and the cycle's sentence.
- **What did not move**: `KIND_ORDER` and the default grid, source over rxm beside λ over TM. `web/tests/node/layout.test.ts`
  held the grid's leaves to `HEADER_ORDER`, which was a coincidence of the old order, and now spells the grid's own order.
- **New tests**: `first-load-views.test.ts` reads the toggles' order across the screen from `getBoundingClientRect`;
  `workspace-stored-views-order.test.ts` restores a workspace whose record is written out as text.

##### WHAT THE REVIEW CAUGHT

Review 1 (`$R/review-1.md`, at `61ac5c6`): no Critical findings, one Important and four Minor. The Important one,
`]` from a first load hiding the TM view, went to the user and is his "yes keep" above, with no code change. In
`8cedbe5`: the design doc names the controller's calls as the controller's, a date leaves a code comment, and the
stored-workspace test asserts the focus it stores. The fifth, the README's image, is below.

##### WHAT THIS DID NOT CLOSE

- **The README's demo image** (`https://daveyhughes.com/readme/redextape/demo.webp`) still shows the old order. It is to
  be retaken after this merges.
- **31 tests in the files this branch touches fail in Firefox, some in every run and some in only some, on `eb12e11`
  and on this branch alike**, named under VERIFICATION. CI does not run Firefox, so no check reports them.
- **Whether the caret at offset 0 reaches a real Firefox user or comes from the test driver** is not answered. Neither
  review 1 nor this lane tried it by hand.
- **The LLVM tier was not run here**: the gate below is `scripts/check-all.sh --no-llvm`, whose last line says the run is
  partial. CI's workflow runs `scripts/check-all.sh --llvm-only`.

runs show that this branch did not bring it; they do not show why it fails only some of the time.

#### IR VIEWS GROUNDWORK PR 4: PANES, LAYOUT AND LINKS (2026-11-18, branch `ir-panes`, `6b77731..3c880f3`, 23 commits, plus this entry and the commits that correct it)

**Spec §5.2 to §5.4** (`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-27-ir-views-groundwork-design.md`), the groundwork's fourth pull
request in §6's order, held by §7.2 (no hot path slows) and §7.3 (the app behaves the same). The plan is
`docs/superpowers/plans/2026-11-18-ir-views-pr4-panes-layout-links.md`, committed as `b2a5c34`. This is a refactor of
the web app: it adds no view, pane kind, leg, stored key or workspace version, and it changes no file under `crates/`.
The lane's record is `~/temp/redextape-ir-panes-record/`, `$R` below. Its ledger and task reports are in the worktree's
`.superpowers/sdd/2026-11-18-ir-views-pr4-panes-layout-links/`, `$S` below.

**§7.2's timing is INCONCLUSIVE.** Nothing flagged, but the machine was too busy for that to mean much: the comparison
could not have seen a rise of up to about 60% in the median frame. VERIFICATION has the figures, and WHAT THIS DID NOT
CLOSE carries it.

##### DECISIONS

The user's four, 2026-11-18, each the plan's recommendation:

| | Question | The user's answer |
|---|---|---|
| Q1 | How are the header toggles generated? | **At build time.** `index.html` holds the container and a slot, a Vite plugin fills the slot, and the shipped page is unchanged. |
| Q2 | Does `PaneKind` derive from `Leg`? | **Yes:** `'source' \| Leg`. |
| Q3 | Do the per-leg display settings move in this PR? | **Yes**, as Task 15, the last panes task. |
| Q4 | Does a click on a TM state carry a pc? | **No.** Only an rxm click carries one, and nothing reads it yet. |

##### WHAT CHANGED

**Layout (§5.3), `8c1320b` to `6270b5e`.**

- `gridLines` and `gridArrangement` (`web/src/layout.ts`) place any number of views by one rule: `ceil(sqrt(count))`
  lines whose lengths are at most one apart, the short lines first. `defaultArrangement` goes through them.
- `PaneKind` is `'source' | Leg`, and `HEADER_ORDER` names every kind.
- The header's toggles are generated when the page is built. `web/src/view-toggle-markup.ts` writes one button a kind
  from `HEADER_ORDER` and `KIND_WORD`, and the `redextape-view-toggles` plugin in `web/vite.config.ts` fills the
  `<!-- view-toggles -->` slot in `web/index.html`. The whole-branch review built `6b77731` and `cf16caf` and found
  `dist/index.html` identical once asset hashes and the whitespace between tags are set aside.
- Tests of the kinds read the tables, except those that pin the user's order.

**Links (§5.4), `c708664` to `ca4855a`.**

- `LINKED` in the new `web/src/linked-legs.ts` holds each linked leg's rows of a `Link`, its view and its words on the
  status line. `link-status.ts`, `link-wiring.ts` and `draw.ts` fan out over it.
- A `Pin` can name one rxm instruction: `pinAtInstr` (`web/src/link.ts`) writes `pc` when an rxm row is clicked.

**Panes (§5.2), `b74658f` to `f7ce15d`.**

- `placeLabels` (`web/src/label-rows.ts`) is the one walker under `listingRows` and `programRows`.
- `MachineViewChrome` (`web/src/machine-view-chrome.ts`) is the header, step strip, `⋯` menu and copy editor that the
  rxm and TM views share.
- `followedGridPanel` (`web/src/followed-grid-panel.ts`) is the grid both views follow a run with, and `ListingPanel`
  (`web/src/listing-panel.ts`) sits on it for rxm.
- `valuesPanel`, `callStackPanel` and `heapPanel` (`web/src/machine-panels.ts`) draw finished rows, which `rxmValues`,
  `rxmStack` and `rxmHeap` (`web/src/rxm-view.ts`) build.
- `LEG_PANELS` (`web/src/panes.ts`), `PANE_BUILD` and `buildPane` (`web/src/pane-host.ts`) build each view from tables.
- `LEG_DISPLAY` (`web/src/workspace.ts`) stores the λ and TM views' display settings through one table.

**The closing commits.**

- `cf16caf` writes the comment budget (below).
- `d712dc7` fixes the whole-branch review's one Important finding: a display leg added to `LEG_DISPLAY` passed `tsc` and
  was lost on reload. The stored fields and both prunes now walk the table.
- `c408b98` fixes eight minor findings deferred from the task reviews.
- `3c880f3` fixes the forced-colours race (below).

**This branch added comment lines to `web/src`.** The share fell because code grew faster:

##### THE SEVEN DEPARTURES FROM THE DESIGN

From the plan's section of that name. Line numbers are at `6b77731`.

| Design says | The branch does | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| §5.3: the toggles are generated and `index.html` "keeps a container only" | The source file keeps the container and one slot comment. The buttons are generated from the tables at **build time**, not at run time. | The view layouts spec moved them into the markup because building them after the wasm loaded moved four controls right by 147.5 to 154.0 px (`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-11-view-layouts-design.md:500-502`, `:1073`). `web/tests/browser/view-toggles-first-paint.test.ts` holds that. |
| §5.2: `ListingPanel`, with "both use the extractions" | Two layers. `followedGridPanel` (the grid, its panel and the re-attach) is used by both views. `ListingPanel` sits on it and is used by rxm alone. | TM's rule table has no listing or labels: its rows are `StateIndex`'s states and rules (`web/src/tm-pane.ts:269-286`). What the two share is `web/src/rxm-pane.ts:141-181` against `web/src/tm-pane.ts:250-310`. |
| §5.2: "The heap panel reads the heap core's tagged view", with `registerRows`, `calleeOf` and `wordText` passed in | The panels take finished text rows. Pure builders in `rxm-view.ts` call those three. | The tags reach the web only as `RxmCell` and `RxmBox` windows on `RxmState` (`crates/redextape-core/src/viewmodel.rs:799-817`). native-rt's heap is `Heap<NoTags>` (`crates/redextape-native-rt/src/lib.rs:35`), so a later native pane would have no tags to pass. |
| §5.4: `link-wiring.ts`, `draw.ts` and `link-status.ts` fan out over a table | A fourth fan-out moves too: `main.ts`'s direct `setLink([], false)` calls go into `clearLink`. | `web/src/main.ts:2836-2837`. Left alone, a new leg would keep its marks on a keystroke. |
| §5.2: "`listingRows` and `programRows` become one" | One walker, `placeLabels`, under both. The two keep their names. | `programRows` adds a tier gate, a `steps` row and a runtime tail (`web/src/program-level.ts:39`, `:41-44`, `:52-55`) that a listing has no use for. |
| §5.3: unit tests of `defaultArrangement` over synthetic lists of 5 to 7 | The tests go through `gridArrangement`, over 5 to 9 views. | `defaultArrangement` takes `PaneKind[]` and filters by `KIND_ORDER` (`web/src/layout.ts:139`), so a synthetic kind would be dropped. |
| §5.3: tests that pin four "derive from the tables" | Most do. The ones that pin the user's order keep their literals. | A derived line follows the table "right or wrong" (`web/tests/node/view-keys.test.ts:49`), so deriving them would blind the tests to #186's order. |

##### THE FORCED-COLOURS RACE

The case "tells a pressed toggle from one that is not in forced colours" in `web/tests/browser/first-load-views.test.ts`
failed the gate's first coverage run at `c408b98`, reading `dashed Highlight` on the λ toggle.

**The root cause is a race in the test, and it was present on the base.** The pointer stays where the test file before
this one left it, and in forced colours Chromium edges a hovered button in `Highlight`. So the case failed whenever an
earlier file left the pointer on the toggle it read. `3c880f3` moves the pointer off the toggles and `+ view` and waits
until none of them is hovered. It changes no product code.

| Runs that failed | `c408b98`, before the fix | `6b77731`, the base | With the fix |
|---|---|---|---|
| A scratch file parks the pointer on the λ toggle first | 10 of 10 | 10 of 10 | 0 of 10 |
| A scratch file parks the pointer away from the toggles first | 0 of 10 | 0 of 10 | 0 of 10 |
| 14 browser files in shuffled order, seeds 1 to 12, one worker | 7 of 12 | 7 of 12 | 0 of 12 |

##### WHAT THIS DID NOT CLOSE

- **§7.2 is not settled.** The timing under VERIFICATION is inconclusive, so a slowdown could still be present.
  `programRows.200.p95_us` leans from 2.8 to 3.0 µs across the 12 clean runs, and that path did change: `programRows`
  now calls `placeLabels` with two callbacks where the base had the loop inline. A firmer answer needs a quiet machine.
- **M1, known work for the CLIF view's design: a new linked leg's click is wired by hand.** `LINKED` drives only the
  outbound half of a link. A new leg's rows get no click handler until someone widens the `slot.binding.leg === 'rxm'`
  spread at `web/src/transport.ts:526`, and `linkInstr` (`web/src/link-wiring.ts:308`) always records origin `'rxm'`.
- **M2, known work for the CLIF view's design: the pc stops at the `Pin`.** `rows(l: Link)`
  (`web/src/linked-legs.ts:31`) receives only the `Link`, so the first view that marks one instruction must change that
  signature and its callers.
- **M3: `web/src/draw.ts` asks `isLinkedLeg` three times for one pane** (lines 216, 230 and 255). It is left alone
  because it is on the per-frame path the timing measured.
- **`normaliseWorkspace`'s display prune, `web/src/main.ts:1376`.** No browser test run against it caught its removal:
  45 of the 46 files chosen for arrangements, parking and display passed, and the other 190 were not run against it. The
  190 are the rest of the `browser` project's 236 files. The one failure was the forced-colours case, and the same
  sabotage at the base passed the 45 of those files that exist there. The helper it calls, `withLegDisplaysKept`, is
  held by node tests.
- **Playwright could not click a TM copy's editor with four views at 1800 x 1300**, on the base as well. The cause was
  not investigated. The walkthrough's item 6 edits each copy with two views on screen instead.
- **The header moves as the fonts arrive**, on the base as well: `#views-shown` shifts under 2 px and widens by up to 6
  px.
- **Firefox failed these tests at `6b77731` and on this branch when Tasks 4, 5, 12 and 13 ran them, each on that task's
  tree. None was re-run at this head.** They come from the browser files each task listed. Neither
  `scripts/check-all.sh` nor CI runs Firefox, and the whole Firefox tier was not run here.

| File | Tests failing | Runs |
|---|---|---|
| `view-keys.test.ts` | 16, 18, 17 and 17 on the branch; 16, 16, 17 and 17 at the base. The set varies from run to run, and every name that failed on the branch also failed at the base at least once | 4 a side |
| `virtual-grid.test.ts` | 8 | 1 a side |
| `panel-boundaries.test.ts` | 3 | 1 a side |
| `follow-kept.test.ts` | 2 | 1 a side |
| `tm-follow-clamp.test.ts` | 2 | 1 a side |
| `app.test.ts` | 1 | 1 a side |
| `controls-gate.test.ts` | 1 | 4 a side |

- **Why one coverage run at this head could not load a test file is not known.** VERIFICATION gives the run.
- **The header's width with a fifth toggle.** The view layouts spec's §6.1 measured Instrument's header at 1280 px with
  6.0 px to spare at its widest, on the joined buttons that the view switcher restyle has since replaced. This PR adds
  no kind, so nothing here measures a fifth.
- **A default grid can go under `MIN_VIEW_PX`.** Five to nine views take three lines, which need 480 px at the 160 px
  floor, and a default arrangement does not apply that floor, so a narrower area gets views under it. No page can show
  five kinds yet.
- **`pin.pc` has no reader yet.** §5.4 carries it for later views.

##### VERIFICATION

**§7.2, the timing, measured at `f7ce15d`: INCONCLUSIVE.** Task 16 timed `draw()` and `programRows`, the paths this PR
moves. §7.2's rxm, native and compile-time measurements were not run, because no `crates/` or worker file changed. The
machine is an AMD Ryzen 9 9950X3D, 16 cores and 32 threads, with 60 GiB of RAM, on Linux 7.3.4-arch1-2, Node v26.13.1
and Chromium through Playwright 1.64.1. Each run was pinned with `taskset -c 8-15,24-31`. Both sides used the same wasm
and glue. The record is `$R/timing.md`, and `$S/task-16-verify.md` is its independent check.

```
python3 -I $R/ab/instrument.py <each worktree>
zsh -f $R/ab/run-unit3.zsh r2 8                       # the same for r3
python3 -I $R/ab/cmp3.py $R/ab/rounds/r2 $R/ab/rounds/r3   # r2 and r3 alone, then pooled
```

A figure flags when the final median exceeds the base median by more than the base's spread, its largest run less its
smallest. Pooled over the 16 pairs:

```
  figure                                base    spread       final   ratio
  programRows.200.median_us            2.600     1.000       2.600   1.000
  programRows.200.p95_us               2.900     4.400       3.000   1.034
  programRows.2000.median_us          31.667    28.333      30.833   0.974
  programRows.2000.p95_us             35.000    50.000      33.333   0.952
  programRows.20000.median_us        475.000    50.000     450.000   0.947
  programRows.20000.p95_us           537.500   400.000     512.500   0.953
  draw.median_ms                       3.650     2.200       3.600   0.986
  draw.p95_ms                          5.000    10.200       4.900   0.980
FLAGGED (pooled) 0 of 8
```

- **0 of 8 figures flagged** in r2, in r3 and pooled.
- **Only 12 of the 32 compared runs were clean** (5 of 16 in r2, 7 of 16 in r3), and **only 4 of the 16 pairs** had both
  runs clean: r2 pair 1 and r3 pairs 2, 3 and 5. A clean run had every 1-second `vmstat` line, from 1 s before it to 1 s
  after it, at us+sy of at most 20 and r of at most 8.
- **That test reads the CPU and the run queue only.** 3 of the 4 clean pairs include a run paging at 20 MiB/s or more:
  r2 pair 1's final run at 20.4 MiB/s in, r3 pair 2's base run at 20.5 MiB/s out, and r3 pair 5's runs at 25.3 and 34.2
  MiB/s out.
- **20 of the 32 compared runs had a busy second.** Over the limit were 24.5% of r2's whole window (131 of 534 s), 28.6%
  of r3's whole window (364 of 1,272 s) and 20.6% of the seconds inside the 32 compared runs (180 of 873 s).
- **The busy runs widened the rule's threshold.** Pooled `draw.median_ms` has a spread of 2.200 ms on 3.650 ms, so a
  rise of up to about 60% could not have flagged. The same reading is 204.0% for `draw.p95_ms` and 151.7% for
  `programRows.200.p95_us`.
- **The 4 clean pairs, shown and not the verdict:** `draw.median_ms` is 3.300 ms at the base and 3.350 ms on the branch,
  and 1 of 8 figures flags, `programRows.200.p95_us`. Across the 12 clean runs that figure is 2.8 µs in all 5 base runs,
  and 2.8, 2.8, 3.0, 3.2, 3.0, 3.0 and 2.8 µs in the 7 on the branch.
- **What must not vary did not**, across all 36 runs with the warm-ups: 831 frames drawn, TM step 69,008 and the pin
  held at the end.
- **The timing was not repeated after `f7ce15d`.** The later commits leave `draw.ts` and `program-level.ts` alone, and
  in `label-rows.ts` they change only a doc comment.

#### A VIEW WHOSE ID IS `__proto__` STORES NO DISPLAY SETTING AGAIN, AND THREE BEHAVIOURS #187 MOVED HAVE TESTS (2026-11-19, branch `ir-panes-minors`, `ed94dd9..bf8a532`, 2 commits, plus this entry and the commits that correct it)

The second whole-branch review of #187 left two Minor findings that did not hold up its merge, M1 and M2 in
`~/temp/redextape-ir-panes/.superpowers/sdd/2026-11-18-ir-views-pr4-panes-layout-links/final-review-2.md`. This branch
closes both. The lane's record is `~/temp/redextape-ir-panes-minors-record/`, `$R` below.

##### WHAT CHANGED

**`08cfb91`, M1.** At `6b77731`, `serializeWorkspace` built each display field by assignment, so an entry for a view whose
id is `__proto__` set the object's prototype and wrote no key. #187 builds the fields with `Object.fromEntries`, which
writes an own key. `serializeWorkspace` in `web/src/workspace.ts` now leaves that id out of `display` and `tmDisplay`, and
every other id stores as it did. The check is there and not in `keptLegDisplays`, because `withLegDisplaysKept` shares that
helper and both prunes in memory, on a close and on a normalise, kept such an entry at `6b77731`. New cases, one a leg,
hold `withLegDisplaysKept` to that.

**Parsing did not change.** `parseWorkspace` read 7 stored shapes with an own `__proto__` key alike at `6b77731` and at
`ed94dd9`. With a leaf of that id and a valid entry, in either field, it accepts the workspace, the entry becomes the
parsed object's prototype and not an entry of it, and writing the workspace again stores no key. With no leaf of that
id, or with a malformed entry, it refuses the workspace.

**`bf8a532`, M2.** `web/tests/node/rxm-view.test.ts` pins that a frame whose callee is unknown reads `?`, for a return pc
that follows no call and for one past the listing. `web/tests/browser/rxm-pane.test.ts` holds a link and a running focus,
asserts that the rows draw both, sets a new program and asserts that the rows draw neither.

##### WHAT THIS DID NOT CLOSE

- **The §7.2 timing from #187 stays inconclusive.** This branch measured no timing, so that entry's verdict stands.
- **A view whose id is `__proto__` keeps no display setting across a reload,** as at `6b77731`. This branch restores that
  result and does not make such a setting persist.
- **Not run on this branch:** the rest of the browser tier, Firefox beyond `rxm-pane.test.ts`, coverage,
  `scripts/check-all.sh`, `scripts/check-slow.sh`, the app build and the Docker image. The sabotages of the browser
  case ran in Chromium.

#### CLIF VIEW PR 1: THE PACKAGE, NO UI (2026-11-19, branch `clif-view`, `2cf0de1..fa6a220`, 18 commits, plus this entry and the commits that correct it)

**Spec §7.1** (`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-18-clif-view-design.md`): the CLIF view's first pull request, which lands
§5 in full with the build, CI and licence wiring, and adds no UI. The plan is
`docs/superpowers/plans/2026-11-19-clif-view-pr1-package.md`, committed as `28f6250`, the range's first commit. Its 13
tasks ran one subagent each, in the order 1 to 8, 10, 9, 11, 12, 13: Task 9's `ClifInput` deserialises `Ty`, whose serde
derive is Task 10's. Task 12 measured and committed nothing. The whole-branch review's fixes are `0d2b274` to `4aaf6c2`,
and `fa6a220`, the last code commit, corrects a doc comment after them. Task 13's comment budget had nothing to write.
No view changes; `web/src/third-party-licences.json` gains 27 entries for the crates `pkg-clif/` bundles. The lane's
record is `~/temp/redextape-clif-view-record/`, `$R` below. Its task briefs, reports and reviews are in `$R/sdd/`, and
Task 12's figures in `$R/measurements.md`.

##### WHAT CHANGED

**Cranelift 0.137.2 (§5.1), `589fbce`.** Every `cranelift-*` requirement in `crates/redextape-native/Cargo.toml` moves
from 0.137 to 0.137.2, the version `cranelift-interpreter` is published at. The lock moves the 16 `cranelift-*` crates,
and `wasmtime-internal-core` and `wasmtime-internal-jit-icache-coherence` from 50.0.1 to 50.0.2. No `.clif`, `.ll` or
`.opt.ll` snapshot changed, and the x86-64 size baseline changed only its `# cranelift:` line.

**Value labels (§5.2), `669c169`.** Core's `tm::rxm` gains `reg_label` and `label_reg` beside `reg_str`: `rr` is 0,
`a<n>` is 1 + 2n and `r<n>` is 2 + 2n. `build_clif` alone calls `collect_debug_info`, and codegen labels a value where
`read_reg`, `write_reg` and the prologue read or define a register. A test holds that the module paths collect none.

**The optimised listing without an ISA (§5.3), `c96ece8`.** `build_listing(prog, Listing)` in `redextape-native` under
`clif`: `AsBuilt` is `build_clif` under `isa_free_config()`, and `Optimised` runs `Context::optimize`'s steps on each
function with plain `Flags` that set only `opt_level = speed`. `target-lexicon` 0.13.6 joins under `clif` (the lock had
0.13.5). A test holds both listings equal to the snapshot sections for all 72 corpus programs, the optimised one to
both targets' `speed: optimised`.

**One runtime (§5.4), `5be46f9`.** native-rt's `Runtime<T: Tags = NoTags>` makes its methods public. `cons`, `new_box`
and `box_set` take `(word, tag)` pairs, the reads still return the bare word, and `heap()` gives the heap with its tags.
`raise_cap(caps, Tripped)` undoes the tripping call's own count and clears the stop. The disassembled `rt_*` bodies in
native-rt's staticlib, 12 symbols over 949 lines, are identical before and after.

**The stepper (§5.5), `7cff098`.** A new rlib, `crates/redextape-clif`. `Stepper` runs one CLIF instruction at a time
with `cranelift_interpreter::step::step`, keeps its own frames, and answers the 11 runtime imports through
`Runtime<VecTags<WordTag>>`, telling them apart by `RtFn::ALL`. A run ends `Ran`, `Fault` (at the pc of the call that
faulted), `Capped`, `Trap` or `Broken`. `tests/agreement.rs` holds its end equal to the JIT's (`compile_and_run` at O0)
in both listings: all 72 snapshot programs at tight caps, the 67 that are not `measure-*` at default caps, and 64 of the
native oracle's random programs. The slow tier runs the `measure-*` programs at default caps.

**The frame (§5.5), `8715d8c`.** `Stepper::state` gives a `ClifState`: the frame's values with the registers their
labels name and their tags, the call stack, and the heap's cells and boxes. The tag rule is written once, beside the
stepper's value tracking. `RxmState::window`'s cell and box code moves into core's `heap_cells` and `heap_boxes`, which
both legs call.

**Caps and frame memory (§5.4, §5.5), `bfe305c`.** A call that would take the frames calls have pushed past `caps.mem`
stops the run at `Capped(Mem)` before it pushes, counting `FRAME_BYTES_PER_VALUE`, 33 B, per value. A cap stop pauses
at the call that tripped it, and `raise_caps` continues it: the continued run reaches the end, at the step, that a
fresh run under the raised caps reaches.

**Listing rows (§5.5), `2d29f04`.** `listing(funcs, names)` gives a `ClifListing` whose rows come from a `FuncWriter`
that hands each line to Cranelift's `PlainWriter`. Each row has its kind (function, declaration, blank, block,
instruction, alias or close), its indent, its pc in decimal and, for an instruction, its `ClifAt`. The rows joined, each
pc put back as `@xxxx`, equal `func.display()` for every corpus program in both listings.

**The `Program` crossing (§5.6), `fd06944` and `ea8ba85`.** `Ty` derives serde under core's `serde` feature, and
`pkg/`'s session gains `clifInput()`: the program the rxm leg runs, its type and compile's caps, with numbers past 2^53
as `BigInt`, or `null` when the rxm leg declined. `ea8ba85` writes `None` as `null`, as `redextape_wire::to_value`
does.

**The leg (§5.5), `2ea8669`.** `ClifLeg` has `RxmLeg`'s shape: `new` builds the listing and opens a cursor and a scout,
`find_end(budget)` runs the scout in chunks, and `status`, `rewind`, `step`, `state`, `value`, `raise_cap` and
`listing` serve the view. The end value decodes with the rxm leg's decoder, `tm::decode_rxm_ty`. `self_cell` 1.3.0
lets the leg own the functions its steppers borrow.

**The package (§6's build wiring), `f1dcecb` and `28ae00c`.** A new cdylib, `crates/redextape-clif-wasm`, exports
`ClifSession` into `pkg-clif/`, built by `pnpm run build:clif-wasm` beside `pkg-lsp/`. The wiring: the workspace
members, `.gitignore`, `web/package.json`'s `build`, the Dockerfile's first two stages, CI's `web` job, a wasm32 row in
`scripts/check-all.sh`, the comment budget, `.pre-commit-config.yaml`, `docs/development.md` and `docs/architecture.md`.
`web/scripts/licences.ts` reads `pkg-clif/` as a third build. `cranelift-assembler-x64`, `cranelift-bitset` and
`wasmtime-internal-core` publish no licence file, so the Apache-2.0 WITH LLVM-exception text their siblings ship is
committed once, as `web/scripts/crate-licences/wasmtime/LICENSE`, and mapped to those three.
`web/tests/node/clif-package.test.ts` runs the real wasm32 build in node: fact's value and steps in both listings,
fact's listings equal to its snapshot sections, `head(nil)`'s fault, a word past 2^53 crossing from `pkg/`, the two
errors `new` throws, and the `null` input. `28ae00c` corrects that test's header.

**The whole-branch review's fixes, `0d2b274` to `4aaf6c2`.** The leg's `total_steps` gives the cursor's steps once the
cursor has ended at any end but a pause, so a worker that never sends the scout ahead still learns the run's length.
`stored_tag` asks `Runtime::faulted` whether the run has stopped instead of restating native-rt's rule, and a const
assert holds a frame value at 33 B on wasm32 too. `redextape-clif-wasm` builds as a cdylib alone, and the licences
generator throws when a crate its `CRATE_LICENCES` map names ships a licence file of its own. New tests read
`partition`'s names off the leg's listing and read the word past 2^53 back out of `state()` in node. `fa6a220` makes
`ClifLeg::status`'s doc say what the `total_steps` field's doc says.

##### DECISIONS

**Q1, answered by the user on 2026-11-19: frame memory counts bytes.** The rxm cursor's `caps.mem` counts words; the
stepper holds the bytes of its pushed frames to it.

**The plan's departures from the brief** (`$R/plan-brief.md`):

| The brief says | PR 1 does | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `raise_cap(&mut self, caps, tripped: RtFn)` | `raise_cap(&mut self, caps: Caps, tripped: Tripped)`, with native-rt's own `Tripped { Tick, Enter, Alloc }`; the stepper maps `RtFn` to it | `RtFn` lives in `redextape-native`, which depends on native-rt |
| the methods the `rt_*` wrap become public, with tags | `cons`, `new_box` and `box_set` take `(word, tag)` pairs; `head`, `tail` and `box_get` return the bare word, and the stepper reads a read's tag from `heap()` | in the probe, reads returning pairs changed the compiled `rt_head`, `rt_tail` and `rt_box_get`; bare-word reads left all 12 `rt_*` bodies identical |
| frame memory "32 B x num_values per frame" | 33 B per value, `size_of::<Option<DataValue>>() + size_of::<Option<WordTag>>()`; only frames a call pushed count, never main's | the stepper keeps a tag-or-unset byte per value; rxm's `caps.mem` counts saved frames, not the running one |
| JIT agreement at default caps over every corpus program | the five `measure-*` programs at default caps run in the slow tier, the rest in the fast tier | in the probe's dev profile the default-caps tally took 58.0 s, 41.5 s of it `measure-loop1000000` |

**Rulings while it ran** (`$R/progress.md`): Task 10 ran before Task 9; the licence text above for the three crates
with none; `clif-package.test.ts` sends its word past 2^53 as `{ let mut x = 1; let x = 18446744073709551615; x + 1 }`,
because `pkg/`'s compile aborts on the plain `18446744073709551615 + 1`; §7's Rust tests read as below; and
`snapshots/llvm-version.txt` stays as `main` has it. The last three are under WHAT THIS DID NOT CLOSE.

##### SPEED AND SIZE

Task 12's figures, `$R/measurements.md`, taken at `28ae00c`, before the review's fixes, with rustc 1.100.0, wasm-pack
0.15.0 (CI and the Dockerfile pin 0.15.1), wasm-opt 130, wasm-bindgen 0.2.130 and node v26.13.1. **The machine was never
quiet**: the timed passes ran at a one-minute load average of 43.69 to 55.54, with other lanes' builds and tests at full
CPU. The sizes, the step counts and the CLIF-to-rxm ratios are the firm figures. **The absolute steps per second were
taken under that load**: a CLIF median moved by up to 1.32x between the two passes, an rxm median by up to 3.3x.

**`pkg-clif/` at `28ae00c`: 1,256,487 B raw, 391,100 B gzip -9**, 2.6 times the spike's ~150 KB. By retained size, from
twiggy's dominator tree on a named twin that is byte-identical to the shipped file without `-g` (`$R/twiggy.txt`):

##### WHAT THIS DID NOT CLOSE

- **§6 apart from its build wiring is PR 2**, with §8's checks that need it: no fetch without intent, the recording,
  the links and the hot paths.
- **TypeScript bindings for the CLIF types** (`ClifListing`, `ClifState`, `ClifStatus` and the rest) are not generated.
- **Whether the CLIF leg reports its end at compile or when the recording reaches it** is now decidable from the speed:
  its run-ahead is 15 to 78 times the rxm leg's in wasm. The leg reports its length once the cursor reaches the end, and
  a chunked scout finds it sooner; PR 2 chooses how far the worker runs ahead.
- **`pkg-clif/` is 391,100 B gzip (391,404 B at `4aaf6c2`) against the spike's ~150 KB.** `ClifLeg::new` retains 59%,
  of it the e-graph optimiser's `insert_pure_enode` 26%; `Stepper::step` 15%; the verifier 5%, on under plain `Flags`.
- **At default caps `loop1000000` ends `Unfinished` in the rxm leg but runs to its end in the CLIF leg**, whose steps
  cap counts `rt_tick` calls as the JIT does. So the CLIF leg's run-ahead is bounded only by the tick cap: a loop of
  this shape that reaches 5,000,000 ticks would take about 145 M CLIF steps as built, some 13 s in wasm at 11 M
  steps/s. That is an extrapolation from this program, not a measurement.
- **A number literal of 33,554,431 (2^25 − 1) or more aborts `pkg/`'s compile on `main`**: `33554431 + 1` throws
  `RuntimeError: unreachable` in node. The λ backend is the likely cause, not traced. It needs a separate fix.
- **No Rust browser-tier test.** Spec §7's "tests in Rust (native and wasm32)" is met by the wasm32 `cargo check` rows
  and the node test, which runs the real wasm32 build.
- **`snapshots/llvm-version.txt` records 23.1.4 while this machine has LLVM 23.1.5**, under which every `.ll` and
  `.opt.ll` snapshot is identical. Updating it is a change for `main`.
- **Tests call `run(u64::MAX)` in 14 places**, so a regression that never ends a run hangs them instead of failing:
  nothing times a test out.
- **`pkg-clif/` exports native-rt's 12 `rt_*` symbols**, harmless but unused. Gating them needs a change to native-rt's
  build outside this PR, a follow-up feature gate.
- **For PR 2: a build failure crosses to the page as `LowerError`'s `Debug` text**, and the Task 6 review's minor 3:
  after a fault, `cons` and `new_box` give a 0 tagged `List` or `Box` while reads in the same state are tagged `Value`,
  so a stopped run's state can show a list-tagged 0 (`$R/sdd/task-6-review-7cff098..8715d8c.md`).
- **For PR 2: if the scout never runs, `rewind()` forgets the length the cursor found**: `total_steps` goes from
  `Some(n)` back to `None`. The worker must keep it or run the scout.
- **The `unused dependency redextape-native-rt` manifest warning** under clippy config D, `redextape-native` with no
  default features, predates this branch.
- **The slow tier's release build warns of an unused import** in `crates/redextape-core/src/tm/encoding/binary.rs`, a
  file this branch does not change.

##### WHAT CHANGED

**Links take their origin and their pin (Task 1), `4849f83`.** A click on an rxm row or a TM state links through the leg
table, records the origin it is given, and each leg's rows receive the pin. Nothing a user sees changes; Task 11's CLIF
links build on it.

**The leg keeps its length and says why it cannot build (Task 2), `2731575` and `31681fc`.** `ClifLeg` hands an unraised
cursor's end to a scout that has not ended, with one `raised: bool`, so `status()` and `value()` keep the run's length
and value across `rewind()`, and a pause under the input's caps gives its length too:
`crates/redextape-clif/tests/leg.rs` reads `Some(1205)` there. `ClifSession`'s constructor throws `decline_reason`'s
sentence for a program the CLIF build cannot lower: `Unsupported`'s own words, or for `TooDeep` the rxm leg's sentence.
`31681fc` makes `ClifLeg::status`'s doc defer to `ClifStatus::total_steps`.

**The CLIF types in TypeScript (Task 3), `f88d1f4` and `e92f4f1`.** `crates/redextape-clif/tests/ts_bindings.rs`
generates the CLIF types into `web/bindings/` as core's and wire's do, and `scripts/build-web-bindings.sh` checks each
of the three crates' output on its own. `web/tests/node/bindings-contract.test.ts` pins the six nullable sites, so a
dropped `| null` reddens `tsc`.

**The toggle, the key and the help (Task 4), `987f744`, `25f2c2e` and `e301060`.** The header gains a fifth `views`
toggle, CLIF, after rxm and off by default, and the key `5`. `KIND_GLOSS.clif` and `web/help.html` name five views, the
switch and the CLIF step cap (**DRAFT** copy). A CLIF view says it is loading. The layout cycle, the default grid and
stored workspaces stay as they were. So that the header keeps one row at 1280 px wherever four toggles kept it, the
toggles keep their padding and the gaps narrow: `.bar`'s column gap is 0.8125rem, Terminal's 0.3125rem over 30rem up to
85rem and Paper's 0.5625rem over 30rem, and the spacer before the run gives one gap back.

**The worker records the CLIF leg (Task 5), `86d7288`.** For a run that shows a CLIF view, the session worker loads
`pkg-clif/`, builds a stepper once the other legs have posted their result, records it under the CLIF leg's own epoch,
posts a second `result` when its first fill stops, and drops it with the session. Nothing waits on it. A CLIF frame is
charged `FRAME_OVERHEAD_BYTES` plus `CLIF_WORD_BYTES`, 60 B, a word, counting each value, each register entry, each
call-stack entry, both halves of each heap cell and each box's content; the fix wave adds a fixed part.

**Rebuild, drop and load on intent (Task 6), `4776da7` and `48508b0`.** A `clif` request rebuilds the stepper for
another listing or a newly shown view, or drops it for a hidden one, under a new epoch; a `clif-load` request loads the
package without recording. A rebuild's result carries the new listing's part, never the old listing's end, and a rebuild
stops the recording in flight.

**The page's side (Task 7), `56f751c` and `d2b0152`.** `ClifSync` (`web/src/clif-sync.ts`) tells the worker whether a
CLIF view is shown and which listing it wants, and a hidden CLIF view's history is dropped. The page fetches `pkg-clif/`
on intent, when the pointer rests on the CLIF toggle or the toggle takes focus (`web/src/clif-intent.ts`), and a run

each run times compile, the λ, rxm and TM legs' recording, the app's reply handling and stepping in the mounted app, 37
timings, and pins 54 fixed counts. By #160's rule a figure flags when head's median of its 8 runs is above base's by

null`), or native compile time, for which no round is prepared; outside `tests/`, the branch changes only

**The CLIF frame charge (I2, `$R/sdd/fix-wave-report.md`)**, Chromium's retained heap per frame against the mean charge,

fewest words a frame, kept 975.3 B a frame against a charge of 791.5 B. With `CLIF_FRAME_BYTES` at 236 B: `map30000`
15,618 frames, a charge of 2,148.5 B against 1,815.0 B kept (18.4% margin); `arithmetic` 20,000 frames, 1,027.5 B

##### WHAT THIS DID NOT CLOSE

- **The CLIF leg's own recording is not timed** (I3): the hot-path A/B's base has no CLIF leg and its head's runs show
  no CLIF view, so recording with one shown is compared with nothing (SPEED AND SIZE).
- **Hidden-recording PR B's `head.shown` overlaps `run.clif` and the `clif` request** (W3): PR B, unbuilt, plans a
  `head.shown` flag, while a run's `clif` and the `clif` request already tell the worker whether a CLIF view is shown.
  CLIF neither waits for it nor builds it; PR B is to fold the two in.
- **The scout is built and never driven** (W6): `findEnd` is never called, so the CLIF leg's length is known only once
  the recording reaches its end.
- **PR 1's review minor 3**: after a fault, `cons` and `new_box` give a 0 tagged `List` or `Box` while reads in the same
  state are tagged `Value`, so a stopped run's state can show a list- or box-tagged 0.
- **The cycle sentence says *all four* beside five views** (G2): CLIF is out of the layout cycle, so its last stop has
  four kinds.
- **`build:bindings` now compiles `redextape-clif`'s dev-dependencies** in CI's `web` job (`redextape-native`'s
  Cranelift JIT, no LLVM): a CI time cost to watch on the first CI run; a feature-gated dev-dependency is the fix if it
  bites.
- **N3: no case reaches a CLIF `[continue]` at a steps cap.** The CLIF steps cap is 5,000,000 loop ticks, which no
  example reaches; Rust's `tests/leg.rs` covers `raise_cap`, not the worker's entry or the page's continue.
- **N5: the CLIF step bar uses two words for the same wait.** A shown CLIF leg with no frames reads *not run* after a
  run that carried a listing, and *step 0 of 0…* when the view was shown after the run.
- **The CLIF charge is proven on per-program means only.** A linear fit of the two programs puts a frame's fixed part at
  about 430 B and a word at about 45 B, against a charge of 300 B and 60 B a word, so a frame of 2 to 4 values may be
  charged less than it keeps. Programs that fill the ring average 30.8 to 102.5 words a frame.
- **47 deferred minors the whole-branch review marked CAN WAIT**, listed in `$R/sdd/final-review.md`.
- **No case holds a pin's scroll through a listing switch**: `clif-link.test.ts` holds that a standing pin is marked
  after the switch, not where the view stands. By reading, the pin's rows no longer scroll off after a switch: the new
  listing lands with its first frames, so the seed's scroll to the pin is held against step 0 until the run moves, where
  the first frames used to release it. A compile's CLIF listing still lands a message before its frames, so a pin made
  before it lands can lose its scroll to step 0 when they come.
- **The CLIF values panel draws no *changed* mark**, though every CLIF step defines a value and loops set them again;
  the rxm view marks the register the last step wrote.
- **No browser case chooses a listing after a link's run is posted and before its `compiled`**:
  `share-open-clif.test.ts`'s case chooses before the run is posted, holding the compile's debounce open. The node cases
  hold `forget` for a held position and for a pending one.
- **The case of a load asked for after a failed one drives the pointer's rest, not focus**: the toggle taking focus
  calls the same `askClifLoad`, and no case fails a load and then focuses the toggle.
- **A Firefox flake in `clif-worker.test.ts`'s `drops the stepper for a request with no listing`**:
  `expected 2 to be less than or equal to 1`, in 2 of 5 runs of the file with the follow-ups' worker, and in 1 of 6 runs
  of its describe with `session-worker.ts` as it was at `eaab70c` against none of 6 with the follow-ups' worker, so it
  predates them. The case allows one CLIF chunk in flight when its `clif` request lands, and two were. No Chromium run
  in `$R/logs/` or `$R/gate/` has shown it, and Firefox is not in CI.
- **A stepper that throws reads as a program the CLIF view declines**: the view gives *No CLIF for this program:* and
  what the stepper threw (*the stepper threw* in `clif-app-threw.test.ts`), since the page shows every `null` listing's
  error that way. Whether a throw should read differently is copy for the user to judge.
- **A stepper throw that crosses a rewind leaves the CLIF view waiting with no reason**, and the readout keeping its
  CLIF rows (`$R/sdd/followup-rereview-r1-c950ed1..1517a04.md`, Out-of-Scope Observations): if the stepper throws in a
  loop chunk after the page has raised the leg's epoch and posted a rewind, the page drops the error listing as stale,
  and the worker then takes the rewind, finds no stepper and sends nothing. It needs a throw no known input produces.
- **Four added lines stay over 120 columns**: doc lines in `app-header.ts` and `share-link.ts`, whose wrap would grow a
  block already over the comment check's cap of 8 lines, and two `it()` names, in `linked-legs.test.ts` and
  `protocol.test.ts`, that biome keeps on their call's line.
- **A listing chosen while a link's program compiles still shows that compile's own frame**: the CLIF view goes from the
  old program's rows to *Loading CLIF…* with its line at *not run*, as every compile with a CLIF view draws until its
  CLIF listing comes, and then to the listing chosen in one frame. Keeping the old program's rows through the compile
  would show them beside the new program's other views (`$R/sdd/flash-report.md`, fix round r1).
- **A CLIF view's step line re-wraps in a narrow view as its text changes**, in any recording, not only a switch's:
  *step 0 of 256…* takes one line where a link's step or *— history is full* takes two, and the listing grows and
  shrinks with it, 279 to 247 px over one recording in a probe (`$R/sdd/flash-report.md`). The TM view's open
  header-wrap item is the same class.
- **No test holds the compact layout's per-function indent**: compact reads each function's instruction indent from its
  first instruction, and every function the cases list is at 36, so a constant 36 would pass them. Every function of
  every real program tried has source locations: `$R/scratch/probe-bare.mjs`, run at `ddfe7de`, read 48 functions over
  the 26 listings of 13 programs, each with its instructions at 36 and one or more carrying a pc
  (`$R/logs/final4-indent-probe.log`).

  in Firefox at the caret assertion its siblings fail at on `main`.
