##### WHAT THIS DID NOT CLOSE

- **The records.** 6 other specs and 10 other plans say `+ view` and stay as written. The view-layouts spec's §20 names
  its own lines that describe the app before the removal, §2.2, §4.5, §5.6 and §12, and those that are records of their
  time, §6's first build, §9.2, §16.2 and §17. Its §1, §4.1 and §6 give four toggles, asm among them, which was out of
  date at `798fa38`, before this branch: the toggles are source, λ, TM, rxm and clif.
- **The plan's *Open, for Davey*** holds nothing unanswered.
- **The view-layouts spec's §16.3**: this branch answers its first point and closes its third. The second was answered
  on 2026-10-12, and the fourth decided that day as left as built, with a change wanted later; the fifth, sixth and
  seventh stand as written.
- **The Firefox failures this branch did not add** (*VERIFICATION*). `controls-gate`'s *walks every toggle, each named
  by its own word* fails at `798fa38` too, at the same assertion; at `26b8e34` the walk runs before the group is back in
  the header, since its `beforeAll` widens the window and does not wait for the move. `view-keys.test.ts`'s caret
  failures move from case to case between runs on either tree. Firefox is not in CI.
- **`clif-app`'s known race**, a follow draw of `VirtualGrid` writing an old scroll position over the test's, failed the
  second coverage run here, as the panels-row lane found it can on main; the third run passed.
- **Widths measured on this machine.** `notice-float`'s 836 and 848 px, and `edge-spacing`'s about scan of 200 to 220
  px, where Task 6's probe found the widths that scan needs at 208 to 211 px in both engines, and at 303 to 305 px in
  Chromium alone. CI's fonts may move either band; each case's precondition fails where its band has moved, as
  `notice-float`'s did at 900.
- **`stage-gestures`' remaining case runs at 414 px**, where the toggles are in the workspace menu; it drives `✕` alone.
- **`view-keys-focus`'s Stage caret case**, *leaves the caret in the source editor, and the key chooses the tabs*,
  fails in Firefox at times: in 1-S12's run and in Task 6's green run (`06-green-firefox.log`), and it passed in Task
  6's rerun (`06-ff-rerun1.log`) and in Task 8's run (`08-firefox.log`). After the rebase it failed in the gate's
  Firefox run and in 2 of 3 runs of its file alone, `$R/rebase-1/ff-view-keys-focus-1.log` to `-3.log`, each time at
  *the caret is not where it was*, as in 1-S12's run and Task 6's green run.
- **What the task reviews and the whole-branch review deferred**, each standing at `11fa301`; the ones Task 11 fixed are
  in *THE REVIEW'S FIXES*:
  - `app-header.ts`'s `wireMenu` leaves `autofocus` on the `source` toggle after a narrow menu opens, where
    `view-header.ts` clears a stale one for the same reason. The review's probe, `$L/review-probe-autofocus.mjs` with
    its log beside it, found that it takes no focus on a later widening in Chromium or Firefox: with the menu opened at
    390 px and shut by a click elsewhere, the focus stayed on `<body>` through 1280, 600 and 1280 px, the attribute
    still on the toggle; shut by `Escape`, the focus stayed on `#workspace`.
  - `view-keys-focus.test.ts`'s `start` widens the window and asserts its precondition without waiting for the group to
    come back to the header, the race in 1-S12's run; `controls-gate`'s wide describe reads the header in the same way
    (*The Firefox failures this branch did not add*).
  - `userSplit` repeats `add-view-floor`'s `openSplit`, and its casts fail as a bare null dereference rather than a
    named throw; `add-view-floor`'s `choosePreset` keeps a `'stage'` no caller passes, its snapshot's `tabs` is always
    empty, and `dragTopDivider`'s doc says "these cases" of one.
  - `share-open-hashchange`'s `pane-2` count, after the id assertion, cannot fail alone and has no message.
  - `scroll-kept-moved-editor`'s and `scroll-kept`'s moved setups are checked in Chromium alone: Firefox fails both
    files at arming, before the split, at their Step 0 too.
  - `stage.test.ts`'s press on the made view's tab may change nothing, the split having focused that view already.
  - `app-header.test.ts`'s λ press in the reset case leaves its precondition true without making it so.
  - `copy-editor-mount.test.ts`'s doc has a "one" whose antecedent is unclear.
  - The design's *Today* says a user on the Stage would have had only *reset preset*; there the `views` switch to tiles
    and a split bring views back too. The design is the approved record and stays as written.
  - `clif-fetch-focus.test.ts`, which this branch did not change, reads that nothing was fetched before `Tab` walks
    through the other toggles to the clif one, and not after: the class of m2, found by Task 11's search for its
    siblings.
  - `tm-view-narrow.test.ts` prints a `console.error` count on every run, on main too.

- **Not run in Firefox**: the browser files outside Task 8's list. Davey has not tried the branch. At 390 px Firefox
  sizes the workspace menu to its `20rem` minimum and the `show` row wraps `clif` under its label, as the preset, step
  controls and *reset preset* rows wrap (`$L/hand/narrow-2-menu-open.png`), which `style.css`'s comment on
  `#workspace-menu` allows for.

#### COPIES ARE GONE FROM THE WEB APP: NO COPY CAN BE MADE, EDITED, SEEN, STORED OR RESTORED, THE APP REMOVES `redextape.buffers` AT EVERY START-UP, AND IT LOADS ONLY THE `redextape` GRAMMAR AND OPENS LSP DOCUMENTS ONLY IN `redextape` (PR 1 of three; 2026-11-23 and 24, branch `remove-copies` on `b627fe3`: the design and the plan in `12e5e2b` and `c6c1758`, then `c6c1758..5ac7e9b`, 38 commits, `0fa0e0d` and its revert `8c6cc4b` among them; this entry, with the design's *As built*, in `515f655..31861cf`; the fixes of the review of the whole branch in `31861cf..752963a`, 13 commits; and this entry brought up to them in the commit after)

Davey said on 2026-11-23: "I don't really want copies anymore as things stand. maybe they can be introduced later again,
however the site is pretty cluttered as is, and I think the main usage of the site right now is just explore the
different compilations of the source code. copies only really makes sense if the site is a better editor of these other
things, and would need essentially an entirely second page/view to do this." The design is
`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-23-remove-copies-design.md`, resting on two surveys of `f3b2bd3`,
`~/temp/redextape-remove-plus-view-record/copies-extent-survey.md` and `copies-survey.md`, whose facts it checked again
at `5b5ef1f`, whose tree is `b627fe3`'s. It takes the whole feature out in three pull requests: this one, the web app's;
PR 2, the Rust and wasm code only copies used; and PR 3, which narrows the code that holds several sessions to the
program's one. Davey chose that split, took every pick the design put to him (Q1 to Q3, *DECISIONS*) and approved the
design on 2026-11-23.

The plan is `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-11-23-remove-copies.md`. `12e5e2b` committed the design and the plan, and
`c6c1758` the rulings on the plan's pre-flight scan. The build is the 54 commits after that, 50 of them under `web/`.
The first 38 are Tasks 1 to 14 in order, a subagent each with a reviewer after it and a fix round where a review asked
for one; from Task 9 each task ran as two dispatches, the removal with its commit, then the wide runs, the sabotages and
what they found. Tasks 1 and 2 moved the tests that borrowed a copy for their content or for a second view onto the
program or a component fixture while copies still existed; Task 3 took the stored copies and added the removal at
start-up; Tasks 4, 5 and 9 each took a way in, rxm, TM and λ, with its view's copy parts; Task 6 took the state
diagram's tiers that only a hand-written machine reached; Task 7 the TM and rxm views' editor panels; Task 8 `copies ▾`;
Task 10 the copy editors and their custody; Task 11 what showed a copy; Task 12 the copies' sessions; Task 13 the
languages; and Task 14 the pages, the docs and the last words. Task 15 ran the full gate and a pass by hand in Firefox,
and changed nothing. Task 16 wrote this entry and *As built* in 3 commits; Task 17 reviewed the whole branch, four
reviewers each over a slice of it; and Task 18 fixed what held of the review in 13 commits, every one under `web/`, ran
the gate again and brought this entry up to the fixes (*WHAT THE WHOLE-BRANCH REVIEW FOUND*). The Rust changes are
comments (*HOW IT IS BUILT*). The lane's record is `~/temp/redextape-remove-copies-record/`, `$R` below; this branch's

##### WHAT CHANGED FOR A PERSON

- **No copy can be made, edited, seen, stored or restored.** The header has no `copies ▾`, so no *new TM copy*, *new rxm
  copy*, delete, undo, pause or resume; the ⋯ menus of the λ, TM and rxm views have no *edit a copy*, *move the editor
  here* or *format*, and the source view's keeps its *format*; the λ view has no *text* panel and the TM and rxm views
  no *text* or *outline* panel; no view reads `copy · not linked`; and the title menu's copy pairs, such as `λ · copy
  1`, the readout's copy rows, the link line's sentences on views of copies, the share popover's "copies are not
  included", the storage line's words on copies and the copies' notices went with them. The program's views are as they
  were: steps, links, the other panels, splits, the Stage, the toggles, the keys, the presets, and the source editor
  with its ⋯ *format*. Titles keep `· program` until PR 3 (Q1).
- **The app removes `redextape.buffers` at every start-up**, silently where the storage refuses. A page that finds the
  key, copies and views bound to them in it, opens every view and every Stage tab on the program, titled `· program`,
  and leaves the other keys as they were. `privacy.html`'s row for the key reads: "Nothing. The app deletes this key
  each time it starts; earlier versions kept the text of copies under it."
- **A share link, stored workspace, remembered arrangement or stored program from before the change loads**, one that
  holds state for the panels that went among them: each panel that stays opens and sizes as stored, and no *text* or
  *outline* panel shows.
- **The notice line's focus falls to *settings*.** A resting storage sentence put away with *hide* from the keyboard
  leaves the focus on `#settings`, drawn, at 390 and at 1280 px, where it went to `copies ▾`'s `#buffers`.
- **The web app loads only the `redextape` grammar and opens LSP documents only in `redextape`.** Its build emits that
  grammar's `.wasm` and the `web-tree-sitter` runtime alone, where it also emitted the λ, TM and rxm grammars'. The
  grammars and the language servers keep all four languages.
- **The pages.** `help.html` drops *edit a copy* and `copies ▾`, titles its keys table *Keys in the source editor* and
  gives the source editor as where F12, Shift+F12 and F2 work; `privacy.html` speaks of one editor; `README.md` says the
  site's editor uses the same server and the `.rxt` grammar; `docs/architecture.md` drops the copy editors and the
  copied text; and the grammar READMEs say the site colours its source editor with the `redextape` grammar and that the
  other three colour other editors.

##### WHAT IT COST

**What only copies did, which nothing replaces** (the design's non-goals: nothing replaces copies, and nothing is kept
for bringing them back):

- a λ term, a Turing machine or an rxm program edited by hand and run, forked from a view or begun blank;
- a machine with no instruction map in the state diagram, whose `name` and `none` tiers only such a machine reached;
- a session beside the program's, and so a view on anything but the program;
- copies kept from one page load to the next.

**The IR views' copies are withdrawn** (Q3): the CLIF copies and the LLVM copies, the second and fifth pieces of
`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-27-ir-views-groundwork-design.md` §9 (`:441`, `:446`), which
`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-18-clif-view-design.md:28` left out of the CLIF view. The next IR piece is §9's third,
machine code, and then the LLVM IR view. Copies, if they return, come back as a page of their own with a design of their
own.

**The code that existed only for copies went**, each piece in the task that removed its last caller (G4):

- whole, in `web/src`: `scratch.ts` (`ScratchBuffers` and the warm-copy cap, `MAX_WARM_BUFFERS`), `buffer-list.ts`

##### HOW IT IS BUILT

- **The removal at start-up** is `forgetCopies(store?: Storage)` in `program-store.ts`, the module that owns the
  program's key, called once at every start-up beside `readProgramStorage` (ruling 3). It reads `localStorage` inside
  its `try`, so a storage that throws on access is silent, as a failed read of the program is. It runs at every
  start-up, not once behind a flag, since a tab still running the previous build can write the key again (the design's
  *Decided*).
- **The machine views.** `MachineViewChrome` stays, shrunk to the header, the step strip, the menu and its choices,
  built with `super(on)`, since `ClifPane` extends it too (ruling 5). The TM, rxm and clif views hold no editor; ↺ on
  each restarts it at step 0 and throws nothing (R1), the custody's flush having been narrowed in Task 7 to the views
  that hold an editor and removed with the custody in Task 10 (ruling 6).
- **A focus move draws at once.** `focus-draw.ts` deferred the draw after a focus move because the move could redraw the
  readout or the inspector at another height; Task 2 found no focus move on the program's views that changes the layout
  (`$S/task-2-report.md`), so Task 5 deleted `focus-press.test.ts`, whose way in was a TM copy, and Task 9 the module
  and its wiring (ruling 10).
- **The state diagram groups a machine's states by instruction alone**: a state built for no instruction is a runtime
  routine's, the level shown is the one chosen, the *program* choice is never disabled, and `isGuard` knows the overflow
  guard by the name the core reserves for it (ruling 7).
- **`readout.ts`'s `data-describes`** reads `program` or `none`, where it read `copy` for no program, which the
  program's own first frames are, so the dim on a running compile still applies to a program alone (ruling 8).
- **The notice line's default fallback is `#settings`**, a header control shown at every width; *hide* on the resting
  sentence has no fallback of its own (ruling 4).
- **The colour registry** takes its language key as a type parameter that defaults to `LanguageId`, which is
  `'redextape'`; the tests that load all four grammars name their own ids and sources (ruling 13), which the compiler
  requires whenever the keys are not the app's (`aff0e1d`).
- **The worker's one-occupant rule** is `claim.ts`, with `tests/node/claim.test.ts`.
- **Rust: comments only.** `crates/redextape-wasm/src/session.rs` is the one Rust file the branch changes, in 4 hunks
  and 29 lines, each a `///` line: `forkable`'s two citations (`3e980c7`) and `rxm-copy-corpus.ts`'s `CASES`
  (`4b71485`), which the attribution check fails once the file or the symbol is gone (ruling 15), and `MAX_FORK_RULES`
  in `MAX_SCRATCH_TM_BYTES`' doc (`9f06b9e`, Task 5's fix round).

##### DECISIONS

**Davey's** (2026-11-23): the whole feature removed, with nothing kept for bringing it back; three pull requests in
order, the design's approach 1, with PR 1 planned as about six tasks that each leave a working app and pass the
pre-commit gate; the code for several sessions stripped in PR 3 rather than kept; Q1, `· program` dropped from the
titles in PR 3; Q2, the README's and the portfolio's images retaken once after PR 1 merges, the NAS upload waiting for
his word; Q3, the IR views' CLIF and LLVM copies withdrawn; the design approved; and the build begun once the plan
needed no decision of his: "if it doesn't need any decisions, you can continue with subagent driven dev". During the
build he made the one comment budget raise the classifier refused, `web/tests` from 0.2262 to 0.2263 in `7354696`, under
the controller's rule below.

**The plan's rulings** (its *Global Constraints*; *As built* in the design says where they part from it):

- **The task split**: fourteen code tasks for the design's six steps, the two moving tasks first, since a removal cannot
  move a case whose way in it has just taken (ruling 1).
- **What is total over `CopyLeg` stayed until Task 12**, since `CopyLeg` and `COPY_LEGS` also type the program's
  recording (ruling 2).
- Rulings 3 to 8, 10 and 13 are under *HOW IT IS BUILT*.
- **A test that put hand-written content in a view through a copy** moved onto a compiled program where one has the
  shape, otherwise onto a component fixture, `tm-fixture.ts`, whose every state carries an instruction (ruling 9).
- **Of the design's 70 whole files**, 4 stay and 3 more go (ruling 11; *THE TESTS*).
- **`rebind`'s same-leg branch for a session other than the view's went in PR 1**, in Task 9, with the cases that made a
  copy only to reach a second session: the pre-flight reversed ruling 12, which had left it for PR 3, since every taker
  of the branch was a copy path. `split`'s `choice.session` stays for PR 3.
- **`wasm-vocabulary.test.ts`** went in Task 12 (ruling 14); CSS went with the markup it styled (ruling 16);
  `state-diagram-local-layout.test.ts`'s case of two two-tape rules and `lsp-hover.test.ts`'s TM-rule case were deleted,
  not moved, since no compiled machine has two two-tape rules from one state to another, and only a copy's editor opened
  a `redextape_tm` document (rulings 17 and 18).
- **The pre-flight's general rules**: every commit fixes the importers, callers, citations and cases its removals break,
  and lowers a comment budget the guard reports stale; each sabotage re-introduces the regression it guards, so that it
  can fire; the old panels' checks read the stored sizes too; and `privacy.html`'s row may say what the key held.

**The controller's rulings during the build** (the ledger, `$S/progress.md`):

- **Task 1.** `state-diagram-local-fan-row` moved onto a fixture of `bmul17.s9.up31`'s neighbourhood built with
  `tm-fixture.ts`, since no walk of a compiled program reaches it at a bearable cost; the fans' label case, which no
  placement edit fails, on `b627fe3`'s setup too, was parked as older than the branch.
- **Task 2.** `retitleStage` and its wiring only retitled a Stage tab for a copy, and went in Task 11.
- **Task 3.** The comment budgets' rule: lower a share the guard reports stale; raise one only when deleted code, not
  added comments, moved it, by exactly the value the guard prints, with the reason in the commit message; an edit the
  classifier refuses goes to Davey.
- **Task 4.** `record-cost.test.ts`'s case (h) fails at `b627fe3` too, its hand-built session having no clif leg, and
  got one in Task 18 (`972392a`).
- **Task 5.** `0fa0e0d`, a fix of an older Firefox bug, an editor's caret left stale when a view key, a divider's drag
  or a Stage switch moves the focus, went out of PR 1: `8c6cc4b` reverts it, and its tree is `3e980c7`'s. It changes
  format-on-blur's timing and wants its own review; the patch and its diagnosis are in `$R/firefox-caret/`. A fix round

##### WHAT THE WHOLE-BRANCH REVIEW FOUND

Task 17 read `b627fe3..31861cf` as four reviewers, each over a slice of the diff with the whole tree to read: A,
`web/src`'s UI; B, its sessions and protocol with the pages, docs, scripts, this entry and *As built*; and C1 and C2,
the two halves of `web/tests`. Their reports are merged into `$L/review.md`: no Critical finding, 5 Important and 27
Minor. Task 18 checked each before acting on it. Every Important one held, and each was fixed test first, in a commit of
its own:

- **A-I1** (`73c3622`): `viewMenu.setFormattable` and its flag, which only a copy's view turned off, and
  `KeymapSetting.unfollow`, whose callers were the copy editors, with docs that described them falsely. *format* is in
  the source view's ⋯ from the start, which a new `view-menu.test.ts` case holds.
- **B-I1** (`0aad7de`): `tm-seed.ts`, `rxm-seed.ts` and `SessionEntry.programs` named a cool or a retire among the ways
  a view comes to show a session, and `hidden.test.ts` a λ view forked to a copy, the sibling the search for the class
  found.
- **B-I2** (`80ce7dc`): `LambdaTrees.prune`, called in each frame, pruned nothing, since no session leaves the registry
  now, and `main.ts`'s `sessions.has` guard was never false. They went with `LambdaTrees.want`'s arm for a session with
  no client and `SessionRegistry.has`, which only such a session reached.
- **C1-I1** (`852a14a`): the case that the source view, closed and brought back by *reset preset*, still holds the
  program went with `two-lambda-panes.test.ts`, and no other case held it. It is in `pane-picker.test.ts` now.
- **C2-I1** (`653c43e`): `storage-blocked.test.ts` had lost its assertion of the views a page whose storage cannot be
  read opens on, `source` and `tm-0`, and holds it again.

With them went what the task reviews had carried to Task 18 (`972392a`, `aff0e1d`, `db81aeb`): `record-cost.test.ts`'s
case (h) builds its session with a clif leg; `session-memory.test.ts`'s wasm case drops an array that held nothing its
readings needed; `lsp-diagnostics.test.ts`'s case that shows every view runs last; `createGrammarRegistry` requires its
sources for keys that are not the app's; `assetsInlineLimit` came back; `main.ts` filters the capture tables on
`LANGUAGE_IDS`; and the comments and the notice that gave an editor per view as their reason give one that holds for the
one source editor. Then the Minor findings (`3e2e22c`, `6d972c0`, `08c1542`, `0b7de71`, `752963a`): comments re-flowed
to 120 columns or re-said, `privacy.html`'s row, `.gitignore`'s clause, the design's header, `unsaved.ts` for the
program's writer alone, the tests' docs, and tests that hold what they name, among them `satisfies
Required<SessionLegs>` on the hand-built sessions of `replies.test.ts` and `record-cost.test.ts`, `view-title.test.ts`'s
ellipsis, and `tm-fixture.ts`, which admits a state billed to no instruction and throws on one billed past the listing.
B M2 and B M3, on this entry and *As built*, are fixed in the commit that brings this entry up to date; C1 M9 waits for
R1-4 (*WHAT THIS DID NOT CLOSE*); `review.md`'s *Answers (Task 18)* gives the reasons. The sabotages of what Task 18
added are its rows of *THE SABOTAGES*.

#198 found why, `~/temp/redextape-duet-patches-record/mc-packages/rebase/ci-flake.md` with its probe and logs beside it,
and found the fault on `main`. The change to intent that removes it was written on the machine code panel's branch,
`machine-code-panel`, in `93c65d2`, with its test, which `54422b8` made hold on a slow machine; this branch takes that
change out on its own so that it can land first, and adds the test-side half. The lane's record is
`~/temp/redextape-duet-patches-record/intent/`, `$R` below; its logs, one line per pair run in `$R/logs/summary.txt`,
and its runners are in `$R/logs/` and `$R/scripts/`, its saved copies and probes in `$R/sabotage/`.

| Commit | What |
|---|---|
| `21dc3fb` | intent starts at the first `pointermove`, a press fetches at once; `clif-intent.test.ts`; the design's D3, §6 and §8 |
| `cc9cff7` | the preconditions in five browser files; `failRequests` replaces an armed abort, and `0` drops one |

##### WHAT SHOWED

- **For a user.** The clif toggle's intent watcher, `watchIntent`, began its 150 ms rest at `pointerenter`. A browser
  sends `pointerenter`, and no `pointermove`, to an element a layout puts under a pointer that has not moved: a page
  opened, or a header rebuilt, where the pointer already rests on the spot the clif toggle is drawn at. So such a page
  fetched `pkg-clif` 150 ms later with nothing asked of it, against the clif view design's G3.
- **In CI.** Run 791 of #198 failed `clif-app-failed.test.ts` at line 43, `timed out after 10000ms waiting for the CLIF
  view to say the load failed`, after 10,363 ms. Here the two files in CI's order in one tab, `--no-cache` and
  `VITEST_MAX_WORKERS=1`, failed 2 of 2 on `e65a533`'s code the same way, at the same line (`before-pair-1.log` and
  `-2.log`).

##### THE MECHANISM

Playwright's mouse belongs to the tab, and no setup file moves it between files. `clif-app-failed-intent.test.ts` ends
with the pointer resting on the clif toggle at 1280 by 1600, and with `--no-cache` vitest runs it before
`clif-app-failed.test.ts`, the larger file first, as a fresh CI container does. The next file draws the same header
under the pointer; Chromium sends the toggle a trusted `pointerenter`, the rest fires during `beforeAll`, and the
session worker loads `pkg-clif` and keeps it. The file then arms one failed request, shows the view and waits for `clif
could not be loaded.`, but the view's load fetches nothing, so the abort is never spent, the notice never comes, and the
unspent abort stays on the tab's browser context for the next file that asks for `pkg-clif`.

##### THE FIX

`watchIntent` (`web/src/clif-intent.ts`) is `93c65d2`'s, byte for byte: the rest starts at the first `pointermove` over
the toggle and lasts until `pointerleave`, a `pointerdown` fetches at once, as a focus does, and `pointerenter` starts
nothing. `main.ts`'s comment on the watcher and the clif view design's D3, §6 *Loading* and §8 *No fetch without
intent* say so; `web/help.html` says nothing of when the package loads, so it is unchanged. With it the pair, run as
above, passed 5 of 5 (`after-pair-1.log` to `-5.log`).

For a user nothing fetches later but the case the fault is. A mouse that moves onto the toggle sends `pointermove`
with its `pointerenter`, so a rest starts when it did. A press starts the load at its `pointerdown`, before the click
shows the view, in a browser that gives a pressed button no focus as in one that does. A touch or a pen's tap sends
`pointerdown` with no move before it, and that starts the load. A focus fetches as before. Only a toggle drawn under a
still pointer waits, until the pointer moves on it or the toggle is pressed or focused, which is what G3 asks.

##### THE TESTS

- **`clif-intent.test.ts`** is the machine code branch's at `f6b5761`, `93c65d2`'s file as `54422b8` left it, with 3
  hunks changed for `main`: the file's doc names the clif view design and the clif toggle where it named the machine
  code panel's design and its target choice, the watched element reads `clif` where it read `arm64`, and the
  still-pointer case's doc names a header rebuilt where it named a view. Its four cases: an element drawn under a still
  pointer fetches nothing, once the browser has been seen to enter it; a pass fetches nothing and a rest fetches, the
  rest's timer faked; a press fetches, counted around its own `pointerdown`; a focus fetches.
- **Preconditions.** `clif-fixture.ts`'s `clifLoads` lists every `clif-load` the ear heard, asked for or answered.
  `clif-app-failed`, `clif-app-failed-intent` and `clif-app-threw` assert it empty before they arm their failure or
  stub, `clif-app-failed` with an ear it did not have; `clif-fetch`'s first case asserts the page asked for no
  `clif-load` before its claim, with a new ear, and its second that nothing was fetched before the pass;
  `clif-fetch-stored` that the page asked for no `clif-load` before it counts the run's fetch. `clif-fetch-focus`,
  `clif-fetch-menu` and `clif-fetch-rest` already asserted that nothing was fetched before their gesture. A file whose
  precondition is spent now fails at once, by its name, not after a 10 s wait.
- **The unspent abort.** `vite.config.ts`'s `failRequests` sets the plan's count where it added to it, so `0` drops an
  abort no request came for, as `stubRequest(match, null)` drops a stub. `clif-app-failed` and
  `clif-app-failed-intent` drop theirs after their case, and `clif-worker` after each of its.

##### WHAT THIS DID NOT CLOSE

- **No file parks the pointer.** A file still inherits the last file's pointer; with this fix a clif toggle drawn under
  it loads nothing, and the five preconditions name a load that came first, but a hover-sensitive check in another file
  could still meet a pointer it did not put there.
- **A toggle moved under a resting pointer.** `watchIntent` keeps its rest until `pointerleave`. Where the toggle
  leaves the header for the workspace menu while the pointer rests on it, as a window narrowed past 40rem does, a
  browser that sends the moved toggle no `pointerleave` leaves the rest standing, and a later rest on it in the menu
  fetches nothing until the press. Clearing the rest at `pointerenter` would close it; it is left as `93c65d2` has it so
  the machine code branch rebases cleanly, and is not measured here.
- **`clif-fetch`'s pass case still races real time.** Its precondition holds the two moves under `INTENT_MS`;
  `54422b8` faked the timer for `clif-intent.test.ts`'s pass, and this file's was not changed.
- **`holdRequests`** leaves a hold no request came for on the context until `releaseRequests` in the same file; no file
  here was checked for one left at its end.
- **Not run here:** CI's LLVM job, `check-slow.sh` and `cargo llvm-cov`. The branch changes nothing under `crates/`.
- **Touch and pen** are held by reading alone: `watchIntent` listens for `pointerdown` whatever the pointer's type, and
  no browser test here taps.

##### WHAT CHANGED

**When a view marks the result.** At the last step of a run that finished with a value, and at no other. A view marks it
when the result reply the page holds is of the generation of the frames the view shows, the leg's recording `ended`, the
view stands on its newest frame, that frame proves the run's end, and the leg's value is a decoded `Value` other than
Unit's `()`. The proof is the frame's own: a TM frame with no rule to fire, an rxm frame with no instruction next, a
clif frame with none next and a returned value, a λ tree at a normal form. The recording's end alone would not do, since
`endOf` maps a cursor still `Running` to `ended`. So nothing is marked for a run stopped by its step cap or a full
history, an overflow, a fault, a trap or a function's result (`Undecodable`). `resultMarked`, in the new
`web/src/result-mark.ts`, decides, and `draw.ts` asks it for every view at every draw, so a result that lands after the
frames marks the views with the draw it brings, and a step back takes the mark away.

**The mark.** An emerald tint, an inset edge of 1px in the same colour, and the word `result` after what it marks,
smaller than the value (0.75em) and in a colour held to the text floor on that tint: in rxm the `rr` register; in clif
the value main returns; in the TM, REG's field 0, its cells in one box; in λ the root, when it is a chip, a numeral or a
Bool, drawn on one row. In λ the edge is an outline, which composes with the link's and the contractum's box-shadows;
the word is generated content with empty alternative text, and `data-marks` says `result:` where the root starts, as it
says the other marks. Where the root is also the contractum or a pinned link, the result's ground is drawn alone, in
place of theirs: the contractum keeps its underline and its words, the link its edge (*The review's fixes*).

**Whole, in the first row.** In rxm's registers panel and clif's values panel the marked row comes first and spans every
column, and its value wraps rather than ending in an ellipsis: the row breaks before what follows the value first, and
inside the value only where the value alone is wider than the row. In clif the registers a value stands for and the word
go in one box, so fact(12)'s result in a one-column panel reads `479001600`, then `rr result` under it. In the TM the
word pushes the rest of REG's cells right. These moves stay inside the view, at the last step only.

**clif's returned value** crosses from Rust as `ClifState::returned`, set only at a run's normal end: the operand of
main's `return`, its aliases followed. sum_to(5) as built ends on `return v9`, with `v9 -> v8`, so its view marks `v8`
and not `v3`, which also stands for `rr`. The frame's values always hold the returned value's row: where the first ones
miss it, it takes the window's last place.

**`little-endian`.** Under the binary encoding, the TM status line ends with ` · little-endian` at the result, a binary
field's leftmost cell being its least significant digit, where the line has room for it: the words are dropped rather
than wrapped, and weighed again when the line's width changes. The encoding is the one the session client posted for the
generation on screen, which it now keeps for each generation it posts (`encodingOf`).

**The colours.** Two palette tokens: `result`, the edge and the colour mixed at 20% into the ground, `--result-bg`; and
`result-word`, the word. Each of the 5 built-in palettes sets both in its light and dark variants, and the stylesheet's
fallback copy holds the default's: the user's emerald, `#047857` light and `#34d399` dark, with the darker `#065f46` for
the light word. Four contrast floors join the others, 39 in all: the edge on `bg` and on `bg-raised` at 3, and the word
at 4.5 on the edge's tint over each, measured on the colour the browser composites. Each colour palette's `result`
stands `BINDER_APART` from every token but `result-word`; Grayscale's is a grey of its own ramp, where the edge and the
word carry the mark. An imported base16 scheme gives both tokens its `base0B`, the green its binders take, so the binder
rule leaves the two out. The import's check names the new floors, and *apply adjusted* walks the word after the
surfaces' foregrounds, against the result its first pass left. A palette imported before this branch is completed from
the scheme colours it stored, and its stored tokens are never repainted; the import dialog's changes panel lists the
colours such a half moved from the tokens the page draws from it, completed ones included.

**The help page** says it after the step controls: which views mark a number, a Bool and a list, a list by its pointer,
that the λ view marks a number or a Bool only on one line, that no view marks a run that ends with `()`, with a function
or with a value too large to print, that the rxm and clif views show the result whole in their first row, and that
`little-endian` means a field's leftmost cell is its least significant digit.

**The tests.** Rust: 2 new tests in `crates/redextape-clif/tests/state.rs`, C1 and C2 below, and the every-step test
checks the window at a normal end. Node: the new `web/tests/node/result-mark.test.ts`, and cases in the contrast,
palette, base16, custom palette, skin, rxm and clif view, tape and session client tests. Browser, 5 new files:
`result-values` (both machine views, drawn by hand), `result-app` (rxm and clif in the app), `result-tm`,
`result-lambda` (the word's ratio read on the ground the page draws among them) and `result-stopped` (the runs that end
without a mark, `()` and a recording said to have ended before its run among them, both themes in every palette, nothing
outside a view moving); a sixth, `result-copy`, went with the copies when main was merged in (*The merge with main*).
`cut-text-app.test.ts`'s clif case now reads fact(12)'s result one step before the end, the latest step at which it is

##### THE REVIEW'S FIXES

The review of the whole branch at `5794b71` (`$L/review.md`) found 3 important issues, the λ word under its floor on a
layered ground, no app case for a run that ends with `()`, and this entry stopping at `eda115d`; 4 minor ones; and, with
the small items the task reviews had left, 16 it ruled must be fixed before merge. Each finding was checked before it
was acted on, and each held. The fixes are 11 commits, each test first where a case could fail first:

- `1428439`, **the λ result's ground, drawn alone.** On a root that was both the result and the contractum, the plan's
  pair rule laid `--result-bg` over the contractum's wash, and the word `result` read below its floor there.
  is_even(6)'s root `true` is the contractum at the λ view's last step, and on that ground the browser read the word at
  4.20:1 in Material light and 3.43:1 in Material dark, under 4.5:1 in 7 of the 10 variants; on a root that is also a
  pinned link, in 6. Now `.term .is-result` draws the result's ground alone, and so does
  `.term .is-result.is-linked.is-contractum`, named since `.term .is-linked.is-contractum` outranks the plain rule, so a
  root that is all three takes it too. The contractum keeps its underline and its words, the link its edge. On the

##### THE MERGE WITH MAIN

While the branch was built, main took #196, `e65a533`, which removed copies from the web app: `git diff --stat b627fe3
e65a533` gives 288 files changed, 5762 insertions and 31613 deletions. `66ab998` merges it into the branch, a merge and
not a rebase, since 26 commits over that deletion would conflict commit after commit and the pull request is squashed.
From `b627fe3`, 18 files were changed both on main, to `e65a533`, and on the branch, to `0776dee`; the merge conflicted
in 6 of them, each settled by reading both sides:

- `web/src/draw.ts`: main's removal of the copies' readings, `unlinked` and `onProgram` stands; the branch's `setResult`
  follows main's `setFocus` with no copy guard, and the λ pass hands the view main's `pin` and the mark. The session
  lookup the guard repeated is made once.
- `web/src/linked-legs.ts`, `web/src/rxm-pane.ts` and `web/src/session-client.ts`: the branch's `setResult` and
  `encodingOf` stay, and main's deletions beside them, `setEditorAvailable`, `setScratch` and `scratch()`, stand.
- `web/src/tm-pane.ts`: main's narrower imports with `resultField` added, `setResult` kept beside main's deletion of
  `setDetached`, and main's status line, without a copy's words, followed by `#fitEndian`.
- This roadmap, rebuilt rather than resolved block by block: main's file whole, then this entry as it was at `0776dee`,
  where the branch had only appended to the file. Main's file is an exact prefix of the result, its last two `####`
  headings are #196's and this entry's, and the entry was byte-equal to `0776dee`'s.

**The copy guard went with the copies.** The plan had `draw.ts` mark no view of a copy, by `unlinked` for the machine
views and `sessions.entryOf(session).detached` for λ, and `result-copy.test.ts`'s 2 cases, an rxm copy and a λ copy at
their run's end, asserted no mark; X-5 and X-5b, each letting `draw.ts` mark a copy, failed one case each. #196 deleted
what the guard read, `SessionEntry.detached` and `unlinked`, and the harness helpers the file used, `copyShown` and
`pickInViewMenu`, and on main `sessions.add` has one caller, which registers the program's session, so no view can show
a copy. The merge commit drops the guard and the file, since the hook's typecheck refuses code that reads what main
deleted, and `6247aff` drops the last sentence that sent a copy's case to that file. `result-lambda` and
`result-stopped` read the λ term by main's `lambdaTerm()?.textContent` where they read `lambdaTermText()`, which main
deleted; both read the text of the same element.

**A view built after the run's end.** Each of `result-copy.test.ts`'s cases also asserted that the program's view, split
from the copy's after the run had ended, marked the result, and no other `result-*` case split a view. `cc9ba69` adds
one to `result-app.test.ts`: at fact(12)'s end it splits the rxm view through its `⋯` menu, pressed as a user presses,
takes the second rxm view to its newest step, `step 181 of 181`, and asserts that it marks `rr`, first, `479001600
result`, across the whole list. It passed in Chromium and in Firefox, 5 tests of 5 in its file. It cannot fail first,
since it holds what was built; S-split, a `draw.ts` that tells a view the mark only when its leg's mark changes, fails
it at `the rows marked`, and the file's other 4 cases pass under it. As `cc9ba69` wrote it, the case took fact(12) from
the case before it, and run alone it failed at a precondition, `step 84 of 84` for `step 181 of 181`, on the run of
sum_to(5) that the file's `beforeAll` compiles. `10f6c0e` has it set that case's viewport and compile fact(12) itself,
as that case does: run alone it passed, 1 test with 4 skipped, and its file 5 of 5, in Chromium and in Firefox, and
S-split, run again on it, fails it at `the rows marked` both run alone and in its file, whose other 4 cases pass under
it.

**The comment budget went out and back.** During the merge the hook's comment guard measured from `b627fe3`, the merge
base before the merge, counted main's deleted test comments as the branch's, and asked for `web/tests`'s share to be
written down from main's 0.2036 to 0.1967, which the merge commit holds. Measured from `e65a533` the branch removes no
comment line in `web/tests`, and a share that fell only as code grew is no gain to lock, so `a76742a` puts main's 0.2036
back and the branch leaves `scripts/comment-budget.json` as main has it.

**What else the merge left.** A sweep of every exported symbol, class member, type field, CSS class, data attribute,
Rust `pub` item and file that `b627fe3` had and `e65a533` lost, against the branch's added lines
(`$L/11-sweep-list.txt`), found the hits above and the plan, whose facts are stated at `b627fe3` (*What this did not
close*). `web/vite.config.ts`'s coverage thresholds are the same on both sides. The merge's checks, the node project
and, in Chromium, the 5 `result-*` files and the 10 that drive the five conflicted modules, passed before the merge

rulings, in the lane's ledger: a merge and not a rebase; the guard's removal inside the merge commit, since a merge
commit that typechecks cannot keep code that reads what main deleted; and main's budget kept.

**The second merge, with `2a96b84`.** After the second review's fixes main took #199, `2a96b84`, which changes 14 files
from `e65a533`, with 381 insertions and 24 deletions, none under `crates/`: `web/src/clif-intent.ts`, `web/src/main.ts`

main's file at `2a96b84` whole, then this entry as it was at `dde2703`. Main's file is an exact prefix of the result,
its last two `####` headings are `2a96b84`'s and this entry's, and the entry was byte-equal to `dde2703`'s. The merge
commit holds that resolution and nothing else, and the hook passed it. What #199 changed in the two files whose tests

##### THE SECOND REVIEW'S FIXES

A second review of the whole branch, at `9f44df0` (`$L/review-pr201.md`), found 2 important issues and 3 minor ones.
Each was checked before it was acted on, and each held, but for the input the first named. The fixes are 3 commits, test
first where a case could fail first, and this entry's commit, which tells the probe:

- `57b7eeb`, **a leg's own value, held by a test.** Nothing failed if `result-mark.ts` read another leg's value: with
  `r.legs[leg].value` read as `r.legs.rxm.value` (12-I1), `result-mark.test.ts` passed 3 of 3 and the 5 `result-*`
  browser files 35 of 35. A TM that outgrows its field halts with no rule to fire and its recording ended while the
  other legs end with the program's value, so its own `Fault` is all that leaves it unmarked. The review named sum_to(5)
  at width 4 as `field-width.test.ts` drives it, but that file's program is `let a = 9; let b = 9; a + b`, and
  sum_to(5)'s width under binary is 4 already, where its TM ends with 15; `9 + 9` at width 4 halts in `overflow` at step
  299 with REG opening on field 0's `#`, while rxm ends with 18. `result-mark.test.ts`'s `reads each leg's own value,
  never another leg's` asks a result whose TM leg is a `Fault` and whose rxm leg is a `Value` about each leg, rxm first
  as the control. `result-stopped.test.ts`'s `marks no TM that halted in overflow, beside an rxm view that marks the
  value` sets the TM's width box to 4 as a user does, asserts the TM view at its newest step in the state `overflow` and
  the rxm view marking `18`, then that the TM view draws no mark, and puts the width back to auto in a `finally`. 12-I1
  fails each at its last assertion.
- `825bbe8`, **an unadjusted stored half, completed and not adjusted.** With `half.adjusted && ` dropped from
  `halfTokens`, every incomplete stored half was adjusted and every test passed, since both unadjusted fixtures, Day and
  Night, pass every floor. `custom-palette.test.ts`'s `completes an unadjusted half from its colours alone, though its
  word fails a floor` takes Closing, whose base0B fails the word's floor, stored as applied and before the result
  tokens, and asserts that both result tokens are its base0B; 12-M2 fails it, alone of the node project, the word

- `ad8fbdb`, **the adjust line's ground for a tinted floor.** For STUCK the import dialog said no lightness passes `on

- **The flake probe** (the review's Important 2 and Minor 3): the pull request's text reported a probe this entry said

  and `clif-app-failed-intent` in Chromium as one vitest run per round and tree, main's `e65a533` and then the branch,

##### THE RULINGS

What the design left to the builder, the plan settled, and these were not reopened:

- **The decision.** `resultMarked(r, leg, state, ended)` is true exactly when `r` is a result of the leg's generation,
  the leg's `done` is `ended`, its play head is on its newest frame, `ended` holds, which is the frame's or the tree's
  own proof of the end, and the leg's value is a `Value` whose text is not `()`. `draw.ts` asks again at every draw;
  `replies.ts`'s `result` arm already calls `draw()`. The plan also had `draw.ts` pass `false` for a view of a copy,
  which went with the copies (*The merge with main*).
- **clif's returned value** is an `Option<u32>` on `ClifState`, set at a `Ran` end only, through `resolve_aliases`, and
  the values window always holds its row.
- **Two tokens, `result` and `result-word`,** appended to `COLOUR_TOKENS`. The ground mixes `result` at `contrast.ts`'s
  `RESULT_TINT`, 0.2, which a palette test holds to the stylesheet's 20%; a floor may name a tint token, and is measured
  on that token composited over its surface, per sRGB channel. The binder rule leaves the two tokens out.
- **rxm and clif.** The result's row first, found in clif by its number, never by an `rr` label; it spans
  `grid-column: 1 / -1`, its edge is an inset box-shadow, since `is-changed` owns the outline, and its `dd` wraps.
- **TM.** `resultField` in `tape.ts`, REG field 0's cells in one `span.tm-result`, and `little-endian` from
  `SessionClient.encodingOf`, kept only where it adds no row to the line and leaves the state name no more cut, decided
  at each status draw and again when the status line's width changes.
- **λ.** `MARKS` gains `'is-result': 'result:'`; the root is marked only as a chip on one row; the edge is an outline;
  pair rules laid the result's ground over the link's and the contractum's, which the review's fix replaced; the word is
  `::after { content: "result" / "" }`.

Rulings made during the build, in the lane's ledger:

- **The floor covers the word alone.** The pre-flight measured the other text on the tint below 4.5:1 and asked the user
  whether the result's own text must meet a floor there; with no answer, the build follows the design, and the design's
  *As built* gives the figures.
- **The design's drawing over the plan's break rule** (Task 3's review). The plan had a result's row break at the space
  before the word first, which drew fact(12) in clif as `479001600 rr`, then `result`; the design draws `479001600`,
  then `rr result`. `9a6ac30` puts the registers and the word in one box, `span.result-tail`.
- **D-3 holds the node test alone** (Task 3's review). At the step before the end the frame already rules the mark out,
  so no app case can see the newest-step condition; the plan's row for D-3 named app cases in error, and nothing below
  rests on D-3 for an app case.
- **The TM's word may give REG's row a scroll bar** with classic scroll bars, at the last step only (Task 4's review):
  accepted, as the design's *As built* says.
- **L3 is drawn by hand** (Task 5's review): no pin in the app reaches sum_to(5)'s root, and the rule L3 checks is the
  same either way.
- **A view still `— recompiling` keeps the old run's mark** (Task 6's review): that step line shows only while every leg
  still holds the old recording's frames, so the mark is the old run's, on its own frame.
- **X-3 must fire** (Task 6's review). The review found that a real ⏭ can bring a new program's views to their end while
  the last program's result is still the one stored; `eda115d` adds a case that holds the result reply back from the app
  there and asserts no view is marked until it lands.

The whole-branch review's findings were ruled on before the fixes (`task-10-findings.md`, in the SDD folder beside the
plan's task briefs):

- **The word on a layered λ ground** (the review's Important 1): of its three remedies, the result's ground drawn alone,
  measured in the browser before the fix, the word's ratio asserted on the ground the page draws, and a sabotage that
  restores the layered rule failing at that ratio.
- **The frame's proof of the end** (Minor 1): a case where one could be made cheaply, and the gap recorded where it
  could not.
- **Of the triage's *may* items** only T4's whole words, A-clif-2's order, its stronger step check and its `finally`,
  and `contrast.test.ts`'s ground were taken; the others, and the *leave* items, stay open (below).

##### WHAT THIS DID NOT CLOSE

- **The rest of the lane,** pull request 3, list results: their heap cells lit, an example whose result is a list, and a
  mark on a λ list result. Until then a list result marks only its pointer word, rxm's `rr`, the clif value and TM field
  0.
- **Squeezed values,** a value cut mid-run while its panel has room, are a pull request of their own, outside this lane.
- **Function results:** every leg answers `Undecodable`, so none is marked. A later feature, λ printing a function
  result's normal form, may change that.
- **The final `halt` or `return` row** of the rxm and clif listings: at the end no listing row is marked, and the
  listing does not scroll there.
- **A TM field wider than the frame's window** is marked where it is on screen; widening the window is not this
  branch's.
- **The result's own text has no floor on its tint** (F5): the user chose on 2026-11-25 to leave it so. The floors
  hold the word alone there. The other text drawn on the tint is held only on the bare surface: the marked value in an
  rxm or clif row and REG's cells in `fg`, rxm's `rr` label and clif's registers in `fg-dim`, and the λ chip in its
  token's colour. Computed in node with `contrast.ts`'s `tinted` and `contrastRatio`, not measured in a browser, these
  have a ratio under 4.5:1 on the tint over `bg` or `bg-raised` (the two in that order): in Material light, the default
  palette, `fg` and `fg-dim` 3.94 and 3.46, `tok-nat` and `tok-bool` 3.93 and 3.45; in Material dark `fg-dim` 3.61 and
  3.00, `tok-nat` and `tok-bool` 4.49 and 3.73; in Grayscale light `fg-dim`, `tok-nat` and `tok-bool` 3.93 and 3.34; in
  Grayscale dark `fg-dim` 3.77 and 2.91, `tok-nat` and `tok-bool` 4.50 and 3.47; in Paper dark `fg-dim` 4.48 and 4.15;
  in Terminal dark `fg-dim` 4.50 and 4.26; in Instrument light `fg-dim` 4.36 over `bg`; in Instrument dark `fg-dim` 4.40
  and 4.03. A floor there changes a ruling: the tint's share, the palette values or the floor table.
- **The λ ground on a root that is also the contractum or a pinned link:** the user confirmed it on 2026-11-25. The
  review's Important 1 was ruled during the build: the result's ground drawn alone there, so the word meets its floor on
  the ground the floors measure, the contractum keeping its underline and its words and the link its edge, rather than
  new floors for the layered grounds, which could move palette colours. Keeping the contractum's wash or the link's
  ground under the result's would cost one stylesheet rule, and on that ground the word reads under its floor in 7 of
  the 10 built-in variants at is_even(6)'s root unless palette colours move (*The review's fixes*).
- **The λ half of the frame's proof:** nothing fails if `draw.ts` passes `true` for `lambdaEnded(treeFor)`. M1-lambda,
  that edit, left `result-stopped` and `result-lambda` passing whole. The λ mark needs a chip at the root, which is a
  normal form, so a tree with a redex next never has one, and what the guard has left to refuse is a stale tree, which
  no case reaches without rebuilding the harness. N2 holds `lambdaEnded` itself, in node.
- **A value too large to print,** `TooLargeToPrint`, has no app case; the wasm tests reach one, with a small DAG that
  decodes to an enormous value. N1 holds that it is unmarked, and the help page says such a run has no mark.
- **With classic scroll bars,** the word can give REG's row a scroll bar at the last step, inside the view. No test
  asserts it. Every Chromium project but `browser-scrollbars` launches with Playwright's `--hide-scrollbars`, under
  which a scroll bar takes no width; `browser-scrollbars` runs the files `SCROLLBAR_FILES` lists,
  `machine-row-scrollbars` and `state-diagram-local-scrollbars`, neither a result case; and in the Firefox projects,
  which pass no such flag, no case reads REG's row for a scroll bar. A fix needs a mechanism that reserves a horizontal
  bar's room, such as a bar always shown on REG's cells, or the word's width held at every step.
- **The small items the review left open,** each a *may* not taken or a *leave*: `controlIn` repeated in `result-app`
  and `cut-text-app`; an ill-typed `ResultLegs` fixture behind `as never` in `result-mark.test.ts`; no test that
  `draw.ts` reads the encoding of the generation on screen; the session client's encodings, which grow by one entry a
  run posted; the `::after` case, which does not assert the empty alternative text; the step helpers copied between the
  `result-*` test files, among them the settings helper `result-lambda` took from `result-stopped` in `1428439`; the X-3
  run, which proves only the λ assertion of its case; X-4, which proves only X5's first assertion; X4's skip of a
  recompiling view, which could assert that view's mark instead; the hold in X-3's case, which lets clif replies arrive
  before the held result; no test reaching `#fitEndian`'s state-name check, which no TM today reaches, since none halts
  on a name long enough; the plan's *settled here*, which still gives the break rule `9a6ac30` replaced, and its facts
  at `b627fe3`, which still name the copy guard, X6, `unlinked`, `setEditorAvailable` and `rxm-copy.test.ts`, the plan
  being a record that the design's *As built* and this entry supersede; `result-stopped`'s case for a recording cut
  short, which leaves the cut armed if it fails before the cut, so that one failure would spread to the cases after it;
  Task 6's report, whose table is stale, a record outside the tree; and Task 8's affected set, run after its commit
  rather than before.

**The clif-app timeouts and #199.** `2a96b84`'s entry tells of a timeout of the same file: #198's CI run 791 failed
`clif-app-failed.test.ts` at line 43, `timed out after 10000ms waiting for the CLIF view to say the load failed`. By its
account `clif-app-failed-intent.test.ts` ends with Playwright's pointer resting on the clif toggle, the next file in the
tab draws the same header under it, the toggle's rest fires during `beforeAll` and the session worker loads `pkg-clif`,
so the view's load fetches nothing, the armed abort is never spent and the notice never comes. #199 starts the rest at
the first `pointermove` over the toggle and has a `pointerdown` fetch at once; has `clif-app-failed`,
`clif-app-failed-intent` and `clif-app-threw` assert that no clif load was asked for or started before they arm their
failure or stub, so that, in its words, "a file whose precondition is spent now fails at once, by its name, not after a
10 s wait"; and has `failRequests` replace an armed abort rather than add to it, with `clif-app-failed` dropping its
unspent one after its case. That is 15 lines in and 2 out in `clif-app-failed.test.ts`, and 13 in and 1 out in
`clif-app-threw.test.ts`. Its entry says the two files in CI's order in one tab failed 2 of 2 on `e65a533`'s code and
passed 5 of 5 with its change; it says nothing of `clif-app-threw` timing out in a whole run, nor of this branch's two
timeouts, so nothing here reads #199 as their cure. Both timeouts, at `ea000dd` and at `a76742a`, and the flake probe,
which ran the branch beside main's `e65a533`, came before #199. The one whole coverage run on the merged tree lost no
test: `clif-app-failed` and `clif-app-threw` passed in it, 1 test each.

well, copied the file back and compared it with `cmp`, on its own task's tree. `$L/01-sab-results.txt` to

#### A CLIF RUN THAT A FAULT STOPPED SHOWS A CONS OR BOX MADE AFTER THE FAULT AS A PLAIN 0, WHERE ITS VALUES PANEL READ `nil` OR `box #0` (2026-11-24, branch `clif-fault-tags`, `b627fe3..26cdc08`, 4 commits, plus this entry, rebased onto `e65a533` as `e65a533..dcdcc3e`; the fixes of the review of the whole branch in `dcdcc3e..0e398a8`, 3 commits, and this entry brought up to them in `10a2bbc`; the fixes of that review's re-review in `10a2bbc..2cc3ec0`, 2 commits; and this entry brought up to them in the commit after)

**This closes PR 1's review minor 3**, which #190's entry, `#### CLIF VIEW PR 2: THE VIEW`, lists under WHAT THIS DID
NOT CLOSE, at line 38683 of this file: "after a fault, `cons` and `new_box` give a 0 tagged `List` or `Box` while reads
in the same state are tagged `Value`, so a stopped run's state can show a list- or box-tagged 0".

The two commits that make the change, `7e79438`, the stepper's rule, and `9068b30`, the web tests, were drafted outside
this repo's usual flow, in a cloud sandbox that had no browser and ran Node 22, and were applied here on `b627fe3`. Here
they were reviewed, each new test was seen to fail without the fix, and the gates CI runs were run (VERIFICATION). The
review found the code right and four minor points, in the tests and in the design's wrapping, which `5476067` and
`26cdc08` fix. The lane's record is `~/temp/redextape-duet-patches-record/fault-tags/`, `$R` below; the review is
`$R/findings.md`.

After #196 merged, the branch was rebased onto `e65a533`, which made those four commits `1066585`, `8020ae2`, `b7c797e`
and `056b8e6`, and this entry `dcdcc3e`; the entry names the commits it was verified at. A review of the whole branch at
`dcdcc3e`, `$R/final-review.md`, found the code and its tests right, and two minor points and a nit: a sentence of this
entry that was false, and web tests whose claim held for almost any row they read. `6a29622`, `82e5666` and `0e398a8`
fix them, and `10a2bbc` brought the entry up to them (*WHAT THE WHOLE-BRANCH REVIEW FOUND*). A re-review of those four
commits at `10a2bbc` closed both points and found one more sentence of the first point's class, in the design, and two
nits, which `e047b6f` and `2cc3ec0` fix and this revision of the entry takes in.

##### WHAT CHANGED

**How it showed.** A callee that faults or trips a cap leaves through its exit block, which returns to its caller, and
the caller runs on to its next guard (`crates/redextape-native/src/lib.rs`, *After a fault*). A `cons` or box right
after such a call runs once the runtime has latched the fault, so `Runtime` allocates nothing and returns 0, and the
stepper tagged that 0 by the import alone, `List` for a cons and `Box` for a box. Built from `b627fe3`'s stepper, the
values panel reads `nil` for `fn f(x) { head(nil) } cons(f(0), nil)`, and `box #0`, a box that does not exist, for
`fn f(x) { head(nil) } let mut v = f(0); let get = |x| v; get(0)`, in both listings.

**The rule.** `Stepper::answer` passes every word a runtime call answers through `answered_tag`, which gives `Value`
once `Runtime::faulted` says the run has stopped, as `stored_tag` did for the three reads alone; `stored_tag` now gives
the tag the heap stores with the word read, and `Value` for a read that faulted. Every import but `rt_box_set` and
`rt_leave`, which answer no word, goes through the rule. A cons or box that the heap cap refuses defines no value, since
the stepper ends the step at the cap before it sets the call's result. `Stepper::raise_caps` clears that stop through
`Runtime::raise_cap`, and the call runs again on the next step, so the repeat keeps its `List` or `Box`. The app's
`[continue]` never repeats it: it calls `ClifLeg::raise_cap`, which raises the steps cap alone and resumes a steps pause
and no other, and a heap pause ends the recording as `heap-full`, which has no continue. The design's §5.4 says the same
in its sentence on tags: "constants and arithmetic make plain numbers, as every runtime call does once a fault or a cap
has stopped the run"; and, since `0e398a8`, that `Stepper::raise_caps` repeats the call a cap refused and that the
view's `[continue]` resumes a steps pause and no other.

##### THE TESTS

- `crates/redextape-clif/tests/state.rs`'s `a_cons_or_box_after_a_fault_is_a_plain_number` builds both programs in both
  listings, runs each to its `Fault`, holds that nothing was allocated, finds the value the cons or box call sets by the
  call itself (`result_of_call`), and holds the four words `(0, Value)` in one assertion, so a failure shows every case
  and listing that fails.
- `tests/state.rs`'s `a_cons_or_box_repeated_after_a_heap_pause_is_a_list_or_box`, from `6a29622`, holds the other side
  of the rule: the same two programs with a callee that does not fault, `fn f(x) { x }`, under a heap cap of 0, in both
  listings. Each must pause at `Capped(Heap)` with the call's value unset; after `raise_caps(DEFAULT_CAPS)` and one
  step, the repeated call's word is `(1, List)` or `(1, Box)`, the four words held in one assertion.
- `stepper.rs`'s unit tests hold the rule's parts apart: `a_read_takes_the_tag_its_cell_stores`,
  `a_faulting_read_is_a_plain_number`, `a_word_answered_while_the_run_goes_on_keeps_its_tag`, and
  `a_word_answered_after_the_run_stopped_is_a_plain_number`, at a fault and at a cap.
- `web/tests/node/clif-fault-tags.test.ts` runs the two programs through `pkg/`'s `clifInput()` and `pkg-clif/`'s
  `ClifSession` in both listings, and holds that `clifValues`, the values panel's reader, gives the value the call set
  the text `0`. `web/tests/node/clif-fault-fixture.ts` holds the two programs, their controls and `madeBy`, which finds
  that value in the listing's rows, the declaration `fn0 = u0:0 sig0` and the call `v15 = call fn0(…)`. It names an
  import by its place in `RtFn`'s order, as the listing does, so a change to that order must change the fixture too. At
  a fault's end nearly every value in `$main` reads `0`, so that `0` cannot show which row was read; since `82e5666`
  each case has a control, the same program with `fn f(x) { x }`, whose call's value must read `#1` or `box #1` in both
  listings, on the row `madeBy` finds; since `2cc3ec0` each control also holds that the row is the one its fault case
  reads, the same value name.
- `web/tests/browser/clif-fault-tags.test.ts` runs the two programs in the app, steps the clif view to the run's end,
  and holds that its values panel reads that value `0`, found in the as-built listing, the one the view opens on. Since
  `82e5666` it runs the two controls after them, which must read `#1` and `box #1`, on their fault cases' rows in the
  as-built listing since `2cc3ec0`; run after, a control cannot leave a `0` for a fault case to pass on.

##### THE SABOTAGES

S1 to SP are the first review's. Each saved the file it edits, `stepper.rs` or, for SP, the browser test, made one edit,
ran, put the file back from the copy and compared it with `cmp`; `$R/fin/sab-restores.txt` has 7 lines that say so. S1
is the fix reverted, `stepper.rs` as on `b627fe3`, so its Rust run holds `b627fe3`'s unit test and not the branch's
four; SA to SE each break one line of the rule. For S1, `pkg-clif/` was built from that stepper, wasm sha256
`ededb92f…`, for the web tests, and built again after the restore, `6d9e3520…`, the hash of the review's first build.

##### THE REVIEW'S FIXES

The review (`$R/findings.md`, *Findings*) found no critical or important point in the code and four minor ones.
`5476067` fixes the first three and `26cdc08` the fourth.

- **M1, a test named for half of what it held.** `a_read_takes_the_tag_its_cell_stores` also held that a faulting read
  is a plain number, and its sibling on `answered_tag` held that a word answered while the run goes on keeps its tag.
  Each of those is now a test of its own, named for it.
- **M2, an assertion after the claim, and loops that stopped at their first case.** The browser test's check that the
  heap panel draws no line came after its claim, so a regression stopped before it, and neither program allocates on
  `b627fe3`'s stepper either; it is gone, and the node test holds that nothing was allocated from the state's counts.
  The Rust and node tests asserted inside their loops, so with the fix reverted the Rust test stopped at the cons as
  built and its box case was never seen to fail. The Rust test now reads every case and listing, and the node test both
  listings, before one assertion.
- **M3, names that said more than the assertions held.** The web tests were named "as a plain 0" and held only that no
  value read as a list or box, which a run that lost the call's value would pass. They now find the call's value and
  hold its text `0`.
- **M4, a short line.** The fix's clause in the design's §5.4 left a 59-character line in a paragraph wrapped near 115
  columns. The paragraph's tail is wrapped again, which also joins a 38-character line it had on `b627fe3`; no word
  changes.

##### WHAT THE WHOLE-BRANCH REVIEW FOUND

The review of `e65a533..dcdcc3e`, a fresh read rather than one leaning on `$R/findings.md`, is `$R/final-review.md`: the
code and its tests right, no critical or important point, and two minor points and a nit. Each was checked again before
it was fixed.

- **M1, a false sentence.** WHAT CHANGED said that `[continue]` repeats a cons or box a cap refused, so the repeat keeps
  its `List` or `Box`, and the pull request's text said so too. A refused cons or box is a heap pause, which the app's
  `[continue]` does not resume (*The rule.*); `Stepper::raise_caps` alone repeats the call, and there the repeat does
  keep its tag, which no test held. *The rule.* says so now; the design's §5.4, which said `[continue]` repeats the call
  a cap refused, says since `0e398a8` that `Stepper::raise_caps` does; and `6a29622` holds the repeat's tags (THE TESTS;
  SR1 and SR2). A search for `continue` in everything the branch adds or changes, and in its first five commits'
  messages, found the repeat put down to `[continue]` in those two places and in the pull request's text, and nowhere
  else. The re-review searched past the branch's changes and found one more in the same design, #189's §8, "`[continue]`
  after each cap resumes to the outcome a run with the raised cap reaches", which since `0e398a8` contradicted §5.4;
  `e047b6f` gives that resume to `Stepper::raise_caps`, which the tests behind §8 call, and says the view's `[continue]`
  does so at a steps pause alone.
- **M2, a claim almost every row met.** At a fault's end nearly every value in `$main` reads `0`, so the web tests' `0`
  could not tell the call's value from its neighbours, and which row they read rested on `madeBy` and the import's place
  in `RtFn`'s order alone; W2 is a wrong row the fault case passed on. `82e5666` adds the controls (THE TESTS), which W1
  and W2 fail and S1b passes.
- **The nit.** The sabotages were a part of VERIFICATION; they have their own section now, as in the two entries before
  this one.

A re-review of `6a29622`, `82e5666`, `0e398a8` and `10a2bbc` at `10a2bbc`, `$R/final-review.md`'s *Re-review at
10a2bbc*, found M1 and M2 closed, re-ran SR2 and the web tests, and found one more phrase and two nits:

- **m1, one more sentence of M1's class**, the design's §8 (M1's bullet above), fixed in `e047b6f`. A sweep of the whole
  design for `[continue]` then checked the three sentences left against `leg.rs` and `record-loop.ts` and kept them:
  §2's "▶ at the end or `[continue]` extends by `EXTEND_STEPS`", on the rxm leg's recording; §4's *End*, "`[continue]`
  works as the rxm view's does for the same cap"; and §10's "`[continue]` behaves as in the rxm view". The other two
  places it appears are the sentences `0e398a8` and `e047b6f` wrote.
- **A helper's doc that said the program was typed.** The browser test's `shownAtEnd` said its program was "typed into
  the app"; the harness's `compile` replaces the editor's text and waits for the build, as `2cc3ec0`'s doc now says.
- **A row no test held.** `82e5666` said the controls read on the row the fault case reads, which held, but only by
  `$main` making the same import calls in both programs. Since `2cc3ec0` each control holds that its call's value name
  is its fault case's, in both listings in the node test and in the as-built listing in the browser test; SM fails it.

#### IN FIREFOX, A VIEW KEY, A DIVIDER'S DRAG OR A STAGE SWITCH MADE WHILE THE SOURCE EDITOR HAS THE FOCUS LEAVES ITS CARET WHERE IT WAS (2026-11-24 and 25, branch `firefox-caret` on `f818cca`, rebased onto it from `e65a533` by way of `2a96b84` and
`f59ef8e`: the fix in `e9415ee`, `6bcae2f` after the rebases, this entry in the two commits after it, and this entry
brought up to the rebases in the commits after those)

In Firefox, a person typing in the source editor who pressed a view key, dragged a divider with the pointer or switched
views in the Stage could find the caret at the start of the text, and the next key they typed went there. Chromium left
the caret where it was. The defect is older than #196: Task 5 of that branch, `remove-copies`, met it in
`view-keys-focus.test.ts`'s Stage case, diagnosed it and wrote the fix as `0fa0e0d`, which `8c6cc4b` took back out of
that branch for a pull request of its own. This branch is `0fa0e0d` applied onto `e65a533` by `git am`, with no conflict
and no change to its code or its message. The diagnosis is
`~/temp/redextape-remove-copies-record/firefox-caret/diagnosis-report.md`; this lane's record is that directory, `$F`
below, and its logs are in `$F/impl/`, `$L` below.

##### THE CAUSE

**Firefox sends no `blur` to an element that leaves the page with the focus.** `layout-view.ts`'s `renderLayout` takes
every host off the page with `root.replaceChildren()`, and `renderStage` moves the shown view's host out of `#views` and
back. `pane-host.ts`'s `keepingFocus` then gives the focus back to the editor by `moveFocus`, which calls CodeMirror's
`focus()`. That writes the state's selection to the page only where it differs from CodeMirror's last reading of the DOM
selection, and only CodeMirror's `blur` handler clears that reading. In Chromium the detach sends the blur. In Firefox
nothing does, so the reading still names the caret while the browser has put the DOM selection at the start of the text,
`focus()` writes nothing, and the next `selectionchange` makes CodeMirror take the start of the text for the user's
caret. Whether a run fails is a race: other work in the rebuild can refresh the reading first, so a case could pass one
run and fail the next.

##### THE FIX

`layout-view.ts`'s `blurEditorIn(root)` blurs the focused editor under `root` before the render takes the views off the
page: in `renderLayout` before `root.replaceChildren()`, and in `renderStage` before the host moves. Every browser then
sends the blur Chromium sends at the detach, and `focus()` writes the state's selection back. It blurs an editor alone:
a divider still on the page takes a `blur` for the end of its keyboard gesture (`separator.ts`'s `commitKeys`), and
would commit it in the middle of the render. The blur falls inside `keepingFocus`'s rebuild, which runs under
`rebuilding`, so a view key and a divider's drag still format nothing with *format on blur* on.

**What changes beyond the case.** In Firefox the editor is now sent a `blur` by every layout render that runs while it
has the focus, as Chromium sends one. So a render outside `keepingFocus` with *format on blur* on now formats the text
in Firefox, as it already did in Chromium.

**The renders checked.** Every render that takes views off the page is `pane-host.ts`'s `applyLayout`, which calls
`renderStage` or `renderLayout`, so the two calls cover them. The app has one editor, the source view's, which `main.ts`
builds, and the pass of `applyLayout` in which a pane's constructor empties its host with `host.replaceChildren(…)`
skips the source leaf. `banner.ts`'s `showBanner` replaces what `#views` holds when the app did not start, and nothing
gives the editor the focus after that, so it needs no blur. `applySwitches` moves the readout's hosts between the strip
and the inspector, and they hold no editor.
