#### TAB AND SHIFT+TAB INDENT IN THE SOURCE EDITOR, AND THE KEYBOARD LEAVES IT BY ESCAPE AND THEN TAB, OR BY CTRL+M (SHIFT+OPTION+M ON A MAC), WHICH THE EDITOR SAYS TO A SCREEN READER AND SHOWS UNDER ITSELF TO A KEYBOARD USER WHO TABBED IN (2026-11-25, branch `editor-tab` on `65392ce`, `65392ce..57550ef`, 4 commits, this entry among them, and this entry brought up to `57550ef` and to the runs below in the commit after; then `41a321f`, the final review's fixes, and this entry brought up to it in the commit after that)

Before this, Tab in the source editor moved the focus out of it, as CodeMirror leaves Tab to the browser unless an app
binds it, and an editor whose Tab never indents reads as broken to anyone who writes code in it. The user asked for Tab
to indent, chose each behaviour below, and asked that it be done as well as it can be for keyboard and screen reader
users. Their choices: Tab with no selection adds spaces at the caret up to the next stop four columns apart; Tab with a
selection indents every line it touches by four spaces and keeps the selection; Shift+Tab takes up to four spaces off
the caret's line or each selected line; the way out is CodeMirror's own, Escape and then Tab, or Ctrl+M (Shift+Alt+M on
a Mac, which the app names by a Mac's own word, Option); under vim, Tab and Shift+Tab move the focus in normal and
visual mode and indent only in insert mode, since vim indents with `>>` and `<<`.

This lane's logs are in `~/temp/redextape-editor-tab-record/logs/`, `$L` below, its scripts in
`~/temp/redextape-editor-tab-record/scripts/`, and its reports in `~/.local/state/agents/redextape/editor-tab/`, `$S`
below.

##### THE CHANGE

- **The keys.** The new `web/src/editor-tab.ts`'s `tabKeymap` binds Tab and Shift+Tab, Escape and Ctrl+M, above
  CodeMirror's default keymap and below the vim slot. Tab at a caret is `indentAtCaret`, which counts columns with
  `countColumn` and a tab character as the state's `tabSize`, and counts a second caret on a line after the spaces
  the first one added; with any range selected it is CodeMirror's `indentMore`, and Shift+Tab is `indentLess`. The
  indent unit is four spaces, the formatter's `INDENT` in `crates/redextape-core/src/printer.rs`, so Tab and a format
  agree; it was CodeMirror's default of two, so vim's `>>` and `<<` now move four columns too.
- **The way out.** CodeMirror's tab-focus mode, in which the editor hands Tab and Shift+Tab to the browser before any
  handler, vim's included. CodeMirror opens it for two seconds at an Escape no handler takes, and closes it at the next
  key that is not Tab, Escape or a modifier, so a second Escape keeps it open, for two seconds from that one. The app's
  Escape clears a selection and opens it in one press, where CodeMirror's own `simplifySelection` would take the first
  Escape and leave the way out to a second. Ctrl+M sets the mode outright, on or off, rather than toggling CodeMirror's,
  so the sentence it says is always the mode it leaves.
- **A Mac's key.** CodeMirror binds Shift+Alt+M on a Mac, and its keymap never fires it there: Option types a
  character, `Â` on a US layout, and since 6.38.1 CodeMirror does not fall back to the key code for an Option
  combination on macOS. So the app matches the key by `event.code`, `KeyM` with Shift and Option and neither Ctrl nor
  Command, where `MAC` is true, that is where `navigator.platform` names a Mac, an iPhone, an iPod or an iPad. It
  matches it in `macSwitchKey`, a keydown handler at the highest precedence, which runs before vim's: vim sits above
  every keymap, and on a Mac it takes an Option key it does not map in normal and visual mode, so a keymap binding
  would not see the key there. Ctrl+M stays in the keymap, since vim maps no `<C-m>` and lets it through in every mode.
- **What a screen reader hears.** The editor's content element has `aria-describedby` on a hidden paragraph,
  `editorNote`: "Tab indents and Shift+Tab takes an indent off. To leave the editor, press Escape and then Tab, or
  Ctrl+M to make Tab move the focus until you press it again." Under vim it says that Tab indents in insert mode and
  moves the focus in normal and visual mode, and while Ctrl+M has Tab moving the focus it says that. The paragraph is
  `hidden`, which `aria-describedby` reads all the same, so a screen reader browsing the page does not meet it again
  after the editor. A description rather than words in the label, so it is said after the editor's name, `source program
  editor`, and a user can turn descriptions off. Each Ctrl+M is said through the live region with `notices.announce`,
  not `notices.notify`, since a notice would end the one up now, and a pick's undo, which a keyboard user may be
  leaving the editor to reach, would go with it.
- **What a sighted keyboard user sees.** A line under the editor, CodeMirror's bottom panel, with the same words as the
  description: shown while Ctrl+M has Tab moving the focus, and while a Tab or Shift+Tab brought the focus in, which the
  editor knows by a Tab keyup that lands in it with no keydown there before it, and with no Ctrl, Command or Alt held,
  since Ctrl+Tab brings the focus back from another browser tab. A click in shows nothing, so a pointer user's editor
  keeps its height; the line a Tab in showed goes when the editor is left. It is `aria-hidden`, as the description
  already says it. `style.css` gives CodeMirror's panels the palette's panel colours, text on `--bg-raised` as the hover
  tooltip has, a pair `contrast.ts` already holds to 4.5:1. The rule is CodeMirror's panels', so vim's command line, a
  panel too, takes the palette's colours where it had CodeMirror's fixed light ones.
- **The help page.** `#editor-keys` gains rows for Tab, Shift+Tab, Escape and Ctrl+M, and `#editor-leave` says how to
  leave the editor by keyboard, with and without vim, and that the line under the editor says it too.

##### THE TESTS

- **`tests/node/editor-tab.test.ts`**, on editor states with no DOM: Tab at columns 0, 3, 4, 5 and 7 adds 4, 1, 4, 3 and
  1 spaces with the caret after them; a tab character counts as the tab size; a second caret on a line counts after
  the first one's spaces; each of several carets on several lines gets its own;
  a selection's lines are indented and the selection holds the same text, and Shift+Tab takes it off; Shift+Tab takes
  no more than a line has; under vim, Tab and Shift+Tab decline in normal and visual mode and take the key in insert
  mode, where Tab adds four spaces; Escape over a selection clears it and opens the way out, and over a caret leaves

  and visual modes, and the description under vim and after it; Ctrl+M under vim, and a Mac's Shift+Option+M with vim
  told it is on a Mac, each pressed in normal mode, making Tab move the focus in insert mode and then indent again; and

##### THE REVIEW

A review of the whole branch at `ce9c545`, on `f818cca`, read the code and the CodeMirror and vim sources in
`web/node_modules` and ran no test (`$S/c-review.md`). It found 1 important defect and 12 nits. The defect: under vim on
a Mac, Shift+Option+M did nothing in normal and visual mode, as vim took the key before the keymap binding that matched
it could run. `macSwitchKey` (*A Mac's key*) answers it, and S1 shows the browser cases hold it.

##### WHAT THIS DID NOT CLOSE

- **Not run: a Mac, a screen reader, or the app driven by hand with a keyboard.** The Mac path ran only on Linux with
  the Mac setting forced: the browser cases set `macKeys` and `CodeMirror.isMac`, and there Playwright's Shift+Option+M
  arrives as `m` with `KeyM` (`$L/d-probe.log`), where a US Mac types `Â`; only the node case sends `Â`.
- **A Mac's Shift+Option+M no longer types its character in the editor**, `Â` on a US layout, as `macSwitchKey` takes
  the key. It takes it by its place, `event.code` `KeyM`, so on a layout that puts another letter there the key that
  switches is the one in a US M's place, not the one labelled M; AZERTY, for one, puts M elsewhere. Neither was tried
  on a Mac or on another layout.
- **Ctrl+Tab back into the page** is held by reading alone; no test switches browser tabs.
- **Shift+Tab on the way back to a pick's undo** now takes an indent off an indented line, which withdraws the undo,
  so the way back from the editor is Escape and then Shift+Tab.
- **Firefox binds Ctrl+M to muting the tab.** The editor's binding prevents the default. In Firefox the Ctrl+M case
  passed (`editor-tab.test.ts`, 18 of 18 alone at `57550ef`, `$L/ff-alone/e-branch-editor-tab.log`), which shows the
  page got the key. It cannot show whether Firefox muted the tab as well, and that was not checked: only a hand check in
  Firefox can tell.
- **Tab over a selection with bare carets beside it** indents each caret's whole line too, since `indentMore` indents
  every range's line. The review reported it, and it was left.
- **Tab held down while tabbing in** may indent and keep the line under the editor from showing, as the repeats land in
  the editor. The review read this from the code, and no test tried it.
- **The two seconds after Escape** are CodeMirror's, not the app's. WCAG 2.2.1 asks for a way past a time limit;
  Ctrl+M is the way out with none.
- **Character key shortcuts (WCAG 2.1.4).** None of the keys here is a character key. Vim's single-letter commands are
  active only while the editor has the focus, and only where a user chose vim, which 2.1.4 allows.

##### WHAT CHANGED

As built at `20994d6`; `377d36f` changes the design's words alone.

**The frames.** At a halt whose `rr` is a list, `RxmState::result` (`ResultCells`) names the cells the list reaches,
through each tail and, for a list of lists, each head: the newest of them up to the window's `result`, 64 in the app
(`RXM_WINDOW` in `protocol.ts`), which the frame's cells carry beside the window's own, and how many it reaches in all.
`ClifState::result` does the same from the list main returns, at a `Ran` end, under `CLIF_WINDOW`'s 64. For the TM,
`tm::result_heap_runs` walks the halted HEAP by the result's type, and `Session::tm_state` sets `TmState::result` to the
runs those cells lie in, as materialized indices. Every other frame carries `None`, so only the end frame pays, and
`protocol.ts`'s frame sizers charge what it carries.

**Only where the result can be marked.** The walk follows every List-tagged word, and a closure is a List-tagged cell of
its tag and its environment, so each leg names a result's cells only where it decodes the result to a value and prints
it, `Decoded::Value`, the one result a view marks: a list of functions, which does not decode, and a list too large to
print, `TooLargeToPrint`, carry no result cells, and no unlit cell of either sits among a heap's lines (`ee705cd`,
`0f188a7`).

**The TM names its runs on the accept state's frame.** The cursor reports `Halted` only from the step call after the one
that reached the accept state, a call that takes no step, and the page's recorder takes one frame per step taken, so it
never records a frame with that status. `tm_state` names HEAP's runs where the cursor stands in an accept state, on the
last frame the recorder takes, whose status still reads `None`; the overflow guard's halt is no accept state and names
none (`b6e426c`, `ac1342b`).

**The views.** `resultMarked` decides, unchanged from #201. In the rxm and clif heap panels each line of a lit cell is
`is-result`, tinted, edged down both sides and closed at a run's first and last line, and described as "part of the
result"; a run is a run of lit lines, so two lit cells share a box though a cell the frame does not carry lies between
them. Every heap line is padded at its sides, lit or not, so the box's edges clear the glyphs and nothing moves at the
step that lights it. Where the list reaches cells the frame does not carry, the older cells' note says how many of them
are the result's, as one note: `+36 older, 36 of them result cells`. The TM boxes each run on HEAP, cut to HEAP's window
by `tape.ts`'s `resultRuns`, in one `span.tm-result` with no word, finding HEAP by the name the core gives the tape; the
word stays on REG's field 0. The λ view marks the root whatever it is: on one row round its run, as #201 marked a chip,
and over several as one block, each row `.term-line.is-result-row` in the result's ground, one edge round them all, the
word after the first row's text, the block's left edge a shadow off the mark strip's right side; so an opened numeral
chip over several rows gets the block too. `[]` keeps its pointer's mark and its λ mark on `λn c. n`, and lights no
cell. The help page says so.

**The λ word is dropped where it has no room, never wrapped** (R2-1): `wordFits` in `lambda-body.ts` weighs the root's
first row and the word's 6 columns against the columns the view shows without scrolling sideways, the layout's width or,
below its floor of 24 columns, the fewer the view has; a result whose word is dropped keeps its ground, its edge and
`data-marks`'s `result:`.

**Forced colours**, which drop the tints and the inset edges, outline in `Highlight` the marks no word stands beside: a
lit heap line, a box on HEAP and a λ result whose word is dropped, the last whatever else the node is, linked and the
contractum among them (`e0fadd5`). A wordless block's left edge is a 1px `Highlight` border on the strip's right side,
its width given back by a negative margin (`1dba295`). A mark with its word keeps the word.

**The λ rows stand where main draws them** (the gutter ruling, `257bb1c`): every `▸`/`▾` on the strip's right side, its
text 2ch past it, marked or not, and a block's left edge takes about a pixel of its first row's `▾` box. Each row keeps
3px at its end and the rows 1px after them, 4px in all, inside the 2ch `room()` keeps clear, so the block's right edge
clears the widest row's last glyph and stays inside a view at a fractional place (`660cdff`).

**A pixel of room past each far edge** (`3788a52`): `.term-spacer`, content-box, and `.rxm-heap` keep 1px below the last
row or line, and `.cells` 1px after the last cell, in every view at every step, marked or not, since Chromium can clip a
view's last pixel when it is scrolled to its end. Following and the keys, End, ↓ and PageDown, take a λ view down to the
spacer's end through one `#foot(i)` (`78289a2`, `e244185`).

**The example.** countdown(4), a `while` loop that conses 1 to 4 onto `nil`, comes after *map and fold*, its value
`[4, 3, 2, 1]`, its four legs `ended`. Under binary its TM HEAP window holds the four cells at the halt, so the TM boxes
them whole. It joins `WEB_EXAMPLES` (8) and the clif agreement corpus (73; the JIT's tallies `[57, 2, 14]` and
`[66, 2, 0]`), with its `.clif`, `.ll` and `.opt.ll` snapshots, and `llvm-version.txt` names LLVM 23.1.5, the release
that wrote every snapshot (*The decisions and the rulings*).

##### THE DECISIONS AND THE RULINGS

Taken without asking the user, for them to overturn (`ledger.md`):

- **Q1** An opened numeral chip over several rows, or a number in expand-all mode, gets the block at the run's end,
  where #201 drew nothing, so the result is always marked.
- **Q2** Two lit heap lines share one box though a cell number between them is not shown.
- **Q3** A forced-colours outline in this PR, for the new marks no word stands beside.
- **Q4** One note where both apply, `+36 older, 36 of them result cells`; the wording is the user's to change.
- **Q5** Lit heap lines below the heap panel's visible area are left, and named below.
- **Q6** Past the 64 cap the lit cells are the newest by allocation, not by list order: left, and named below.
- **Q7** A result's cells are carried only where the result can be marked.
- **The LLVM stamp.** CI's `rust-llvm` job runs LLVM 23.1.6 (run 827, job 16146), neither main's stamp, 23.1.4, nor this
  machine's 23.1.5. The two new snapshots and the stamp are committed at 23.1.5, the release that wrote every snapshot
  (`ff04cf0`): the strict comparison runs where the running release equals the stamp, and CI on 23.1.6 prints its note
  and passes, as it does on main.

The user's rulings:

- **R2-1, 2026-11-25: option B.** A list on one row that nearly filled the λ view drew the word past the view at the
  last step alone, by 1 to 25 px. Of A, accept it as #201 accepted REG's word, B, drop the word where the row has no
  room, as #201 drops the TM status line's `little-endian`, and C, lay the last step out to the room the word leaves,
  the user took B, with the forced-colours outline covering a result whose word is dropped.
- **The λ gutter, 2026-11-26: option B.** Rows exactly as main draws them, the block's left edge off the strip's right
  side, about a pixel inside row 0's `▾` box. It replaced `4dc09f7`'s `EDGE_ROOM`, 4px after the strip on every row,
  which moved every row's text 4px right and put a glyph of edge-spacing's 390x844 case on the pane's edge (gate B2),
  and `d3b3cc4`'s narrower gutter, `calc(2ch - 4px)`, which kept the text where main has it and brought each `▸`/`▾` 4px
  nearer it, an ink gap of 5 to 7 px where main's is 9 to 10 (drive2).
- **review4's finding 2, 2026-11-27: option A.** Keep the 4px of room at each λ row's end and name the overflow it costs
  with classic scroll bars (below), since without it the block's right edge takes the last pixel of a numeral chip's
  overline or of a 3's stroke (fix6). review6's second nit and review7's first, the pixel past a far edge in a box
  within a pixel of fitting, are the same class and come under it.

##### WHAT THIS DID NOT CLOSE

Each item was read again against `20994d6`'s code.

- **The call stack's lines are not padded** as the heap's now are (`.rxm-frame` beside `.rxm-cell-line` in `style.css`),
  so in rxm and clif the call stack's text starts 4px left of the heap's.
- **The TM's glyphs sit about 0.3ch inside a HEAP box's edge**, as in #201's REG box: the box is drawn on the cells' own
  edges.
- **A lit heap line can lie below the heap panel's visible area** at the last step, and nothing scrolls it into view
  (Q5): the drive saw countdown(4)'s heaps below the view at 1412x896.
- **Past the 64 cap** the lit cells are the newest by allocation, not by list order (Q6), and the note counts the rest.
- **Binary countdown(4)'s HEAP box runs past the TM view's right edge**, 166px in Chromium and 171 in Firefox at
  1412x896 (the drive, `bc51185`), so its right edge is unseen until the row is scrolled.
- **Up to 64 result cells are drawn unlit**, under a bare `+N older` note, from the end frame's arrival until the result
  message lands, which the worker posts after the legs' recordings (review3's first report, item 2); nothing moves when
  it lands.
- **The end frame decodes and capped-prints the result twice** in each leg, once for the gate on its cells and once for
  the result message, and again at each re-recording after a rewind (review3's first report, item 3); a list too large
  to print spends the capped print twice. The worker pays it, never the page's thread.
- **The λ word is dropped up to 2 columns before it would overflow**, since it is weighed against the width that keeps
  2ch clear, and **a resize alone keeps it as weighed** until the view next lays the term out.
- **Main's edge-spacing case at 390x844 sits exactly at its 4px threshold** (fix4): the branch draws the λ rows where
  main does, so the case is as near its edge as on main.
- **With classic scroll bars, a λ row exactly as wide as the layout allows overflows by 1 to 3 px** at a step where the
  vertical scroll bar first appears, until the next layout, where main's does not (review4's finding 2, ruling A). The
  pixel past each far edge overflows a box within a pixel of fitting by up to 1px at any step, so with classic scroll
  bars it can draw a bar main does not; and End, ↓ or PageDown onto the last row of a λ view that holds every row with
  no pixel to spare scrolls it by that pixel and stops following, where main's keys scroll nothing (review6's second
  nit, review7's first).

#### THE CONFIG D ROWS AND THE RELEASE TEST BUILD PRINT NO WARNING, `pkg-clif/` EXPORTS NONE OF THE NATIVE RUNTIME'S `rt_*` FUNCTIONS, AND AN AOT LINK BUILDS THE RUNTIME WITH THEIR NAMES BEFORE IT LOOKS FOR ITS STATICLIB (2026-11-26, branch `native-rt-hygiene`, `7033883..d00d77a`, 6 commits, plus this entry)

The branch closes what earlier entries left open: `cargo`'s `unused dependency redextape-native-rt` warning
on `redextape-native` built with no default features or with `clif` alone (*RUST 1.100.0 TURNS `main` RED TWICE* and
*CLIF VIEW PR 1*), the unused import a release build of `redextape-core`'s tests warned of (*CLIF VIEW PR 1* and
*COPIES ARE GONE FROM THE WEB APP*), and the `rt_*` functions `pkg-clif/` exported with no caller (*CLIF VIEW PR 1*).
The first four commits were drafted in a cloud sandbox with no browser, on `52fc8c6`, and applied unchanged onto
`7033883`; the last two answer the first review, which ran on this machine. The licence check the same handoff asked
for is the branch `licence-pin`.

| Commit | What |
|---|---|
| `c985edc` | `redextape-native`'s dependency on the runtime is optional: `cranelift` and `llvm` turn it on, `clif` does not |
| `12dc4be` | `binary.rs`'s test module is gated on `all(test, debug_assertions)`, and its two tests carry no gate of their own |
| `44ff71d` | `redextape-native-rt`'s `link-names` feature, on by default, puts the `no_mangle` on each `rt_*` function; `redextape-clif` depends on the runtime with no default features; `aot.rs`'s build names the feature; `web/tests/node/clif-exports.test.ts`, which CI's `pkg-clif/` step and `docs/development.md` name among the package's readers |
| `125accf` | the roadmap only: the sandbox's draft of the branch's entry |
| `9866463` | `aot.rs`'s `locate_staticlib` builds the runtime with `link-names` before every search, not only when it finds no staticlib |
| `d00d77a` | the two manifests' comments: `aot.rs` names `link-names` itself, the default serves a plain `cargo build -p redextape-native-rt`, and `redextape-native`'s dependency serves the JITs |

##### WHAT CHANGED FOR A PERSON USING REDEXTAPE

Nothing they can see. `pkg-clif/`'s module exports 22 names where it exported 34, the 12 gone all `rt_*` functions,
which no code under `web/` names, and its `.wasm` is 1,246,819 bytes where it was 1,257,723. For a person building
redextape, the two warnings no longer print, and a staticlib that a hand-run
`cargo build -p redextape-native-rt --no-default-features` leaves in the target dir no longer breaks every AOT link
after it.

##### THE CAUSES

1. **The unused dependency.** `redextape-native` listed the runtime unconditionally, but every use of it is under
   `cranelift` or `llvm`: the JITs call its functions in-process and size their run thread's stack by its
   `RUN_STACK_SIZE`. A build with no default features, or with `clif` alone, compiled the runtime and used none of it,
   and cargo 1.100.0's `unused_dependencies` lint says so. The warning is cargo's, not rustc's, so clippy's
   `-D warnings` exits 0 with it printed.
2. **The unused import.** Both tests in `binary.rs`'s test module expect a `debug_assert!` to panic, so each was gated
   on `debug_assertions`. A release build of the tests, which `check-slow.sh` makes with
   `cargo test --release --workspace`, dropped both and kept the module, whose `use super::*` was then unused.
3. **The exports.** Each `rt_*` function was `#[unsafe(no_mangle)]`, and a `cdylib` exports every `no_mangle` function
   of every crate it links. `redextape-clif`'s stepper calls the runtime from Rust, so `pkg-clif/` linked it and
   exported all 12. Only the AOT link needs the names: the object `aot.rs` emits imports each `rt_*` function by name,
   while both JITs bind each import to the function's address.

##### DECISIONS

1. **`link-names` is on by default and `redextape-clif` turns it off**, rather than off by default and turned on where
   it is needed. A plain `cargo build -p redextape-native-rt` keeps building a staticlib that links, and the JITs need
   nothing. The cost is that a new path from `pkg-clif/` to the runtime with its default features turns the names back
   on with every Rust build green; `clif-exports.test.ts` is what fails then.
2. **`44ff71d` rests on `c985edc`.** Before `c985edc`, `redextape-native`'s manifest listed the runtime with neither
   `optional` nor `default-features = false`, so every build of `redextape-native` pulled it in with its default
   features, `clif` alone included, and cargo's feature unification would have turned `link-names` back on in
   `pkg-clif/`.
3. **The machine code packages lose the runtime too.** `redextape-mc-wasm` reaches `redextape-native` with `clif`
   alone, so `c985edc` takes the runtime out of its graph. `pkg-mc-x86-64/` built at `7033883` exported no `rt_*`
   function either, since nothing in it called one, so `clif-exports.test.ts` reads `pkg-clif/` alone: a test of
   `pkg-mc-x86-64/` could not have failed there.
4. **The test module is gated as a whole**, so a test added to it later is debug-only too, as both of its tests are.
5. **An AOT link builds the runtime every time** (`9866463`). `locate_staticlib` built the staticlib only when it
   found none, which was harmless while every build of the runtime carried the names. With `link-names`, a hand-run
   `cargo build -p redextape-native-rt --no-default-features` leaves a staticlib with no `rt_*` symbol in `debug/`,
   and at `44ff71d` the next `aot_oracle` run failed to link it, `undefined reference to 'rt_run'`. `locate_staticlib`
   now runs `cargo build -p redextape-native-rt --features link-names` before it searches, which rebuilds that
   staticlib, and which builds nothing when the staticlib is fresh: 0.031 s here, with no `Compiling` line.
6. **Shipping:** as Davey chose, these three items as one PR and the licence check as its own.

##### HOW EACH WAS SEEN TO FAIL

- **The node test**, against `pkg-clif/` built at `7033883`, fails and lists the 12 `rt_*` names; against `pkg-clif/`
  built at `d00d77a` it passes.
- **A staticlib without the names, at `44ff71d`:** after `cargo build -p redextape-native-rt --no-default-features`,
  `nm` finds no defined `rt_*` symbol in `debug/libredextape_native_rt.a`, and
  `cargo test -p redextape-native --test aot_oracle` exits 101 on `undefined reference to 'rt_run'`. The same sequence
  at `d00d77a`: the test passes, and the staticlib it leaves defines all 12.
- **The two warnings, at `7033883`:** each of the two clippy runs on `redextape-native` prints one
  `unused dependency`, and the release build of `redextape-core`'s tests one `unused import`. At `d00d77a` none of the
  three prints a warning.

##### THE REVIEWS

- **The first review** read the branch at `125accf` and ran it on this machine, with `main`'s side built in a worktree
  whose crates and `web/` equal `7033883`'s. It found the code sound, and each of its findings minor: `aot.rs` took
  any staticlib already in place, so the one a hand-run `--no-default-features` build leaves broke every later link
  (answered by `9866463`); the runtime's manifest gave the default as what made `aot.rs`'s build link, and
  `redextape-native`'s gave the AOT link as a reason for its dependency (answered by `d00d77a`); and `125accf`'s entry
  cited the sandbox's logs by paths outside the repo, and claims this machine contradicts, among them
  `share-link.test.ts` cases failing under Node 22, which pass under Node 26.
- **The fix round** made `9866463` and `d00d77a`, the pre-commit hook passing on each.
- **The whole-branch review** read `7033883..d00d77a` and found it ready after a minor point: `125accf`'s entry still
  said that `aot.rs` builds a staticlib only when none is found, which `9866463` reversed. What it checked and found
  sound: every `cfg` that names the runtime; every build of it, in the Dockerfile, CI's jobs and `check-all.sh`'s
  rows; `locate_staticlib`'s build beside parallel builds, where a fresh build leaves the staticlib's file as it is,
  so no link finds it missing; `aot_oracle` under `cargo llvm-cov nextest` with `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` unset, CI's case,
  which passed; and feature unification across `redextape-clif-wasm`, `redextape-mc-wasm` and `redextape-clif`'s
  dev-dependency on `redextape-native`.

##### WHAT THIS DID NOT CLOSE

- **`44ff71d`'s message is stale.** The first of its five bullets gives the default as what makes the build `aot.rs`
  runs link, and the fourth says a staticlib already in place is taken as it is; `9866463` and `d00d77a` changed both.
  The branch is not rebuilt, so the message stays as it is, and a squash message should not carry those two bullets.
- **No Rust test holds the exports.** `clif-exports.test.ts` needs `pkg-clif/` built, as CI's web job builds it;
  `cargo` alone stays green if the names come back.
- **No clippy row reads the runtime without `link-names`.** `check-all.sh` builds that configuration only in its
  wasm32 `cargo check` rows of `redextape-clif` and `redextape-clif-wasm`. Run by hand here,
  `cargo clippy -p redextape-native-rt --no-default-features --all-targets -- -D warnings` exits 0 with no warning.
- **Merging with `llvm-ir-text`.** Both branches change `redextape-native`'s features, and `git merge-tree` finds 3
  files in conflict: `crates/redextape-native/Cargo.toml`, `docs/development.md` and the roadmap. The `ll` feature
  `llvm-ir-text` adds must not list the runtime. The resolution, as `llvm-ir-text`'s whole-branch review gives it, is
  in this branch's PR.
- **Not run on this machine:** the browser tier and Firefox (the branch changes no line under `web/src`), either
  coverage run, `check-slow.sh` itself (the release build of the workspace's tests it runs printed no warning), CI's
  `opt_report` step, `build:app` and the Docker image.
- **The sandbox's open questions.** Its `share-link.test.ts` failures under Node 22: here, under Node 26.13.1, the
  file's 70 tests pass, and CI's web job runs in a `node:26` image. Its other two questions, the licence files' pins
  against GNU's and a `.gitattributes` for them, belong to `licence-pin`.

##### VERIFICATION

On this machine: rustc and cargo 1.100.0, cargo-nextest 0.9.149, LLVM 23.1.5, Node 26.13.1, pnpm 11.20.0 and wasm-pack
0.15.0. The cargo, wasm-pack and `check-all.sh` runs held the machine's heavy-build lock, all but the binding build
inside `pnpm run typecheck`, and every build, test and gate ran in a systemd scope with `MemoryMax=16G`, with
`CARGO_TARGET_DIR` set; `TREE_SITTER` named a tree-sitter CLI that `check-all.sh` accepts, as it refuses this
machine's 0.28.

#### THE MACHINE CODE READERS DECLINE A LISTING WHOSE CODE HOLDS DATA THEY CANNOT PLACE, A DECLINED RELOCATION NAMES WHAT IT POINTS AT, §8'S TWO PC CLAIMS ARE TESTED, AND CI'S COVERAGE COUNTS `arm64.rs` (2026-11-25 to 27, branch `mc-followups`, `7033883..a692cc6`, 11 commits, plus this entry)

The open items #198 and #200 left in the machine code crate, from a handoff that quoted each entry's *WHAT THIS DID NOT
CLOSE*: §8's two pc claims had no test, a Cranelift library call's relocation was declined without being named, the data
finders held for today's code only, and `arm64.rs` was in no coverage figure; and, needing the user's choice, iced's
decimal immediates and a row field telling a register move from a clif instruction with no pc. The first six commits,
the sixth duet's roadmap entry, were written in a cloud sandbox, duet, from that handoff, and applied onto `main` at
`7033883` (#204); the five after them answer the first review. The change is in `crates/redextape-mc`, in
`crates/redextape-native`'s `module_free.rs` and its exports, in CI's coverage step, in the machine code spec's §5.2 and
in one line of `Cargo.lock`. No file under `web/` and no binding or wasm crate changes.

| `b8d7a49` | `module_free.rs`: a declined relocation's error names the function, the relocation, its byte and its target in words, where it printed the target's `Debug` form |
| `e1620c6` | `redextape-mc`: each reader refuses at the first instruction that shows data it cannot place, and the listing declines with the reason |

##### WHAT CHANGED FOR A PERSON USING THE MACHINE CODE PANEL

Nothing, for any program the reviews listed. At `a692cc6` the whole-branch review listed each of the 79 programs in
`web/src/examples/*.rxt` and `crates/redextape-native/snapshots/*.clif` on x86-64 and arm64, as built and optimised,
with a scratch example not kept in the tree, and again with the five changed source files taken from `main`: every
listing listed both times, and the hash of each listing's JSON was the same both times.

For code that holds a jump table or a constant pool, the panel shows its existing decline, *No machine code for this
program:*, with a reason such as
`u0:12's x86-64 code holds data the listing cannot place: at byte 0x22, an indirect jump, as through a jump table placed in the code`,
the reason a test gets from Cranelift's own `br_table`. #198's entry said what such code would have listed: on x86-64
the code after a jump table as `.quad` rows, and on arm64 a constant pool or a jump table as instructions. A declined
relocation, which no listed program reaches either, now reads
`native codegen: u0:12's Abs8 relocation at byte 0x8 names Cranelift's library call FloorF64, which is neither a runtime import nor a subroutine`.

##### DECISIONS

1. **A refusal declines the whole listing**, the functions before the refusing one included: the user's pick, as duet's
   README records it. Showing that function's rest as `.byte` rows would read as decoder failures and still carry pcs;
   an *unknown* row kind would change the TS bindings and need browser work. The decline takes the path a declined
   relocation already takes, `LowerError::Unsupported`, which `redextape-mc-wasm` hands the worker as a string and the
   panel shows as the reason, so no binding, worker or panel code changes.
2. **Each reader refuses on a sign, not on proof of data**, at the first instruction that shows it. x86-64: an indirect
   `jmp`; a branch into the bytes read as constants, their first byte included; or a rip-relative operand that reads
   back into the code, as a forward read is where the constants start. arm64: `br`; an `adr` no relocation fills in; or
   a literal `ldr`/`ldrsw` from anything but a far call's address, an absolute relocation at the literal. The tests
   compile a `br_table` and an `f64` constant as they run, with the Cranelift in `Cargo.lock`, 0.137.2, at `speed`,
   through `machine_function`, the compile `machine_code` runs for each function, and the readers refuse that code at
   three of the signs: x86-64's indirect `jmp`, for the `br_table`; arm64's `adr`, for the `br_table`, and its literal
   load, for the `f64` constant. x86-64's other two signs and arm64's `br` are held only by the hand-built bytes and
   words of *THE TESTS*. x86-64's constants after its code still read as `.quad` rows; arm64, which finds data only
   through relocations, refuses the `f64` constant x86-64 lists.
3. **Coverage turns the feature on rather than merging a second run.** `--workspace` builds `redextape-mc` with `x86`
   alone, by `redextape-mc-wasm`'s default, so `arm64.rs` was in no figure. `redextape-mc-wasm` reads its own features,
   so it still builds as the x86-64 package, and `redextape-native`'s tests already turn on Cranelift's arm64 ISA, so
   the flag adds the crate's arm64 code and 7 packages, as `cargo tree` lists them: `yaxpeax-arm`, `yaxpeax-arch`,
   `bitvec`, `funty`, `radium`, `tap` and `wyz`. With it, the figure counts `arm64.rs`: 96.00% of its 125 lines.
4. **`machine_function` and `machine_isa` are public in `redextape-native`**, the two halves `machine_code` composes, so
   that a test in `redextape-mc`, another crate, puts code no program makes through the same compile and the same
   relocation check; `pub(crate)` cannot reach it. They add no type and no capability: `build_clif` already returns
   Cranelift `Function`s. `compiled.rs`, which calls them, is declared under `#[cfg(test)]`, and `cranelift-frontend`,
   which it builds with, is a dev-dependency, so no package or wasm build compiles it.
5. **Left, as duet's README records the user's choice:** iced's decimal immediates, and the row field (*WHAT THIS DID
   NOT CLOSE*).

##### THE TESTS

- **`tests/listing.rs`**, over the snapshot programs on both targets at both levels:
  `every_row_inside_a_range_carries_its_pc`, asked of the ranges `machine_code` returns rather than through `pc_at`; and
  `prologue_rows_carry_no_pc`, which also wants a prologue row on each target at each level, so that a range made for
  one of them cannot hide its prologue.
- **`module_free.rs`**: `a_relocation_naming_no_import_or_subroutine_is_refused_by_name` holds each of the 5 kinds of
  target `reloc_target` names to its whole sentence; `a_declined_relocation_names_the_function_it_is_in` compiles an
  `f64` `floor` for x86-64 with no SSE4.1, which Cranelift makes a call to its library's `FloorF64`, in a function named
  `u0:13`, and holds the decline to that name.
- **`x86.rs`**, on hand-built bytes: a jump through a table placed in the code, refused at its indirect jump; a branch
  to the constant's first byte and one a byte further in; a rip-relative read back into the code; and constants after
  the code, read forward, as `.quad` rows. `cranelifts_jump_table_is_refused_and_its_constant_pool_read` compiles a
  `br_table` and an `f64` constant.
- **`arm64.rs`**, on hand-built words: a far call's literal as one `.8byte` row; a literal load no relocation marks; a
  literal load from a call's relocation; and a jump table's `adr` and its `br`, each refused alone.
  `cranelifts_jump_table_and_constant_pool_are_refused` compiles both.
- **`lib.rs`**: `a_jump_table_declines_the_whole_x86_64_listing` and `a_constant_pool_declines_the_whole_arm64_listing`
  list a compiled plain function alone, then decline it with Cranelift's `br_table`, or on arm64 its `f64` constant, as
  the second function, with the whole sentence;
  `a_decline_names_the_function_the_target_the_byte_and_the_kind_of_instruction` holds `decline`'s sentence.

empty after. A case stops at its first failed check, so the checks after it are not shown by that sabotage.

  "and nothing else".

##### WHAT THIS DID NOT CLOSE

- **iced prints small immediates in decimal** (`movl $4`) where Cranelift's own text reads `$0x4`; iced's one setting
  covers immediates and displacements alike, and Cranelift prints `8(%rsp)`, so either choice reads unlike the snapshot
  somewhere. Left, as duet's README records the user's choice.
- **Rows with no pc inside a current block stay unmarked**, so the block reads as two. The Rust half, a field on the
  row, changes the TS bindings and so the web side. Left for later, as duet's README records the user's choice.
- **A refusal is a sign, not a proof.** An indirect `jmp` through a function pointer, or an arm64 `br` that is a tail
  call through a register, would decline a listing that holds no data. No file under `crates/` names `return_call`, so
  no tail call reaches either today. If one comes, a reader needs the jump table's own bounds, from `MachBuffer`'s
  labels, rather than a sign.
- **The first sign declines everything**: a function with a jump table lists nothing, and neither do the functions
  beside it.
- **`every_row_inside_a_range_carries_its_pc` finds a row's range as `pc_at` does**, the first range that holds it, so
  it would not notice ranges that overlap; Cranelift's sorted source-location ranges do not overlap (the first review,
  by reading).
- **One line of the new reader code is not covered:** line 123 of `x86.rs`, where `unplaced` stops at an invalid
  instruction that takes no byte, as `decode` does at lines 55-58, which `main` leaves uncovered too.
- **Merging beside `llvm-ir-text`.** Besides the roadmap, `crates/redextape-native/src/lib.rs` conflicts in its
  `pub use module_free::{...}` list: this branch adds `machine_function` and `machine_isa`, and `llvm-ir-text` takes
  `decline_reason` out, as it re-exports it from `shared`. Whichever merges second writes
  `CodeRange, CodeReloc, Listing, MachineFunction, build_clif, build_listing, isa_free_config, machine_code, machine_function, machine_isa`.
  The merged tree has not been built.
- **Duet's open questions.** Should the tests compile Cranelift's `br_table` and `f64` constant as they run rather than
  keep 0.137's bytes? Yes: `a591f0f` does, and before the arrays went, a test kept out of the commit held the compiled
  code equal to them byte for byte on both targets. Does `check-licences.sh` pass on this machine? Yes: after a real
  `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`, it and `check-licence-editions.sh` exit 0 with and without `--self-test` (the first
  review).

#### LLVM IR VIEW PR 1: THE WRITER AND ITS PACKAGE, NO UI. `redextape-native` WRITES THE LLVM BACKEND'S MODULE AS BUILT, AS LLVM PRINTS IT, WITHOUT LLVM, AND `pkg-llvm/` HANDS IT TO A PAGE LINE BY LINE WITH EACH LINE'S RXM PC (2026-11-26 and 27, branch `llvm-ir-text`, `7033883..9326c84`, 16 commits, plus this entry)

**IR views design §9, piece 4** (`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-27-ir-views-groundwork-design.md`): the LLVM IR view's
first pull request, the writer, the check that holds it to LLVM, and its wasm package. No page imports the package; the
pane, which lists this text and follows the run by pc, is PR 2. The first five commits, the fifth a roadmap entry, were
written in a cloud sandbox, duet, which had no LLVM 23 and no browser, from a handoff, and applied onto `main` at
`7033883` (#204); the other eleven answer the reviews below, run on this machine.

##### WHAT THE WRITER IS

**The sink.** `crates/redextape-native/src/ll_text.rs` is the lowering walk's third `LowerSink`, beside `ClifSink` and
`LlvmSink`, under a new `ll` feature that turns on the walk, `rt_imports` and `shared` and nothing of inkwell or
Cranelift, so it builds for wasm32. `llvm_text(prog)` answers an `LlModule`: its lines, each with the pc of the
instruction whose lowering wrote it, in its `i<pc>` block and the `cont` blocks its guards open, and `None` for every
other line; and each function's printed name, rxm label and first line. Nothing compiles the text: `llvm.rs` still
builds its module with inkwell's builder, and the writer exists so that a page with no LLVM can show that module.

**What it copies from LLVM.** The text is the module `llvm::build_module` builds before any pass, the same at `O0`-`O3`,
for x86-64 Linux, since the module names its target and data layout. A name already taken in its symbol table, one per
function for blocks and values and one per module for functions, gets the table's next number, as
`ValueSymbolTable::makeUniqueName` gives it: `%cons1`, `cont4`, `@rt_cons.1`. Blocks print in creation order:
`prologue`, one `i<pc>` per body instruction, `exit`, then each guard's `cont`. A block's `; preds =` comment lists its
branches newest first, LLVM's use-list order, padded to column 50. Constants print signed. A name is bare when its bytes
are letters, digits, `-`, `.` and `_` and it does not start with a digit; any other is quoted, a backslash doubled and a
quote or a byte outside printable ASCII written `\XX`. A subroutine's name ends at its first NUL, as inkwell's C string
ends it, and one with nothing before its NUL is refused. The intrinsics' attribute group is spelled as the LLVM that
printed the snapshots spells it.

**A subroutine named with LLVM's `llvm.` prefix is refused.** LLVM takes any function so named for an intrinsic and
refuses a body for it, so the module inkwell builds for such a program fails, and the writer refuses the program before
writing a line. `decline_reason` moves from `module_free.rs` to `shared.rs`, exported under `clif` or `ll`, so the
refusal reads as the clif packages' do.

##### THE PACKAGE

`crates/redextape-llvm` turns the module into an `LlvmListing` of `LlvmLine`s and `LlvmFunction`s, serde types with
ts-rs bindings under `ts`, and reads a `clifInput()` for its program alone. `crates/redextape-llvm-wasm` exports
`llvmIr(input)`, built into `pkg-llvm/` by `pnpm run build:llvm-wasm`; it exports that, `init`, `memory` and
wasm-bindgen's glue, and no `rt_*` function. Its `.wasm` is 149,919 bytes, 59,596 gzipped at level 9, built here with
rustc 1.100.0, wasm-pack 0.15.0 and binaryen's `wasm-opt` 130; the bytes depend on the toolchain. It is wired as
`pkg-mc-*` is: the workspace, `pnpm run build`, the `web` CI job, a leg of `build-web-bindings.sh` with its empty and
collision checks, `licences.ts` and the licence scan's list of builds, `.gitignore`, `check-all.sh` and the comment
budget, the Docker image and `docs/development.md`'s account of it, the fresh-clone build line there and in
`.pre-commit-config.yaml`, and `docs/architecture.md`'s crate list, which counts 16.

##### THE TESTS

- **`every_snapshot_is_the_writers_text`** holds the writer to the built section of each of the 72 `.ll` snapshots, byte
  for byte, and names the first line that parts.
- **`edge_programs_quote_and_rename_as_llvm_does`**, under `ll` alone, reads the text of the edge programs, written for
  what the snapshots need not hold: `rt_cons` and `$main` renamed, `1st` quoted, `a-b` bare, a quote and a backslash
  escaped, `naïve` written in `\XX`, a name cut at its NUL, a name empty before its NUL refused, built by hand and read
  back from rxm text, `u64::MAX` and 2^63 printed signed, and an argument the caller never set passed as `0`.
  **`lines_carry_the_pc_that_wrote_them`** holds which lines carry which pc, a `cont` block's among them.
- **`a_subroutine_with_llvms_prefix_is_refused`**, with a hand-built program and `fn llvm(n)`, whose label is `llvm.0`.
- **With both `llvm` and `ll`, `parsed_by_llvm`** is the CI check §9 asks for. For the 72 snapshots, the 15 edge
  programs and 64 random first-order programs, the writer's text must equal LLVM's print of the module inkwell builds,
  comments included, and LLVM must parse the text, verify it and print it back the same. Its
  `inkwell_refuses_a_subroutine_with_llvms_prefix_too` fails if LLVM ever accepts such a body, so the writer's refusal
  goes when the backend's does. `check-all.sh` runs it in its LLVM tier's `llvm,ll` rows, and CI's `rust-llvm` job runs
  that tier, `check-all.sh --llvm-only`.
- **`redextape-llvm`'s `listing.rs`**: each listing is its snapshot's built module, each function starts at its `define`
  and marks only pcs of its own subroutine, and an input is read for its program alone; `ts_bindings.rs` is
  `redextape-mc`'s gate.
- **`web/tests/node/llvm-package.test.ts`**, through the built packages: for each of the 7 examples, `llvmIr` of
  `pkg/`'s `clifInput()` is the snapshot's built module, and each line's pc is the one its text gives, the number of its
  `i<N>` block, or of the block whose guard branches to its `cont` block, and `null` elsewhere; a word of 2^53 or more
  is written whole; `fn llvm` gets the refusal's sentence; and an input `clifInput()` did not write is refused. 10
  cases.

##### WHAT THIS DID NOT CLOSE

- **The LLVM backend refuses `fn llvm(n) { n + 1 } llvm(41)`**, which `pkg/` compiles: its label `llvm.0` takes LLVM's
  intrinsic prefix, and the writer refuses it too (duet's first open question). Both reviews' answer: keep the refusal
  here, and in a pull request of its own rename such a subroutine in `llvm.rs` and drop the writer's refusal. No `.ll`
  snapshot defines a function with the prefix, so no snapshot changes, where duet expected names to. The node test's
  refusal case uses `fn llvm`, and will need another program the backend refuses.
- **A subroutine whose name is empty before its NUL is refused** (duet's second), where inkwell leaves the function
  unnamed and LLVM numbers it. rxm text makes such a name: `parse_rxm` reads a label that starts with a NUL, and the
  edge test holds the refusal for one. Both reviews' answer: keep the refusal.
- **The random programs are first-order** (the writer's review's Minor 2): `arb_expr_below` writes `+`, `-`, `>`, `==`
  and `if` alone, and in the writer's review's instrumented count they reached no arm of the writer the snapshots do
  not; the generator is unchanged. The edge programs reach the rest: the fix round's instrumented copy of the writer
  found no arm the snapshots reach that no edge program does, and the exact check runs every edge program. A write to a
  register with no slot cannot happen, so nothing tests it.
- **LLVM's patch release.** The snapshots come from 23.1.4, this machine runs 23.1.5, and CI's `rust-llvm` job takes any
  23.1 release. The exact check compares with the running LLVM's print, as the built-IR snapshot test already does byte
  for byte, so a release that prints otherwise trips both.
- **The countdown snapshot.** `list-results` adds `example-countdown.ll` and moves `llvm-version.txt` to 23.1.5, and the
  snapshot test and `listing.rs` read every `.ll` snapshot. On a scratch merge of the two branches, which holds 73, the
  `ll` tests, the writer's tests with `llvm` and `ll`, and `redextape-llvm`'s tests pass.
- **The pane, the stepper and the technical page** are PR 2 and later. No browser test ran, and none is affected: no
  file under `web/src` changes, and none imports `pkg-llvm`. When PR 2 re-exports the Llvm binding types from
  `web/src/types.ts`, the comment there that lists the shapes crossing another package's boundary gains the LLVM IR
  ones.
- **Not run on this branch:** `cargo llvm-cov` and its 90% floor, `check-slow.sh` and the browser tier; and since
  `c2f6843`, the Docker image and the whole node tier, which the package review ran there.

#### A SCREEN READER HEARS EACH λ ROW'S PLACE AMONG ITS SIBLINGS, HEARS share's LINE SAYING A LINK IS LONG, TELLS THE clif VIEW'S TWO RETRY BUTTONS APART, AND HEARS THE HEADER'S AND EACH VIEW'S POPOVER BUTTONS AS BUTTONS THAT OPEN SOMETHING, NOT AS MENUS (2026-11-27, branch `a11y-leftovers` on `main` at #207, 6 commits, this entry among them)

Four small items left open by earlier entries' *What this did not close*, gathered in a handoff with no request in the
user's words, and built in a cloud sandbox with no browser. The user chose, on 2026-11-27, answering "1a, 2a, 3a": the
five buttons that claimed `aria-haspopup="menu"` become disclosures, as `share` and `about ▾` already were, which
settles the question #121's fix task 4b left open; the two Retry buttons are named "Retry loading clif" and "Retry
loading machine code"; and the sandbox may install the lockfile's packages and the tools to build the wasm packages.
The third item needed no ruling: a probe found that neither λ layout ever writes a row more than one level past the row
above it (*Verification*).

##### THE CHANGE

- **The λ rows' sibling counts.** `lambda-layout.ts`'s new `treePlaces` gives each row its `aria-setsize` and
  `aria-posinset` among its siblings, the rows at its level under the same parent, the parent being the nearest
  shallower row above it. It keeps a stack of the sets still open and counts the whole list in one pass. `LambdaBody`
  counts it each time its lines change, empties it with them for flat text, and `#row` reads it, since the view draws a
  window of rows and a set runs on past its edges. Before, every row's set was the whole list: in `g (a b c d) (e f g h)` each row was one
  of 3, where `g` stands alone and its two arguments are a pair.
- **share's long-link line.** The link's field takes the focus when the popover shows, before the link is made, and the
  line saying the link is past 2,000 characters comes with the link. It still describes the field, and is now said
  once through the live region as well, with `notices.announce`, since the popover already shows it. It is said only
  while that open's field is on show, so a link that arrives after the popover closed, or opened again, says nothing.
- **The two Retries.** A clif view with both packages failed shows the listing's notice and the machine code panel's,
  each with a button reading Retry. `CLIF_COPY.retryName` and `MC_COPY.retryName` name them, as their `aria-label` and
  their `title`: a name that starts with the word the button shows still answers a spoken "click Retry", and the
  controls gate holds a control's name to its text or its tooltip.
- **The disclosures.** `#workspace`, `#examples` and `#settings` in `index.html` and in the browser harness's `SHELL`,
  and a view's title and `⋯` in `view-header.ts`, lose `aria-haspopup` and keep `aria-controls` and `aria-expanded`.
  None of their popovers holds a menu item, and none has arrow keys between its items but a radio group's own.
  `wireMenu`'s doc now names every header popover a disclosure.

##### THE TESTS

- **`tests/node/lambda-layout.test.ts`**, 7 cases for `treePlaces`: a spine at two widths, a broken λ head, an outline's
  eleven arguments, levels that skip, no rows, and a sweep of 7 terms through both layouts, both ways of writing
  variables, every width from 1 to 60 and three fold patterns, which holds every row to at most one level past the row
  above it and to the siblings counted out by hand.
- **`tests/node/mc-view.test.ts`**: the two names differ and each starts with Retry.
- **`tests/node/app-header.test.ts`**, reading `index.html`: none of the header's five popover buttons has
  `aria-haspopup`, and each has `aria-controls` naming its popover and `aria-expanded="false"`.
- **Browser, written and NOT RUN**: `lambda-body.test.ts`, the counts on known terms and on a 400-argument term drawn in
  a window; `lambda-tree-app.test.ts` and `app.test.ts`, the number of rows laid out read from the spacer's height,
  where they read the first row's `aria-setsize`; `share-popover.test.ts`, the line said once in the live region and
  not drawn as a notice; `clif-pane.test.ts`, both Retries drawn with their names and tooltips, and `mc-pane.test.ts`,
  the machine code panel's; `about-menu.test.ts`, the five header buttons; `view-title.test.ts`, `view-menu.test.ts`
  and `view-header.test.ts`, no `aria-haspopup` where they expected `menu`.

##### THE SABOTAGES

Seven, each of a node test, run at the last code commit: the file copied, broken, the test run, the file restored from
the copy and `cmp` found equal. Every one fired.

| Sabotage | What failed |
|---|---|
| `treePlaces` giving every row the whole list, as before | 6 of the 7 `treePlaces` cases |
| `treePlaces` setting rows by level alone, whatever their parent | 3: a new set under each parent, the nearest shallower parent, and the sweep |
| the outline's arguments two levels down | 3: two `outlineLines` cases and the sweep's check that no level is skipped |
| the machine code Retry named Retry | the `mc-view` case |
| the clif Retry named so it does not start with Retry | the `mc-view` case |
| `aria-haspopup="menu"` back on `#settings` | the `app-header` case and the harness's `SHELL` case |
| `aria-controls` off `#examples` | the `app-header` case |

No browser case could be sabotaged here.

##### THE REVIEW

A fresh reviewer read the whole branch's diff and every commit, ran the touched node files, the comment guard, biome
and three sabotages of its own, each of which fired, and found no defect. It found two things to fix: no roadmap entry
yet, which this is, and `wireMenu`'s doc setting `share` apart as the one disclosure, now fixed. Of its four nits, a
test's precondition message and the both-failed clif case not holding its Retries drawn are fixed; two commit subjects
named the attributes rather than what a reader hears, and one body put the reason for the parent rule backwards, and
those were reworded before the patches left the sandbox, with no change to the code; and the fourth is under *What
this did not close*.

##### WHAT THIS DID NOT CLOSE

- **Not run: any browser case, in Chromium or Firefox, or a screen reader.** What a reader says for the λ rows, for
  share's line in the live region and its description, and for a button whose `title` repeats its name was not heard.
- **In the code layout a broken λ head's body and its application's arguments are siblings**, as their `aria-level`s
  make them: in `(\x. x x x x) y`, the body is 1 of 2 and `y` 2 of 2. The counts follow the levels; whether the levels
  should differ there is a question for the accessibility close-out.
- **The header's popovers are still called menus** in the app's words and class names (the workspace menu,
  `.header-menu`): only the ARIA claim changed.
- **The handoff's other leftovers stay open**: a λ mark said on its first row only, a count hidden when it has no room,
  Chromium's empty width box, the term map's clickable `role="img"`, a clamp notice said three times, and Plan 7 part 7.
- **Branches in flight touch the same files**: hidden-recording-b changes the harness, `view-title.test.ts`,
  `app.test.ts`, `lambda-tree-app.test.ts`, `share-popover.test.ts` and `main.ts`; move-a-view changes `view-header.ts`
  and `view-menu.test.ts`; listing-follows-end will change `clif-pane.ts`.
